'''James Forrest''' (born 7 July 1991) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2025/may/19/james-forrest-s-16-seasons-of-scoring-for-celtic/|title=James Forrest's 16 seasons of scoring for Celtic|first=Celtic|last=FC|date=19 May 2025|website=Celtic FC}}</ref>

Forrest joined [[Celtic F.C. Reserve and Youth squads|Celtic's youth academy]] in 2003 and made his first team debut for the club in May 2010, during the [[2009–10 Celtic F.C. season|2009–10 season]]. A [[List of one-club men in association football|one-club man]], he has been a linchpin in a successful era for Celtic, and is the most decorated player in the club's history, having won 28 trophies.

Forrest played at every youth level for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]], winning 13 caps for the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19 team]], scoring two goals, and four caps for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21 team]]. He made his senior international debut on 29 May 2011 against the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]]. He was part of the Scotland squads at [[UEFA Euro 2020]] and [[UEFA Euro 2024]].

==Early life==
Forrest attended [[Prestwick Academy]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hepburn |first=Henry |title=Scotland players' old schools send good luck messages |language=en |work=[[TES (magazine)|TES]] |url=https://www.tes.com/magazine/archived/scotland-players-old-schools-send-good-luck-messages |access-date=2022-02-09}}</ref> He had the prospect of a professional [[tennis]] career when he was younger.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 August 2011 |title=I gave up tennis for Celtic – now I'll win match point against Utrecht, says Hoops starlet James Forrest |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/2010/08/23/i-gave-up-tennis-for-celtic-now-i-ll-win-match-point-against-utrecht-says-hoops-starlet-james-forrest-86908-22507602/ |access-date=24 November 2011 |website=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=Media Scotland}}</ref> He was consistently approached by Prestwick Tennis Club to play for them, but he refused as he wanted to pursue his career in football. He was described by coaches at the club as being a naturally talented player, who could just "pick up a racquet and play".<ref name="Tennis">{{Cite web |last=Berry |first=Gavin |date=24 August 2011 |title=Celtic whizzkid James Forrest could have signed for Rangers, admits scout who unearthed the Parkhead winger |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/celtic/2010/08/24/celtic-whizzkid-james-forrest-could-have-signed-for-rangers-admits-scout-who-unearthed-the-parkhead-winger-86908-22509792/ |access-date=24 November 2011 |website=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=Media Scotland}}</ref> His younger brother, [[Alan Forrest]], plays for [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]]; their sister Lisa is also a professional footballer for [[Glasgow City F.C.|Glasgow City FC]].<ref>[https://glasgowcityfc.co.uk/blogs/latest/lisa-forrest-signs-first-city-professional-contract Lisa Forrest signs first City professional contract], Glasgow City FC, 18 January 2023</ref><ref>[https://www.pressreader.com/uk/sunday-mail-uk/20230611/282978224404454 Brother's advice has given me new Lisa life], Alison McConnell, ''Sunday Mail'', 11 June 2023, via [[PressReader]]</ref>

==Club career==

===Early career===
Forrest played for South Ayr Boys Club, and consistently shone at every level. He was scouted by Celtic's talent spotter for [[Ayrshire]], Jim Began, at the age of 11. Several other clubs such as [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] were also interested in him. He signed youth terms with Celtic at the age of 13 and then joined Celtic's coaching school in [[Hamilton, South Lanarkshire|Hamilton]], which his coach Martin Millar credits with helping his development.<ref name="Tennis" />

===Celtic===
====2009–10====
Forrest had always excelled at Celtic, with a match program from 2004 singling him out for exceptional performances in the under-13 squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 September 2009 |title=McCart delighted at Youth Academy signings |url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/stories/news_020909125702.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100111015611/http://www.celticfc.net/news/stories/news_020909125702.aspx |archive-date=11 January 2010 |publisher=Celtic FC}}</ref> He made his first team debut for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on 1 May 2010, coming on as a late substitute against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]. He scored the third of Celtic's goals in a 4–0 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 May 2010 |title=Celtic 4–0 Motherwell |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/8653021.stm |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

He won the [[Scottish Youth Cup]] with the club in 2009–10, beating rivals [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] 2–0 at [[Hampden Park]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 May 2015 |title=Famous Faces – Youth Cup Final |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/famous-faces-youth-cup-final/ |access-date=15 May 2019 |publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]]}}</ref>

====2010–11====
[[File:James Forrest - Jul2010.jpg|thumb|upright|Forrest playing for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2010]]

He made his first European appearance for Celtic in a [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] qualifying game against [[SC Braga|Braga]] in July 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kelso |first=Paul |date=2 July 2012 |title=London 2012 Olympics: Stuart Pearce names Team GB football squad |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/olympics/football/9369976/London-2012-Olympics-Stuart-Pearce-names-Team-GB-football-squad.html |via=www.telegraph.co.uk}}</ref> A few days later he won the [[man of the match]] award for his performance in the [[Emirates Cup]] game with [[Olympique Lyonnais]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 July 2010 |title=Celtic 2–2 Lyon – Forrest |url=http://www.skysports.com/video/inline/0,26691,12606_6288510,00.html |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref> He continued this fine form into the league campaign, scoring against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in a 4–0 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 August 2010 |title=Celtic 4–0 St Mirren |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/8930126.stm |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Forrest played in both legs of Celtic's Europa League qualifier against [[FC Utrecht|Utrecht]]. Forrest was named the [[Scottish Premier League monthly awards|SPL Young Player of the Month]] for August 2010<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 September 2010 |title=Celtic's James Forrest wins SPL young player award |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/celtic/8990768.stm |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> In the following month Forrest opened the scoring against Hearts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lindsay |first=Clive |date=11 September 2010 |title=Celtic 3-0 Hearts |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/8986073.stm |access-date=25 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He made his [[Old Firm]] debut in a 2–0 win at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]] in January 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lindsay |first=Clive |date=2 January 2011 |title=Rangers 0-2 Celtic |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/9330644.stm |access-date=10 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He received the first red card of his career in the following match against [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 January 2011 |title=Celtic's James Forrest loses red card appeal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/celtic/9360812.stm |access-date=10 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He scored against Hearts, before being rewarded for his form with a new five-year deal on 28 January 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 January 2011 |title=Celtic 4-0 Hearts |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/9372934.stm |access-date=25 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=28 January 2011 |title=Celtic give teenage midfielder James Forrest a new five-year deal |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/celtic/2011/01/28/celtic-give-teenage-midfielder-james-forrest-a-new-five-year-deal-86908-22882627/ |access-date=24 November 2011 |website=Daily Record |publisher=Media Scotland}}</ref> Forrest collected his first winner's medal on 21 May 2011 when he came on a late second-half substitute for [[Kris Commons]] in Celtic's 3–0 [[Scottish Cup Final]] win over Motherwell.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Forsyth |first=Roddy |date=21 May 2011 |title=Scottish Cup final 2011: Celtic 3 Motherwell 0 match report |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/celtic/8528267/Scottish-Cup-final-2011-Celtic-3-Motherwell-0-match-report.html |access-date=8 March 2014 |website=The Daily Telegraph}}</ref> He finished the season with 3 goals and 1 assist after 25 appearances.

====2011–12====
In August 2011, [[Scott Brown (footballer, born June 1985)|Scott Brown]] said that Forrest was the best player to come out of the [[Celtic F.C. Reserve and Youth squads|Celtic youth academy]] since [[Aiden McGeady]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 September 2011 |title=Celtic starlet James Forrest is the best youngster we've had since Aiden McGeady, says skipper Scott Brown |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/2011/09/13/celtic-starlet-james-forrest-is-the-best-youngster-we-ve-had-since-aiden-mcgeady-says-skipper-scott-brown-86908-23416960/ |access-date=24 September 2011 |website=Daily Record |publisher=Media Scotland}}</ref> Forrest scored his first goal of the season in a 5–1 victory against Dundee United and his performances in the month of September, including two goals in a 4–0 victory against Motherwell and another goal against Inverness Caledonian Thistle, saw him win [[Scottish Premier League monthly awards|SPL Young Player of the Month]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 October 2011 |title=Celtic winger James Forrest picks up September award |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15415767 |access-date=9 December 2011 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> In Celtic's [[Scottish League Cup]] quarter-final tie with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on 26 October, Forrest was credited with a match-winning performance. Celtic went in at the break 1–0 down but Forrest was instrumental in reigniting the tie after half-time, with two early goals.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 October 2011 |title=Hibernian 1–4 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15363366 |access-date=26 November 2011 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In November 2011, the [[Scottish Football Association]]'s Dutch performance director [[Mark Wotte]] said that he saw Forrest as being "the light in the darkness" of Scottish football.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 November 2011 |title=James Forrest & Gregg Wylde can brighten Scottish game |last=Keown |first=Gary |url=https://www.express.co.uk/sport/football/282376/James-Forrest-Gregg-Wylde-can-brighten-Scottish-game |access-date=24 November 2011 |website=Daily Express |publisher=Northern and Shell Media Publications}}</ref> He said that if more players like Forrest are produced then the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland team]] will be able to match the performance of countries like [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]], who got to the [[2010 FIFA World Cup knockout stage|2010 World Cup semi-final]] and at the time were fourth in the [[FIFA World Rankings]] despite having a population smaller than Scotland's.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 November 2011 |title=Produce more players like James Forrest and Scotland can match sides like Uruguay, says Mark Wotte |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/scotland/2011/11/08/produce-more-players-like-james-forrest-and-scotland-can-match-sides-like-uruguay-says-mark-wotte-86908-23546147/ |access-date=24 November 2011 |website=Daily Record |publisher=Media Scotland}}</ref>

Forrest played in all of Celtic's matches in the Europa League qualifiers and group stage. He scored against Dunfermline and won the SPL Young Player of the Month award for November, his second of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Forsyth |first=Roddy |date=23 November 2011 |title=Celtic 2 Dunfermline 1: match report |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/celtic/8911230/Celtic-2-Dunfermline-1-match-report.html |access-date=25 May 2018 |website=The Daily Telegraph}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 December 2011 |title=Celtic's Neil Lennon, Gary Hooper and James Forrest win awards |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16110735 |access-date=9 December 2011 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> In January 2012, Forrest was named one of the 13 players to watch in 2012 by world football governing body [[FIFA]].<ref>[http://static.fifa.com/photos/galleries/y=2012/m=1/gallery=players-watch-2012-1567835.html#1508206 Players to watch in 2012]{{dead link|date=October 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}, [[FIFA]]</ref> He scored against St Mirren and Dunfermline<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murray |first=Ewan |date=21 January 2012 |title=St Mirren 0-2 Celtic {{!}} Scottish Premier League match report |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/jan/21/st-mirren-celtic-spl |access-date=25 May 2018 |website=The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Murray |first=Ewan |date=22 February 2012 |title=Celtic 2-0 Dunfermline {{!}} Scottish Premier League match report |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/feb/22/celtic-dunfermline-spl-match-report |access-date=25 May 2018 |website=The Guardian}}</ref> before his season ended after suffering an injury during Celtic's defeat to Kilmarnock in the [[2012 Scottish League Cup Final]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Swan |first=Craig |date=12 April 2012 |title=Celtic fear ankle injury could rule starlet James Forrest out for the rest of season |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/celtic-fear-ankle-injury-could-1119049 |access-date=25 May 2018 |website=Daily Record}}</ref> He finished the season having scored 9 goals and made 7 assists in 43 appearances and won his second major honour at the end of the season when Celtic finished as SPL Champions.<ref name="lgwin">{{Cite web |last=Swan |first=Craig |date=4 May 2012 |title=Young Player of the Year James Forrest pleads with Celtic not to sell him in summer |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/young-player-of-the-year-james-forrest-877062 |access-date=8 March 2014 |website=Daily Record}}</ref> His form over the season also saw him win two personal awards as both the [[Scottish Football Writers' Association]] and [[Professional Footballers' Association Scotland]] voted him their respective Young Player of the Year as well as being named in the PFA Scotland SPL Team of the Year.<ref name="lgwin" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=6 May 2012 |title=PFA Scotland Player of the Year Awards |url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/pfa-scotland-player-of-the-year-awards.17518669 |access-date=8 March 2014 |website=The Herald}}</ref>

====2012–13====
[[File:James Forrest 2012.jpg|thumb|upright|Forrest playing for Celtic in 2012]]

Forrest played in all four [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League qualifying phase and play-off round|Champions League]] qualifiers in August 2012, as Celtic reached the group stage for the first time since 2008. He played in three out of six group stage matches and made an impact as a substitute in a 3–2 victory away to [[FC Spartak Moscow|Spartak Moscow]], which was Celtic's first away victory in the Champions League.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Esplin |first=Ronnie |date=2 September 2012 |title=Spartak Moscow 2 Celtic 3: match report |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/celtic/9582588/Spartak-Moscow-2-Celtic-3-match-report.html |access-date=9 May 2018 |website=The Daily Telegraph}}</ref> He missed Celtic's famous 2–1 victory against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] due to injury. Forrest suffered with injury throughout the season scoring four and assisting eight goals in 29 appearances.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 May 2013 |title=Celric: Bobby Petta's James Forrest injury fears |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/teams/celtic/celtic-bobby-petta-s-james-forrest-injury-fears-1-2942435 |access-date=10 May 2018 |website=The Scotsman}}</ref> He scored his first goal of the season in a 4–0 victory against [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in December.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lamont |first=Alasdair |date=22 December 2012 |title=Celtic 4-0 Ross County |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20738249 |access-date=25 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He scored his first goal in the [[Scottish Cup]] against [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Stevie |date=3 February 2013 |title=Raith Rovers 0-3 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21218450 |access-date=25 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He played in both legs of Celtic's 5–0 aggregate defeat to [[Juventus F.C|Juventus]] in the last 16 of the Champions League. He scored a penalty against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] and scored on the final league game of the season against [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Forsyth |first=Roddy |date=24 February 2013 |title=Celtic 5 Dundee 0: match report |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/celtic/9891362/Celtic-5-Dundee-0-match-report.html |access-date=25 May 2018 |website=The Daily Telegraph}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lindsay |first=Clive |date=11 May 2013 |title=Celtic 4-0 St Johnstone |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22409613 |access-date=25 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Forrest finished the season with a second consecutive league title and his second Scottish Cup winners medal after starting Celtic's 3–0 win against Hibernian in the final.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lamont |first=Alasdair |date=26 May 2013 |title=Scottish Cup final: Hibernian 0-3 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22585339 |access-date=10 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

====2013–14====
In July 2013, Forrest scored his first European goal for Celtic in a second round Champions League Qualifier against [[Cliftonville F.C.|Cliftonville]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Petrie |first=Richard |date=17 July 2013 |title=Cliftonville 0-3 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23251252 |access-date=10 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> In the following month he scored against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in the league and scored a memorable third and decisive goal in the final moments of the second leg of the Champions League play-off against [[FC Shakhter Karagandy|Shakhter Karagandy]] - which Celtic won 3–2 and qualified for the group stage for the second year in a row.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murray |first=Keir |date=17 August 2013 |title=Aberdeen 0-2 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23644812 |access-date=24 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Forsyth |first=Roddy |date=28 August 2013 |title=Celtic 3 Shakhter Karagandy 0; 3-2 agg: match report |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/celtic/10272143/Celtic-3-Shakhter-Karagandy-0-3-2-agg-match-report.html |access-date=10 May 2018 |website=The Daily Telegraph}}</ref> Having played in every qualifying match Forrest missed all of Celtic's games in September after suffering from a virus.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Halliday |first=Stephen |date=21 September 2013 |title=James Forrest's hospital stay has Lennon fretting |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/teams/celtic/james-forrest-s-hospital-stay-has-lennon-fretting-1-3104726 |access-date=10 May 2018 |website=The Scotsman}}</ref> His return to action in October saw Forrest score an impressive goal against Hibernian and he played in four Champions League group stage matches, and scored a penalty in Celtic's 2–1 victory against [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lindsay |first=Clive |date=19 October 2013 |title=Hibernian 1-1 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24503746 |access-date=10 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Keith |date=23 October 2013 |title=Celtic boss Neil Lennon says that penalty strike against Ajax showed James Forrest has composure at the highest level |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/celtic-boss-neil-lennon-says-2482331 |access-date=10 May 2018 |website=Daily Record}}</ref> Forrest was arrested by police in November 2013 over allegations of indecent exposure and sexual assault at a nightclub in [[Prestwick]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 November 2013 |title=Celtic player James Forrest arrested over alleged sexual assault |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-glasgow-west-25102654 |access-date=10 May 2018 |publisher=BBC News}}</ref> He would score two further goals in the league against Hearts and Aberdeen before injury ended his season in March.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Campbell |first=Andy |date=21 December 2013 |title=Celtic 2-0 Heart of Midlothian |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25376933 |access-date=24 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Southwick |first=Andy |date=25 February 2014 |title=Aberdeen 2-1 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25892139 |access-date=24 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McCarthy |first=David |date=12 March 2014 |title=New injury blow for Celtic winger James Forrest as he picks up groin strain on Scotland duty |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/new-injury-blow-celtic-winger-3232297 |access-date=10 May 2018 |website=Daily Record}}</ref> He scored 7 goals and assisted 5 in only 27 appearances in another injury dominated season as Celtic won three league titles in a row.

====2014–15====
Forrest's injury issues continued after suffering a hamstring injury against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in the first home game of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Waddell |first=Gordon |date=17 August 2014 |title=Celtic hit Dundee United for six but James Forrest and Adam Matthews are doubts for Euro clash |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/celtic-hit-dundee-united-six-4063548 |access-date=10 May 2018 |website=Daily Record}}</ref> He only returned from injury in November and despite scoring his first goal of the season against St Mirren in December, Forrest was in and out of the team throughout the winter as both the player and coaching staff did not feel confident that Forrest's injury problems were over.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McVake |first=Roddie |date=14 December 2014 |title=Celtic 4-1 St Mirren |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30366033 |access-date=10 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=30 December 2014 |title=Celtic must take care with James Forrest - Ronny Deila |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30638893 |access-date=10 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Two of Forrest's three European appearances came in the [[2014–15 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] including coming on as a substitute in the second leg of Celtic's 4-3 aggregate defeat to [[Inter Milan]] in the last 32 of the competition. He featured more often in the Spring and came on as a substitute in Celtic's 2–0 victory against Dundee United in the [[2015 Scottish League Cup Final|Scottish League Cup Final]], scoring the second goal before earning his side a penalty which he would fail to convert.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Richard |date=15 March 2015 |title=Dundee United 0-2 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31785677 |access-date=10 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He would score two further goals in the league against St Mirren and Dundee.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Richard |date=3 April 2015 |title=St Mirren 0-2 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32077466 |access-date=24 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Southwick |first=Andrew |date=1 May 2015 |title=Celtic 5-0 Dundee |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32443335 |access-date=24 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Forrest made 29 appearances and scored and assisted 4 goals as Celtic won the league for the fourth consecutive season.

====2015–16====
Despite playing more games in a season free of injury Forrest only scored and assisted 2 goals in 33 appearances - scoring his two goals against Aberdeen and Hamilton in the league.<ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=31 October 2015 |title=Celtic 3-1 Aberdeen |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34623816 |access-date=23 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=19 January 2016 |title=Celtic 8-1 Hamilton Academical |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35107167 |access-date=24 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He featured in much of the first half of the season, including five appearances in both the Champions League qualifiers and the [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] group stage, before being dropped by manager [[Ronny Deila]] after rejecting a new contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Valente |first=Allan |date=22 February 2016 |title=Celtic's James Forrest set for exit after rejecting new contract |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11787/10177623/celtics-james-forrest-set-for-exit-after-rejecting-new-contract |access-date=15 September 2018 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref> He only made nine more appearances after the new year as Celtic won the league for the fifth year in a row.

====2016–17====
Forrest signed a three-year contract with Celtic in August 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 August 2016 |title=James Forrest: Celtic winger signs up until 2019 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37036659 |access-date=10 August 2016 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He started the season strongly scoring Celtic's first goal of the season away to Hearts and scored in the following two league games against St Johnstone and Aberdeen.<ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=7 August 2016 |title=Heart of Midlothian 1-2 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36934942 |access-date=9 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=20 August 2016 |title=St Johnstone 2-4 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37067774 |access-date=23 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=27 August 2018 |title=Celtic 4-1 Aberdeen |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37139495 |access-date=23 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> In September he scored on his 200th appearance for Celtic against [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] in the league cup and scored his fifth goal of the season against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dale |first=James |date=22 September 2016 |title=Celtic 2-0 Alloa - Match Report & Highlights |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/celtic-vs-alloa/366672 |access-date=9 May 2018 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=24 September 2016 |title=Celtic 6-1 Kilmarnock |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37393462 |access-date=23 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Forrest played in every match Champions League qualifier and five group stage matches including draws home and away to [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]. On 27 November 2016 Forrest scored the second goal and won a penalty in a man of the match performance in the [[2016 Scottish League Cup Final (November)|League Cup final]] as Celtic defeated Aberdeen 3–0 to win the club's 100th trophy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fowler |first=Craig |date=27 November 2016 |title=James Forrest justifies selection with man-of-the-match award |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/teams/celtic/james-forrest-justifies-selection-with-man-of-the-match-award-1-4302498 |access-date=9 May 2018 |website=The Scotsman}}</ref> After the winter break Forrest only scored two more goals against Motherwell and Kilmarnock.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 February 2018 |title=James Forrest seals victory as Celtic canter past Motherwell |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/feb/18/celtic-motherwell-scottish-premiership-match-report |access-date=23 May 2018 |website=The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Barnes |first=John |date=8 April 2017 |title=Celtic 3-1 Kilmarnock |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39463978 |access-date=23 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Forrest was an unused substitute as Celtic defeated Aberdeen 2–1 in the [[2017 Scottish Cup Final|Scottish Cup Final]] to win the [[Treble (association football)|treble]] for the fourth time in their history and for the first time in 16 years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=27 May 2017 |title=Celtic 2-1 Aberdeen: Brendan Rodgers' side win Scottish Cup and domestic treble |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39984102 |access-date=9 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Forrest made 46 appearances and scored 8 goals and assisted 13 as Celtic finished the domestic season without defeat after 47 matches to be nicknamed the "Invincibles".

====2017–18====
[[File:20170701 SK Rapid Wien vs Celtic FC 1554.jpg|thumb|upright|Forrest playing for Celtic in 2017]]

The beginning of the [[2017–18 Celtic F.C. season|2017–18 season]] saw Forrest play in every Champions League qualifier as he helped Celtic qualify for the group stage by scoring the decisive goal away to [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] in a 1–0 aggregate victory in the third round and he scored another goal in an 8–4 aggregate win against [[FC Astana|Astana]] in the play-off round.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 August 2017 |title=Celtic progress thanks to stunning James Forrest strike |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40732241 |access-date=22 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Richard |date=16 August 2018 |title=Celtic 5-0 FC Astana |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40936642 |access-date=22 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Forrest scored against Kilmarnock as he played as a striker in the absence of [[Moussa Dembélé (French footballer)|Moussa Dembélé]] and [[Leigh Griffiths]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Andrew |date=19 August 2018 |title=Changed Celtic coast to victory |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/competitions/premiership/kilmarnock-0-2-celtic-changed-celtic-coast-to-victory-1-4536537 |access-date=22 May 2018 |website=The Scotsman}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McConnell |first=Alison |date=29 July 2017 |title=James Forrest can play striker's role if Leigh Griffiths doesn't make it, says Brendan Rodgers |url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/15442334.James_Forrest_can_play_the_striker__39_s_role_if_Leigh_Griffiths_doesn__39_t_make_it__says_Brendan_Rodgers/ |access-date=22 May 2018 |website=The Herald}}</ref> His strong start to the season continued into September as he scored twice against Ross County in the league and scored another two goals in the following match against Dundee in the League Cup.<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 September 2017 |title=Forrest and Dembélé steal the show as Celtic thrash Ross County |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/sep/16/celtic-ross-county-scottish-premiership-match-report |access-date=22 May 2018 |website=The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McLaughlin |first=Chris |date=20 September 2017 |title=Dundee 0-4 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41234604 |access-date=15 September 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Forrest played in all of Celtic's group stage matches in the Champions League including an impressive performance against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] as he provided the assist for [[Callum McGregor]] to equalise in a 2–1 defeat at Celtic Park.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cameron |first=Neil |date=2 November 2018 |title=Unsung hero James Forrest is Celtic's bemusing and sometimes brilliant winger |url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/news/15633378.Unsung_hero_James_Forrest_is_Celtic_s_bemusing_and_sometimes_brilliant_winger/ |access-date=21 May 2018 |website=Evening Times}}</ref> On 26 November 2017, Forrest scored his third goal in a League Cup final – becoming the first Celtic player since [[Bobby Lennox]] to score in three winning League Cup finals – after opening the scoring in a 2–0 win against Motherwell.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cameron |first=Neil |date=27 November 2018 |title=James Forrest equals Celtic legend Bobby Lennox's record of scoring in three winning League Cup finals |url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/15684978.James_Forrest_equals_Celtic_legend_Bobby_Lennox_s_record_by_scoring_in_three_winning_League_Cup_finals/ |access-date=21 May 2018 |website=The Herald}}</ref>

In December, Forrest's goal tally for the season reached double figures for the first time after scoring twice against Motherwell in the league and he scored two more goals against Hamilton and Dundee before the winter break.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McLaughlin |first=Chris |date=2 December 2017 |title=Celtic 5-1 Motherwell |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42119901 |access-date=22 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Spiers |first=Graham |date=15 December 2017 |title=James Forrest fired up for more after hitting double figures for Celtic |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/james-forrest-fired-up-for-more-after-hitting-double-figures-with-celtic-ff2n6mwhc |access-date=21 May 2018 |website=[[The Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Forsyth |first=Roddy |date=26 December 2017 |title=James Forrest and Leigh Griffiths goals move Celtic 11 points clear |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/12/26/dundee-0-celtic-2james-forrest-leigh-griffiths-goals-move-celtic/ |access-date=22 May 2018 |website=The Daily Telegraph}}</ref> After returning to action in January Forrest opened the scoring against [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] in the Scottish Cup.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 January 2018 |title=James Forrest sparks Celtic's Scottish Cup romp against Brechin City |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/jan/20/celtic-brechin-scottish-cup-match-report |access-date=22 May 2018 |website=The Guardian}}</ref> In the following month Forrest scored the first hat-trick of his career against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in a 3–2 win in the fifth round of the Scottish Cup.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 February 2018 |title=Celtic 3-2 Partick Thistle |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42927891 |access-date=21 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He played in both legs of Celtic's 3–1 aggregate defeat to [[FC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit]] in the round of 32 of the Europa League. His performances throughout the season saw him nominated for [[PFA Scotland Players' Player of the Year]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 April 2018 |title=Kris Boyd, John McGinn & Celtic's Scott Brown & James Forrest up for PFA award |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43891579 |access-date=21 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 29 April 2018, Forrest scored his first goal in an Old Firm derby as Celtic won the league for the seventh season in a row after a 5–0 win against Rangers at Celtic Park – the club's biggest winning margin in an Old Firm league fixture.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Halliday |first=Stephen |date=29 April 2018 |title=Celtic crush rivals to secure title |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/competitions/premiership/celtic-5-0-rangers-celtic-crush-rivals-to-secure-title-1-4732038 |access-date=21 May 2018 |website=The Scotsman}}</ref> Forrest played in Celtic's 2–0 victory against Motherwell in the Scottish Cup Final as Celtic became the first Scottish club to win back-to-back trebles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=19 May 2018 |title=Celtic 2-0 Motherwell |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44091573 |access-date=21 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Forrest ended his most successful season to date having made 58 appearances – among the highest number of games played in professional football that season – and scored 17 goals and assisted 10.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McConnell |first=Alison |date=19 May 2018 |title=Celtic's Iron Man James Forrest ready for one last push |url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/16236633.Celtic__39_s_Iron_Man_James_Forrest_ready_for_one_last_push/ |access-date=21 May 2018 |website=Evening Times}}</ref>

====2018–19====
Forrest began the [[2018–19 Celtic F.C. season|2018–19 season]] as first choice right-winger and he scored in both legs in the first round of Champions League qualifiers against [[FC Alashkert|Alashkert]]. He conceded a penalty and was sent off as last defender in a 3–1 [[2018–19 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] group stage defeat away to [[FC Red Bull Salzburg]] on 4 October 2018,<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 October 2018 |title=Red Bull Salzburg 3-1 Celtic: James Forrest sent off as Celtic beaten in Europa League |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/salzburg-vs-celtic/401953 |access-date=8 October 2018 |website=Sky Sports}}</ref> at which time he was yet to score in the domestic campaign. However he kept his place for the next league fixture against St Johnstone at [[McDiarmid Park]] and responded positively, scoring four goals (the first Celtic player in six years to do so)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celtic Hattrick List |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/celtic/player_hattricks.php |access-date=8 October 2018 |website=FitbaStats}}</ref> in the first half of an eventual 6–0 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 October 2018 |title=St Johnstone 0-6 Celtic: James Forrest scores four for Brendan Rodgers side |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45696331 |access-date=8 October 2018 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Further goals against Hearts in the semi-final of the league cup and Dundee in the league saw him win [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners|Scottish Premiership Player of the Month]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2 November 2018 |title=Celtic: Brendan Rodgers & James Forrest win monthly awards for October |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46074376 |access-date=23 January 2022}}</ref>

In November he helped Celtic progress to the knock out stage of the Europe league by providing assists in wins against [[RB Leipzig]] and [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sutherland |first=Jonathan |date=8 November 2018 |title=Celtic 2-1 RB Leipzig |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46087337 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Palmer |first=Bryn |date=29 November 2018 |title=Celtic 1-0 Rosenborg |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46335948 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He started Celtic's 1–0 victory against Aberdeen in the league cup final against Hearts in the league. In December Forrest scored twice against Kilmarnock in a 5–1 win.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sutherland |first=Jonathan |date=8 Dec 2018 |title=Celtic 5-1 Kilmarnock |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46409220 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Following the winter break Forrest opened the scoring against St Johnstone in the league and would score against the Perth side again in the Scottish Cup.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lindsay |first=Clive |date=3 February 2019 |title=St Johnstone 0-2 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47018251 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=10 February 2019 |title=Celtic 5-0 St Johnstone |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47106087 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He opened the scoring in a 2–1 win against Hearts in the first match of Neil Lennon's second tenure as Celtic manager.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Duncan |first=Thomas |date=27 February 2019 |title=Hearts 1-2 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47301045 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He played in both legs of the Europa League defeat against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] in the Europa League round of 32.

In March Forrest opened the scoring with a long range strike against Hibernian in the Scottish Cup quarter-final.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 March 2019 |title=Hibernian 0-2 Celtic: Lennon lauds 'Celtic greats' Brown & Forrest |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/47430509 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 31 March 2019 he scored a late winning goal against Rangers in a 2–1 win in the league.<ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=31 March 2019 |title=Celtic 2-1 Rangers |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47682925 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 14 April 2019 Forrest opened the scoring against Aberdeen in the Scottish Cup semi-final with a long range strike.<ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=14 April 2019 |title=Aberdeen 0-3 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47792155 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> After the match manager Neil Lennon described Forrest as "One of the best players in Britain right now".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lamont |first=Alasdair |date=14 April 2019 |title=James Forrest: Celtic winger 'one of best players in Britain' - Neil Lennon |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/47928822 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He started Celtic's 2–1 victory against Hearts in the Scottish Cup final to complete a historic third consecutive treble.

Forrest equalled his goal tally from the previous season with 17 goals as Celtic won an eighth consecutive Scottish league championship, and Forrest won the [[PFA Scotland Players' Player of the Year|PFA Scotland]], [[SFWA Footballer of the Year|Scottish Football Writers']] and [[Scottish Professional Football League yearly awards|SPFL Player of the Year]] awards.<ref name="POTY">{{Cite web |date=5 May 2019 |title=James Forrest, Steve Clarke & Ryan Kent win PFA Scotland annual awards |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48171966 |access-date=6 May 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=James Forrest: Celtic winger is Scottish Premiership player of the year |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48380812 |access-date=23 May 2019 }}</ref><ref name="SPFLpoy19">{{Cite web |date=23 May 2019 |title=Celtic winger James Forrest completes personal treble by winning Ladbrokes Premiership Player of the Year |url=https://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/17659658.celtic-winger-james-forrest-completes-personal-treble-by-winning-ladbrokes-premiership-player-of-the-year// |access-date=25 May 2019 |website=[[Evening Times]]}}</ref>

====2019–20====
Forrest started the 2019–20 season in excellent goal scoring form with six goals in the month of August. He scored in both legs of Celtic's defeat to [[CFR Cluj|Cluj]] in the third round of qualifying in the Champions League.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Southwick |first=Andrew |date=7 August 2019 |title=Cluj 1-1 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49258651 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=13 August 2019 |title=Celtic 3-4 Cluj |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49323840 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He also scored in both legs of the Europa League play-off against [[AIK Fotboll|AIK]] as Celtic progressed to the group stage.<ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=22 August 2019 |title=Celtic 2-0 AIK |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49400135 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mullen |first=Scott |date=29 August 2019 |title=AIK 1-4 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49498377 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Forrest found the net against Motherwell in the league, then scored the winning goal against Dunfermline with a deflected strike in extra time in the League Cup.<ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=10 August 2019 |title=Motherwell 2-5 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49214576 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Duncan |first=Thomas |date=17 August 2019 |title=Celtic 2-1 Dunfermline |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49324298 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> In September, Forrest scored the winning goal against Hamilton in the Premiership.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Watt |first=Martin |date=14 September 2019 |title=Hamilton 0-1 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49617946 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> and in the Europa League he won a penalty to help Celtic earn a 1–1 draw in their opening match against [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Stade Rennais]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Idessane |date=19 September 2019 |title=Rennes 1-1 Celtic: Christie's penalty earns visitors Europa League point |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/49663645 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In October 2019 he spoke of his hope of a new contract with Celtic. On 30 October, he signed a new contract, keeping him at the club until 2023.<ref>{{Cite news |date=28 October 2019 |title=James Forrest: Celtic winger ready to extend stay with Scottish champions |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50211621 }}</ref> He scored three goals in the league in that month with strikes against Ross County, Aberdeen and St Mirren.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lamont |first=Alasdair |date=19 October 2019 |title=Celtic 6-0 Ross County |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50024362 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Southwick |first=Andrew |date=27 October 2019 |title=Aberdeen 0-4 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50113518 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Watt |first=Martin |date=30 October 2019 |title=Celtic 2-0 St Mirren |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50148207 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 7 Nov 2019, Forrest scored in the equalising goal in the [[Stadio Olimpico]] against [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]] in the Europa league. Celtic would go on to win the game to earn their first-ever away victory in Italy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Idessane |first=Kheredine |date=7 November 2019 |title=Lazio 1-2 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50253786 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Forrest played in five group stage matches in the Europa League and provided assists in wins against Cluj and Stade Rennais as Celtic finished top of their group for the first time in their history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=English |first=Tom |date=28 November 2019 |title=Celtic 3-1 Rennes |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50489724 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Later in November he scored two goals in a league win against Livingston.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Southwick |first=Andrew |date=23 November 2019 |title=Celtic 4-0 Livingston |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50443022 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> In December he scored against St Mirren and started Celtic's 1–0 win against Rangers in the League Cup Final.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Watt |first=Martin |date=26 December 2019 |title=St Mirren 1-2 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50847211 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Following the winter break he scored two further goals in the league against St Johnstone and Hamilton.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Elgott |first=Jordan |date=29 January 2020 |title=St Johnstone 0-3 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51201804 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lamont |first=Alasdair |date=2 February 2020 |title=Hamilton 1-4 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51253100 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He played in both legs of Celtic's defeat to [[F.C. Copenhagen|Copenhagen]] in the Europa league round of 32. The Coronavirus pandemic saw the season end early as Celtic won the league for a [[Nine in a row|ninth consecutive season]]; Forrest finished the season with 16 goals.

====2020–21====
In August Forrest scored his first goal of the 2020–21 campaign by opening the scoring against Motherwell in the league - making him only the ninth player in the previous 45 years to score in the 12 consecutive seasons in the top flight of Scottish football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Andrew |date=10 September 2020 |title=James Forrest's scoring feat sees him match the likes of Ally McCoist, Davie Cooper, Paul McStay and John Robertson |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/celtic/james-forrests-scoring-feat-sees-him-match-the-likes-of-ally-mccoist-davie-cooper-paul-mcstay-and-john-robertson-2966779 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=The Scotsman}}</ref> In September he scored the winning goal against St Mirren with a header in a 2–1 league victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Watt |first=Martin |date=17 September 2020 |title=St Mirren 1-2 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53655368 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 24 September 2020 Forrest was forced off with an ankle injury against [[Riga FC|Riga]] in the third round of Europa league qualification. The injury would rule Forrest out until March 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Currie |first=David |date=19 February 2021 |title=James Forrest: Celtic & Scotland winger close to return after rehab setback |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56128915 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He missed all of Celtic's Europa league group matches as well as the delayed 2020 Scottish Cup final which saw Celtic win a fourth consecutive treble against Hearts. By the time Forrest returned to action [[John Kennedy (Scottish footballer)|John Kennedy]] had been appointed caretaker manager after Celtic's faltering league campaign saw Neil Lennon resign as manager. Forrest made his return as a substitute in a 0–0 draw with Dundee United which saw Rangers confirmed as league champions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Duncan |first=Thomas |date=7 March 2021 |title=Dundee United 0-0 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56227416 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> In April Forrest scored his third and fourth goals of an injury plagued season against Falkirk in the cup and Livingston in the league as Celtic finished the 2020–21 season without a trophy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Campbell |first=Andy |date=3 April 2021 |title=Celtic 3-0 Falkirk |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55776821 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Watt |first=Martin |date=10 April 2021 |title=Celtic 6-0 Livingston |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56563703 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

====2021–22====
Forrest's pre-season was disrupted as he went into self-isolation due to being a close contact to a positive Coronavirus case.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 July 2021 |title=Celtic: James Forrest missing from Newport training camp after 'close contact' with Covid case |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57743840 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He scored his first goals for [[Ange Postecoglou]] in both legs against [[FK Jablonec|Jablonec]] in the third round of Europa league qualifying.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Watt |first=Martin |date=5 August 2021 |title=Jablonec 2-4 Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58007178 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Southwick |first=Andrew |date=12 August 2021 |title=Celtic 3-0 Jablonec |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58138071 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Forrest sustained an injury in the first league of the Europa league play-off against [[AZ Alkmaar]] which ruled him out until late October. On 20 November 2021 Forrest came on as a substitute and scored the only goal of the game as Celtic defeated League Cup holders St Johnstone in the semi-final of the competition.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McPheat |first=Nick |date=20 November 2021 |title=Celtic 1-0 St Johnstone |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59293414 |access-date=23 January 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He would miss Celtic's 2–1 victory against Hibernian in the League Cup final due to injury.

====2022–23====
Forrest reached the mark of 100 club goals for Celtic with a hat-trick against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on 15 October 2022,<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63182414 Celtic 6–1 Hibernian], BBC Sport, 15 October 2022</ref> becoming the 30th player in the club's history to do so.<ref>[https://www.celticway.co.uk/news/23052029.celtics-30-goalscoring-centurions-full-james-forrest-adds-name-illustrious-list/ Celtic's Goalscoring Centurions], Celtic Way, 15 October 2022</ref> On 17 December 2022, Forrest became the third player, along with [[Jimmy Johnstone]] and [[Henrik Larsson]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.glasgowlive.co.uk/sport/football/james-forrest-incredible-celtic-record-25778576 |title=James Forrest incredible Celtic record as veteran joins two Hoops icons in exclusive club after Aberdeen assist |website=Glasgow Live |date=17 December 2022 |accessdate=2 August 2023 |first=Matthew |last=Fulton}}</ref> for Celtic to reach both 100 goals and assists for the club, when he set up [[Callum McGregor]] in a 1–0 against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] at Pittodrie.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63896768 |title=Aberdeen 0-1 Celtic:Callum McGregor scores late winner for champions |website=BBC Sport |date=17 December 2022 |accessdate=2 August 2023 |first=Thomas |last=Duncan}}</ref>

====2023–24====
Celtic announced on 25 May 2023 that Forrest would be given a [[testimonial match]], which was played against [[Athletic Bilbao]] on 1 August.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/celtic-to-play-athletic-bilbao-in-james-forrest-testimonial-match |title=Celtic to play Athletic Bilbao in James Forrest testimonial match |website=STV News |date=25 May 2023 |accessdate=25 May 2023 |first=Andy |last=Coyle}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/23684968.celtic-raise-money-charity-james-forrest-testimonial/ |first=Rebecca |last=Newlands |date=27 July 2023 |accessdate=22 May 2024 |title=Celtic raise money for charity at James Forrest testimonial |newspaper=Glasgow Times}}</ref> Forrest was a bit-part player for much of the 2023–24 season, but was reintroduced to the first team during the spring and had his highest scoring season since 2019–20.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/24329062.reborn-celtic-star-forrest-ready-play-anywhere-scots/ |title=Reborn Celtic star Forrest ready to play anywhere for Scots |newspaper=Glasgow Times |date=17 May 2024 |accessdate=22 May 2024}}</ref>

====2024–25====

Forrest signed a new contract in November 2024, keeping him at the club until May 2026. On 15 December 2024, Celtic won the [[2024 Scottish League Cup final]] against Rangers, giving Forrest his 25th trophy. This moved him level with [[Bobby Lennox]] as the Hoops' most decorated player of all time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/james-forrest-celtic-neil-lennon-scotland-ange-postecoglou-b2665049.html|title=James Forrest hails Celtic's golden era as he wins 25th major honour with club|date=16 December 2024|website=The Independent}}</ref> During the final, Forrest suffered a knee injury which kept him out of action for over three months.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cly7zjgy3pdo|title=Celtic's Rodgers on potential Tierney return, Forrest injury & final fallout|date=20 December 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He made his long-awaited return against Hearts on 29 March 2025 as a substitute for [[Jota (footballer, born March 1999)|Jota]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/25058832.celtic-winger-james-forrest-eager-make-lost-time/|title=Celtic stalwart James Forrest ready to fight for his place after injury return|date=2 April 2025|website=The National}}</ref>

Upon Celtic sealing a 55th Scottish league title on 26 April, Forrest surpassed Lennox and became the most decorated player outright.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/25117681.forrest-creates-celtic-history-moves-beyond-lisbon-lion/|title=Forrest creates Celtic history, moves beyond Lisbon Lion|last=McCafferty|first=Josh|date=26 April 2025|work=The National|accessdate=26 April 2025|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Forrest played down the milestone, telling ''[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]]'', "I think it's nice personally hearing about milestones and stuff like that, but I think it's happened because you've been part of such a really good team over the years, a really good squad, players, staff."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/25086174.forrest-reacts-celtics-decorated-player/|title=Forrest on surpassing Bobby Lennox, and the one quality of all good Celtic teams|last=McGarry|first=Graeme|date=13 April 2025|website=The Herald|accessdate=26 April 2025}}</ref>

After coming on as a substitute during the final league game of the season against St Mirren, Forrest scored a 94th-minute equaliser to earn Celtic a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/25171305.celtic-1-st-mirren-1-instant-reaction-burning-issues/|title=Celtic 1 St Mirren 1: Instant reaction to the burning issues |work=Glasgow Times |date=17 May 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cy8dnz1xg23t|title=Celtic vs St Mirren: Scottish Premiership updates & match report|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> In doing so, he became the first Celtic player since [[Paul McStay]] to score in 16 consecutive seasons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/brendan-rodgers-so-pleased-for-james-forrest-after-he-maintains-celtic-run|title=Rodgers 'so pleased' for Forrest after he maintains Celtic run|author=PA Sport|date=17 May 2025|website=STV News}}</ref>

====2025–26====
Forrest scored against Aberdeen on 21 December and has now scored for Celtic for 17 straight seasons, moving him ahead of McStay and [[Jimmy McGrory]], and level with Bobby Lennox.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c20g36redqzt|title=Nancy survives scare against Aberdeen to claim first Celtic win|last=Canavan|first=Amy|date=21 December 2025|website=BBC Sport|accessdate=22 December 2025}}</ref> The only player to score in more than that was [[Jimmy McMenemy]], who did so for 18 consecutive seasons from 1902 to 1920.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c8r3nem625vo|title=Celtic: James Forrest's 17-season scoring feat in numbers|last=Watt|first=Martin|date=22 December 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

With Celtic's decisive 3-1 victory against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] on the final day of the [[2025-26 Scottish Premiership|league season]], Forrest won his 14th top-flight league title, a British record.<ref>{{cite web |last1=McDonald |first1=Ryan |title=James Forrest's astonishing Celtic record grows as one factor makes double the sweetest of his career |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/james-forrests-astonishing-celtic-record-37198033 |website=Daily Record |access-date=23 May 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Forrest was capped for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] at under-16 and [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19 level]]. He made his debut for the under-19s on 20 October 2008 in a [[UEFA European Under-19 Football Championship|European Championship]] qualifier against [[Azerbaijan national football team|Azerbaijan]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 October 2008 |title=Scotland U19 1–1 Azerbaijan U19 |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/international_fixture_details.cfm?page=106&matchID=81978 |publisher=Scottish FA}}</ref>

Following his fine club form at the start of the [[2010–11 Celtic F.C. season|2010–11 season]], Forrest was called into the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21 side]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 August 2010 |title=James Forrest in Scotland under 21 squad for Euro qualifying double header |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/scotland/2010/08/24/james-forrest-in-scotland-under-21-squad-for-euro-qualifying-double-header-86908-22510496/ |website=Daily Record}}</ref> On 7 September, he came off the bench for Scotland U21s and assisted in the 89th minute for [[Chris Maguire]] to score the winning goal against [[Austria national under-21 football team|Austria]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 September 2010 |title=Scotland U21 2–1 Austria U21 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/scotland/8974522.stm |access-date=23 September 2011 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 17 May 2011, Forrest was selected in Craig Levein's [[Scotland national football team|Scotland senior team]] to face [[Wales national football team|Wales]] and the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] in the [[Nations Cup (football)|Nations Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 May 2011 |title=Scots call for Russell Martin and James Forrest |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/scotland/13423913 |access-date=23 September 2011 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He made his full international debut on 29 May 2011 in the match against the Republic of Ireland.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 May 2011 |title=Celtic's James Forrest aims for more Scotland caps |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/scotland/13593367 |access-date=31 May 2011 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Forrest then came on as a substitute in Scotland's 2–1 win over [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]] on 10 August.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 August 2011 |title=Scotland 2–1 Denmark |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/scotland/14438700 |access-date=24 September 2011 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 22 December 2011, it was revealed that Forrest had been invited to the [[Great Britain men's Olympic football team|Great Britain team]] for the [[2012 Summer Olympics]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 December 2011 |title=Celtic trio receive Team GB Olympic invites |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16306435 |access-date=22 December 2011 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> but did not make the final cut for the Games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 June 2012 |title=London 2012: No Scotland or N Ireland in Olympic football squad |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/olympics/18653453 |access-date=5 August 2012 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=23 May 2012 |title=Scotland winger James Forrest ruled out of Team GB |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/scottish/scotland-winger-james-forrest-ruled-out-of-team-gb-7778777.html |access-date=5 August 2012 |website=The Independent}}</ref>

On 17 November 2018, Forrest scored his first two goals for Scotland in their 4–0 away victory over [[Albania national football team|Albania]] in the [[2018–19 UEFA Nations League|UEFA Nations League]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Matthew Lindsay |date=17 November 2018 |title=Albania 0 Scotland 4: James Forrest at the double as Alex McLeish's injury-ravaged side coast to emphatic win |url=https://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/celtic/news/17231243.albania-0-scotland-4-james-forrest-at-the-double-as-alex-mcleishs-injury-ravaged-side-coast-to-emphatic-win/ |access-date=21 November 2018 |website=Evening Times}}</ref> Three days later, he netted a treble as Scotland beat [[Israel national football team|Israel]] 3–2<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 November 2018 |title=Scotland 3-2 Israel: James Forrest treble wins Nations League group for Alex McLeish's side |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46189774 |access-date=20 November 2018 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> to qualify for the [[UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying play-offs]]. He became the first Celtic player to score a hat-trick for Scotland since [[Jimmy Quinn (footballer, born 1878)|Jimmy Quinn]] did so in 1908, and the first Scotland player to score at least two goals in consecutive matches since [[Denis Law]] in 1963.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tom English |date=21 November 2018 |title=Alex McLeish's Scotland: Fine lines and signs of progress after Nations League |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46290290 |access-date=21 November 2018 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He was awarded as the 2018–19 ''International Player of the Year'' by the [[Scottish Football Writers' Association|SFWA]].<ref name="sfwaint">{{Cite web |date=15 May 2019 |title=Forrest top of the Scots |url=https://www.scottishfwa.com/news/2019/5/14/forrest-top-of-the-scots |access-date=25 May 2019 |publisher=[[Scottish Football Writers' Association]]}}</ref>

Forrest was part of the Scotland squad at [[UEFA Euro 2020]]. He made his only appearance in the tournament as a substitute in Scotland's opening game 2–0 defeat to the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] at Hampden Park on 14 June 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mullen |first=Scott |title=Euro 2020: Scotland 0-2 Czech Republic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51197776 |access-date=14 June 2021 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

He did not feature for Scotland over the next few years, but a run of form for Celtic in 2024 led to a recall for the [[UEFA Euro 2024]] squad.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/12017/13149130/scotlands-final-euro-2024-squad-craig-gordon-john-souttar-out-as-lewis-morgan-tommy-conway-included|title=Scotland's final Euro 2024 squad: Craig Gordon, John Souttar out as Lewis Morgan, Tommy Conway included|last=Jaidka|first=Sahil|date=10 June 2024|website=Sky Sports|accessdate=28 April 2025}}</ref> However, he did not play a moment of any of the three group stage games, as Scotland finished bottom of the group and were subsequently eliminated.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.67hailhail.com/news/celtic-player-admits-he-was-gutted-and-frustrated-after-what-happened-to-him-at-euro-2024/|title=Candid James Forrest has his say on Steve Clarke's use of Celtic star at Euro 2024|first=Patrick|last=Sinat|date=23 July 2024|website=67 Hail Hail|accessdate=28 April 2025}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Although Forrest's favoured position is on the [[Winger (football)|right wing]], he can also play on the left or as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]].<ref name="GreggWylde">{{Cite web |date=4 November 2011 |title=Gregg Wylde ready to switch sides to cover for Stevie Naismith |last=Macfarlane |first=Iain |url=http://www.express.co.uk/posts/view/281619 |access-date=24 November 2011 |website=Daily Express |publisher=Northern and Shell Media Publications}}</ref><ref name="RedknappIrksLennon">{{Cite web |date=2 November 2011 |title=Lennon irked by Redknapp comments on James Forrest |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15559922 |access-date=24 November 2011 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Forrest is noted for his pace and ball control, with an emphasis on dribbling. His former manager, Neil Lennon, observed that during his first few seasons at Celtic, Forrest developed the distance of his runs from 15–20 yards to 30–40 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dineen |first=Sean |date=30 January 2012 |title=Spurs Target; James Forrest of Celtic – Who is he? |url=https://footballblog.co.uk/spurs-target-james-forrest-celtic/ |url-status=live |access-date=8 June 2026 |website=FootballBlog}}</ref> He is considered a capable finisher and, although predominantly right-footed, is able to use his left foot when required. He has been described by commentators as a high-energy player with strong fitness levels, noted for his work rate and willingness to press throughout a match.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 October 2011 |title=Scotland's King James in waiting |work=The Scotsman |url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/top-football-stories/scotland-s-king-james-in-waiting-1-1892724 |access-date=5 August 2012 |publisher=Johnston Publishing}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=15 November 2011 |title=Win gives Wotte hope for the more immediate future |url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/more-scottish-football/win-gives-wotte-hope-for-the-more-immediate-future-1.1134864 |access-date=24 November 2011 |website=Herald Scotland |publisher=Herald & Times Group}}</ref><ref name="BertieAuld"/> Former [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] winger and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] teammate [[Gregg Wylde]] described him as a player who takes on responsibility during matches.<ref name="GreggWylde"/>

Former Celtic player [[Bertie Auld]] compared him to [[Jimmy Johnstone]], and described him as being the kind of player who "puts bums on seats" and then has the technical ability to "lift bums off the seats once the game starts".<ref name="BertieAuld">{{Cite web |date=24 August 2011 |title=Celtic star James Forrest reminds me of a young Jinky Johnstone, says Lisbon Lion Bertie Auld |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/celtic/2010/08/24/celtic-star-james-forrest-reminds-me-of-a-young-jinky-johnstone-says-lisbon-lion-bertie-auld-86908-22509899/ |access-date=24 November 2011 |website=Daily Record |publisher=Media Scotland}}</ref>
