'''Samuel Luke Johnstone''' (born 25 March 1993) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], on loan from [[EFL Championship]] club [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]].

A product of the [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] academy, Johnstone spent time on [[Loan (association football)|loan]] with [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]], [[Scunthorpe United F.C.|Scunthorpe United]], [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]], [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]], [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]], [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] and [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], before his transfer to [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] in 2018. He was an England youth international, winning caps at [[England national under-16 football team|under-16]], [[England national under-17 football team|under-17]], [[England national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[England national under-20 football team|under-20]] levels.

==Early life==
Samuel Luke Johnstone<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4110099 |title=2024/25 Premier League squad lists |publisher=Premier League |date=13 September 2024 |access-date=13 September 2024}}</ref> was born on 25 March 1993<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sam Johnstone - Wolverhampton Wanderers Goalkeeper - ESPN (UK) |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/player/_/id/162338/sam-johnstone |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> in [[Preston, Lancashire|Preston]], Lancashire.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe259493/sam-johnstone/ |title=Sam Johnstone: Profile |website=worldfootball.net |publisher=HEIM:SPIEL |access-date=6 June 2021}}</ref> His father is [[Glenn Johnstone]], a former professional footballer.<ref>{{cite web |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Johnstone signs for Preston on loan |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2015/Jan/sam-johnstone-joining-preston-north-end-on-loan.aspx |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=12 January 2015 |access-date=12 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Preston North End : 1946/47 – 2013/14 |url=http://www.neilbrown.newcastlefans.com/preston/preston.html |website=Post War English & Scottish Football League A – Z Player's Transfer Database |access-date=12 January 2015}}</ref> Johnstone's younger brother, Max, joined [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] as a youth-team player in September 2016.<ref>{{cite web |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Two keepers added to academy squad |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2016/Jun/manchester-united-confirms-new-academy-players-for-2016-17-intake-including-angel-gomes.aspx |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=2 September 2016 |access-date=2 September 2016}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Manchester United===
====Early career====
Johnstone joined Manchester United at academy level from [[Chorley]]-based club [[Euxton Villa F.C.|Euxton Villa]], after being spotted by club scout Colin Fairhurst.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Law |first=Matt |last2=Ducker |first2=James |last3=McGrath |first3=Mike |last4=Wallace |first4=Sam |last5=Percy |first5=John |last6=Dean |first6=Sam |last7=Edwards |first7=Luke |last8=Wilson |first8=Jeremy |last9=Bascombe |first9=Chris |date=2021-07-09 |title='I'm crying writing this': Final good luck messages for England's stars - by those who know them best |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/euro-2021/2021/07/09/crying-writing-final-good-luck-messages-englands-stars-know/ |access-date=2026-04-01 |work=The Telegraph |language=en-GB |issn=0307-1235}}</ref> In the [[2010–11 Manchester United F.C. season|2010–11 season]], he was first-choice goalkeeper in the academy, after sharing the duties the previous season.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

On 26 July 2011, Johnstone joined [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]] on [[Loan (association football)|loan]], as both of their first-choice [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeepers]] were sidelined by injury.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.oldhamathletic.co.uk/page/NewsUpdate/0,,10337~2401792,00.html |title=Sam's the man for Latics |publisher=Oldham Athletic A.F.C. |date=26 July 2011 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120805075451/http://www.oldhamathletic.co.uk/page/NewsUpdate/0,,10337~2401792,00.html |archive-date=5 August 2012}}</ref> On 9 September, Johnstone joined League One club [[Scunthorpe United F.C.|Scunthorpe United]] on a one-month loan after their first-choice goalkeeper [[Josh Lillis]] suffered a long-term injury.<ref>{{cite news |title=Iron sign Man Utd keeper |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,12875_7165123,00.html |website=Sky Sports |date=9 September 2011 |access-date=9 September 2011}}</ref> The following day, he made his debut in a 1–1 home draw against [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14773031 |title=Scunthorpe 1–1 Sheffield Utd |date=10 September 2011 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=10 September 2011}}</ref> On 19 October, Johnstone dislocated his finger during a training session, forcing Scunthorpe to search for an emergency goalkeeper once again.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15374332 |title=Scunthorpe United suffer injury blow to Sam Johnstone |date=19 October 2011 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=19 October 2011}}</ref> On 10 November, Scunthorpe extended the loan until 9 December,<ref>{{cite web |title=Johnstone deal extended |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2011/Nov/johnstone-completes-scunthorpe-return.aspx |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=10 November 2011 |access-date=10 November 2011}}</ref> which was then extended to 10 January 2012.<ref>{{cite web |title=Loan watch: Sam deal |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2011/Dec/loan-watch-johnstone-continues-at-scunthorpe.aspx?pageNo=1 |first=Adam |last=Marshall |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=12 December 2011 |access-date=12 December 2011}}</ref>

On 20 March 2013, Manchester United agreed for Johnstone to spend the rest of the [[2012–13 Walsall F.C. season|2012–13 season]] on loan to League One club [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Johnstone loaned to Walsall |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2013/Mar/sam-johnstone-joins-walsall-on-loan.aspx |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=20 March 2013 |access-date=20 March 2013}}</ref> He kept consecutive clean sheets in his first few matches and was first-choice goalkeeper during his loan. On 17 August, Johnstone was loaned to Championship club [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]] for a period of three months.<ref>{{cite web |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Johnstone joins Yeovil on loan |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2013/Aug/sam-johnstone-joins-yeovil-town-on-loan.aspx |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=17 August 2013 |access-date=17 August 2013}}</ref> Johnstone made his debut on the same day in a 2–0 loss to [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23644641 |title=Burnley 2–0 Yeovil |date=17 August 2013 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=17 August 2013}}</ref> but it was later confirmed that he had suffered a finger injury prior to his debut and returned to Manchester United for treatment.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.westerngazette.co.uk/Yeovil-Town-resume-hunt-keeper-Manchester-United/story-19682986-detail/story.html |title=Yeovil Town resume hunt for keeper after Manchester United youngster's injury |newspaper=Western Gazette |location=Yeovil |date=20 August 2013 |access-date=20 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130917015050/http://www.westerngazette.co.uk/Yeovil-Town-resume-hunt-keeper-Manchester-United/story-19682986-detail/story.html |archive-date=17 September 2013}}</ref>

====2014–2017====
On 31 January 2014, Johnstone was loaned to Championship club [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]] for four weeks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sam Johnstone for Rovers |url=http://www.doncasterroversfc.co.uk/news/article/rovers-johnstone-1332268.aspx |publisher=Doncaster Rovers F.C. |date=31 January 2014 |access-date=1 February 2014}}</ref> With the first-choice goalkeeper [[Ross Turnbull]] injured, Johnstone made his debut the following day at the [[Keepmoat Stadium]] against [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Doncaster Rovers v Middlesbrough |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25891684 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=1 February 2014}}</ref> On 4 April, Johnstone agreed a loan extension until the end of the [[2013–14 Doncaster Rovers F.C. season|2013–14 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Johnstone Loan Extension 'agreed' |url=http://www.doncasterroversfc.co.uk/news/article/johnstone-loan-extension-agreed-1467744.aspx |publisher=Doncaster Rovers F.C. |date=4 April 2014 |access-date=4 June 2014}}</ref> On 27 October, Johnstone again joined Doncaster Rovers, with the club now in League One, on loan, initially until January 2015.<ref>{{cite web |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Johnstone joins Doncaster on loan |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2014/Oct/sam-johnstone-signs-for-doncaster-rovers-on-loan.aspx |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=27 October 2014 |access-date=27 October 2014}}</ref>

On 12 January 2015, Johnstone joined his hometown club, [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] of League One, on loan until the end of the [[2014–15 Preston North End F.C. season|2014–15 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester United: Preston sign keeper Sam Johnstone on loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30781312 |website=BBC Sport |date=12 January 2015 |access-date=12 January 2015}}</ref> On 25 May, Johnstone kept a clean sheet in the [[2015 Football League One play-off final|2015 League One play-off final]] as Preston won promotion to the [[EFL Championship|Championship]] with a 4–0 win over [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]] at [[Wembley Stadium]].<ref name="2015PlayoffFinal"/> On Manchester United's pre-season tour of the United States in July 2015, Johnstone played as second-choice goalkeeper ahead of [[Anders Lindegaard]], covering for [[David de Gea]] while the Spaniard recovered from a knock. He started in the victories over [[Club América]] and [[San Jose Earthquakes]] (playing the entire game) and came on as a second-half substitute against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in a 3–1 victory.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

After rumours of De Gea's potential transfer [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] caused the Spaniard to be dropped from the Manchester United squad, Johnstone was named on the bench behind [[Sergio Romero]] for the first game of the season against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33744640 |title=Man Utd 1–0 Tottenham |first=Alistair |last=Magowan |website=BBC Sport |date=8 August 2015 |access-date=9 August 2015}}</ref> After De Gea returned to the United first-team, following the collapse of his move, Johnstone failed to make the bench again in 2015.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

On 31 December 2015, he re-signed for Preston on an initial 28-day loan, after Sunderland recalled [[Jordan Pickford]] on the same day.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2015-12-31 |title=Sam Johnstone: Man Utd keeper returns to Preston on loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35205668 |access-date=2026-04-01 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He made his first appearance of his second stint at Preston in a 2–1 home win over [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] on 2 January 2016.<ref name="sb1516"/> On 16 October 2016, Johnstone extended his contract at Manchester United until June 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2016/Oct/Goalkeeper-Sam-Johnstone-signs-new-Manchester-United-deal.aspx |title=JOHNSTONE PENS NEW UNITED DEAL |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=16 October 2016 |access-date=4 November 2017}}</ref>

====Loans to Aston Villa====
[[File:Sam Johnstone 2018 play-off (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Johnstone playing for [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in 2018]]

On 5 January 2017, Johnstone joined Championship club [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on loan until the end of the [[2016–17 Aston Villa F.C. season|2016–17 season]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38519185 |title=Sam Johnstone: Manchester United keeper joins Aston Villa on a half-season loan |website=BBC Sport |date=5 January 2017 |access-date=5 January 2017}}</ref> He made his debut on 8 January 2017, in an [[FA Cup]] match against Tottenham Hotspur at [[White Hart Lane]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/tottenham-vs-a-villa/report/368160 |title=Tottenham Hotspur 2–0 Aston Villa |date=8 January 2017 |access-date=8 January 2017 |website=Sky Sports}}</ref> During the period of this loan spell, he kept more clean sheets in the Championship than any other goalkeeper.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Evans |first=Gregg |date=2017-05-18 |title=Villa's prospects of taking Sam Johnstone back on loan given a boost |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/aston-villas-prospects-taking-sam-13058031 |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=Birmingham Live |language=en}}</ref> In July 2017, he returned to Aston Villa on a loan deal until the end of the [[2017–18 Aston Villa F.C. season|2017–18 season]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35231552 |title=Sam Johnstone: Manchester United goalkeeper re-signs for Aston Villa on loan |website=BBC Sport |date=14 July 2017 |access-date=14 July 2017}}</ref>

===West Bromwich Albion===

On 3 July 2018, Johnstone signed a four-year contract with newly relegated Championship club [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]], for a transfer fee reported by ''[[BBC Sport]]'' to be an initial £6.5 million.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2018-07-03 |title=Sam Johnstone: Man Utd goalkeeper joins West Bromwich Albion for £6.5m |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44698532 |access-date=2026-04-01 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Fifield |first=Dominic |date=2022-07-01 |title=trực tiếp bóng đá hôm nay |url=https://vua.live/ |access-date=2026-04-01 |work=vua.live |language=en-US |archive-date=12 April 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260412195842/https://vua.live/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was part of the West Brom team that lost to Aston Villa in the EFL Championship play-off semi-finals on penalties in May 2019. However, the following season, Sam Johnstone helped the club gain automatic promotion to the Premier League for the 2020–21 season. Despite some criticism from fans, Johnstone kept his place as West Brom's first-choice goalkeeper and went on to have a great season despite the club being relegated that year. Sam Johnstone produced a number of 'world class' saves throughout the season, securing vital points for the club on numerous occasions. 

On 15 December 2020, Johnstone produced two stoppage-time saves to deny [[İlkay Gündoğan]] and [[Raheem Sterling]] to secure a 1–1 draw for the club away at the home of future Premier League Champions, [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Flood |first=George |date=2020-12-15 |title=Man City 1-1 West Brom: Johnstone preserves shock point for Baggies |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/manchester-city-vs-west-brom-result-premier-league-2020-sam-johnstone-b327575.html |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=The Standard |language=en}}</ref> Johnstone also played well against former club Manchester United and reigning champions Liverpool, securing 1–1 draws against both.<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Donnell |first=Dale |date=2021-02-14 |title=Watch: Sam Johnstone makes incredible fingertip save v Man Utd to recuse point for Baggies |url=https://strettynews.com/2021/02/14/video-sam-johnstone-makes-incredible-fingertip-save-v-man-utd-to-recuse-point-for-baggies/ |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=Stretty News |language=en}}</ref> His fine form resulted in a trio of club awards at the end of the season, winning the Supporter's Player of the Year, Player's Player of the year and PFA Community Champion Award for his work off the field.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Johnstone claims trio of awards {{!}} West Bromwich Albion |url=https://www.wba.co.uk/news/johnstone-claims-trio-awards |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=www.wba.co.uk |language=en}}</ref> West Brom were relegated again after the 2020–21 season, and [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] approached them with a £10 million offer for Johnstone, which was rejected.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stone |first=Sam |date=2021-07-15 |title=Sam Johnstone: West Ham have £10m bid for West Brom and England goalkeeper rejected |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57791313 |access-date=2026-04-01 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> With the club stuck mid-table in the Championship, Johnstone didn't extend his contract.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fifield |first=Dominic |date=2022-07-01 |title=Sam Johnstone completes free transfer to Crystal Palace after West Brom release |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4175536/2022/06/10/sam-johnstone-completes-free-transfer-to-crystal-palace-after-west-brom-release/ |access-date=2026-04-01 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

===Crystal Palace===
On 21 June 2022, Johnstone agreed to join [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] on a free transfer as backup to [[Vicente Guaita]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61881162 |title=Sam Johnstone: Crystal Palace to sign West Bromwich Albion and England goalkeeper |website=BBC Sport |date=21 June 2022 |access-date=21 June 2022}}</ref> He made his debut in a 2–0 [[EFL Cup]] win against [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]] on 23 August.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62558193|title=Oxford United 0–2 Crystal Palace|website=BBC Sport|date=23 August 2022|access-date=11 April 2023}}</ref> He made his first Premier League appearance for Palace against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] on 9 April 2023, and was praised for his performance in the 5–1 win.<ref name=PalaceLeeds>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2023/04/09/leeds-vs-crystal-palace-premier-league-live-score-updates/|newspaper=The Daily Telegraph|last=Aizlewood|first=John|title=Crystal Palace revival continues as Hodgson's men run riot at Elland Road|date=9 April 2023|access-date=11 April 2023}}</ref> Coincidentally, the last time Palace had scored five goals in a game had been against Johnstone's West Brom in December 2020.<ref name=PalaceLeeds/>

===Wolverhampton Wanderers===
On 30 August 2024, [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] signed Johnstone on a four-year deal for a reported fee of £10 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wolves.co.uk/news/mens-first-team/20240830-johnstone-becomes-latest-recruit/ |title=Johnstone becomes latest recruit |publisher=Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C. |date=30 August 2024 |access-date=30 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cp9rjm1pd4jo |title=Wolves complete £10m Johnstone signing |website=BBC Sport |date=30 August 2024 |access-date=30 August 2024}}</ref>



==International career==
[[File:Connor Ripley and Sam Johnstone (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Johnstone playing for [[England national under-19 football team|England U19]] in 2012]]

Johnstone was a part of the victorious [[England national under-17 football team|England under-17 squad]] at the [[2010 UEFA European Under-17 Championship]].<ref>{{cite web |title=England U-17s beat Spain to win European Championship |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/8713980.stm |date=31 May 2010|access-date=23 February 2018 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He made his debut for the [[England national under-19 football team|England under-19 team]] against [[Slovakia national under-19 football team|Slovakia]] in September 2010.<ref>{{cite web |title=Samuel Johnstone |url=http://www.thefa.com/England/All-Teams/Players/J/Samuel-Johnstone |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=10 September 2011}}</ref> 

On 28 May 2013, he was named in the 21-man squad for [[England national under-20 football team|England under-20s]] at the [[2013 FIFA U-20 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Final squad named |url=https://www.thefa.com/england/mens-u20s/News/2013/u20s-world-cup-squad-announcement-280513 |publisher=The Football Association |date=28 May 2013 |access-date=17 June 2013}}</ref> He made his debut on 23 June in England's first match of the tournament, a 2–2 draw with [[Iraq national under-20 football team|Iraq]].<ref name="EnglandU20Caps">{{cite web |url=http://www.englandfootballonline.com/MatchRsl/MatchRslTmU20.html |title=Match Results Under 20: 1989–2019 |website=England Football Online |date=5 June 2021 |access-date=6 June 2021}}</ref> He played in England's three matches at the tournament as they were eliminated at the group stage.<ref name="EnglandU20Caps" />

On 18 March 2021, Johnstone received his first call-up to the England senior team when he was named in the 26-man squad for their [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualifiers]] against [[San Marino national football team|San Marino]], [[Albania national football team|Albania]] and [[Poland national football team|Poland]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2021/mar/18/england-mens-senior-squad-named-for-march-internationals-20210318 |title=Two new faces in the Three Lions squad as Ollie Watkins and Sam Johnstone called up |access-date=26 May 2021 |date=18 March 2021 |publisher=The Football Association }}</ref> He was named in the 26-man squad for [[UEFA Euro 2020]], along with fellow goalkeepers Jordan Pickford and [[Dean Henderson]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57321188 |title=Euro 2020: Trent Alexander-Arnold named in England's 26-man squad |website=BBC Sport |date=1 June 2021 |access-date=6 June 2021}}</ref> and made his debut on 6 June in England's final pre-tournament [[Friendly (association football)|friendly]], a 1–0 win over [[Romania national football team|Romania]] at the [[Riverside Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57297066 |title=England 1–0 Romania |first=Phil |last=McNulty |website=BBC Sport |date=6 June 2021 |access-date=6 June 2021}}</ref>

Johnstone was not included in England's squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] but was recalled for the team's [[UEFA Euro 2024]] [[UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying|qualifiers]] against [[Malta national football team|Malta]] and [[North Macedonia national football team|North Macedonia]] in June 2023.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.englandfootball.com/articles/2023/May/24/england-mens-senior-squad-named-for-malta-north-macedonia-EURO-qualifiers-20232405|title=England men's squad named for June's EURO qualifiers|date=24 May 2023|access-date=17 October 2023|publisher=The Football Association}}</ref> On 13 October 2023, he made his first international appearance in two years, keeping his fourth clean sheet in four [[Cap (association football)|caps]] as England beat [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]] 1–0 at [[Wembley Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cpfc.co.uk/news/club/crystal-palace-internationals-roundup-october-2023/|title=October Internationals: Andersen assists and Johnstone impresses|date=15 October 2023|publisher=Crystal Palace Football Club}}</ref>

'''John Francis Souttar''' (born 25 September 1996) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]]. He previously played for [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] and [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] before joining Rangers in 2022.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Rangers Sign John Souttar on Pre-Contract Agreement|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/rangers-sign-john-souttar-on-pre-contract-agreement/2zAMNHHbj4shK7t0EFceze|access-date=2022-01-14|publisher=Rangers F.C.|language=en-gb|website=www.rangers.co.uk}}</ref>

Known as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|central defender]], Souttar was converted to play as a [[midfielder]] towards the end of his stay at Dundee United, however he reverted to once again playing as a centre-back for Hearts.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Winners and Losers: Kieran Tierney {{!}} John Souttar {{!}} Hearts fans |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/competitions/premiership/winners-and-losers-kieran-tierney-john-souttar-hearts-fans-1-4053887 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180831072031/https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/competitions/premiership/winners-and-losers-kieran-tierney-john-souttar-hearts-fans-1-4053887 |archive-date=2018-08-31 |access-date=2026-05-20 |language=en}}</ref> He is the youngest player to have appeared for Dundee United's first team, having made his debut for the club in January 2013 at the age of 16. After previously representing the country at [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]], [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] levels, he made his full international debut in September 2018.

==Early life==
Souttar was born on 25 September 1996 in [[Aberdeen]]<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.uefa.com/under17/teams/players/250056853--john-souttar/ | title=John Souttar | publisher=[[UEFA]] | access-date=2 January 2013}}</ref> to parents Jack and Heather. His father had previously been a professional footballer, with [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=John Souttar: From Howe o' the Mearns to Heart of Midlothian |url=https://www.mearnsleader.co.uk/sport/football/john-souttar-howe-o-mearns-heart-midlothian-2108356 |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=The Scotsman |language=en}}</ref> His mother was born in Australia.<ref name=AUS/> Growing up in the village of [[Luthermuir]], Aberdeenshire, Souttar attended Luthermuir Primary and then [[Mearns Academy]] in nearby [[Laurencekirk]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mearnsleader.co.uk/sport/john-capped-for-scotland-u17s-1-2513224|title=John capped for Scotland U17s |publisher=Mearns Leader|work=mearnsleader.co.uk|date=8 September 2012|access-date=2 January 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Mearns youngsters extend contracts for Dundee United|url=http://www.mearnsleader.co.uk/sport/local-sport/mearns-youngsters-extend-contracts-for-dundee-united-1-2781269|access-date=9 September 2015|work=Mearns Leader|date=8 February 2013|location=Stonehaven}}</ref>

In 2002, Souttar began to play for Brechin City Boys Club (later Brechin City Youths), where he was coached by his father in a successful team also containing [[Ryan Gauld]] and [[Euan Spark]]. The trio also developed their skills at coaching schools run in Dundee by [[Ian Cathro]], before joining [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]'s youth system in 2006 at the age of nine.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.brechincityyouths.co.uk/club/History|title=Former Players with Senior Clubs|publisher=Brechin Boys Club|work=brechincityyouths.co.uk|date=1 October 2011|access-date=2 January 2013|archive-date=3 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170103000005/http://www.brechincityyouths.co.uk/club/History|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Souttar has a younger brother,<ref>{{cite news|last1=Kennedy|first1=Liam|title=Dundee United youth coach: John Souttar's had a tough summer but I know his time will come|url=http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/2014/08/22/dundee-united-youth-coach-john-souttars-had-a-tough-summer-but-i-know-his-time-will-come/|access-date=16 September 2015|work=Eventing Telegraph|date=22 August 2014|location=Dundee}}</ref> [[Harry Souttar|Harry]], who plays for [[Leicester City]] and is an [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australian]] international.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Stoke City sign teenage defender Harry Souttar from Dundee United |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11701/10598328/stoke-city-sign-teenage-defender-harry-souttar-from-dundee-united |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241210160633/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11701/10598328/stoke-city-sign-teenage-defender-harry-souttar-from-dundee-united |archive-date=2024-12-10 |access-date=2026-05-20 |work=Sky Sports |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/conversation-which-sparked-souttars-australia-call |title=The conversation that sparked Souttar's Australia call-up |first=Jacob |last=Windon |date=1 June 2019 |accessdate=28 September 2021 |website=socceroos.com.au |publisher=Football Australia}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-01-31 |title=Australia’s Harry Souttar makes Premier League move to Leicester City |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/feb/01/australias-harry-souttar-makes-premier-league-move-to-leicester-city |access-date=2026-05-20 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Dundee United===

After progressing through the various youth team levels at Dundee United, Souttar signed a professional contract in July 2012 and became a member of the club's under-20 development squad.<ref name=DUFC>{{cite web|title=First Team — John Souttar|url=http://dufc.co/the-teams/first-team/6087/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140911154408/http://dufc.co/the-teams/first-team/6087/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=11 September 2014|publisher=Dundee United F.C.|access-date=9 September 2015}}</ref> After just four months in the development team, injuries and suspensions led to Souttar making his first team debut on 2 January 2013, playing in [[central defender|central defence]] from the start in a 2–2 draw with [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] at [[Pittodrie Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aberdeen v Dundee Utd - 2nd Jan 2013 {{!}} Report {{!}} Scots Prem {{!}} Sky Sports Football |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/262067/report |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140101103805/http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/262067/report |archive-date=2014-01-01 |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=www1.skysports.com |language=en}}</ref> Aged 16 years and 99 days, he became the youngest ever player to play for Dundee United.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20843051 | title=Aberdeen 2–2 Dundee United |publisher=BBC Sport | date=2 January 2013 | access-date=2 January 2013}}</ref> 

On 24 January 2013, Souttar signed a contract extension keeping him at the club until January 2016.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21190697 | title=Ryan Gauld and John Souttar extend contracts |publisher=BBC Sport | date=24 January 2013 | access-date=24 January 2013}}</ref> Still aged 16, Souttar returned to the first team in April 2013 following an injury to [[Brian McLean]] and started regularly for the remainder of the season, playing against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in a 4–3 [[Scottish Cup]] semi-final defeat on 14 April 2013 at [[Hampden Park]].<ref name="DUFC" />

Souttar's form began to attract the attention of other clubs, with English [[Premier League]] team [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] having a bid of £600,000 accepted by Dundee United in October 2013.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dundee United defender John Souttar knocks back move to Sunderland after Terrors agree £600k bid|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/dundee-united-defender-john-souttar-2659566|access-date=10 September 2015|work=Daily Record|date=31 October 2013|location=Glasgow}}</ref> After speaking to Sunderland officials, Souttar decided to turn down the transfer. On 4 November 2013, Souttar signed another extension to his contract, keeping him at Dundee United until May 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee Utd: Ryan Gauld and John Souttar extend their contracts|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24812193|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 November 2013|access-date=7 November 2013}}</ref> Souttar continued to play regularly in central defence throughout the 2013–14 season and scored his first goal for the club in a [[Scottish Premiership]] match against Aberdeen on 1 January 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee Utd 1–2 Aberdeen|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25513221|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 January 2014|access-date=2 January 2014}}</ref>

Souttar missed the first three months of the 2014–15 season due to an ankle injury sustained in pre-season.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Swan|first1=Craig|title=Dundee United's John Souttar: How could I moan about my op when mate Jordan was battling cancer?|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-uniteds-john-souttar-how-4726012|access-date=14 September 2015|work=Daily Record|date=1 December 2014}}</ref> After his return to the first team, Dundee United successfully experimented with Souttar in a defensive midfield role in matches against Celtic and Aberdeen during April 2015, a position in which he has subsequently featured regularly.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Roache|first1=Ian|title=Dundee United's John Souttar right at home in midfield|url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-united/dundee-united-s-john-souttar-right-at-home-in-midfield-1.869857|access-date=14 September 2015|work=The Courier|date=29 April 2015|location=Dundee}}</ref> In October 2015, new United head coach [[Mixu Paatelainen]] played Souttar at [[right back]] in his first two matches in charge.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Nicolson|first1=Eric|title=Dundee United's John Souttar can be a 'top, top' right-back, says Mixu|url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/st-johnstone/dundee-united-s-john-souttar-can-be-a-top-top-right-back-says-mixu-1.907369|access-date=29 October 2015|work=The Courier|date=29 October 2015|location=Dundee|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151102023724/http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/st-johnstone/dundee-united-s-john-souttar-can-be-a-top-top-right-back-says-mixu-1.907369|archive-date=2 November 2015}}</ref> In all he made seventy three appearances in all competitions, scoring twice.<ref name = "Soc"/>

===Heart of Midlothian===
On 1 February 2016, Souttar signed for fellow Scottish Premiership club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], agreeing a three-and-a-half-year contract for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web|title=Souttar Signs|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/4935|publisher=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|date=1 February 2016|access-date=1 February 2016}}</ref> Speaking about his move Souttar said that he was "looking forward to getting stuck in and getting my career back on track".<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35466803 | title=Hearts complete deal for Dundee United defender | publisher=BBC Sport | date=2 February 2016 | access-date=2 February 2016}}</ref>

Souttar played regularly for Hearts during the 2016–17 season until he suffered a ruptured [[achilles tendon]] during a match against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in January 2017 which ended his season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38814559 |title=John Souttar: Hearts defender ruled out for rest of season |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 February 2017 |access-date=3 February 2017}}</ref> He made a full recovery (though then missed three months in late 2018 with a hip injury which was aggravated on international duty),<ref name="McLeish">{{cite news|url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/17007048.alex-mcleish-hearts-scotland-centre-half-john-souttar-will-stronger-fitter-makes-comeback/|title=Alex McLeish: Hearts and Scotland centre half John Souttar will be stronger and fitter when he makes his comeback|last=Lindsay|first=Matthew|date=25 October 2018|work=The National|access-date=2026-05-20}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Pilcher |first=Ross |date=26 October 2018 |title=Hearts defender shares post-operation update |url=https://www.edinburghlive.co.uk/news/hearts-john-souttar-gives-injury-15331874 |website=Edinburgh Live |language=en|access-date=2026-05-20}}</ref> and took part in the run to the [[2019 Scottish Cup Final]] which Hearts lost to the same opponents.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=539373|title=Celtic clinch 'Triple Treble' with Scottish Cup win|date=25 May 2019|publisher=ESPN|access-date=9 August 2020}}</ref>

After missing much of the [[2019–20 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2019–20 season]] with an ankle injury requiring an operation, Souttar returned to the team only to tear the achilles in his other leg during a Scottish Cup tie with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in February 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51693447 |title=Scotland: Scott McKenna and John Souttar injuries blow to play-off hopes |publisher=BBC Sport |date=29 February 2020 |access-date=1 March 2020}}</ref> Initially fearing his career was over, the recovery took six months.<ref name=hell>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/john-souttar-opens-up-hearts-22490589 |title=John Souttar opens up on Hearts injury hell as he admits he feared career was over |last=McDermott |first=Scott |date=9 August 2020 |work=Sunday Mail |access-date=9 August 2020 }}</ref> Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]], the 2019–20 Scottish league season was curtailed and Hearts were consequently relegated.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53526063 |title=Hearts & Partick Thistle relegations confirmed by arbitration panel |publisher=BBC Sport |date=28 July 2020 |access-date=9 August 2020}}</ref> Soon after returning to training, Souttar snapped the same achilles tendon that had been injured earlier in 2020.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53875788 |title=John Souttar: Hearts defender suffers 'relapse' of achilles injury |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 August 2020 |access-date=24 August 2020}}</ref>

=== Rangers ===
[[File:John Souttar 2023.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Souttar with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in 2023.]]

On 14 January 2022, [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] announced Souttar had signed a pre-contract agreement to bring him to the club at the end of the [[2021–22 Scottish Premiership|2021–22 season]] once his contract with Hearts runs out.<ref name=":0" /> The move was completed on 1 June 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/john-souttar-im-physically-and-mentally-ready-to-join-rangers |title=John Souttar: I'm physically and mentally ready to join Rangers |first=Lewis |last=McKenzie |website=STV Sport |date=1 June 2022 |accessdate=1 June 2022}}</ref> He made his debut for the club against [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], starting the match, in a 2–1 win on 30 July.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-07-30 |title=Livingston 1-2 Rangers: Visitors open with win after two goals in two minutes |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62275140 |access-date=2026-05-20 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>  

Souttar suffered injury problems during the 2022–23 season and did not play for Rangers again until early March.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/john-souttar-rangers-respect-felt-29380569 |title=John Souttar and the Rangers respect felt through the dressing room as team-mates have his back |newspaper=Daily Record |first=Andrew |last=Newport |date=6 March 2023 |accessdate=14 May 2023}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club on 13 May 2023, in a 3–0 [[Old Firm]] derby win against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fassihi |first=Mazzetti |date=2026-05-19 |title=nowgoal |url=https://nowgoal.tel |access-date=2026-05-20}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cx9nrldyq4eo |title=Souttar 'feeling good' and ready to become 'mainstay' |website=BBC Sport |date=14 May 2023 |accessdate=14 May 2023}}</ref>

==International career==
Souttar has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] level,<ref name="Scot">{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=1848&playerID=114832&squadID=13 | title=John Souttar Under–17 | publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]]  | access-date=2 January 2013}}</ref> making his debut on 28 August 2012, in a 0–0 draw against [[Belgium national under-17 football team|Belgium]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/international_fixture_details.cfm?page=1921&matchID=120262 | title=Scotland v Belgium | publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] | date=28 August 2012 | access-date=2 January 2013}}</ref> In May 2013, Souttar made his debut<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=2492&playerID=114832&squadID=9 | title=U19 Squad Matches | publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] | access-date=1 February 2016}}</ref> for the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland under-19]] team, against [[England national under-19 football team|England]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/international_fixture_details.cfm?page=1921&matchID=128381 | title=England compound Scotland Under-19s' Euro misery | publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] | date=29 May 2013 | access-date=1 February 2016}}</ref>

[[Alex McLeish]] called Souttar into the senior [[Scotland national football team|Scotland squad]] for the first time in May 2018,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44111727 |title=Scotland pick Johnny Russell plus seven uncapped players including Lewis Stevenson & Lewis Morgan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=14 May 2018 |access-date=14 May 2018}}</ref> but he was forced to withdraw due to hip and hamstring injuries.<ref>{{cite news |first=Barry |last=Anderson |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/surgery-fear-for-john-souttar-as-hearts-defender-forced-out-of-scotland-squad-1-4742570 |title=Surgery fear for John Souttar as Hearts defender forced out of Scotland squad |work=Edinburgh Evening News |date=21 May 2018 |access-date=21 May 2018}}</ref> In August 2018, Souttar's manager at [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]], [[Craig Levein]], suggested that Souttar may be called up for [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]] if not selected for Scotland.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://au.eurosport.com/football/scotland-risk-losing-john-souttar-to-australia-craig-levein_sto6897970/story.shtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181016125955/https://au.eurosport.com/football/scotland-risk-losing-john-souttar-to-australia-craig-levein_sto6897970/story.shtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 October 2018|title=Scotland risk losing John Souttar to Australia – Craig Levein|publisher=[[Eurosport]]|date=23 August 2018|access-date=16 October 2018}}</ref> Souttar later admitted he had not considered playing for Australia or been contacted by [[Football Federation Australia]], and that he was unaware Levein was going to make the suggestion.<ref name=AUS>{{cite news|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/hearts-star-john-souttar-admits-13199266|title=Hearts star John Souttar admits Craig Levein mischief over 'Australian granny' comment|work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |date=5 September 2018|access-date=16 October 2018|last=Jackson |first=Keith}}</ref>

Souttar was again selected for Scotland in September 2018, and he made his full international debut in a 4–0 defeat against [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] on 7 September.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/ruthless-belgium-display-a-learning-curve-for-hearts-john-souttar-1-4796976 |title='Ruthless' Belgium display a learning curve for Hearts' John Souttar |work=Edinburgh Evening News |date=7 September 2018 |access-date=11 September 2018 |first=Barry |last=Anderson}}</ref> A month later, in his third appearance, he was sent off for two bookings in a 2–1 loss away to [[Israel national football team|Israel]], later stating that he had been suffering with a hip injury (which caused him to miss three months of club football) but chose not to ask to be substituted as his defensive colleague [[Charlie Mulgrew]] had already come off injured.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-01-08 |title=Hearts' John Souttar: My desire to play through pain for Scotland led to red card |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts-john-souttar-my-desire-to-play-through-pain-for-scotland-led-to-red-card-179911 |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=Edinburgh News |language=en}}</ref>

In November 2021, Souttar was called up by [[Steve Clarke]] to the Scotland squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] qualifiers against [[Moldova national football team|Moldova]] and [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]]. On 15 November he scored his first international goal, a header from a corner, against Denmark in a 2–0 home win.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Scotland beat Danes to secure seeding|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59202146|access-date=2021-11-15}}</ref>

Souttar was named in the provisional squad for [[UEFA Euro 2024]], but was omitted from the final list.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cjmm73ny1ddo |title=Scotland to cut Craig Gordon & John Souttar from Euros squad |website=BBC Sport |date=7 June 2024 |accessdate=8 June 2024}}</ref> Called up for [[2024–25 UEFA Nations League]] fixtures against [[Poland national football team|Poland]], [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] and [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]], he was named player of the match against Portugal as Scotland earned a point from a 0–0 draw at Hampden, and was joined on the field by childhood companion Ryan Gauld, the first time they had played together since their Dundee United spell in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-16 |title='It’s amazing': Souttar loving Scotland reunion with childhood friend Gauld |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/its-amazing-john-souttar-loving-scotland-reunion-with-childhood-friend-ryan-gauld |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=STV News |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 19 May 2026, Souttar was selected in the 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/scotland-squad-announced-steve-clarke|title=Veteran Gordon and youngster Curtis named in Scotland squad|date=19 May 2026|access-date=13 June 2026|language=en}}</ref>

'''Callum William McGregor''' (born 14 June 1993) is a Scottish professional [[Football player|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for and [[Captain (association football)|captains]] [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].

A Celtic academy graduate, McGregor has spent his entire professional career at the club, except for a single season on loan at [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]] in [[2013–14 Notts County F.C. season|2013–14]]. He is the second-most decorated player in Celtic's history, winning eleven [[Scottish Premiership]]s, seven [[Scottish Cup]]s and eight [[Scottish League Cup]]s. He succeeded [[Scott Brown (footballer, born June 1985)|Scott Brown]] as captain from the [[2021–22 Celtic F.C. season|2021–22 season]]. He has won the Scottish domestic [[Treble (association football)|treble]] five times, once as captain.

Internationally, McGregor represented Scotland at every youth level before making his debut for the [[Scotland national football team|senior side]] in 2017, representing them at [[UEFA Euro 2020]] and [[UEFA Euro 2024|Euro 2024]]. He went on to earn 63 caps before retiring from international football in 2024.

==Club career==

=== Celtic ===
==== Early career ====
McGregor began his career with Scottish club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], coming through the club's [[youth system]] alongside [[Dylan McGeouch]],<ref name="celebration">{{cite news| url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/15165510.Double_celebrations_looms_for_Callum_McGregor/ | title=Double celebrations looms for Callum McGregor | last=McConnell | first=Alison | newspaper=[[Evening Times]] | date=16 March 2017 | accessdate=2 May 2017}}</ref> who was a teammate in youth [[Victory Shield]] internationals at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|Under-16]] level.<ref name="shield" >{{cite web|date=7 November 2008|title =Under 16 Sky Sports Victory Shield Scotland v Northern Ireland|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=1986&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=4078|website=www.scottishfa.co.uk|publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]]|accessdate=24 May 2017}}</ref> He scored a hat-trick for Celtic in the 8–0 [[2012 Scottish Youth Cup Final]] victory over [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] at [[Hampden Park]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Eightsome reel at Hampden as young Celts lift Youth Cup|url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/2522|publisher=Celtic FC|website=www.celticfc.net|last=Henderson|first=Mark|date=23 April 2012|accessdate=4 August 2014}}</ref> McGregor appeared in four successive [[Scottish Youth Cup]] finals between 2010 and 2013, with the club winning all of them.<ref name="who is">{{cite news | url=https://videocelts.com/2014/07/blogs/latest-news/who-is-callum-mcgregor/ | title=WHO IS CALLUM MCGREGOR? |website=videocelts.com | publisher=Video Celts | date=16 July 2014 |accessdate=27 May 2019|last=Joe|first=McHugh}}</ref>

McGregor has spoken of the influence that the late [[Tommy Burns (footballer)|Tommy Burns]] had on him as a young footballer, stating that Burns had always indicated his belief that McGregor would be the next successful product of Celtic's youth academy. McGregor particularly cites a conversation with Burns as a 13-year old as staying with him throughout his whole career, where he urged him to coincide his ability with the correct attitude and a desire to prove himself.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=celticfc|author=Celtic FC|number=965632244047020033|title=He loves Celtic too! Man of the moment, Callum McGregor, on @CelticTV's The Locker Room in January giving credit to Tommy Burns and Ronny Deila for helping him in his early days.|access-date=27 July 2021}}</ref>

==== 2013–14 season: Loan to Notts County ====
McGregor joined English [[Football League One|League One]] club [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]] on a five-month loan in August 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=Notts County sign Celtic midfielder on loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23608277|date=7 August 2013|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=18 August 2013}}</ref> Among his teammates that season was fellow loanee midfielder [[Jack Grealish]], a future [[England national football team|England international]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Murray |first=Ewan |date=2021-06-17 |title=Callum McGregor: ‘Notts County gave Jack Grealish and me a real education’ |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/jun/17/callum-mcgregor-notts-county-gave-jack-grealish-and-i-a-real-education |access-date=2026-07-26 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> He scored on his debut for the "Magpies" on 7 August, in a 3–2 win over [[Fleetwood Town F.C.|Fleetwood Town]] at [[Meadow Lane]] in the first round of the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Notts County 3 - 2 Fleetwood|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23513175|access-date=18 August 2013 |website=www.bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=BBC Sport |date=7 August 2013}}</ref> Following a man of the match appearance against [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]] where McGregor netted two goals, Notts County boss [[Chris Kiwomya]] challenged McGregor to reach 10 goals for the season in his loan spell.<ref>{{Cite web|title=McGregor Over Half Way|url=https://www.nottscountyfc.co.uk/news/2013/october/mcgregor-over-half-way-/|access-date=2021-07-27|website=www.nottscountyfc.co.uk |publisher=Notts County FC|language=en-gb}}</ref>

McGregor played the full match in a memorable League Cup encounter for the club, facing off against a [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] side which featured future Rangers manager [[Steven Gerrard]], [[Raheem Sterling]], and [[Daniel Sturridge]], as well as being managed by his future Celtic manager, [[Brendan Rodgers]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Match Report : 27/08/2013|url=https://www.nottscountyfc.co.uk/news/2013/august/match-report--27082013/|access-date=2021-07-27|website=www.nottscountyfc.co.uk |publisher= Notts County FC|language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Pearce|first=James|date=2013-08-28|title=James Pearce's match report on Liverpool FC's win over Notts County|url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/james-pearces-match-report-liverpool-5794325|access-date=2021-07-27|newspaper=Liverpool Echo|language=en}}</ref> County fought back from two goals down to bring the game to extra time, going on to lose the game 4-2.<ref name=":0" />

McGregor's loan expired at the start of January 2014, with his 12 goals in all competitions making him the current top scorer for Notts County at that stage.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Derry Overjoyed By Return Of The Mac|url=https://www.nottscountyfc.co.uk/news/2014/january/derry-overjoyed-by-return-of-the-mac/|access-date=2021-07-27|website=www.nottscountyfc.co.uk |publisher= Notts County FC |language=en-gb}}</ref> Kiwomya's successor, [[Shaun Derry]], described his departure as causing a sense of disappointment in the squad.<ref name=":1" /> Following the expiry of his loan in January, clubs such as [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] were credited with an interest in McGregor.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Grealish returns to Villa Park|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/grealish-returns-to-villa-park_sto4086677/story.shtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241210200851/https://www.eurosport.com/football/grealish-returns-to-villa-park_sto4086677/story.shtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 December 2024|access-date=2021-07-27|website=www.eurosport.com |date=13 January 2014 |publisher=Eurosport}}</ref> After missing three games while waiting for negotiations to conclude, it was confirmed on 24 January 2014 that McGregor's loan had been extended until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Callum McGregor Returns To Notts On Loan|url=https://www.nottscountyfc.co.uk/news/2014/january/callum-mcgregor-returns-to-notts-on-loan/|access-date=2021-07-27|publisher= Notts County FC |website=www.nottscountyfc.co.uk|language=en-gb}}</ref> McGregor was put straight to the Notts County squad for their game against [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]] and marked his return with a goal, a 25-yard free kick into the top left corner.<ref>{{Cite web|title=McGregor To Make Up For Lost Time|url=https://www.nottscountyfc.co.uk/news/2014/january/mcgregor-to-make-up-for-lost-time-/|access-date=2021-07-27|website=www.nottscountyfc.co.uk|language=en-gb |publisher= Notts County FC}}</ref>

McGregor ended the season with 14 goals in all competitions <ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Shaun Derry Pays Tribute To Notts County's Departing Loan Stars |publisher= Notts County FC |url=https://www.nottscountyfc.co.uk/news/2014/may/shaun-derry-pays-tribute-to-notts-countys-departing-loan-stars/|access-date=2021-07-27|website=www.nottscountyfc.co.uk|language=en-gb}}</ref> and as the club's top goalscorer. Shaun Derry has since praised McGregor's attitude,<ref name=":2" /> describing him as "brilliant to work with", and felt that the club would not have avoided relegation that season had it not been for the efforts of McGregor and Grealish.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Curtis|first=Leigh|date=2020-04-02|title='We'd have never stayed up without them' - Derry hails Grealish and McGregor|url=https://www.nottinghampost.com/sport/football/football-news/wed-never-stayed-up-without-4014154|access-date=2021-07-21|newspaper=Nottingham Post|language=en}}</ref> McGregor credits the loan spell for allowing him to develop as a player and learn the game, and felt that being involved in a relegation battle where his teammate's livelihoods were on the line caused him to "grow up a bit".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-04-21 |title=Celtic's Callum McGregor thanks Neil Lennon for loan spell |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/rugby-union/celtics-callum-mcgregor-thanks-neil-lennon-for-loan-spell-1430381 |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=The Scotsman |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2014–15 season: Celtic debut and first goal ====

McGregor made his first team debut for Celtic against [[Knattspyrnufélag Reykjavíkur|KR Reykjavík]] on 15 July 2014 in a [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] qualifier and he scored the only goal of the game.<ref>{{cite web |title=KR Reykjavík 0-1 Celtic|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28278531 |website=www.bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 July 2014|accessdate=16 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Goal hero Callum McGregor dreaming of going from public park to Celtic Park for Champions League nights|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/goal-hero-callum-mcgregor-dreaming-3867364|last=McDermott|first=Scott|newspaper=Daily Record|date=16 July 2014|accessdate=24 May 2017}}</ref> He also scored against [[Legia Warsaw]] and [[NK Maribor]] in subsequent qualifying rounds. He made his [[Scottish Premiership]] debut against [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on 13 August 2014 and scored a goal in a 3–0 victory for Celtic. On 29 August 2014, McGregor signed a new five-year contract with Celtic.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28983136|title=Celtic's Callum McGregor signs new five-year contract|date=29 August 2017|publisher=BBC Sport |website=www.bbc.co.uk/sport}}</ref>

==== 2015–16 season ====
{{Empty section|date=July 2023}}

==== 2016–17 season ====
McGregor made his 100th appearance for the club in a 2–1 win at [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on 19 March 2017.<ref name=celebration/><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/12311 | title=McGregor: We'll continue to be relentless in pursuit of success | publisher=Celtic FC |website=www.celticfc.net | date=29 March 2017 | accessdate=27 March 2017}}</ref> He scored in two successive [[Old firm|Old Firm]] victories against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in the space of a week in April 2017.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39612250 | title=Celtic 2:0 Rangers | publisher=BBC Sport  |website=www.bbc.co.uk/sport| date=23 April 2017 | accessdate=2 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39676372 | title=Rangers 1:5 Celtic | publisher=BBC Sport  |website=www.bbc.co.uk/sport| date=29 April 2017 | accessdate=2 May 2017}}</ref> In the [[2017 Scottish Cup Final]], he started in his usual midfield position but played the majority of the match at [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left back]] after an injury to [[Kieran Tierney]]. His replacement in midfield, [[Tom Rogic]], scored the winning goal for Celtic.<ref name="final17">{{cite news| url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/05/27/celtic-2-aberdeen-1tom-rogic-shatters-dons-secure-historic-clean/ | title=Celtic 2 Aberdeen 1: Tom Rogic shatters Dons to secure historic clean sweep with Scottish Cup final win |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]] | date=27 May 2017 | accessdate=30 May 2017|last=Roddy|first=Forsyth}}</ref>

==== 2017–18 season ====
[[File:Zrn-Cel (4).jpg|thumb|upright|McGregor playing for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2018]]

Having previously been on target in qualifying matches, on 31 October 2017 McGregor scored his first goal in the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group B|group stages]] of the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], striking the equaliser at home to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] ([[James Forrest (footballer, born 1991)|James Forrest]] providing the assist), although the German team responded to claim a 2–1 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2021638--celtic-vs-bayern-munchen/|title=Celtic 1-2 Bayern|publisher=UEFA |website=[[UEFA]]|date=31 October 2017|access-date=1 November 2017}}</ref> 

Celtic then dropped into the [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League]], in which McGregor scored the only goal in the first leg of the last-32 tie with [[FC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit St Petersburg]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43037852 |title=Celtic 1–0 Zenit St Petersburg |publisher=BBC Sport|website=www.bbc.co.uk/sport|first=Martin |last=Dowden |date=15 February 2018 |accessdate=18 February 2018}}</ref> On 19 May 2018, McGregor scored the opening goal in the [[2018 Scottish Cup Final|Scottish Cup final]].<ref name="sc1718" /> This secured a second consecutive domestic treble for Celtic, the first time this had been done in Scottish football history.<ref name="sc1718">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44091573|title=Celtic 2–0 Motherwell|date=19 May 2018|publisher=BBC Sport |website=www.bbc.co.uk/sport|accessdate=20 May 2018}}</ref>

==== 2018–19 season ====

McGregor signed a new contract with Celtic in December 2018, due to run until the end of the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46634734 |title=Celtic: Midfielder Callum McGregor signs new deal |publisher=BBC Sport  |website=www.bbc.co.uk/sport|date=20 December 2018 |accessdate=20 December 2018}}</ref> He made his 200th Celtic appearance against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] at [[Easter Road]] in the same month.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/15483 | title=McGregor: We're focused on delivering positive result at Paradise | publisher=Celtic FC |website=www.celtifc.net| date=19 December 2018 | accessdate=16 June 2019|last=Joe|first=Donnelly}}</ref> 

In May 2019, he was nominated for the season's [[PFA Scotland Players' Player of the Year]]; the award was won by teammate James Forrest.<ref>{{cite web|title=Player of the Year: Old Firm quartet vie for PFA Scotland top prize|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/scotland/48124177|publisher=BBC Sport  |website=www.bbc.co.uk/sport|date=5 May 2019|access-date=6 May 2019}}</ref> However, McGregor beat Forrest to [[Celtic F.C. Player of the Year|Celtic's club awards]], winning both the official and the players' category accolades.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cal Mac clinches a double at Player of the Year awards |url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/16098|publisher=Celtic FC |website=www.celticfc.net |date=30 April 2019|accessdate=6 May 2019|last=Joe|first=Donnelly}}</ref> He played more minutes than any other player in world football for club and country during [[2018–19 in Scottish football|2018–19]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carton |first=Hamish |date=2019-06-12 |title=Callum McGregor looking forward to a break after long season |url=https://www.67hailhail.com/news/callum-mcgregor-looking-forward-break-long-season/ |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=67 Hail Hail |language=en-GB}}</ref> as Celtic won a third consecutive treble.<ref>{{Cite news |title=The incredible stats behind Celtic's unprecedented treble treble |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/celtic/the-incredible-stats-behind-celtic-s-unprecedented-treble-treble-1-4936307 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190923200741/https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/celtic/the-incredible-stats-behind-celtic-s-unprecedented-treble-treble-1-4936307 |archive-date=2019-09-23 |access-date=2026-07-26 |work=[[The Scotsman]] |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2019–20 season ====
His contribution during [[2019–20 in Scottish football|2019–20]] was equally important, starting all 30 matches of the curtailed Premiership campaign (being off the field for just 26 minutes in total), all four of the [[2019–20 Scottish League Cup|League Cup]] fixtures and four of the five [[2019–20 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]] matches – including two that were delayed until the end of the calendar year – as a fourth treble was secured.<ref name="bt20">{{Cite news |title=Callum McGregor draws on Scotland experience in Celtic’s shoot-out success |url=https://www.bt.com/sport/news/2020/december/callum-mcgregor-draws-on-scotland-experience-in-celtic-s-shoot-out-success |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230424013625/https://www.bt.com/sport/news/2020/december/callum-mcgregor-draws-on-scotland-experience-in-celtic-s-shoot-out-success |archive-date=2023-04-24 |access-date=2026-07-26 |work=BT |language=en}}</ref> Along with continental (14) and international appearances (6), he was again among Europe's most active footballers.

==== 2020–21 season ====
In [[2020–21 Celtic F.C. season|2020–21]] the club lost control of all three trophies and did not win any of their matches against Rangers, with McGregor scoring an own goal in one visit to [[Ibrox Stadium]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-01-02 |title=Rangers go 19 points clear of Celtic after own goal settles Old Firm derby |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/scottish/rangers-celtic-result-old-firm-title-b1781495.html |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref> and being sent off in the first half of another.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-05-03 |title=Celtic boss insists Callum McGregor won't be tempted by England |url=https://www.glasgowlive.co.uk/sport/football/callum-mcgregor-wont-ditch-celtic-20517029 |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=Glasgow Live |language=en}}</ref> His contribution in terms of minutes played remained very high, with 49 appearances for Celtic (4256 minutes, not including the aforementioned Scottish Cup matches although completed within the span of that season) and 14 for the national team (954 minutes) up to the delayed [[UEFA Euro 2020]] finals.<ref name="bt20" />

==== 2021–22 season: Celtic captaincy ====
On 19 July 2021, following former club captain [[Scott Brown (footballer, born June 1985)|Scott Brown]]'s move to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], McGregor was awarded the Celtic captaincy after making 326 appearances for the club, scoring 53 goals and winning 14 trophies – six league titles, four Scottish Cups and four League Cups. He became the 22nd captain of the club<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cuddihy |first=Paul |date=2021-07-19 |title=Callum McGregor is the new Celtic club captain |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2021/july/Callum-McGregor-is-the-new-Celtic-club-captain/ |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=Celtic FC |language=en}}</ref> and described it as a "very proud day for myself, my family, everyone connected with myself".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cuddihy |first=Paul |date=2021-07-20 |title=Captain: It's a huge honour to wear the armband and lead the team |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2021/july/Captain-It-s-a-huge-honour-to-wear-the-armband-and-lead-the-team/ |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=Celtic FC |language=en}}</ref> Celtic manager [[Ange Postecoglou]] described McGregor's appointment as "an easy decision but also the best decision",<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cuddihy |first=Paul |date=2021-07-19 |title=Manager: Making Callum captain was an easy decision and the best one |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2021/july/Manager-Making-Callum-captain-was-an-easy-decision-and-the-best-one/ |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=Celtic FC |language=en}}</ref> further stating "I think he's a natural leader. He's the kind of guy people gravitate towards. He drives things."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Taylor |first=Louise |date=2021-07-19 |title=Rehabilitated Callum McGregor handed Celtic captain’s armband |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/jul/19/rehabilitated-callum-mcgregor-handed-celtic-captains-armband |access-date=2026-07-26 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> 

On 20 July 2021, in his first competitive appearance as club captain, McGregor was awarded Man of the Match in a 1–1 draw against [[FC Midtjylland]] in the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League qualifying phase and play-off round|UEFA Champions League Second qualifying round]].<ref>{{Cite tweet|title=Who's been your MOTM?|user=celticfc |number=1417592573749862405|access-date=2021-07-21|date=2021-07-20}}</ref> McGregor opened the scoring in the return leg with a 25 yard volley, however Celtic lost 2-1 and were knocked out of the competition.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Media |first=P. A. |date=2021-07-28 |title=Ange Postecoglou rues transfer failings after Celtic exit Champions League |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/jul/28/celtic-out-of-champions-league-after-extra-time-defeat-to-midtjylland |access-date=2026-07-26 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> On 24 September 2021, McGregor signed a new five-year contract with Celtic, due to expire in the summer of 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=FC |first=Celtic |date=2021-09-24 |title=Celtic delighted as Callum McGregor signs new five-year deal |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2021/september/Celtic-delighted-as-Callum-McGregor-signs-new-five-year-deal/ |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=Celtic FC |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2022–23 season ====
McGregor became the first player to win five domestic trebles for a club, after winning both the Scottish Cup (against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle]]) and the Scottish League Cup final (against rivals Rangers) and rounded of the season by winning an 8th league title for himself and a 53rd for Celtic.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-04 |title='If that's a parting gift, what a way to go' |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c80djgrxzqno |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==== 2023–24 season ====
On 10 July 2023, McGregor signed a new five-year contract with Celtic, keeping him at the club until 2028.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Callum McGregor signs new Celtic contract as skipper pens five-year extension |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/callum-mcgregor-signs-new-celtic-30411357 |access-date=2023-07-10|website=Daily Record |date=10 July 2023 }}</ref>

==== 2024–25 season ====
McGregor scored several long-range goals in the first few months of the 2024–25 season, putting him top of the goalscoring charts in the Scottish Premiership.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cd753jyeleno|title=In numbers: Celtic captain Callum McGregor's free-scoring league season|date=2 December 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==== 2025–26 season ====
On 16 May 2026, on the final match of the [[2025–26 Scottish Premiership|2025–26 season]], McGregor started in Celtic's 3–1 victory over [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts of Midlothian]]. The match saw Celtic win their fifth consecutive Scottish Premiership [[2025–26 Scottish Premiership|title]], and their 56th title in the club's history.<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 May 2026 |title=Celtic snatch title from Hearts with last-gasp victory on final day |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/celtic-snatch-title-hearts-with-final-day-victory-2026-05-16/ |access-date=5 October 2026 |website=Reuters}}</ref>

==International career==
Making his debut in October 2013, McGregor made five appearances and scored one goal for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland national under-21 team]].<ref name = "intl"/> He was added to the full [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] senior squad for the first time in August 2014, soon after he broke into the Celtic first team.<ref name="intl">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28924479 |title=Gordon Strachan calls up Callum McGregor and Craig Gordon |publisher=BBC Sport |date=25 August 2014 |access-date=26 August 2014}}</ref>

[[File:Callum McGregor (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|McGregor lining up for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] in 2019]]

In October 2017, McGregor was once again included in the full squad for two [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]] qualifiers against [[Slovakia national football team|Slovakia]] and [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]], but remained on the bench during [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group F|both games]]. He made his debut a month later, starting in a friendly against [[Netherlands national football team|the Netherlands]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41840573|title=Scotland 0—1 Netherlands|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 November 2017|accessdate=10 November 2017}}</ref> 

In late 2020 he scored in penalty shootouts against both [[Israel national football team|Israel]] and [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]] as Scotland won the [[2018–19 UEFA Nations League C]] playoffs and qualified for the [[UEFA Euro 2020]] finals tournament (played in 2021; delayed by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]), their first such achievement in 23 years.<ref name="bt20" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Ames |first=Nick |date=2020-11-12 |title=Serbia 1-1 Scotland (4-5 pens): Scotland seal dramatic Euro 2020 place – as it happened |url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2020/nov/12/serbia-v-scotland-euro-2020-play-off-live |access-date=2026-07-26 |work=the Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> He scored his first international goal during the final group fixture of the tournament against [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-23 |title=Callum McGregor both hero and villain for Scotland against Croatia, says Borders football legend John Collins |url=https://www.thesouthernreporter.co.uk/sport/football/callum-mcgregor-both-hero-and-villain-for-scotland-against-croatia-says-borders-football-legend-john-collins-3283121 |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=The Southern Reporter |language=en}}</ref>

McGregor was selected in the Scotland squad for [[UEFA Euro 2024]]. He played in the opening game of the tournament against hosts [[Germany national football team|Germany]] on 14 June 2024; his 31st birthday, in a 5–1 defeat in Munich.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ronay |first=Barney |date=2024-06-14 |title=Germany kickstart Euro 2024 in style and pile on the pain for 10-man Scotland |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/jun/14/germany-scotland-euro-2024-match-report |access-date=2026-07-26 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> In Scotland's second fixture on 19 June, McGregor assisted [[Scott McTominay]]'s opening goal as the team drew 1–1 with [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Murray |first=Ewan |date=2024-06-19 |title=Scotland keep knockout hopes alive after battling draw with Switzerland |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/jun/19/scotland-switzerland-euro-2024-group-a-match-report |access-date=2026-07-26 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> He went on to start against [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]] in the third match on 23 June, which Scotland lost 1–0 to finish bottom of [[UEFA Euro 2024 Group A|Group A]] with one point from three matches.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/match/2036186--scotland-vs-hungary/lineups/|title=Scotland vs Hungary: Line-ups|access-date=24 June 2024|website=UEFA}}</ref>

On 9 August 2024, McGregor announced his retirement from international football.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c5y83l52de8o|title=Celtic captain McGregor retires from Scotland duty|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 August 2024|accessdate=9 August 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
McGregor was a pupil at [[Lochend Community High School]] in [[Easterhouse]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/news/15020674.A_year_on_Callum_McGregor_reflects_on_mistake_he_feared_cost_him_his_Celtic_career/|title=A year on Callum McGregor reflects on mistake he feared cost him his Celtic career|last=Mullen|first=Scott|date=9 January 2017|accessdate=24 May 2017|newspaper=The Herald}}</ref> In February 2016, McGregor was stopped by the police and charged with [[driving under the influence]] of alcohol, having already been convicted and banned for [[Road speed limit enforcement in the United Kingdom|speeding]] the previous year; he was later disqualified for 12 months.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-glasgow-west-35720795|title=Celtic player Callum McGregor banned for drink driving|date=3 March 2016|website=BBC News}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/news/15020674.A_year_on_Callum_McGregor_reflects_on_mistake_he_feared_cost_him_his_Celtic_career/|title=A year on Callum McGregor reflects on mistake he feared cost him his Celtic career|date=9 January 2017|access-date=24 May 2017|publisher= |newspaper=The Herald}}</ref>
