'''Lawrence Shankland''' (born 10 August 1995) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], which he [[Captain (association football)|captains]], and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]].

Shankland began his career at [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] before moving to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in 2013. He played on loan with [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] and [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] before joining [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in 2017. He signed for [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in 2019 and made his international debut later that year. In 2021 Shankland moved to Belgian club [[K Beerschot VA|Beerschot]], but returned to Scotland after one year, signing with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. At the [[Edinburgh]] club he was appointed [[Captain (association football)|captain]] before departing to join Rangers in the summer of 2026, just prior to making two appearances in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] group stage (he had also featured at [[UEFA Euro 2024]]).

==Club career==
===Queen's Park===
Shankland was born in [[Glasgow]] and attended [[Bannerman High School]] in [[Baillieston]].<ref name=afc15>{{cite web |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2015/02/11/lawrence-shankland-interview-2/ |title=Lawrence Shankland interview |publisher=Aberdeen FC  |date=11 February 2015 |access-date=17 May 2019}}</ref> He progressed through the [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] youth system and was their top goalscorer in the [[2012–13 Scottish Third Division|2012–13 season]], having moved to the senior squad straight from the under-17 team;<ref>{{cite web |url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/shankland-given-opportunity-at-aberdeen/ |title=Shankland given opportunity at Aberdeen |work=www.spfl.co.uk |publisher=Scottish Professional Football League |date=25 June 2013 |access-date=18 October 2014}}</ref> he also worked part-time as a tool setter in a local plumbing supplies company, a position arranged by the amateur club to help their young players earn a wage.<ref name=afc15/> He scored his first senior goal on 4 August 2012, aged 16, in a [[Scottish League Cup]] tie against [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Roache |first1=Ian |title=Sean Burns looks back to when 16-year-old Lawrence Shankland announced his arrival as goalscorer |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/990043/sean-burns-looks-back-to-when-16-year-old-lawrence-shankland-announced-his-arrival-as-goalscorer/ |access-date=16 July 2020 |work=The Courier |date=2 October 2019 |location=Dundee}}</ref>

Shankland signed for [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] at the end of the season.<ref name = "queen's park"/><ref name = "under20">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23030004 |title=Aberdeen sign former Rangers winger Gregg Wylde |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=24 June 2013 |access-date=18 October 2014}}</ref> He was one of three Queen's Park players to move to top flight Scottish clubs at that time, as [[Andrew Robertson (footballer)|Andy Robertson]] and [[Aidan Connolly]] signed for [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref name = "queen's park">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23199925 |title=Young Queen's Park trio make rare jump to SPL from Third Division |first=Kenny |last=Crawford |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=5 July 2013 |access-date=18 October 2014}}</ref><ref name=afc15/> [[Blair Spittal]] also made the move to Dundee United a year later.

===Aberdeen===
Shankland was initially placed in the Aberdeen [[Aberdeen F.C. Reserves and Academy|under-20 squad]], as he adjusted to full-time professional training.<ref name = "under20"/><ref name=afc15/> He made his debut appearance for Aberdeen in September 2014, in a 3–2 victory against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.afc.co.uk/mobile/matches/5115.php#.VEIIJRawS5Y |title=FT: Aberdeen 3 Inverness CT 2 |publisher=Aberdeen FC |work=www.afc.co.uk |access-date=18 October 2014}}</ref> After impressing in the under-20s, scoring plenty of goals, and making first team appearances as a substitute, Shankland signed a new contract to run until summer 2017;<ref>{{cite web|title=Aberdeen: Adam Rooney & Niall McGinn sign new deals|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30582242|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=22 December 2014 |access-date=22 December 2014}}</ref><ref name=afc15/> however, he was loaned to lower-division clubs for the vast majority of its duration. At the end of the [[2016–17 Aberdeen F.C. season|2016–17 season]], Aberdeen confirmed that Shankland would be leaving the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40113519|title=Aberdeen: Ash Taylor & Lawrence Shankland join players leaving Pittodrie|work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=31 May 2017|access-date=5 June 2017}}</ref>

====Dunfermline loan====
Shankland moved to [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on loan for the latter part of the [[2013–14 Scottish League One|2013–14 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25650100 |title=Aberdeen's Lawrence Shankland joins Dunfermline on loan |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=8 January 2014 |access-date=18 October 2014}}</ref> The 18-year-old striker scored seven league goals during his short spell in Fife; however, injury prevented him taking part in the ''Pars''' end-of-season [[2013–14 Scottish Championship#Championship play-offs|promotion play-off]] with [[Fife derby|local rivals]] [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]] which ended in defeat.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cowdenbeath-mad.co.uk/news/tmnw/cowdenbeath_v_dunfermline_at_central_park_match_preview_832903/index.shtml |title=Cowdenbeath V Dunfermline at Central Park – Match Preview |work=CowdenbeathMad |publisher=FootyMad |date=13 May 2014 |access-date=18 October 2014}}</ref>

====St Mirren and Morton loans====
Shankland was loaned to [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in August 2015 for the rest of the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Loan Signing: Lawrence Shankland|url=http://www.saintmirren.net/pages/?p=46391|publisher=St Mirren F.C.|work=www.saintmirren.net|date=26 August 2015|access-date=26 August 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924094054/http://www.saintmirren.net/pages/?p=46391|archive-date=24 September 2015}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the ''Buddies'' in a 2–1 home defeat to [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on 18 September 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=St Mirren 1–2 Raith Rovers match report|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34217202|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=18 September 2015 |access-date=20 September 2015}}</ref> Shankland scored 10 goals in 32 appearances during his loan spell, and returned to Aberdeen at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.saintmirren.net/pages/?p=55088|title=Squad Update|publisher=St Mirren Official website|access-date=3 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160605114158/http://www.saintmirren.net/pages/?p=55088|archive-date=5 June 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In July 2016 it was confirmed that Shankland had returned to St Mirren, on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.saintmirren.net/pages/?p=56577 |title=Loan Signing: Lawrence Shankland |publisher=St Mirren FC |date=19 July 2016 |access-date=19 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160825214145/http://www.saintmirren.net/pages/?p=56577 |archive-date=25 August 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, having failed to score any league goals in the first half of the season, his St Mirren deal was cut short and on 11 January 2017, he moved on loan to their [[Renfrewshire derby|rivals]], fellow [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gmfc.net/2017/01/11/aberdeen-striker-lawrence-shankland-joins-on-loan/ |title=Aberdeen striker Lawrence Shankland joins on loan |first=Jonathan |last=Mitchell |publisher=Greenock Morton FC |date=11 January 2017 |access-date=11 January 2017 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170113091010/http://gmfc.net/2017/01/11/aberdeen-striker-lawrence-shankland-joins-on-loan/ |archive-date=13 January 2017 }}</ref> After helping the club to a fourth-place finish, his final appearance for Morton was in the [[2016–17 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|Scottish Premiership playoff]] defeat to Dundee United.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39833721 |title=Dundee United 3–0 Greenock Morton|work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=12 May 2017 |access-date=5 June 2017}}</ref>

===Ayr United===
In September 2017, free agent Shankland signed a short-term contract to play for [[Scottish League One]] club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] until the following January.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/ayr-united-sign-former-aberdeen-11133101 |title=Ayr United sign former Aberdeen striker Lawrence Shankland as Ian McCall bids to boost side's League One title bid|work=Daily Record |date=8 September 2017 |access-date=8 September 2017}}</ref> On 24 March 2018 he scored a hat-trick against former club Queen's Park.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43528434|title=Scottish League One: Ayr strengthen grip on top spot, Forfar boost hopes|work=BBC Sport|date=24 March 2018|access-date=24 March 2018}}</ref> Ayr won [[2017–18 Scottish League One|the league]] by one point, and after finishing with 29 goals, Shankland was named as the division's [[PFA Scotland Players' Player of the Year]].<ref name=pfa18>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43944186 |title=Scott Brown: Celtic captain voted PFA Scotland player of the year 2017/18 |work=BBC Sport |date=29 April 2018 |access-date=10 May 2018}}</ref>

He started the 2018–19 season with a hat-trick against former club Morton in the [[2018–19 Scottish League Cup|League Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/AyrUnitedFC/status/1018155948362358784|title=GOOOAAAALLLL! | HAT-TRICK @Shankland_25. A cool chip over Ryan Scully.pic.twitter.com/RU3oPLS07a|first=Ayr|last=United|date=14 July 2018}}</ref> On 28 July, he scored a "stunning goal" from 45 yards as Ayr defeated [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] to qualify for the knockout stage of the competition.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44994431 |title=League Cup: Partick Thistle 0-2 Ayr United, Morton 5-0 Albion Rovers |work=BBC Sport |date=28 July 2018 |access-date=28 July 2018}}</ref> With a goal against Dunfermline on 25 August 2018, Shankland moved to 41 goals in 42 games for the ''Honest Men''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45230784 |title=Ayr United 4-1 Dunfermline Athletic |work=BBC Sport |date=25 August 2018|access-date=27 August 2018}}</ref>

In November 2018, he scored four goals in a [[2018–19 Scottish Championship|league fixture]] away to Dundee United which ended 5–0 and put Ayr five points clear at the top of the table.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46312740 |title= Dundee United 0-5 Ayr United |work=BBC Sport |date=30 November 2018|access-date=1 December 2018}}</ref> However he then sustained an injury, and Ayr's form deteriorated in his absence. He returned towards the end of the season, but the team's campaign ended with defeat to Inverness CT in the opening round of the [[2018–19 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|Premiership promotion play-offs]], having finished in fourth position.<ref>{{cite web|title=Inverness CT 1-1 Ayr United (4-2 agg): hosts set up play-off semi-final meeting with Dundee United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48165445|work=BBC Sport |date=11 May 2019|access-date=17 May 2019}}</ref> Shankland, whose total return was 34 goals in 41 games, was nominated for the division's PFA Player of the Year Award,<ref>{{cite web|title=Player of the Year: Old Firm quartet vie for PFA Scotland top prize|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/scotland/48124177|work=BBC Sport |date=5 May 2019|access-date=17 May 2019}}</ref> but lost out to another prolific striker, [[Stephen Dobbie]]. Both were named in the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#2018–19|Team of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/1741717/kilmarnocks-steve-clarke-and-celtics-james-forrest-win-pfa-manager-and-player-of-the-year-awards/ | title=Kilmarnock's Steve Clarke and Celtic's James Forrest win PFA manager and player of the year awards | publisher=[[The Press and Journal (Scotland)|Press and Journal]] | date=5 May 2019 | access-date=17 May 2019}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
On 3 July 2019 it was announced that Shankland had left Ayr to join fellow Championship side Dundee United on a three-year contract, turning down offers from other clubs in both England and Scotland.<ref>{{cite web |title=United Announce Shankland Signing |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/6126/UNITED-ANNOUNCE-SHANKLAND-SIGNING.html?key=dufc |website=Dundee United Football Club |access-date=3 July 2019}}</ref><ref name="BBCsport03072019">{{cite news |title=Dundee Utd confirm Lawrence Shankland signing as striker leaves Ayr Utd |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48862322 |access-date=3 July 2019 |work=BBC Sport |date=3 July 2019}}</ref> He scored on his debut for the club in a [[Scottish League Cup]] tie against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] on 12 July 2019,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48925615 |title=Hearts 1–1 Dundee United  |work=BBC |access-date=15 July 2019}}</ref> and scored four goals in a 4–1 victory against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on the opening day of the [[2019–20 Scottish Championship]] season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee United 4–1 Inverness Caledonian Thistle|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49136071|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Lewis|first=Jane|date=3 August 2019|access-date=3 August 2019}}</ref> Shankland was named [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners#2019–20 season|Scottish Championship Player of the Month]] for August 2019, having scored eight goals in four appearances during the month.<ref name=august19>{{cite web|title=Awards Double For Dundee United|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/awards-double-for-dundee-united|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=10 September 2019|access-date=10 September 2019}}</ref> The season was suspended in March 2020 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]], and curtailed a month later, with Dundee United declared winners and promoted;<ref name=ends20>{{cite news| url= https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11781/11973775/scottish-championship-league-one-and-league-two-seasons-end-after-dundee-vote-for-spfl-resolution| title=Scottish Championship, League One and League Two seasons end after Dundee vote for SPFL resolution| website=[[BBC Sport]]| date=16 April 2020| access-date=23 May 2020}}</ref> up to that point Shankland had scored 24 league goals to finish as the division's top scorer, and maintained the  ratio of almost a goal-per-game he had set at Ayr, with a total of 28 from 33 appearances.

On 12 January 2021, Shankland scored with a "wonder strike" from {{convert|53|yards|m}} to secure a 2–2 draw against [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Goal of the season? Watch Shankland's 53-yard wonder strike |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/av/football/55641336 |access-date=17 January 2021 |work=BBC Sport |date=12 January 2021}}</ref>

===Beerschot===

On 11 August 2021, Shankland moved to Belgian side [[K Beerschot VA|Beerschot]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.beerschot.be/en/news/dundee-united-striker-lawrence-shankland-signs-beerschot|title=DUNDEE UNITED STRIKER LAWRENCE SHANKLAND SIGNS FOR BEERSCHOT|publisher=K Beerschot VA|date=11 August 2021|access-date=11 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/6953/LAWRENCE-SHANKLAND-DEPARTS-FOR-BEERSCHOT.html|title=LAWRENCE SHANKLAND DEPARTS FOR BEERSCHOT|publisher=Dundee United FC|date=11 August 2021|access-date=11 August 2021}}</ref> Shankland scored five league goals for Beerschot during the 2021–22 season as they were relegated from the Belgian top division.<ref name = hearts/>

===Heart of Midlothian===
Shankland returned to Scottish football in July 2022, signing a three-year contract with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref name="hearts">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62242130 |title=Lawrence Shankland: Scotland striker joins Hearts from Beerschot |website=BBC Sport |date=20 July 2022 |accessdate=20 July 2022}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Hearts in a 1–1 draw with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] at [[Easter Road]] on 7 August 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hibernian 1-1 Hearts: Martin Boyle marks Easter Road return with late Edinburgh derby equaliser |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/36621/12665263/hibernian-1-1-hearts-martin-boyle-marks-easter-road-return-with-late-edinburgh-derby-equaliser |access-date=2023-01-27 |website=Sky Sports }}</ref> After a season-ending injury to club captain [[Craig Gordon]] in a match on 28 December 2022, Shankland was named team captain for the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Meikle |first=Blair |date=2022-12-29 |title=Lawrence Shankland Hearts captain for season as Robbie Neilson explains decision |url=https://www.footballscotland.co.uk/spfl/scottish-premiership/lawrence-shankland-captain-hearts-season-25853555 |access-date=2024-07-09 |website=Football Scotland }}</ref> In scoring in a [[2022–23 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]] derby victory over Hibs in January 2023, he became the first Hearts player since [[John Robertson (footballer, born 1964)|John Robertson]] in the [[1991–92 in Scottish football|1991–92 season]] to score 20 goals in all competitions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Galindo |first=Alan |date=2023-01-23 |title=Hearts star Lawrence Shankland tipped for 30 goals after breaking 20-goal mark |url=https://www.edinburghlive.co.uk/sport/hearts-star-lawrence-shankland-tipped-26047523 |access-date=2023-01-27 |website=EdinburghLive}}</ref>

In Gordon's continued absence, Shankland retained team captaincy for the [[2023–24 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2023–24 season]]. His second season at Hearts showed a similar prolific form as his first, hitting 50 club goals by February 2024, less than 18 months after joining the club; he was only the second player to hit the milestone in the 21st century, after [[Jamie Walker (footballer)|Jamie Walker]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-09 |title=Lawrence Shankland backs himself to keep scoring after hitting 50th Hearts goal |url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/24108275.shankland-backs-keep-scoring-50-hearts-goals/ |access-date=2024-07-09 |website=The National}}</ref>

During the [[2024–25 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2024–25 season]], Shankland's goalscoring output in the early part of the campaign was lower than in the previous season, with analysis noting a reduced conversion rate despite a similar volume of chances.<ref>{{cite web |last=Petrie |first=Andrew |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cy5lk57l1p9o |title=What's gone wrong for misfiring Shankland? |publisher=BBC Sport |date=31 October 2024 }}</ref> In July 2025, Shankland signed a new three-year contract with the club.<ref name="auto1">{{cite web |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/shankland-signs-new-deal |title=Shankland signs new deal |publisher=Heart of Midlothian F.C. |date=3 July 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=McLauchlin |first=Brian |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cq53wq1nzn5o |title=Shankland reveals Jock the Jambo role in new Hearts contract |publisher=BBC Sport |date=3 July 2025 }}</ref>

In the [[2025–26 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2025–26 season]], he continued as club captain and contributed key goals in the title challenge, including in a 3–1 victory over [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on 26 October 2025 that increased Hearts' lead at the top of the table.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/report/_/gameId/742387 |title=Hearts beat injury-hit Celtic, go eight points clear in SPFL |publisher=ESPN |date=26 October 2025 }}</ref> He later netted the winning goal in a 2–1 victory against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on 4 May 2026.<ref>{{cite web |last=Murray |first=Ewan |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/04/hearts-rangers-scottish-premiership-match-report |title=Title-chasing Hearts clear crucial hurdle as Shankland shatters Rangers' hopes |publisher=The Guardian |date=4 May 2026 }}</ref> On the final matchday of the season against Celtic, Shankland scored the opening goal in an eventual 3–1 defeat, resulting in Hearts finishing second in the title race behind Celtic.<ref>{{cite web |last=Binnie |first=Adam |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11781/13544422/celtic-win-scottish-premiership-title-but-does-hearts-emergence-mean-the-scottish-football-landscape-has-changed-forever |title=Celtic win Scottish Premiership title but does Hearts' emergence mean the Scottish football landscape has changed forever? |publisher=Sky Sports |date=16 May 2026 }}</ref> He ended the season with 16 league goals, just one short of top scorer [[Tawanda Maswanhise]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://onefootball.com/de/news/celtic-surge-late-as-hearts-surrender-top-spot-42875419 |title=Celtic surge late as Hearts surrender top spot |publisher=OneFootball |date=16 May 2026 }}</ref>

===Rangers===
On 26 May 2026, [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] announced the signing of Shankland on a two-year deal with an option for an additional year.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/rangers-announce-signing-of-lawrence-shankland/3COV8MiuUZ9gqCl3Xt67xu |title=Rangers Announce Signing of Lawrence Shankland |publisher=Rangers FC |date=26 May 2026 }}</ref> On 29 July 2026 Shankland was named club captain by manager Derek McInnes, a role that he had with McInnes at Hearts the season before.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 July 2026 |title=Shankland named Rangers captain |url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/lawrence-shankland-named-mens-first-team-captain/57BOpcjOjPGaRikciPv66p |website=Rangers.co.uk}}</ref> 

==International career==
[[File:Lawrence Shankland 2019.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Shankland with [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] in 2019.]]

Shankland represented [[Scotland national under-18 football team|Scotland under-18s]] in [[Victory Shield]] matches against the other home nations in 2012.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/ssfa/scottish_football.cfm?page=3383 |title=Scotland Under 18s 2012 Photo Gallery |work=Scottish FA |publisher=The Scottish Schools' Football Association 2014 |access-date=18 October 2014}}</ref> He was first selected for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team]] in March 2015; he made his debut away to [[Hungary national under-21 football team|Hungary]], scoring two late goals in a 2–1 victory. He made three other under-21 appearances, also in 2015, producing one draw and two defeats.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=113593 |title=Lawrence Shankland |work=www.scottishfa.co.uk |publisher=Scottish Football Association |access-date=22 September 2018}}</ref>

On 1 October 2019, [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] manager [[Steve Clarke]] called up Shankland to the senior squad for the first time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49893529 |title=Lawrence Shankland: Scotland call-up for Dundee United striker |date=1 October 2019 |website=BBC Sport|access-date=1 October 2019}}</ref> He won his first [[Cap (sport)|cap]] when he came on as a second-half substitute in the side's 4–0 defeat by [[Russia national football team|Russia]] on 10 October<ref name="ScotRussia">{{cite news |last1=Forsyth |first1=Roddy |title=Sorry Scotland thrashed by Russia to leave Nations League as their only Euro 2020 hope |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/10/10/scotland-thrashed-russia-leave-nations-league-euro-2020-hope/ |access-date=10 October 2019 |work=The Telegraph |date=10 October 2019}}</ref> (playing alongside national team captain [[Andy Robertson]] for the first time since their time at Queen's Park in the fourth tier of Scottish football, nearly seven years earlier)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/17939061.queens-park-share-nostalgic-snap-robertson-shankland-teammates-scotland-call-up|title=Queen's Park share nostalgic snap of Robertson and Shankland as teammates after Scotland call-up|publisher=Glasgow Times |date=1 October 2019|access-date=10 September 2021}}</ref> and three days later made his first start and scored his first goal, the fourth in a 6–0 victory over [[San Marino national football team|San Marino]] at [[Hampden Park]].<ref name="BBCScotSanMar">{{cite news |last1=Lamont |first1=Alasdair |title=Scotland 6–0 San Marino |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49949350 |access-date=13 October 2019 |work=BBC Sport |date=13 October 2019}}</ref>

Shankland was recalled to the squad in March 2023, as an injury replacement for [[Ché Adams]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65080102 |title=Scotland call up for Lawrence Shankland as Che Adams & Anthony Ralston drop out |website=BBC Sport |date=26 March 2023 |accessdate=26 March 2023}}</ref> He scored his second international goal on 16 November 2023, a late equaliser in a [[UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying]] match against [[Georgia national football team|Georgia]].<ref name = Georgia>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67444687 |title=Georgia 2-2 Scotland: Should Lawrence Shankland be on the plane to Germany next summer? |first=Nick |last=McPheat |website=BBC Sport |date=16 November 2023 |accessdate=17 November 2023}}</ref> Shankland had again been a late addition to the squad as an injury replacement for Adams.<ref name = Georgia/>

On 23 March 2024, Shankland was named in Scotland's starting XI for the first time since 2019 in a [[UEFA Euro 2024]] warm-up match against the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]].<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/24205834.netherlands-4-scotland-0-instant-reaction-burning-issues/|title= Netherlands 4 Scotland 0: Steve Clarke's men suffer mauling in Euro 2024 warm-up game|website=Herald Scotland|date=23 March 2024|access-date=15 June 2024}}</ref>

On 7 June 2024, he was named in Scotland's 26-man squad for Euro 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/record-breaking-goalkeeper-gordon-out-scotland-euro-2024-squad-2024-06-07/|title=Record-breaking goalkeeper Gordon out of Scotland's Euro 2024 squad|date=7 June 2024|access-date=15 June 2024|website=Reuters}}</ref> He played the final eight minutes of the 5–1 loss to hosts [[Germany national football team|Germany]] in the opening match of the tournament on 14 June.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c844x4y3ee3t|title=Ruthless Germany humble 10-man Scotland in Euro 2024 opener|website=BBC Sport|access-date=15 June 2024}}</ref> He went on to appear as a substitute against both [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] and [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]] as Scotland finished bottom of [[UEFA Euro 2024 Group A|Group A]] with one point from three matches.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/news/028e-1b2c127c5b92-e020507872a2-1000--scotland-1-1-switzerland-clarke-s-men-keep-group-a-hopes-/|title=Scotland 1-1 Switzerland: Clarke's men keep Group A hopes alive|access-date=24 June 2024|website=UEFA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/match/2036186--scotland-vs-hungary/lineups/|title=Scotland vs Hungary: Line-ups|access-date=24 June 2024|website=UEFA}}</ref>

After a year out of the international team, Shankland was recalled for Scotland's [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2026 FIFA World Cup qualifiers]] against [[Greece national football team|Greece]] and [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]] in November 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cn51g1yxl0wo |title=Shankland eyes World Cup after Scotland recall |website=BBC Sport |date=7 November 2025 |accessdate=21 November 2025}}</ref> He scored the second goal in a famous 4–2 win against Denmark on 18 November, allowing Scotland to top their group and qualify automatically for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]]; their first appearance at the tournament since [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Murray |first=Ewan |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/nov/18/scotland-denmark-world-cup-2026-qualifying-match-report |title=Tierney and McLean send Scotland to World Cup with thrilling win against Denmark |work=The Guardian |date=18 November 2025 }}</ref>

On 19 May 2026, Shankland was selected in the 26-man squad for the 2026 World Cup finals.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/scotland-squad-announced-steve-clarke|title=Veteran Gordon and youngster Curtis named in Scotland squad|date=19 May 2026|access-date=13 June 2026|website=[[FIFA]] }}</ref> He started in the 1–0 victory over [[Haiti national football team|Haiti]] and the 3–0 loss to [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]], remaining on the bench in the 1–0 defeat by [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]].

'''Kieran Tierney''' (born 5 June 1997) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]].

Tierney came through the [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] youth system and made his first-team debut in April 2015. After playing 170 games for the club, he joined [[Premier League]] side [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in August 2019 for a fee reported at £25 million. After six years with Arsenal, including one on loan with [[La Liga]] club [[Real Sociedad]], Tierney returned to Celtic in June 2025. He made his Scotland international debut in March 2016, and has since made more than 50 appearances for the senior side.

===Celtic===
====2015–16: Debut and breakthrough====
[[File:Kieran Tierney (26938128442) (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Tierney with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2016]] 

Tierney made his competitive senior debut for Celtic on 22 April 2015, coming on as an 81st-minute substitute in a [[Scottish Premiership]] match against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2015/04/22/scotland/premier-league/dundee-fc/celtic-fc/1704591/|title=Dundee vs. Celtic|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=23 April 2015|archive-date=20 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150320033542/https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2015/04/22/scotland/premier-league/dundee-fc/celtic-fc/1704591/|url-status=live}}</ref> He made one further first-team appearance that season, playing over an hour in a league match away at [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Games Involving Tierney, Kieran in Season 2014/2015|url=http://www.fitbastats.com/celtic/player_games.php?playerid=6774&page=2|website=FitbaStats|access-date=2 August 2015|archive-date=24 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924043302/http://www.fitbastats.com/celtic/player_games.php?playerid=6774&page=2|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Tierney enjoyed a breakthrough season in [[2015–16 in Scottish football|2015–16]], appearing in over 30 matches and displacing the more experienced [[Emilio Izaguirre]] as first-choice [[left back]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/news/14314216.Tierney__I_took_Emilio_s_Celtic_place_but_he_still_helps_me_every_day/|title=Kieran Tierney: I took Emilio Izaguirre's Celtic place but he still helps me every day|last=Macpherson|first=Graeme|date=2 March 2016|work=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]]|publisher=[[Newsquest]]|access-date=17 October 2016|archive-date=18 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161018224621/http://www.heraldscotland.com/news/14314216.Tierney__I_took_Emilio_s_Celtic_place_but_he_still_helps_me_every_day/|url-status=live}}</ref> For his performances he was awarded with both the [[PFA Scotland Young Player of the Year|Players']] and [[SFWA Young Player of the Year|Writers']] Young Player annual awards,<ref name = "players 2016"/><ref name = "writers 2016"/> while Celtic also won the league title. Despite interest from [[Premier League]] clubs, Tierney signed a new five-year contract on 24 June 2016, keeping him at Parkhead until 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36620462|title=Celtic: Kieran Tierney signs five-year contract extension|last=Barnes|first=John|date=24 June 2016|work=BBC Sport|access-date=10 March 2017|archive-date=7 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170407031134/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36620462|url-status=live}}</ref> After making his first appearances in the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group C|group stage]] of the [[UEFA Champions League]], Tierney suffered ankle ligament damage during training on 27 October 2016 and was initially ruled out of action for two months.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37797772|title=Kieran Tierney: Celtic and Scotland defender ruled out for two months|date=29 October 2016|work=BBC Sport|access-date=30 October 2016|archive-date=31 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161031222705/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37797772|url-status=live}}</ref> During the layoff, which caused him to miss the [[2016 Scottish League Cup final (November)|League Cup final]], he received treatment on a recurring shoulder injury and attended several Celtic matches as a typical supporter in the company of his childhood friends.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/scottish/celtic/injured-tierney-savoured-roaring-on-celts-in-stands-35422285.html|title=Injured Tierney savoured roaring on Celts in stands|date=4 February 2017|work=The Belfast Telegraph|access-date=8 November 2017|archive-date=9 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171109023324/https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/scottish/celtic/injured-tierney-savoured-roaring-on-celts-in-stands-35422285.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2017–2019: Back-to-back domestic trebles====
On 22 January 2017, after missing three months, he made his long-awaited return to the Celtic team in a [[Scottish Cup]] tie against [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38626880|title=Albion Rovers 0–3 Celtic|last=Wilson|first=Richard|date=22 January 2017|work=BBC Sport|access-date=8 May 2017|archive-date=20 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170220223739/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38626880|url-status=live}}</ref> Tierney was crowned PFA Scotland Young Player of the Year for the second consecutive season on 7 May, making him the first to achieve this since [[Craig Levein]] in 1986.<ref name = "pfa 2017">{{cite news|url=https://stv.tv/sport/football/1387806-celtic-seal-a-treble-of-awards-at-pfa-scotland-ceremony/|title=Celtic seal a treble of awards at PFA Scotland ceremony|last=Brannan|first=Laura|date=7 May 2017|publisher=[[stv.tv]]|access-date=8 May 2017|archive-date=29 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170929000735/https://stv.tv/sport/football/1387806-celtic-seal-a-treble-of-awards-at-pfa-scotland-ceremony/|url-status=live}}</ref> He suffered a jaw injury early in the [[2017 Scottish Cup final|Scottish Cup final]] and had to be substituted for treatment.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/05/27/celtic-2-aberdeen-1tom-rogic-shatters-dons-secure-historic-clean/ | title=Celtic 2 Aberdeen 1: Tom Rogic shatters Dons to secure historic clean sweep with Scottish Cup final win | work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] | date=27 May 2017 | access-date=30 May 2017 | archive-date=28 May 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170528071539/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/05/27/celtic-2-aberdeen-1tom-rogic-shatters-dons-secure-historic-clean/ | url-status=live }}</ref> Celtic won the match 2–1 to complete a [[Treble (association football)#Domestic trebles|domestic treble]] and [[List of unbeaten football club seasons|undefeated season]]. In spite of his lengthy injury absence, he featured in 40 matches during the campaign.

On 8 August 2017, Tierney was named as [[Captain (association football)|captain]] while also moving to [[Defender (association football)#Central defender|central defender]] to command a back line of teenagers in a [[2017–18 Scottish League Cup#Second round|Scottish League Cup]] fixture against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]]; Celtic won the game 5–0, with Tierney providing an [[Assist (football)|assist]] and scoring with a "wonderful strike" from 40 yards.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40829930 |title=Celtic 5–0 Kilmarnock |work=BBC Sport |date=8 August 2017 |access-date=8 August 2017 |archive-date=5 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180905050605/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40829930 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 30 October, a week after scoring in an important [[2017–18 Scottish Premiership|league]] victory away to closest challengers [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], he extended his contract with Celtic until 2023.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41810466|title=Kieran Tierney: Celtic left-back signs new six-year contract|date=22 February 2017|work=BBC Sport|access-date=8 November 2017|archive-date=7 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107143845/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41810466|url-status=live}}</ref>

By the end of the season, he had collected further personal accolades—winning both the [[PFA Scotland Young Player of the Year|Players']] and [[SFWA Young Player of the Year|Writers']] Young Player awards for the third campaign in succession—and performed a major role in securing a historic 'double treble' for the club, making more than 50 appearances and playing the entirety of the domestic cup finals, both being 2–0 wins over [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref name=lc1718/><ref name=sc1718/> Tierney played in Celtic's victory over Aberdeen in the [[2018 Scottish League Cup Final]] on 2 December 2018.<ref name=lc1819/> Soon afterwards a hip injury meant that he was ruled out of action, returning on 24 February 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Celtic star Kieran Tierney blasts Motherwell over lack of respect after sneaky throw-in goal|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/celtic-star-kieran-tierney-blasts-14048209|work=Daily Record|date=24 February 2019|access-date=25 February 2019|archive-date=25 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190225045215/https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/celtic-star-kieran-tierney-blasts-14048209|url-status=live}}</ref> He then suffered from a hernia, which subsequently required surgery.<ref name="hernia">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48731196|title=Kieran Tierney: Arsenal 'optimistic' over Celtic defender deal|last=Ornstein|first=David|date=22 June 2019|work=BBC Sport|access-date=22 June 2019|archive-date=22 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190622170507/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48731196|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Arsenal===
====2019–2023: FA Cup win and injuries====
On 8 August 2019, Tierney signed for [[Premier League]] club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], for a reported £25 million fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/kieran-tierney-joins-long-term-deal|title=Kieran Tierney joins on long-term deal|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=8 August 2019|archive-date=8 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190808155104/https://www.arsenal.com/news/kieran-tierney-joins-long-term-deal|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49283667 |title=Kieran Tierney: Celtic defender completes £25m Arsenal move |website=BBC Sport |date=8 August 2019 |access-date=8 August 2019 |archive-date=8 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190808170510/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49283667 |url-status=live }}</ref> Tierney missed the early part of the 2019–20 season, having undergone a double hernia operation in May 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49780536 |title=Kieran Tierney: Scotland defender makes injury comeback for Arsenal U23 |website=BBC Sport |date=21 September 2019 |access-date=21 September 2019 |archive-date=21 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190921090511/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49780536 |url-status=live }}</ref> He made his first-team debut for Arsenal in a 5–0 win against [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] in the [[EFL Cup]] on 24 September.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49823156 |title=Kieran Tierney: Scotland full-back enjoys impressive Arsenal debut |website=BBC Sport |date=25 September 2019 |access-date=25 September 2019 |archive-date=25 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190925093458/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49823156 |url-status=live }}</ref> Tierney assisted the first goal in a 4–0 home win against [[Standard Liège]] scored by [[Gabriel Martinelli]] a week later.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49874359 |title=Arsenal 4–0 Standard Liege |website=BBC Sport |date=3 October 2019 |access-date=8 October 2019 |archive-date=3 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191003043401/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49874359 |url-status=live }}</ref> He made his first appearance in the Premier League on 27 October, in a 2–2 draw with [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]]. His season was further disrupted after suffering a dislocated shoulder in the game against West Ham United.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50113576|title=Arsenal 2–2 Crystal Palace: Gunners surrender two-goal advantage as Granit Xhaka booed off|work=BBC Sport |date=27 October 2019|access-date=28 October 2019|archive-date=26 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191026012508/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50113576|url-status=live}}</ref>

Tierney's impressive performances for Arsenal following the resumption of the Premier League after the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] saw him receive Arsenal's Player of the Month award for June.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/tierney-our-june-player-month|title=Tierney is our June Player of the Month!|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=13 July 2020|archive-date=13 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200713150320/https://www.arsenal.com/news/tierney-our-june-player-month|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Arsenal on 26 July, in a 3–2 win against [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] on the final day of the 2019–20 Premier League season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/kieran-tierney-mark-arsenal-former-22419340 |title=Kieran Tierney off the mark for Arsenal as former Celtic star scores first Premier League goal |first=Steven |last=Mair |newspaper=Daily Record |date=26 July 2020 |access-date=26 July 2020 |archive-date=26 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200726161927/https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/kieran-tierney-mark-arsenal-former-22419340 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 1 August 2020, Tierney was selected to start in the [[2020 FA Cup final|FA Cup final]] against Chelsea, as Arsenal won their 14th FA Cup.<ref name="bbc">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53546100 |title=Arsenal 2–1 Chelsea |first=Phil |last=McNulty |website=BBC Sport |date=1 August 2020 |access-date=2 August 2020 |archive-date=1 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200801202716/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53546100 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 28 August 2020, Tierney was in the starting 11 in the [[2020 FA Community Shield]], which Arsenal clinched a 5–4 victory over [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in the penalty shootout after the match was 1–1 after 90 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Arsenal 1–1 Liverpool (5–4 on pens): Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang secures Community Shield shootout win|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12059158/arsenal-1-1-liverpool-5-4-on-pens-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-secures-community-shield-shootout-win|access-date=26 February 2021|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref> On 2 January 2021, Tierney scored the opening goal in a 4–0 away league win over [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] and later assisted the final goal, scored by [[Alexandre Lacazette]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55450393 |title=West Brom 0–4 Arsenal: Arsenal see off Baggies in ruthless display |work=BBC Sport |date=2 January 2021|access-date=16 January 2021}}</ref> His stunning strike was subsequently voted the January Goal of the Month on the Arsenal official website.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kieran Tierney tops January Goal of the Month poll|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/kieran-tierney-tops-january-goal-month-poll|access-date=15 February 2021|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|language=en}}</ref> On 25 February, he scored a goal in a 3–2 win over [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in the [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] round of 32, making him the first Scotsman to score for Arsenal in a European competition since [[Willie Young (footballer, born 1951)|Willie Young]] in March 1980.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56185885 |title=Arsenal 3–2 Benfica |website=BBC Sport |date=25 February 2021 }}</ref> In June 2021, he signed a long-term contract with Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/12341803/kieran-tierney-feels-amazing-after-signing-long-term-arsenal-contract-extension |title=Kieran Tierney 'feels amazing' after signing long-term Arsenal contract extension |website=Sky Sports |date=25 June 2021 }}</ref>

Tierney played regularly for Arsenal during the 2021–22 season until suffering a season-ending knee injury in March.<ref name = march22injury>{{cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/all-or-nothing-documentary-reveals-freak-cause-of-knee-injury-that-blighted-kieran-tierneys-arsenal-season-vt0bmb8kc |title=All or Nothing documentary reveals freak cause of knee injury that blighted Kieran Tierney's Arsenal season |newspaper=[[The Times]] |first=Gary |last=Jacob |date=17 August 2022 |access-date=17 August 2022 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Arsenal lost league games against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton]], [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham]] and [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle]] following his injury, and they narrowly missed out on Champions League qualification.<ref name = march22injury/> It was later revealed in the ''[[All or Nothing: Arsenal]]'' series that Tierney had hyper-extended the knee during a game in February, but aggravated it a month later while walking in the Arsenal training ground.<ref name = march22injury/> He returned to action at the start of the 2022–23 season.<ref name = march22injury/>

Arsenal signed [[Oleksandr Zinchenko (footballer)|Oleksandr Zinchenko]] from Manchester City during the summer of 2022, and during the 2022–23 season the Ukrainian played most Premier League minutes at left back ahead of Tierney.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/arsenal-battle-kieran-tierney-unlikely-29226295 |title=The Arsenal battle Kieran Tierney is unlikely to win as Oleksandr Zinchenko stat comparison shows why Arteta prefers him |newspaper=Daily Record |first=Will |last=Lancaster |date=15 February 2023 |accessdate=2 February 2023}}</ref> This led to speculation that Tierney would look to leave Arsenal during the summer of 2023.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/sport/23353174.arsenals-mikel-arteta-quizzed-kieran-tierney-newcastle-transfer/ |title=Arsenal's Mikel Arteta quizzed on Kieran Tierney Newcastle transfer |newspaper=The Northern Echo |first=Dominic |last=Shaw |date=28 February 2023 |accessdate=2 March 2023}}</ref>

====2023–2024: Loan to Real Sociedad====
On 27 August 2023, Tierney joined [[La Liga]] club [[Real Sociedad]] on a season-long [[Loan (association football)|loan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realsociedad.eus/en/news/details/path-to-the-stars|title=Path to the stars|publisher=Real Sociedad|date=27 August 2023|access-date=27 August 2023}}</ref> He made his full debut in a 5–3 win over [[Granada CF|Granada]], for which he was labelled 'exquisite' by Real Sociedad boss [[Imanol Alguacil]].<ref>{{cite news |date=3 September 2023 |last=Walker |first=Mark |title='Exquisite' – Kieran Tierney handed rave review after stunning Real Sociedad debut |url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/23764128.kieran-tierney-labelled-exquisite-real-sociedad-debut/ |access-date=18 September 2023 |website=The National |language=en |url-access=subscription}}</ref> He followed this up with an impressive performance against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] on 17 September.<ref>{{cite news |last=Galindo |first=Alan |date=18 September 2023 |title=Kieran Tierney 'sparks' Real Sociedad goal at Real Madrid in number of key moments |url=https://www.glasgowlive.co.uk/sport/kieran-tierney-sparks-real-sociedad-27734339 |access-date=18 September 2023 |website=GlasgowLive |language=en}}</ref> His season was interrupted by two hamstring injuries, sustained in September and January.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/feb/14/kieran-tierney-i-was-up-against-mbappe-it-helps-you-in-the-long-run |title=Kieran Tierney: 'I was up against Mbappé … it helps you in the long run' |newspaper=The Guardian |date=14 February 2024 |accessdate=15 February 2024 |first=Sid |last=Lowe}}</ref>

====Return from loan====
Tierney returned to Arsenal over the summer after picking up a hamstring injury at [[UEFA Euro 2024|Euro 2024]]. He made his long-awaited return to training on 21 November 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/kieran-tierney-arsenal-fc-injury-update-training-b1195526.html|title=Forgotten Arsenal star confirms training return after injury nightmare|first=Matt|last=Verri|date=21 November 2024|website=The Standard}}</ref> On 20 April 2025, he made his 100th [[Premier League]] appearance for the club, in a 4–0 win over [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] at [[Portman Road]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tribuna.com/amp/en/news/2025-04-20-kieran-tierney-made-his-100th-premier-league-appearance-for-arsenal/|title=Kieran Tierney made his 100th Premier League appearance for Arsenal|website=tribuna.com |date=20 April 2025 }}</ref> On 25 May 2025, Tierney opened the scoring in a 2–1 win away to [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] in his final game for the club, having made a total of 144 appearances in all competitions, scoring 6 goals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/may/25/southampton-arsenal-premier-league-match-report|title=Ødegaard strikes late to earn Arsenal win at Southampton after Tierney's farewell goal|first=Ed|last=Aarons|date=25 May 2025|work=The Guardian}}</ref>

=== Return to Celtic ===
Tierney's former club, [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], confirmed in February 2025 that they had reached a pre-contract agreement for him to return to the club on a permanent basis in the summer of that year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13306877/celtic-transfer-kieran-tierney-signs-pre-contract-agreement-to-leave-arsenal-and-re-join-the-hoops-this-summer|title=Celtic transfer: Kieran Tierney signs pre-contract agreement to leave Arsenal and re-join the Hoops this summer|website=Sky Sports}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c15z988kpw2o.amp|title=Kieran Tierney: What player are Celtic getting six years after his exit?|date=11 February 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> His departure from Arsenal was announced in June 2025,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/contract-updates-20-players-depart-summer |title=Contract updates: 20 players to depart this summer |date=4 June 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=4 June 2025}}</ref> and he signed a five-year contract with Celtic later that month.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/clyzm439d28o |title=Kieran Tierney: Celtic defender agrees five-year deal on return from Arsenal|date=10 June 2025|accessdate=10 June 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 3 August, he made his second debut for the club in a 1–0 win against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in the league.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celtic began their Scottish Premiership season with a victory, but were far from convincing as they struggled to break down a resilient St Mirren |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c3dpe12k9z8t#Report |website=bbc.com |access-date=9 August 2025}}</ref> He scored the first goal of his second spell on 9 November; the second in Celtic's 4–0 win against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Celtic ease past Kilmarnock to narrow gap at summit|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c9wvxxpddxwt|first=George|last=O'Neill|website=BBC Sport|date=9 November 2025|access-date=16 March 2026}}</ref>  On 1 March 2026, Tierney scored Celtic's first goal against their [[Old Firm|arch rivals]] [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], as the ''Hoops'' came from 2–0 down to draw 2–2 in the Scottish Premiership game at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cr5lrgp4g18t|title=Celtic rescue dramatic draw at Rangers as both spill points in Hearts chase|first=Kheredine|last=Idessane|date=1 March 2026|access-date=1 March 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Kieran Tierney Scotland v Bolivia 6 June 2026-150 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Tierney playing for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] in 2026]]

Tierney played for Scotland at [[Scotland national football team|Scotland U18]] and [[Scotland national football team|Scotland U19]] levels.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=1848&playerID=141507&squadID=9|title=Kieran Tierney|work=scottishfa.co.uk|publisher=Scottish Football Association|access-date=3 October 2015|archive-date=4 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151004012558/http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=1848&playerID=141507&squadID=9|url-status=live}}</ref> He had also considered playing for the [[Ellan Vannin football team|Ellan Vannin team]] that represents the Isle of Man when the [[ConIFA]] World Cup competition was being held.<ref name="iom"/> Tierney received his first call-up to the senior [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] squad on 10 March 2016 for a friendly against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35770855|title=Scotland: Six new call-ups for Czech Republic and Denmark friendlies|date=10 March 2016|work=BBC Sport|access-date=10 March 2016|archive-date=10 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310175550/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35770855|url-status=live}}</ref> Tierney played for the first half of the match on 30 March, which Scotland won 1–0 at [[Hampden Park]]; he was replaced at the break by his Celtic teammate [[Charlie Mulgrew]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35923550 |title=Scotland 1–0 Denmark: McGinn and Tierney shine on debuts |first=Alasdair |last=Lamont |work=BBC Sport |date=30 March 2016 |access-date=6 April 2016 |archive-date=5 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160405045401/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35923550 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Due to his greater versatility compared to fellow left-back [[Andy Robertson]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45459420 |title=Andy Robertson & Kieran Tierney both must play – Gordon Strachan |work=BBC Sport |date=8 September 2018 |access-date=8 September 2018 |archive-date=9 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180909144947/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45459420 |url-status=live }}</ref> Tierney was deployed at [[right back]] in Scotland's matches against [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39302192 |title=Scotland 1–0 Slovenia |last=English |first=Tom |work=BBC Sport |date=26 March 2017 |access-date=9 August 2017 |archive-date=14 November 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191114095953/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39302192 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Lithuania national football team|Lithuania]] and [[Slovakia national football team|Slovakia]], and on the left of a three-man defence in the fixture at home to [[England national football team|England]] during [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group F|World Cup qualifiers]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2017/jun/11/scotland-england-five-talking-points-tierney-strachan-sterling-oxlade-chamberlain |title=Scotland 2–2 England |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=11 June 2017 |access-date=9 August 2017 |archive-date=9 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809041705/https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2017/jun/11/scotland-england-five-talking-points-tierney-strachan-sterling-oxlade-chamberlain |url-status=live }}</ref> Tierney was selected as Scotland captain for a friendly match against [[Netherlands national football team|the Netherlands]] in November 2017, where he played as a central defender in a 1–0 defeat.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41840573 |title=Scotland 0–1 Netherlands |work=BBC Sport |date=9 November 2017 |access-date=10 November 2017 |archive-date=9 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171109234209/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41840573 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In October 2018, Tierney scored a decisive [[own goal]] in a 2–1 loss to [[Israel national football team|Israel]] in a [[UEFA Nations League]] fixture.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/16977913.israel-2-scotland-1-kieran-tierney-own-goal-caps-a-miserable-night-for-alex-mcleishs-men-in-haifa/ |title=Israel 2 Scotland 1: Kieran Tierney own |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181012214541/https://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/16977913.israel-2-scotland-1-kieran-tierney-own-goal-caps-a-miserable-night-for-alex-mcleishs-men-in-haifa/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Speaking after the game, Robertson said that both he and Tierney were being played out of position in the 3–5–2 system adopted by [[Alex McLeish]] to accommodate both players.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45832123 |title=Andy Robertson: Kieran Tierney and I are 'both out of position' |work=BBC Sport |date=12 October 2018 |access-date=13 withdrew from the Scotland squad ahead of their [[UEFA Euro 2020]] qualifiers against Cyprus and Kazakhstan due to a hip injury.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/scotland/50389854|title=Scotland: Andy Robertson, Ryan Fraser and Scott McTominay 'genuinely injured' – Alex Dyer|date=12 November 2019|work=BBC Sport|access-date=12 November 2019|archive-date=12 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191112104223/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/scotland/50389854|url-status=live}}</ref> In October Sport}}</ref> It was later confirmed by Armstrong, Tierney and [[Ryan Christie]] that they had been playing video games in the same room.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Winton |first1=Richard |title=Euro 2020: How Call of Duty might have ended Scotland's dream |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57370130 |access-date=8 June 2021 |work=BBC Sport |date=6 June 2021}}</ref>

Tierney provided three assists in a 4–0 win against the [[Faroe Islands national football team|Faroe Islands]] on 31 March 2021, despite playing from a central defensive position.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56598023 |title=Kieran Tierney: Arsenal defender provides three assists in Scotland romp |website=BBC Sport |date=31 March 2021 |accessdate=1 April 2021}}</ref> He then played in two of Scotland's matches at the delayed [[UEFA Euro 2020]] finals in June 2021, as he missed the opening match with [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] due to injury.{{citation needed|date=October 2023}} Tierney scored his first goal for Scotland on 24 March 2022, in a friendly against [[Poland national football team|Poland]] at Hampden.<ref>{{Cite news |date=24 March 2022 |title=International friendly: Controversial late penalty denies Scotland win over Poland – reaction |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/60807549 |access-date=24 March 2022}}</ref> Soon afterwards he suffered a training ground injury that kept him out of action for the rest of the 2021–22 season.<ref name = march22injury/> This caused him to miss a World Cup playoff against [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]] in June, which Scotland lost 3–1.{{citation needed|date=October 2023}} Tierney appeared five times for Scotland during their successful [[UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying]] campaign, with the team winning all five of the matches he played and conceding only one goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/tierney-gets-scotland-selection-euro-2024?page=3|title=Tierney gets Scotland selection for Euro 2024|date=15 June 2024|access-date=15 June 2024|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

On 7 June 2024, Tierney was named in Scotland's squad for the [[UEFA Euro 2024]] finals in Germany.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/record-breaking-goalkeeper-gordon-out-scotland-euro-2024-squad-2024-06-07/|title=Record-breaking goalkeeper Gordon out of Scotland's Euro 2024 squad|date=7 June 2024|access-date=15 June 2024|website=Reuters}}</ref> A week later, he started the opening match of the tournament, playing 76 minutes before being substituted for [[Scott McKenna]], as Scotland lost 5–1 to hosts [[Germany national football team|Germany]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c844x4y3ee3t|title=Ruthless Germany humble 10-man Scotland in Euro 2024 opener|website=BBC Sport|access-date=15 June 2024}}</ref> Tierney was substituted with an injury in the 61st minute of the second group match against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] on 19 June. This injury made him unavailable for the final match against [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]], which they lost 1–0 to finish bottom of [[UEFA Euro 2024 Group A|Group A]] with one point from three matches.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/news/028e-1b2c127c5b92-e020507872a2-1000--scotland-1-1-switzerland-clarke-s-men-keep-group-a-hopes-/|title=Scotland 1–1 Switzerland: Clarke's men keep Group A hopes alive|access-date=24 June 2024|publisher=UEFA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/match/2036186--scotland-vs-hungary/lineups/|title=Scotland vs Hungary: Line-ups|access-date=24 June 2024|publisher=UEFA}}</ref> Tierney gained his [[Scotland Men's International Roll of Honour|50th cap]] in a 3–1 defeat to [[Iceland national football team|Iceland]] on 6 June 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/sport/national/25221940.scotland-goalkeeper-cieran-slicker-debut-forget-home-defeat-iceland/|title=Scotland goalkeeper Cieran Slicker has debut to forget in home defeat to Iceland|date=6 June 2025|website=Welwyn Hatfield Times}}</ref> On 18 November 2025, he scored a stoppage-time goal in a 4–2 victory over Denmark in the last match of [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group C|Group C]], securing his nation's place in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] for the first time since 1998.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/47011300/scotland-vs-denmark-football-live-follow-world-cup-qualifier-winner-takes-all-hampden-park |title=Scotland vs Denmark as it happened: Scotland reach first World Cup in 28 years with 4-2 win |publisher=ESPN |date=18 November 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/kieran-tierney-very-special-scotland-world-cup-b2868202.html|title=Kieran Tierney revels in 'very special' night after firing Scotland to the World Cup|date=19 November 2025|website=The Independent}}</ref>

On 19 May 2026, Tierney was selected in the 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/scotland-squad-announced-steve-clarke|title=Veteran Gordon and youngster Curtis named in Scotland squad|date=19 May 2026|access-date=13 June 2026|language=en}}</ref> He made his World Cup debut on 19 June 2026, starting in a group stage match against [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/17/285023/289273/400021454 |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=www.fifa.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Tierney became an ambassador for the [[Scottish Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals]] (SSPCA) in June 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/in-your-area/lanarkshire/ex-celtic-star-kieran-tierney-24429176 |title=Ex-Celtic star Kieran Tierney new ambassador for SSPCA |newspaper=Daily Record |first=Leona |last=Greenan |date=30 June 2021 |accessdate=18 October 2022}}</ref>
