Godfrey has represented England from youth to [[England national football team|senior]] level, debuting for the latter in June 2021. ==Early and personal life== Benjamin Matthew Godfrey{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/60426 |title=Retained and released lists submitted by Premier League clubs |publisher=Premier League |date=10 June 2016 |access-date=17 January 2018}} was born on 15 January 1998{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/player/_/id/212953/ben-godfrey |title=Ben Godfrey: Overview |publisher=ESPN |access-date=15 October 2020}} in [[York]], North Yorkshire, England.{{cite web |url=https://www.11v11.com/players/ben-godfrey-242880/ |title=Ben Godfrey |website=11v11.com |publisher=AFS Enterprises |access-date=15 October 2020}} When young, he attended [[Archbishop Holgate's School]]. His father, Alex Godfrey, is a retired professional [[rugby league]] footballer. Godfrey is of [[Jamaicans|Jamaican]] descent through his paternal grandfather.{{Cite news |url=https://www.yorkpress.co.uk/news/7891002.caribbean-call/ |title=Caribbean call |newspaper=The Press |location=York |date=6 March 2004 |access-date=6 January 2025}} ==Club career== ===Early career=== [[File:Ben Godfrey 15-08-2015 1.jpg|thumb|upright|Godfrey warming up for [[York City F.C.|York City]] in 2015]] Godfrey [[Captain (association football)|captained]] the York & District under-13 team that beat Southampton at [[Stadium MK]] in the final of the English Schools' FA Inter-Association Trophy in May 2011.{{cite news |url=http://www.yorkpress.co.uk/news/9044617.York_and_District_U13s_carve_out_niche_in_city_s_football_folklore/ |title=York and District U13s carve out niche in city's football folklore |first=Dave |last=Flett |newspaper=The Press |location=York |date=24 May 2011 |access-date=15 January 2016}} This was the first time a team from York had won an English Schools' FA competition. He started his career with [[York City F.C.|York City]]'s youth system, before moving to [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]]'s [[Middlesbrough F.C. Under-21s and Academy|academy]] in the summer of 2011.{{cite news |url=http://www.yorkpress.co.uk/sport/14042187.West_Brom__Hull_City_and_Cardiff_City_running_the_rule_over_York_City_starlet_Ben_Godfrey/ |title=West Brom, Hull City and Cardiff City running the rule over York City starlet Ben Godfrey |first=Dave |last=Flett |newspaper=The Press |location=York |date=19 November 2015 |access-date=15 January 2016}} After being released by the club, he had trials with [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] and [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]], before returning to York at under-15 level, with whom he started his scholarship.{{cite web |url=http://www.yorkcityfootballclub.co.uk/team/youth-team/ |title=York City FC youth team profiles |publisher=York City F.C. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140826114345/http://www.yorkcityfootballclub.co.uk/team/youth-team/ |archive-date=26 August 2014}} Godfrey captained York's under-18 team in the [[2014–15 York City F.C. season|2014–15 season]],{{cite news |url=http://www.yorkpress.co.uk/sport/11604727.York_City_academy_pass_with_flying_colours/ |title=York City academy pass with flying colours |newspaper=The Press |location=York |date=15 November 2014 |access-date=18 August 2015}} while still a first-year scholar.{{cite news |url=http://www.yorkpress.co.uk/sport/11871993.York_City_boss_Russ_Wilcox_believes_calls_for_his_sacking_are_unhelpful/ |title=York City boss Russ Wilcox believes calls for his sacking are unhelpful |first=Dave |last=Flett |newspaper=The Press |location=York |date=21 March 2015 |access-date=18 August 2015}} His first involvement with the first team came as an unused [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in a [[EFL League Two|League Two]] match against [[Newport County A.F.C.|Newport County]] on 11 October 2014. Godfrey made his debut aged 17 when starting York's 1–0 home win over [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]] on 18 August 2015. He scored his first goal for York in the eighth minute of stoppage time in a 2–1 home loss to [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]] on 14 November 2015 with a shot from 10 yards.{{cite news |url=http://www.yorkpress.co.uk/sport/14032341.York_City_suffer_fifth_straight_defeat_against_table_topping_Plymouth/ |title=York City suffer fifth straight defeat against table-topping Plymouth |first=Dave |last=Flett |newspaper=The Press |location=York |date=14 November 2015 |access-date=11 September 2016}} ===Norwich City=== [[File:Ben Godfrey 2019-05-06 1.jpg|thumb|upright|Godfrey with [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] in 2019]] Godfrey signed for [[Premier League]] club [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] on 15 January 2016 on a three-and-a-half-year contract for an undisclosed fee and would initially play in their academy team.{{cite web |url=https://www.canaries.co.uk/News/2016/january/canaries-sign-yorks-ben-godfrey/ |title=Canaries sign York's Ben Godfrey |publisher=Norwich City F.C. |date=15 January 2016 |access-date=17 January 2018}} He made his debut on 23 August as a substitute in the 65th minute of Norwich's [[EFL Cup]] second round match against [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] and scored in the 87th minute of a 6–1 home win with a shot from outside the [[penalty area]].{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37091247 |title=Norwich City 6–1 Coventry City |website=BBC Sport |date=23 August 2016 |access-date=11 September 2016}} Godfrey made his league debut in a 2–0 home win over [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] on 28 January 2017 as an 81st-minute substitute. He signed a new four-year contract with Norwich on 11 August 2017, keeping him at the club until the summer of 2021.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40903792 |title=Alex Pritchard: Norwich City midfielder out for at least 12 weeks after ankle surgery |website=BBC Sport |date=11 August 2017 |access-date=24 August 2017}} On 24 August 2017, Godfrey joined [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]] on [[Loan (association football)|loan]] until 1 January 2018.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41037247 |title=Ben Godfrey: Shrewsbury Town sign Norwich City midfielder on loan until January |website=BBC Sport |date=24 August 2017 |access-date=24 August 2017}} The deal was later extended to the end of the season.{{cite web |url=https://www.canaries.co.uk/News/2017/december/godfrey-extension/ |title=Ben Godfrey's Shrewsbury loan extended |publisher=Norwich City F.C. |date=27 December 2017 |access-date=15 October 2020}} For the [[2018–19 Norwich City F.C. season|2018–19 season]], Godfrey returned to Norwich. He played in their four EFL Cup games but his appearances in the league were limited to substitute appearances until December: With centre-backs [[Grant Hanley]] and [[Timm Klose]] both injured, Godfrey made his first league start for Norwich in the [[EFL Championship|Championship]] match against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]], partnering [[Christoph Zimmermann]] at centre half in a 3–2 win.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46408816 |title=Norwich City 3–2 Bolton Wanderers |website=BBC Sport |date=8 December 2018 |access-date=11 November 2020}} He remained in the side even when Hanley was fit again and scored his first goal for Norwich at the end of the year to give them an early lead against [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]], although a late comeback from Derby saw Norwich lose the game 4–3.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46656340 |title=Norwich City 3–4 Derby County |website=BBC Sport |date=29 December 2018 |access-date=11 November 2020}} This was only a temporary setback for both Godfrey and Norwich however. Godfrey would score three more goals, all of which would earn Norwich points as they chased promotion back to the Premier League. This was achieved in the penultimate game, a 2–1 win over [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]], with Godfrey in the team.{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/norwich-vs-blackburn/393077 |title=Norwich 2–1 Blackburn - Match Report & Highlights |website=Sky Sports |date=27 April 2019 |access-date=11 November 2020}} In all, Godfrey played 31 league games during the season, starting 26 of them. Godfrey made his first Premier League appearance in the opening game of the [[2019–20 Norwich City F.C. season|2019–20 season]], a 4–1 defeat against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], playing alongside Hanley.{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/liverpool-vs-norwich/407981 |title=Liverpool 4–1 Norwich - Match Report & Highlights |website=Sky Sports |date=10 August 2019 |access-date=11 November 2020}} There were again a number of injuries to centre halves throughout the season, to the point that Godfrey was the only fit regular centre back at one point, and even captained the side with Hanley, [[Alexander Tettey]], Klose and Zimmermann all out injured.{{cite news |url=https://www.vavel.com/en/football/2019/10/06/norwich-city/999058-ben-godfrey-a-captains-performance-to-forget.html |title=Ben Godfrey: A captain's performance to forget |website=Vavel |date=6 October 2019 |access-date=11 November 2020}} After prominent performances by winning two of their first five games, Norwich were soon demoted to the bottom of the table. When they did record a rare win against fellow strugglers [[AFC Bournemouth]], Godfrey was sent off in the second half for a late challenge on fellow Englishman [[Callum Wilson]], having the unfortunate distinction of being the first Premier League player to be dismissed as a result of a referee consulting a [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] monitor.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51073182 |title=Norwich City 1–0 Bournemouth |website=BBC Sport |date=18 January 2020 |access-date=11 November 2020}} Godfrey again made 30 league appearances for Norwich but, in a season disrupted by a three-month suspension during the [[COVID-19 pandemic|2020 COVID-19 pandemic]], the club were relegated back to the Championship. Godfrey would play in Norwich's first three games in the [[2020–21 Norwich City F.C. season|2020–21 season]], making his last appearance for the club in a 1–0 defeat against Bournemouth. ===Everton=== On 5 October 2020, Godfrey signed for Premier League club [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] on a five-year contract for an undisclosed fee,{{cite web |url=https://www.evertonfc.com/news/1856420/everton-seal-godfrey-signing |title=Everton seal Godfrey signing |publisher=Everton F.C. |date=5 October 2020 |access-date=15 October 2020}} reported by ''[[The Athletic]]'' to be an initial £20 million, potentially rising to £25 million in add-ons.{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4234939/2020/10/01/everton-complete-ben-godfrey-transfer-from-norwich/ |title=Everton complete Ben Godfrey transfer from Norwich |website=The Athletic |date=5 October 2020 |access-date=15 October 2020}} He made his debut on 17 October in a [[Merseyside derby]] against local rivals Liverpool in a 2–2 draw at home in the Premier League, coming on as a 31st-minute substitute after an injury to right-back and captain [[Séamus Coleman]].{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54489179 |title=Everton 2–2 Liverpool |first=Phil |last=McNulty |website=BBC Sport |date=17 October 2020 |access-date=17 October 2020}}
{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/everton-godfrey-debut-coleman-injury-19121216 |title=Everton signing Ben Godfrey handed debut against Liverpool after Seamus Coleman injury blow |first=Matt |last=Addison |newspaper=Liverpool Echo |date=17 October 2020 |access-date=17 October 2020}} Adam Jones of the ''[[Liverpool Echo]]'' said that Godfrey "was thrown into the deep end for his debut and stood up to the task very well".{{cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/everton-players-ratings-against-liverpool-19121557 |title=Everton player ratings vs Liverpool as Jordan Pickford stands out in dramatic derby |first=Adam |last=Jones |newspaper=Liverpool Echo |date=17 October 2020 |access-date=17 October 2020}} At the end of his first season at the club, Godfrey was voted by Everton fans as the club's Young Player of the Season.{{Cite web |url=https://www.evertonfc.com/news/2152789/everton-202021-football-award-winners-revealed |title=Everton 2020/21 Football Award Winners Revealed |publisher=Everton F.C. |date=21 May 2021 |access-date=2 June 2021}} ===Atalanta and loans out=== On 28 June 2024, Godfrey moved to Italy, signing for [[Serie A]] club [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] for an undisclosed fee{{Cite web |title=Defender Benjamin Godfrey joins Atalanta! – Atalanta |date=28 June 2024 |url=https://www.atalanta.it/en/news/defender-benjamin-godfrey-joins-atalanta/ |access-date=28 June 2024 |language=en-US}} reported to be in the region of £11 million with a sell-on clause.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cv2g5n5edmpo|title=Atalanta sign Godfrey in £10m deal from Everton|date=27 June 2024 |publisher=BBC Sport|accessdate=28 June 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://talksport.com/football/1939203/everton-ben-godfrey-atalanta-transfer-bid/|title=Ben Godfrey to join Champions League side as Everton agree to sell defender in £10million deal|date=27 June 2024 |publisher=Talksport|accessdate=28 June 2024}}{{cite web|url= https://twitter.com/joe_thomas18/status/1806775428813651970 |title= Final deal believed to have been for around £11m, plus add-ons and a sell-on clause.|publisher=Joe Thomas of LiverpoolEcho|accessdate=28 June 2024}} On 5 January 2025, having made just five appearances since joining Atalanta, Godfrey returned to the Premier League, joining [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] on loan for the remainder of the [[2024–25 Ipswich Town F.C. season|2024–25 season]].{{cite web |url=https://www.itfc.co.uk/news/2025/january/05/town-sign-ben-godfrey-on-loan/ |title=Ben Godfrey joins Town |first=Andy |last=Warren |publisher=Ipswich Town F.C. |date=5 January 2025 |access-date=5 January 2025}} He made his debut a week later when starting in Ipswich's 3–0 home win over [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]] in the [[2024–25 FA Cup third round]]. On 22 August 2025, Godfrey joined [[EFL Championship]] club [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] on loan for the [[2025–26 Sheffield United F.C. season|2025–26 season]].{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cx2x1y8p7p1o |title=Sheff Utd sign Atalanta defender Godfrey on loan |first=David |last=Anderson |website=BBC Sport |date=22 August 2025 |access-date=22 August 2025}} He made his debut the following day in United's 1–0 home defeat to [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]]. On 19 December, it was announced that Sheffield United had terminated Godfrey's loan contract early, sending him back to Atalanta effectively.{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Jack |date=19 December for the first time for their [[2021 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification]] matches against [[Turkey national under-21 football team|Turkey]] and [[Kosovo national under-21 football team|Kosovo]] in September 2019.{{cite web |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2019/aug/30/england-u21s-squad-named-for-turkey-and-kosovo-300819 |title=England U21s kick-off a new campaign and Aidy opening Euro qualifier |publisher=The Football Association |date=6 September 2019 |access-date=15 October 2020}} He started the following match as captain, as England beat Kosovo 2–0 at home on 9 September.{{cite web |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2019/sep/09/england-u21s-kosovo-report-090919 |title=Phil Foden's double helps Young Lions to U21 Euro qualifying victory over Kosovo |first=Nicholas |last=Veevers |publisher=The Football Association |date=9 September 2019 |access-date=15 October 2020}}
{{cite web |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2019/nov/15/ben-godfrey-england-u21s-interview-151119 |title=Ben Godfrey assesses his journey from York City to Norwich City and England captaincy |first=Nicholas |last=Veevers |publisher=The Football Association |date=15 November 2019 |access-date=15 October 2020}} Godfrey scored his first international goal on 8 September 2020 in a 2–1 away win against [[Austria national under-21 football team|Austria]] in 2021 European Under-21 Championship qualification with a sliding finish after a well-timed run.{{cite web |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2020/sep/08/england-mu21s-austria-report-080920 |title=Eddie Nketiah and Ben Godfrey steer England MU21s to crucial victory |publisher=The Football Association |date=8 September 2020 |access-date=15 October 2020}} He was in England's squad for the [[2021 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2021 European Under-21 Championship]] and played in their first two matches in the group stage before missing the third and final match through injury.{{cite web |url=http://www.englandfootballonline.com/MatchRsl/MatchRslTmU21pg5.html |title=Match Results Under 21: 2020–30 |website=England Football Online |date=19 November 2024 |access-date=5 January 2025}} England were eliminated from the tournament after finishing bottom of a four-team group. Godfrey finished his under-21 career with nine appearances and one goal from 2019 to 2021.{{cite web |url=http://www.englandfootballonline.com/MatchRsl/MatchRslTmU21pg4.html |title=Match Results Under 21: 2010–20 |website=England Football Online |date=1 September 2024 |access-date=5 January 2025}}
{{cite web |url=http://www.englandfootballonline.com/MatchRsl/MatchRslTmU21pg5.html |title=Match Results Under 21: 2020–30 |website=England Football Online |date=19 November 2024 |access-date=5 news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57239842 |title=England name provisional Euro 2020 squad: Ben White, Ben Godfrey, Aaron Ramsdale and Sam Johnstone in |website=BBC Sport |date=25 May 2021 |access-date=25 May 2021}} He was not named in the final 26-man squad, with Southgate stating that Godfrey was part of the provisional squad "in order to gain experience",{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57321188 |title=Euro 2020: Trent Alexander-Arnold named in England's 26-man squad |website=BBC Sport |date=1 June 2021 |access-date=2 June 2021}} and remained |date=2 June 2021 |access-date=2 June 2021}} and made his first start four days later, playing the entirety of a 1–0 win over Romania.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57297066 '''Cameron Robert Carter-Vickers''' (born December 31, 1997) is a professional [[Football player|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|center-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]. Born in England, he represents the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States national team]].

Carter-Vickers began his career at the [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C. Reserves and Academy|Tottenham Hotspur Academy]]. He made his debut in the [[2016–17 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2016–17]] season, playing in cup competitions. From 2017 to 2021 he spent time out on loan at [[EFL Championship|Championship]] clubs [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]], [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]], [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]], [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]], [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]], and [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]].

In 2021, he went on loan to Celtic in the [[Scottish Premiership]], before signing permanently in 2022. He has won the Scottish Premiership four times, the [[Scottish League Cup]] three times, and the [[Scottish Cup]] twice. He was included three times on the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year]].

Carter-Vickers has gained 19 caps for the United States and represented his country at the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] and the [[2024 Copa America]].

|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51309426 |access-date=January 30, 2020 |archive-date=January 30, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200130111721/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51309426 |url-status=live }}</ref> Due to the season being extended by the [[COVID-19]] outbreak, Carter-Vickers' loan to Luton was extended till the end of the campaign.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2020/july/cameron-extends-luton-stay/ |title=Cameron extends Luton stay |work=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=July 3, 2020 |access-date=July 5, 2020 |archive-date=July 5, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200705131844/https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2020/july/cameron-extends-luton-stay/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Carter-Vickers joined Championship side [[AFC Bournemouth]] on a season-long loan on October 16, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.afcb.co.uk/news/club-news/carter-vickers-joins-on-loan|title=Carter-Vickers joins on loan|work=[[AFC Bournemouth]]|date=October 16, 2020|access-date=October 16, 2020|archive-date=October 16, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201016191020/https://www.afcb.co.uk/news/club-news/carter-vickers-joins-on-loan/|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Bournemouth in a 2–1 win at [[Bristol City]] on March 3, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56178056 |title=Bristol City 1-2 Bournemouth |date=March 3, 2021 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=March 4, 2021 |archive-date=March 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303214121/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56178056 |url-status=live }}</ref>

====Return to Tottenham====
On August 19, 2021, Carter-Vickers received his first Tottenham appearance since 2017, starting under new manager [[Nuno Espírito Santo]] in the club's first-ever [[UEFA Europa Conference League]] match, a 1–0 loss away at [[F.C. Paços de Ferreira|Paços de Ferreira]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pacos de Ferreira 1-0 Tottenham Hotspur: Spurs lose Europa Conference League play-off first leg - BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58257076|date=August 19, 2021|access-date=August 19, 2021|website=BBC Sportn|archive-date=August 18, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210818224308/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58257076|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Celtic ===
On August 31, 2021, Carter-Vickers joined [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on loan until the end of the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Celtic loan for Carter-Vickers|url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2021/august/celtic-loan-for-carter-vickers/|access-date=September 10, 2021|website=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|archive-date=September 1, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210901081801/https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2021/august/celtic-loan-for-carter-vickers/|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored on his debut with a deflected strike from outside the box in a 3–0 victory over [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on September 13.<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=Pitchside view: Cameron Carter Vickers' debut goal for Celtic|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/onefootball/video/2021/09/13/pitchside-view-cameron-carter-vickers-debut-goal-for-celtic|magazine=Sports Illustrated|access-date=October 28, 2021|archive-date=October 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028051857/https://www.si.com/soccer/onefootball/video/2021/09/13/pitchside-view-cameron-carter-vickers-debut-goal-for-celtic|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Celtit Rangers and go six clear |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60890355 }}</ref>

He played 45 games in all competitions as the team won the [[2021–22 Scottish League Cup|Scottish League Cup]] and the Premiership, with Celtic holding the best defensive record in the latter.<ref name="celtic">{{cite news |title=Cameron Carter-Vickers: Celtic complete permanent signing of Tottenham Hotspur centre-half |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61766138 |access-date=June 10, 2022 |work=BBC Sport |date=June 10, 2022 |archive-date=June 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220610174811/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61766138 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2021-2022 Celtic Stats, Scottish Premiership |url=https://fbref.com/en/squads/b81aa4fa/2021-2022/Celtic-Stats |access-date=2022-12-31 |website=FBref.com |language=en |archive-date=December 31, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221231202220/https://fbref.com/en/squads/b81aa4fa/2021-2022/Celtic-Stats |url-status=live }}</ref>

On June 10, 2022, Carter-Vickers signed with Celtic permanently, subsequently leaving Tottenham. The deal was effective from July 1. The transfer was on a four-year deal for an undisclosed fee, reported to be around £6 million.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://www.msn.com/en-gb/sport/football/cameron-carter-vicker-celtic-complete-permanent-transfer-fee-length-of-contract-what-player-and-coach-had-to-say/ar-AAYjR7O |title=Cameron Carter-Vickers: Celtic complete permanent transfer - fee, length of contract, what player and coach had to say |first=Mark |last=Atkinson |website=msn.com |date=June 10, 2022 |accessdate=June 10, 2022 |archive-date=June 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220610190622/https://www.msn.com/en-gb/sport/football/cameron-carter-vicker-celtic-complete-permanent-transfer-fee-length-of-contract-what-player-and-coach-had-to-say/ar-AAYjR7O |url-status=live }}</ref>

On January 26, 2024, Carter-Vickers signed a five-and-a-half-year contract with Celtic, keeping him with the club until 2029.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2024/january/26/cameron-carter-vickers-commits-his-future-to-celtic/|title=Cameron Carter-Vickers commits his future to Celtic |date=January 26, 2024 |publisher=Celtic F.C. |access-date=26 January 2024}}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth===
In the summer of 2014, Carter-Vickers was playing for Tottenham's academy side at the IMG Cup in [[Bradenton, Florida]], where they beat the [[United States men's national under-17 soccer team|United States under-17 team]] 5–3. During the game, he caught the eye of American coaches who had learned of his eligibility for a [[United States passport]], as his father is an American citizen.<ref name="ussoccer.com"/><ref name="americansoccernow.com">{{cite web|url=http://americansoccernow.com/articles/cameron-carter-vickers-i-am-leaning-to-the-usa|title=ASN article: Cameron Carter-Vickers: "I Am Leaning to the USA"|last=Sciaretta|first=Brian|date=October 21, 2014|publisher=American Soccer Now|access-date=February 7, 2016|archive-date=March 7, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307180804/http://americansoccernow.com/articles/cameron-carter-vickers-i-am-leaning-to-the-usa|url-status=live}}</ref>

Carter-Vickers represented the United States for the first time at [[United States men's national under-18 soccer team|under-18 level]] in August 2014 and by October of that year was a member of the [[United States men's national under-23 soccer team|United States under-23 team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2014/08/13/16/40/140813-u18-czech-roster|title=U.S. U-18 MNT Roster Named For Czech Republic Tournament|access-date=December 10, 2015|archive-date=November 8, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012756/https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2014/08/13/16/40/140813-u18-czech-roster|url-status=live}}</ref> He represented the [[United States men's national under-20 soccer team|United States]] at the [[2015 FIFA U-20 World Cup]] and started several games despite being only 17 at the time. The team were knocked out by [[Serbia national under-20 football team|Serbia]] in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2014/10/13/20/51/141013-u23mnt-brazil-vs-usa|title=U-23 MNT Falls 3–0 to Brazil|date=October 13, 2014|publisher=U.S. Soccer|access-date=March 31, 2018|archive-date=October 17, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017162601/https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2014/10/13/20/51/141013-u23mnt-brazil-vs-usa|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2015/11/09/22/44/151109-u23mnt-herzog-calls-19-players-to-brazil-as-roadtorio-continues|title=Herzog Calls 19 Players to Brazil as #RoadToRio Continues|work=ussoccer.com|access-date=November 10, 2015|archive-date=November 14, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151114172907/http://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2015/11/09/22/44/151109-u23mnt-herzog-calls-19-players-to-brazil-as-roadtorio-continues|url-status=live}}</ref>

In September 2016, it was reported that the English FA had made inquiries about Carter-Vickers and that the United States were prepared to fast track the player into their senior set up.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/england-eye-tottenhams-cameron-carter-8894904|title=England vs USA battle looming over Spurs starlet Carter-Vickers|first=John|last=Cross|date=September 22, 2016|newspaper=Daily Mirror|access-date=December 16, 2017|archive-date=December 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171203143443/http://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/england-eye-tottenhams-cameron-carter-8894904|url-status=live}}</ref> On October 10, 2016, Carter-Vickers captained the United States under-20 team in a 2–0 loss against [[England national under-20 football team|England]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2016/oct/10/england-u20s-2-0-usa-report-101016|title=England Under-20s win three in three at Four Nations Tournament after 2–0 victory over USA|access-date=November 7, 2016|archive-date=November 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107160624/http://www.thefa.com/news/2016/oct/10/england-u20s-2-0-usa-report-101016|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Senior===
On November 6, 2016, Carter-Vickers received his first call up to the [[United States men's national soccer team|senior United States squad]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/cameron-carter-vickers-senior-usa-call-up-061116/ |title=Carter-Vickers gets first senior USA international call-up |date=November 6, 2016 |publisher=tottenhamhotspur.com |access-date=November 7, 2016 |archive-date=January 1, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180101155342/http://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/cameron-carter-vickers-senior-usa-call-up-061116/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He made his senior debut appearance on November 14, 2017, in a friendly as a half-time [[Substitution (association football)|substitute]] in a 1–1 draw away to [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/portugal-vs-usa/teams/385532 |title=Portugal 1 – 1 United States of America |date=November 14, 2017 |publisher=Sky Sports |access-date=November 17, 2017 |archive-date=November 18, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171118102651/http://www.skysports.com/football/portugal-vs-usa/teams/385532 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In May 2022, coach [[Gregg Berhalter]] recalled Carter-Vickers after nearly three years without a cap.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Galindo |first1=Alan |title=Celtic loan star Cameron Carter-Vickers land USA recall after 'outstanding' season |url=https://www.glasgowlive.co.uk/sport/celtic-loan-star-cameron-carter-24023513 |access-date=November 29, 2022 |work=Glasgow Live |date=May 21, 2022 |archive-date=November 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221129144857/https://www.glasgowlive.co.uk/sport/celtic-loan-star-cameron-carter-24023513 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was called up for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] in November<ref>{{cite news |title=Carter-Vickers makes USA World Cup squad, Rangers pair miss out |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c28w8dmp2epo |access-date=November 29, 2022 |work=BBC Sport |date=November 10, 2022 |archive-date=November 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221129144857/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c28w8dmp2epo |url-status=live }}</ref> and made his World Cup debut on November 29 against [[Iran national football team|Iran]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2022/11/29/usmnt-starting-xi-lineup-vs-iran-josh-sargent-cameron-carter-vickers-walker-zimmerman |title=USMNT Starting XI: Sargent Returns, Carter-Vickers In vs. Iran |last=Koons |first=Zach |date=2022-11-29 |website=www.si.com |publisher=Sports Illustrated |access-date=2022-11-30 |quote=Wright. On the opposite end of the pitch, Cameron Carter-Vickers will see his first-ever World Cup action at centerback in place of veteran Walker Zimmerman. |df=mdy-all |archive-date=December 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201043526/https://www.si.com/soccer/2022/11/29/usmnt-starting-xi-lineup-vs-iran-josh-sargent-cameron-carter-vickers-walker-zimmerman |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Style of play==
Carter-Vickers is known as a ball-playing [[center-back]] with accurate passing ability.<ref name="Swansea City"/> He is primarily known for his athleticism and strength, and are often utilized as some of his best qualities when defending. His former Celtic teammate [[Carl Starfelt]] spoke about Carter-Vickers, stating, "Cameron is the strongest in the team — but he is never in the gym...
I think he's just super-strong genetically as he is never in the gym."<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/23359436.anp/ | title=Carl Starfelt names strongest Celtic player who 'never' hits gym |work=Glasgow Times | date=March 2, 2023 | last=Macdonald | first=Aidan | access-date=March 11, 2023 | archive-date=March 11, 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230311190325/https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/23359436.amp/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Carter-Vickers' father is [[Howard Carter (basketball)|Howard Carter]], a retired American [[basketball]] player who spent his professional career in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] and Europe and became a French citizen.<ref name=rising>{{cite news |last1=Sferra |first1=German |title=Rising: Cameron Carter-Vickers |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2018/07/rising-cameron-cartervickers |access-date=November 28, 2019 |publisher=US Soccer |date=July 16, 2018 |archive-date=November 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191128003749/https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2018/07/rising-cameron-cartervickers |url-status=live }}</ref> His English mother, Geraldine Vickers, is from [[Essex]]. Carter and Vickers met while both were working in Greece.<ref name=rising/> He was raised in Essex and attended [[The Eastwood Academy]] in [[Leigh-on-Sea]], while spending summers with his father in [[Louisiana]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/the-rise-of-american-soccer-talent-cameron-carter-vickers/|title=The Rise of American Soccer Talent Cameron Carter-Vickers|work=VICE Sports|date=June 13, 2015 |access-date=November 16, 2015|archive-date=November 17, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117033319/https://sports.vice.com/en_us/article/the-rise-of-american-soccer-talent-cameron-carter-vickers|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.echo-news.co.uk/sport/other/15016937.School_proud_of_star_pupil_s_progress_with_Premier_League_club/ |title=Eastwood Academy proud of former pupil Cameron Carter-Vickers who now plays for Tottenham Hotspur |date=January 11, 2017 |website=echo-news.co.uk |access-date=February 4, 2017 |archive-date=August 25, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825234834/http://www.echo-news.co.uk/sport/other/15016937.School_proud_of_star_pupil_s_progress_with_Premier_League_club/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="ussoccer.com"/>

'''Auston Levi-Jesaiah Trusty''' (born August 12, 1998) is an American professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[center-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States national team]].

In club soccer, Trusty played in the [[USL Championship]] for [[Philadelphia Union II|Bethlehem Steel]] and in [[Major League Soccer]] for the [[Philadelphia Union]] and the [[Colorado Rapids]] before signing for [[Premier League]] club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], and spent the 2022–23 season [[loan (association football)|on loan]] to [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] of the [[EFL Championship]]. In August 2023, Trusty signed for [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]], for which he made his Premier League debut. He moved on to Celtic in 2024. Internationally, he represented his country at under-age levels before making his senior debut in March 2023. He represented his country at the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].

==Early life==
Trusty was born in [[Media, Pennsylvania]]. He is the youngest of six children.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.delcotimes.com/2018/10/14/for-unions-trusty-lineage-has-always-been-a-guide-to-follow/|title=For Union's Trusty, lineage has always been a guide to follow|last=De George|first=Matt|date=October 14, 2018|work=Delaware County Daily Times|access-date=April 7, 2025}}</ref> All of his siblings played collegiate soccer. His sister, Onnie Nicholson, also played internationally.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/i-fell-in-love-with-soccer-watching-her---meet-auston-trusty-the-mls-star-inspired-by-his-former-uswnt-sister/fqpr0na1ef4m1ssasrqwtjf3p|title='I fell in love with soccer watching her' – Meet Auston Trusty, the MLS star inspired by his ex-USWNT sister|last=Ruszkai|first=Ameé|date=October 7, 2019|work=Goal|access-date=April 7, 2025}}</ref>

He began playing soccer with Nether United Soccer Club in [[Wallingford, Pennsylvania|Wallingford]].<ref name="bro1">{{cite news |last1=Abraham |first1=Jonathan |title=MLS players and coaches with ties to Philadelphia |url=https://www.brotherlygame.com/2020/2/28/21156697/mls-players-coaches-ties-to-philadelphia |access-date=May 29, 2021 |work=BrotherlyGame |date=February 28, 2020}}</ref> He attended and played for [[Penncrest High School]] before joining the SockerClub youth setup of the [[Philadelphia Union]] in 2011.<ref name="del1">{{cite news |last1=DeGeorge |first1=Matthew |title=Trusty's ascension reaches World Cup |url=https://www.delcotimes.com/sports/trusty-s-ascension-reaches-world-cup/article_71f90712-1f1c-5a69-95f8-fff8d2071200.html |access-date=May 29, 2021 |work=[[Delaware County Daily Times]] |date=October 19, 2015 |archive-date=June 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210603132250/https://www.delcotimes.com/sports/trusty-s-ascension-reaches-world-cup/article_71f90712-1f1c-5a69-95f8-fff8d2071200.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Club career==
===Bethlehem Steel===
In 2016, Trusty signed an amateur United Soccer League contract with the [[Philadelphia Union]] reserve affiliate [[Philadelphia Union II|Bethlehem Steel]].<ref name="mca1">{{cite news |last1=Shoemaker |first1=Tim |title=Teenager Auston Trusty plays beyond his years for Bethlehem Steel FC |url=https://www.mcall.com/sports/mc-bethlehem-steel-soccer-advance-20160712-story.html |access-date=May 29, 2021 |work=[[The Morning Call]] |date=July 12, 2016}}</ref> The contract with the Steel allowed Trusty to remain eligible to play [[College soccer in the United States|college soccer]] with the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's soccer|North Carolina Tar Heels]].<ref name="mca1"/> He made his debut for the Steel on April 10, 2016, against [[New York Red Bulls II]], starting in the 4–0 defeat.<ref>{{cite web |title=New York Red Bulls II 4–0 Bethlehem Steel |url=https://us.soccerway.com/matches/2016/04/11/united-states/mls-reserve-league/new-york-rb-ii/bethlehem-steel/2196854/ |website=Soccerway|access-date=May 5, 2026}}</ref>

Trusty would go on to play 44 games for the Bethlehem Steel within two seasons.<ref name="soccerway"/>

===Philadelphia Union===
[[File:Dsc 5720 29430463257 o (50120746293) (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|200px|Trusty with the [[Philadelphia Union]] in 2018.]]

On August 10, 2016, Trusty signed a [[Homegrown Player Rule (Major League Soccer)|homegrown player]] deal with the [[Philadelphia Union]], electing not to join the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's soccer|Tar Heels]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Dream comes true for Media native, Union Homegrown Auston Trusty |url=https://www.delcotimes.com/sports/dream-comes-true-for-media-native-union-homegrown-auston-trusty/article_fa4f4adf-242f-5718-8880-02501610b585.html |access-date=May 30, 2021 |work=[[Delaware County Daily Times]] |date=August 10, 2016}}</ref> Despite his signing, Trusty did not make his debut for the Union until March 3, 2018, in the club's season opener against the [[New England Revolution]].<ref name="bro2">{{cite news |last1=Ralph |first1=Matthew |title=Philly MLS 25: Auston Trusty's 2018 season shifted the Union's development narrative |url=https://www.brotherlygame.com/2021/3/25/22349758/philly-mls-25-auston-trusty-philadelphia-union-development |access-date=May 30, 2021 |work=Brotherly Game |date=March 25, 2021}}</ref>

He finished his first season with the Union having played every minute of the season as the club finished sixth in the [[2018 Major League Soccer season#Eastern Conference|Eastern Conference]].<ref name="bro2" /> He also scored his first professional goal on September 15 against the [[CF Montréal|Montreal Impact]], a 4–1 defeat.<ref>{{cite web |title=Philadelphia Union 1–4 Montreal Impact |url=https://us.soccerway.com/matches/2018/09/16/united-states/mls/philadelphia-union/montreal-impacts/2710627/ |website=Soccerway|access-date=May 5, 2026}}</ref>

Going into the [[2019 Major League Soccer season|2019 season]], Trusty continued his game streak, playing in an additional seven matches before being sent off during a match against the [[LA Galaxy]] on April 13.<ref name="bro2" /><ref>{{cite web |title=LA Galaxy 2–0 Philadelphia Union |url=https://us.soccerway.com/matches/2019/04/14/united-states/mls/los-angeles-galaxy/philadelphia-union/2959893/ |website=Soccerway|access-date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> Following his suspension, Trusty would start 15 more matches until July 2019.

===Colorado Rapids===
On November 20, 2019, Trusty was traded to the [[Colorado Rapids]] in exchange for up to $750,000 in allocation money, including performance-based thresholds, as well as a percentage of a future transfer.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rodriguez |first1=Alicia |title=Colorado Rapids permanently acquire Lalas Abubakar, add Auston Trusty in trade |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/colorado-rapids-permanently-acquire-lalas-abubakar-add-auston-trusty-trade |access-date=May 30, 2021 |work=[[Major League Soccer]] |date=November 20, 2019}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on July 17, 2020, against [[Sporting Kansas City]] in the [[MLS is Back Tournament]], coming off the bench.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sporting Kansas City 3–2 Colorado Rapids |url=https://us.soccerway.com/matches/2020/07/18/united-states/mls/kansas-city-wizards/colorado-rapids/3281273/ |website=Soccerway|access-date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> Following his debut season with the Rapids, Trusty signed a new contract on December 16, keeping him with the club through the 2023 season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bogert |first1=Tom |title=Colorado Rapids sign center back Auston Trusty to new contract |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/colorado-rapids-center-back-auston-trusty-agree-new-contract |access-date=May 30, 2021 |work=[[Major League Soccer]] |date=December 16, 2021}}</ref>

===Arsenal===
On January 31, 2022, Trusty signed with [[Premier League]] club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], although he would stay on loan with the Colorado Rapids until July 17, 2022.<ref name="Arsenal F.C">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/trusty-signs-club-remains-loan|title=Trusty signs for club but remains on loan|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=January 31, 2022|access-date=January 31, 2022}}</ref><ref name="trusty">{{cite web|url=https://www.coloradorapids.com/news/colorado-rapids-transfer-auston-trusty-to-arsenal-fc|title=Colorado Rapids Transfer Auston Trusty to Arsenal FC|publisher=Colorado Rapids|date=January 31, 2022|access-date=January 31, 2022}}</ref> He played his last game for the Rapids on July 5, returned to Arsenal, and was immediately loaned to [[EFL Championship]] club [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] for the [[2022–23 Birmingham City F.C. season|2022–23 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/auston-trusty-joins-birmingham-city-loan |title=Auston Trusty joins Birmingham City on loan |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=July 15, 2022 |access-date=July 15, 2022}}</ref>

====Loan to Birmingham City====
Trusty made his competitive debut in English football on July 30, 2022, in his new club's [[2022–23 EFL Championship|opening-day]] 0–0 draw at [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62274826|title=Birmingham grind out opening-day draw at Luton|website=BBC Sport|date=July 30, 2022|access-date=February 8, 2023}}</ref> He scored his first two goals in England in Birmingham's 3–0 win against [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] on October 8.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63099153|title=Trusty double helps Birmingham past Bristol City|website=BBC Sport|date=October 8, 2022|access-date=February 8, 2023}}</ref> His [[own goal (association football)|own goal]] caused Birmingham's elimination from the [[FA Cup]] at the hands of [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64453826|title=Blackburn beat Birmingham to reach round five|website=BBC Sport|date=January 31, 2023|access-date=February 8, 2023}}</ref> but he redeemed himself four days later with the winning goal in the seventh minute of stoppage time of the Championship match away to [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64435569|website=BBC Sport|title=Trusty injury-time header wins thriller at Swansea|first=Michael|last=Pearlman|date=February 4, 2023|access-date=February 8, 2023}}</ref>

As of February 10, Trusty had played every minute of every league match throughout the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/auston-trusty-exclusive-arsenal-american-taking-championship-by-storm-birmingham-city/blt3cde02d8a37715cf |title=Auston Trusty exclusive: Arsenal's American star taking the Championship by storm with Birmingham City |first=Charles |last=Watts |website=Goal.com |date=February 10, 2023 |access-date=February 11, 2023}}</ref> He finished the season with 44 appearances in all competitions and four goals,<ref name="sb2223" /> and was voted Player of the Season by ''Blues'' supporters.<ref name="PotS2223" />

===Sheffield United===
On August 3, 2023, Trusty signed for newly promoted [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Auston Trusty: Sheffield United sign Arsenal defender |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66392858 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=August 3, 2023 |date=August 3, 2023}}</ref> He made his Premier League debut on September 16 in a 2–1 loss away to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66760556 |title=Tottenham 2–1 Sheffield United: Richarlison comes off bench to spark stoppage-time turnaround |website=BBC Sport |last=Beardmore |first=Michael |date=September 16, 2023 |access-date=December 24, 2023}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Sheffield United on August 13, 2024, in an [[EFL Cup]] tie against [[Wrexham F.C.|Wrexham]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c39kny38dxjt|title=Sheffield United 4-2 Wrexham|publisher=[[BBC]] |date=August 13, 2024|access-date=August 17, 2024}}</ref>

===Celtic===

On August 30, 2024, Trusty signed with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on a five-year contract.<ref>{{cite news |title=Auston Trusty joins Celtic on a five-year-deal|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2024/august/30/auston-trusty-signs-for-celtic/ |website=Celtic FC |access-date=August 30, 2024 |date=August 30, 2024}}</ref> The move saw him join his international teammate, and fellow centre back, [[Cameron Carter-Vickers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2024/august/31/auston-trusty-delighted-to-be-reunited-with-usa-team-mate/|title=Auston Trusty delighted to be reunited with USA team-mate|first=Paul|last=Cuddihy|date=August 31, 2024|website=Celtic FC|accessdate=April 7, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Gtn04pX_wU|title=Celtic's American Bhoys: Auston Trusty & Cameron Carter-Vickers in the studio!|author=Celtic FC|date=March 23, 2025|via=YouTube|accessdate=April 7, 2025}}</ref>

He made his debut in the [[UEFA Champions League]] against [[ŠK Slovan Bratislava|Slovan Bratislava]] on September 18.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/24594855.watch-trusty-celebrates-bench-celtic-debut/|title=Watch as Auston Trusty celebrates on bench before Celtic debut in Champions League|last=Irvine|first=David|date=September 19, 2024|website=Glasgow Times|accessdate=April 6, 2025}}</ref> He scored his first goal on January 4, 2025, netting the second goal as the Bhoys beat [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] 3–0 at [[Celtic Park]] in the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gulf-times.com/article/697935/sports/celtic-stretch-lead-to-13-points-after-rangers-held|title=Celtic stretch lead to 13 points after Rangers held|author=AFP|date=January 6, 2025|website=Gulf Times|accessdate=April 6, 2025}}</ref>

After coming on as a substitute during the second leg of Celtic's Champions League play-off against [[FC Kairat|Kairat Almaty]] on August 26, 2025, Trusty tore his [[plantar fascia]], which ruled him out of action for several weeks and left him struggling to walk.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=O'Keeffe |first=Greg |date=November 25, 2025 |title=Auston Trusty interview: 'Everything right now is aligning for me' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6828546/2025/11/25/auston-trusty-interview-usmnt-celtic-world-cup/ |access-date=May 5, 2026 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Even after returning to training, he did not make a further appearance under [[Brendan Rodgers]], who preferred the partnership of Carter-Vickers and [[Liam Scales]]. Rodgers resigned as manager on October 27 and Trusty finally made his comeback when interim manager [[Martin O'Neill]] gave him his first start of the season in 4-0 league victory over Falkirk.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://celtsarehere.com/celtic-fc-news-auston-trusty-message/|title=Celtic Star Exiled Under Rodgers Posts Thursday Social Media Message | Latest Celtic News|author=M.Ross|date=October 30, 2025|work=Celts Are Here|access-date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> He was named man of the match against Rangers in the [[Scottish League Cup]] semi-final on November 2, having controversially avoided being sent off for a late challenge on Rangers goalkeeper [[Jack Butland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/football/rangers-to-seek-sfa-explanation-into-why-auston-trusty-wasnt-shown-red-card-for-foul-on-jack-butland-in-defeat-to-celtic|title=Rangers to ask SFA why Trusty wasn't sent off for foul on Butland|first=Peter|last=Cassidy|date=November 2, 2025|work=STV News|access-date=November 25, 2025}}</ref>

Trusty scored his second Celtic goal in a 2–2 draw with [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]] in the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] on January 22, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c77kkekejj2o|title=Celtic pick up where they left off under Martin O'Neill - Auston Trusty|date=January 23, 2026|website=BBC Sport|access-date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> He also made a series of crucial blocks and tackles to help the Bhoys gain a crucial point, winning [[man of the match]] in the process.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.footballinsider247.com/celtic-have-their-player-of-the-year-already-as-fans-hail-star-who-was-an-absolute-machine-vs-bologna/|title=Celtic have their player of the year already as fans hail star who was an 'absolute machine' vs Bologna|first=Evan|last=Shaw|date=January 23, 2026|website=Football Insider|access-date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> Three days later, however, he was sent off against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] for a [[professional foul]] on [[Pierre Landry Kaboré]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/football/martin-oneill-dismayed-at-auston-trusty-red-card-in-2-2-draw-at-tynecastle|title=O'Neill dismayed at Trusty red card in 2-2 draw at Tynecastle|first=Peter|last=Cassidy|date=January 25, 2026|publisher=STV News|access-date=January 25, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cx20pnz9kp0t|title=Hearts 2-2 Celtic|last=Lindsay|first=Clive|date=January 25, 2026|website=BBC Sport|access-date=January 25, 2026}}</ref> He was sent off again in a 2-1 defeat against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on February 22, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/celtic-see-auston-trusty-red-36763747|title=Martin O'Neill sees Celtic red card verdict instantly clamped|first=Robbie|last=Copeland|date=February 22, 2026|website=Daily Record|access-date=May 5, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/clyvr7p7y4mt|title=Celtic vs Hibernian: Scottish Premiership updates & match report|website=BBC Sport|access-date=May 5, 2026}}</ref>

Trusty was at the center of a highly controversial incident at the end of Celtic's league tie against Motherwell at [[Fir Park]] on May 13, 2026. In the fifth and final minute of injury time, with the score at 2-2, he challenged Motherwell midfielder [[Sam Nicholson]] for the ball in the Motherwell penalty box. After Nicholson appeared to handle the ball away, Trusty went down holding the side of his face and, though referee [[John Beaton]] initially waved play on, he was eventually asked to go and look at the [[video assistant referee|VAR]]. Upon inspection, Beaton decided that Nicholson's hand had made contact with the ball during the header and gave a penalty to Celtic.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/celtic-penalty-var-hearts-motherwell-scottish-title-b2976192.html|title='Worst VAR decision ever seen': Hearts rage at 'disgusting' Celtic penalty call|last=Jackson|first=Kieran|date=13 May 2026|website=The Independent}}</ref> The penalty was converted by [[Kelechi Iheanacho]] to win the game 3-2, meaning that Celtic remained one point behind [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] in a dramatic title race.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/auston-trusty-var-celtic-missed-37157827|title=Motherwell complaint over Trusty sin that VAR snubbed amid Celtic penalty drama|first=Mark|last=Pirie|date=14 May 2026|website=Daily Record}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/26149602.sam-nicholson-inside-story-celtic-penalty/|title=Sam Nicholson Exclusive: The inside story of THAT Celtic penalty|date=29 May 2026|website=The Herald}}</ref> Celtic went on to win the league against Hearts at Celtic Park on the final day, giving Trusty his second consecutive Scottish Premiership title.

==International career==
Trusty has represented the [[United States men's national under-17 soccer team|United States at the under-17 level]], playing in the [[2015 FIFA U-17 World Cup]] in Chile. He started the opening match, against [[Nigeria national under-17 football team|Nigeria]], but was given a [[Red card (association football)|red card]] near the end of the 2–0 defeat for a poor challenge on goalscorer [[Victor Osimhen]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/nigeria-cruise-past-usa-to-start-u-17-world-cup-title-defense |title=Nigeria cruise past USA to start U-17 World Cup title defense |website=[[Fox Sports]] |first=Jamie |last=Trecker |date=October 17, 2015 |access-date=January 29, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34564110 |title=Nigeria begin U-17 defence with a win as Guinea draw opener |website=[[BBC Sport]] |date=October 18, 2015 |access-date=January 30, 2023}}</ref> He missed the second group game through suspension, and was an unused substitute for the third, a 4–1 loss to [[Chile national under-17 football team|Chile]] that confirmed the United States' elimination from the tournament.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.soccertoday.com/usa-out-of-u17-fifa-world-cup-with-4-1-loss-to-chile/ |title=USA out of U17 FIFA World Cup with 4–1 loss to Chile |first=Diane |last=Scavuzzo |work=Soccer Today |date=October 23, 2015 |access-date=January 29, 2023}}</ref> He was a member of [[Tab Ramos]]' [[United States men's national under-20 soccer team|under-20 squad]] for the [[2017 FIFA U-20 World Cup|FIFA U-20 World Cup]], replacing the injured [[Marlon Fossey]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Steel FC's Trusty Added to U.S. U20 Squad |url=https://www.uslchampionship.com/news_article/show/793817 |access-date=May 30, 2021 |work=[[USL Championship]] |date=May 17, 2017}}</ref> He scored one goal during the tournament, the fifth in a 6–0 victory over [[New Zealand national under-20 football team|New Zealand]] on June 1.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ralph |first1=Matthew |title=Auston Trusty scores in U20 World Cup blowout of New Zealand |url=https://www.brotherlygame.com/2017/6/1/15723942/auston-trusty-scores-in-u20-world-cup-blowout-of-new-zealand |access-date=May 30, 2021 |work=Brotherly Game |date=June 1, 2017}}</ref>

On December 20, 2018, Trusty, alongside then teammate [[Mark McKenzie (soccer, born 1999)|Mark McKenzie]], received his first call-up to the senior [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] squad for their January 2019 camp.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tannenwald |first=Jonathan |date=December 20, 2018 |title=Auston Trusty and Mark McKenzie get first senior USMNT call-ups; Union to open 2019 season at home |url=https://www.inquirer.com/soccer/usmnt-january-camp-roster-auston-trusty-mark-mckenzie-20181220.html |access-date=May 5, 2026 |website=Inquirer.com |language=en}}</ref> Trusty was added to the roster for the United States' January 2022 training camp in Phoenix.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Auston Trusty Added To U.S. Men’s National Team Roster For 2022 January Training Camp |url=https://ussoccer.com/stories/2022/01/trusty-added-to-usmnt-roster-for-2022-january-training-camp |access-date=May 5, 2026 |website=[[United States Soccer Federation]] |language=en}}</ref> Trusty made his senior debut on March 24, 2023, starting the [[2022–23 CONCACAF Nations League A#Group D|CONCACAF Nations League A group phase]] match against [[Grenada national football team|Grenada]]. Partnering McKenzie in central defense, Trusty played the whole game, and provided the assist for [[Weston McKennie]]'s second goal of the 7–1 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=U.S. Men's National Team Rout Grenada 7-1 To Move Atop Nations League A Group D {{!}} U.S. Soccer Official Website |url=https://ussoccer.com/stories/2023/03/2022-2023-concacaf-nations-league-usa-7-grenada-1-match-report-stats-standings |access-date=May 5, 2026 |website=[[United States Soccer Federation]] |language=en}}</ref> Trusty was called up for the finals of the [[2024–25 CONCACAF Nations League]], but had to withdraw after suffering an injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cassidy |first=Peter |date=March 19, 2025 |title=Celtic defender Auston Trusty withdraws from USA squad with injury |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/celtic-defender-auston-trusty-withdraws-from-usa-squad-with-injury |access-date=May 5, 2026 |website=STV News |language=en-GB}}</ref> On November 19, he started the USA's 5–1 thrashing of [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] at the [[Raymond James Stadium]] and assisted [[Alex Freeman]]'s second goal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Text |first=Live |title=United States vs Uruguay: Friendlies stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c1j84nz31xgt |access-date=May 5, 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cassidy |first=Peter |date=March 19, 2025 |title=bk33 |url=https://bk3bd.net/ |access-date=May 5, 2026 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Abnos |first=Alexander |date=November 19, 2025 |title=USMNT dominate first-choice Uruguay 5-1, a long-awaited signature win |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/nov/18/usmnt-uruguay-friendly-sebastian-berhalter-alex-freeman |access-date=May 5, 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

On May 26, 2026, Trusty was selected in the 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/usa-squad-announcement-mauricio-pochettino|title=Pulisic, McKennie spearhead USA squad |date=26 May 2026|access-date=12 June 2026|language=en}}</ref> Trusty made his World Cup debut in a 2-0 group stage victory against [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]] on June 19, 2026 at [[Lumen Field]] in [[Seattle]], helping the United States secure its spot in the Round of 32.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2026/06/usmnt/match-recap-highlights-vs-australia-world-cup-knockout-advance |title= U.S. MEN’S NATIONAL TEAM DOWNS AUSTRALIA 2-0 TO EARN BERTH IN FIFA WORLD CUP 2026 ROUND OF 32 WITH ONE GROUP GAME LEFT TO PLAY |date=19 June 2026|access-date=20 June 2026|language=en}}</ref> He earned his first World Cup start against [[Turkey national football team|Türkiye]] on June 25, 2026 at [[SoFi Stadium]] in [[Inglewood, California|Inglewood]], in which he also scored his first international goal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Starting XI & Lineup Notes: USMNT vs. Türkiye |url=https://ussoccer.com/stories/2026/06/usmnt/starting-xi-lineup-notes-vs-turkiye-world-cup |access-date=2026-06-26 |website=ussoccer.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In November 2024, Trusty and his wife, Emily Berardino, announced that they were expecting their first child.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.glasgowlive.co.uk/news/glasgow-news/celtic-star-partner-share-exciting-30486722|title=Celtic star shares exciting baby news in sweet video of 'greatest blessing'|first=Fahad|last=Tariq|date=November 30, 2024|website=Glasgow Live|access-date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> The couple were married in Glasgow in April 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/auston-trusty-celtic-wedding-married-35003235|title=Celtic star ties the knot as he shares adorable loved-up wedding photos|first=Gavin|last=Berry|date=April 6, 2025|website=Daily Record|access-date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> Their daughter arrived later that year.<ref name=":0" />

'''Anthony Ralston''' (born 16 November 1998) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]].

==Club career==
[[File: Celtic-20240722-034.jpg|thumb|upright|Ralston training with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2024]]
Part of the youth system at [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] since the age of eight,<ref name="Delight21"/> Ralston made his debut for the first team on 11 May 2016, in a 2–1 defeat against [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36200297 |first=Scott |last=Davie |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=11 May 2016 |accessdate=26 May 2016 |title=St Johnstone 2–1 Celtic}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in a 5–0 [[Scottish League Cup]] win over [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on 8 August 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40829930|title=Celtic 5-0 Kilmarnock|publisher=BBC|date=8 August 2017 |accessdate=14 August 2017}}</ref> He made further appearances early in the 2017–18 season, including a [[UEFA Champions League]] match against [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]],<ref>{{cite news|date=12 September 2017|title=PSG ace Neymar blanks Celtic teen Anthony Ralston as he tries to shake his hand|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/psg-superstar-neymar-blanks-celtic-11159892|access-date=16 November 2021|website=Daily Record}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11945/11033447/neymar-just-another-player-says-celtics-anthony-ralston-after-pair-clash-in-champions-league|title=Neymar just another player, says Celtic's Anthony Ralston after pair clash in Champions League|last=Thomas|first=Lyall|date=13 September 2017|publisher=Sky Sports News|access-date=12 October 2025}}</ref> but then suffered a knee injury in late September.<ref name = "2022 contract"/> Ralston signed a long-term contract with Celtic in December 2017, with the deal due to run until the end of the 2021–22 season.<ref name = "2022 contract">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42501429 |title=Celtic full-back Anthony Ralston signs deal until 2022 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=28 December 2017 |accessdate=28 December 2017}}</ref>

On 16 March 2018, Ralston joined [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on an emergency loan until the end of the 2017–18 season, a side challenging for promotion from the Championship up to the Premiership.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/14098|title=Anthony Ralston joins Dundee United on emergency loan|publisher=[[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]|date=16 March 2018|accessdate=16 March 2018}}</ref> He made his debut on 20 March, in a 3–2 loss in the league to [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref name="arab">{{cite web |title=Tony Ralston - Player Profile |url=https://www.arabarchive.co.uk/player.php?id=1919 |website=Arab Archive |access-date=16 November 2021}}</ref> In 15 appearances, he helped United reach the semi-final play-off for promotion, scoring two goals, albeit the side lost to [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in the semi-final play-off.<ref name="arab" />

On 2 September 2019, Ralston moved to St Johnstone on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ralston joins on-loan|url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/post/ralston-joins-loan|publisher=St Johnstone F.C.|date=2 September 2019|accessdate=2 September 2019}}</ref> Upon his return from the St Johnstone loan, Ralston played in only one game for Celtic during the following season, coming in a 0–0 draw against [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] when several squad regulars were missing due to a [[COVID-19]] isolation issue,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55598659|title=Celtic 0–0 Livingston|website=bbc.co.uk|first=Martin|last=Watt|date=17 January 2021|access-date= 30 July 2021}}</ref> and when centre-half [[Kristoffer Ajer]] then loanee [[Jonjoe Kenny]] were selected at right-back ahead of him following the sale of [[Jeremie Frimpong]], it appeared his time with the club would be coming to an end.<ref name="Heroics21"/>

At the start of the [[2021–22 Celtic F.C. season|2021–22 season]] under new manager [[Ange Postecoglou]], Ralston signed a contract extension until May 2022 and started in both legs against [[FC Midtjylland]] in the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League qualifying phase and play-off round#Second qualifying round|UEFA Champions League second qualifying round]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57855563|title=Celtic 1–1 FC Midtjylland|website=bbc.co.uk|first=Martin|last=Watt|date=20 July 2021|access-date=30 July 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57972180|title=FC Midtjylland 2–1 Celtic|website=bbc.co.uk|first=Thomas|last=Duncan|date=28 July 2021|access-date=30 July 2021}}</ref> Media outlets praised his performances in the early part of the season, following goals against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] and [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58261406|title=Celtic: Tom Rogic & Anthony Ralston have revived careers under Ange Postecoglou|first=Thomas|last=Duncan|date=18 August 2021|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 2 November 2021, he signed a new long-term contract with Celtic, keeping him at the club until 2025.<ref name="Delight21">{{cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2021/november/02/delight-as-anthony-ralston-signs-new-celtic-contract/|title=Delight as Anthony Ralston signs new Celtic contract|publisher=Celtic FC|date=2 November 2021|accessdate=2 November 2021}}</ref><ref name="Heroics21">{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/anthony-ralston-pens-celtic-extension-25360715 |title=Anthony Ralston signs Celtic contract extension as reward for early season heroics|last=Pirie|first=Mark|work=Daily Record|date=2 November 2021|accessdate=14 November 2021}}</ref>

On 15 December 2021, Ralston headed in a 97th-minute winner against [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in a 2–1 away victory for a Celtic side that had been reduced to ten men.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Celtic beat County with last-gasp goal |date=15 December 2021 |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59573754 |access-date=31 December 2022}}</ref> It has been assessed as one of the most important moments of the season for Celtic as they went on to win the [[2021–22 Scottish Premiership|2021-22 Scottish Premiership]] title, as the result kept them within touching distance of [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] who were four points ahead in the table at that time.<ref>{{Cite web |title=How did Celtic win the Scottish Premiership? Five key reasons for Ange Postecoglou's title success |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/soccer/news/celtic-win-scottish-premiership-reasons-postecoglou/cqnzo5jejzqccmy4dumeuokt |access-date=31 December 2022 |website=www.sportingnews.com |date=5 November 2022 }}</ref> At the end of 2022, Celtic signed Canadian [[Alistair Johnston]] who quickly became the first-choice right-back, with Ralston's role becoming that of a dependable back-up.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/ralston-johnston-hartson-celtic-scotland-33917054|title=Ralston has 'huge respect' of pundit as Celtic lack of games down to one reason|first=Alan|last=Galindo|date=17 October 2024|website=Daily Record}}</ref>

On 26 September 2023, Ralston signed a new four-year contract with Celtic, keeping him at the club until 2027.<ref>{{Cite web|publisher=Celtic FC|title=Anthony Ralston signs new four-year deal with the Hoops|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2023/september/26/anthony-ralston-signs-new-four-year-deal-with-the-hoops/# |access-date=26 September 2023|date=26 September 2023|website=www.celticfc.com}}</ref>

==International career==
Ralston was involved with several Scotland youth squads up to the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21s]].<ref>{{SFA player|143001}}</ref>

Selected for the [[Scotland national under-20 football team|Scotland under-20]] squad in the [[2017 Toulon Tournament]],<ref>{{ cite web | title = Scotland squad for Toulon announced | url = http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=1957&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=16955 | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]] | date = 17 May 2017 | access-date = 3 July 2022 }}</ref> Ralston played as Scotland beat [[Brazil national under-20 football team|Brazil under-20]]s 1–0, which was the nations first ever win against [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] at any level.<ref>{{ cite web | url = https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/15330314.amp/ | title = Toulon semi-final spot would be a dream for Celtic youngster Anthony Ralston | newspaper = [[Glasgow Times]] | date = 6 June 2017 | access-date = 3 July 2022 }}</ref> The team went on to claim the bronze medal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-finish-third-at-toulon-tournament-with-3-0-win/ | title = Scotland finish third at Toulon Tournament with 3-0 win | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]] | date = 10 June 2017 |access-date = 1 July 2022}}</ref> It was the nations first ever medal at the competition.<ref>{{ cite web | title = JULES AND HOLSGROVE TAKE BRONZE WITH SCOTLAND IN TOULON | url = https://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/2017/june/jules-and-holsgrove-take-bronze-with-scotland-in-toulon/ | publisher = Reading FC | date = 11 June 2017 | access-date = 1 July 2022 }}</ref> Selected for the [[2018 Toulon Tournament squads#Group B|under-21 squad]] in the [[2018 Toulon Tournament]].<ref>{{ cite web | title=Scotland Under-21 squad announced for Toulon tournament | url = https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-under-21-squad-announced-for-toulon-tournament/ | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]] | date = 3 May 2018 | access-date = 3 July 2022 }}</ref> They lost to [[Turkey national under-21 football team|Turkey under-21]]s in a penalty-out and finished fourth.<ref>{{ cite web | url = https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-finish-fourth-at-the-toulon-tournament-after-shoot-out-defeat-to-turkey/ | title = Scotland finish fourth at the Toulon tournament after shoot-out defeat to Turkey | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]] | date = 10 June 2018 |access-date = 1 July 2022 }}</ref>

In November 2021, he was called up to the [[Scotland national football team|senior squad]] for the first time ahead of a [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group F|2022 World Cup qualifier]] against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]], as a replacement for the suspended [[Nathan Patterson (footballer)|Nathan Patterson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/celtic/celtics-anthony-ralston-called-for-scotland-duty-against-denmark-3457136|title=Celtic's Anthony Ralston called for Scotland duty against Denmark|work=The Scotsman|date=13 November 2021|accessdate=14 November 2021}}</ref> He made his international debut in the match<ref>{{Cite news|title=Scotland 2-0 Denmark: John Souttar and Che Adams fire Tartan Army to home World Cup play-off|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/scotland-vs-denmark/report/441762|access-date=16 November 2021|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref> as a late substitute for [[Kieran Tierney]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59202146|title=Scotland beat Danes to earn home play-off|last=Lindsay|first=Clive|date=15 November 2021|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=16 November 2021}}</ref> On his second Scotland appearance he scored his first international goal during a [[2022–23 UEFA Nations League]] group match against [[Armenia national football team|Armenia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61740982 |title=Scotland 2-0 Armenia: Anthony Ralston revels in special first start at Hampden |last=Moffat |first=Colin |date=8 June 2022 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=9 June 2022}}</ref>

On 7 June 2024, Ralston was named in Scotland's squad for the [[UEFA Euro 2024]] finals in Germany.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/record-breaking-goalkeeper-gordon-out-scotland-euro-2024-squad-2024-06-07/|title=Record-breaking goalkeeper Gordon out of Scotland's Euro 2024 squad|date=7 June 2024|access-date=15 June 2024|website=Reuters}}</ref> A week later, he started the opening match of the tournament, where Scotland lost 5–1 to hosts [[Germany national football team|Germany]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c844x4y3ee3t|title=Ruthless Germany humble 10-man Scotland in Euro 2024 opener|website=BBC Sport|access-date=15 June 2024}}</ref> He went on to start in both the second match against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] and the third against [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]] as Scotland finished bottom of [[UEFA Euro 2024 Group A|Group A]] with one point from three matches.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/news/028e-1b2c127c5b92-e020507872a2-1000--scotland-1-1-switzerland-clarke-s-men-keep-group-a-hopes-/|title=Scotland 1-1 Switzerland: Clarke's men keep Group A hopes alive|access-date=24 June 2024|website=UEFA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/match/2036186--scotland-vs-hungary/lineups/|title=Scotland vs Hungary: Line-ups|access-date=24 June 2024|website=UEFA}}</ref>

On 19 May 2026, Ralston was selected in the 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/scotland-squad-announced-steve-clarke|title=Veteran Gordon and youngster Curtis named in Scotland squad|date=19 May 2026|access-date=13 June 2026|language=en}}</ref> He made his World Cup debut in a group stage match against [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]] on 19 June 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/17/285023/289273/400021454 |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=www.fifa.com}}</ref>
