'''Mvula Jordan Lotomba''' (born 29 September 1998) is a Swiss professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and the [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland national team]].<ref name="wf">{{Worldfootball.net|jordan-lotomba|access-date=17 February 2021|new_id=pe402261}}</ref>

==Club career==

===Lausanne-Sport===
Lotomba was trained in the [[FC Lausanne-Sport|Lausanne-Sport]] academy. He made his [[Swiss Super League]] debut on 24 July 2016 against [[Grasshopper Club Zürich]].<ref name="soccerway2">{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2016/07/24/switzerland/super-league/grasshopper-club-zurich/fc-lausanne-sport/2243183/|title=Grasshopper vs. Lausanne-Sport - 24 July 2016|website=Soccerway|accessdate=8 September 2016}}</ref>

===Young Boys===
[[File:Jordan Lotomba.jpg|left|thumb|Lotomba with [[BSC Young Boys|Young Boys]] in 2017|311x311px]]
Having joined Young Boys in the summer of 2017, he scored a 90th-minute goal that sealed a 2–0 victory against [[FC Dynamo Kyiv|Dynamo Kyiv]] in the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] third qualifying round, which qualified his club to the play-offs on away goals.<ref>{{cite web |last=Brewin |first=Joe |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/fourfourtwos-100-best-teenagers-world-2017-100-91%3F_format%3D |title=FourFourTwo’s 100 Best Teenagers in the World 2017: 100-91 |publisher=fourfourtwo.com |date=6 November 2017 }}</ref>

He was part of the Young Boys squad that won the [[2017–18 Swiss Super League]], their first league title for 32 years.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Homewood |first1=Brian |title=Soccer - Young Boys end 32-year wait for Swiss title and end Basel dominance |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-swiss/soccer-young-boys-end-32-year-wait-for-swiss-title-and-end-basel-dominance-idUKKBN1HZ0YS |accessdate=23 April 2019 |website=Reuters |date=28 April 2018}}</ref> During the [[2019–20 BSC Young Boys season|2019–20 season]], Lotomba became a key member of the squad, making 35 appearances for the club as they won a third successive Super League title.<ref name=SSLW />

===Nice===
On 3 August 2020, Lotomba signed for [[Ligue 1]] side [[OGC Nice|Nice]] for €7 million.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Jordan Lotomba est Niçois|url=https://www.ogcnice.com/fr/actualite/40218/jordan-lotomba-est-nicois|access-date=4 August 2020|publisher=OGC Nice|language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=3 August 2020|title=Official {{!}} OGC Nice sign right-back Jordan Lotomba from Young Boys|url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2020/official-ogc-nice-sign-right-back-jordan-lotomba-from-young-boys/|access-date=3 August 2020|website=Get French Football News}}</ref> Later that year, on 23 December, he scored his first goal in a 2–2 draw against [[FC Lorient|Lorient]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ligue1.fr/Videos/2020/12/23/but-jordan-lotomba-18-ogc-nice-fc-lorient-2-2-2020-2021 |title=But Jordan LOTOMBA (18') / OGC NICE |publisher=Ligue 1 |language=fr |date=23 December 2020 }}</ref> On 19 May 2024, he scored his second Ligue 1 goal on the final matchday of the [[2023–24 Ligue 1|2023–24 season]] in the stoppage time of a 2–2 away draw against [[LOSC Lille|Lille]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Midda |first=Sunil |url=https://www.flashscore.com/news/lille-nice-report-2024-05-19/dtS3cCfS/ |title=Lille miss out on Champions League qualification as Nice score late to break hearts |publisher=Flashscore.com |date=19 May 2024 }}</ref>

===Feyenoord===
On 2 September 2024, Lotomba joined Dutch club [[Feyenoord]] on a three-year contract.<ref name="Lotomba">{{cite web |url=https://www.vi.nl/nieuws/feyenoord-presenteert-de-opvolger-van-geertruida |title=Feyenoord presenteert de opvolger van Geertruida |trans-title=Feyenoord presents successor Geertruida |language=Dutch |date=2 September 2024 |access-date=2 September 2024}}</ref>

===Celtic===

On 2 September 2026, Lotomba signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] for an undisclosed fee on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2026/september/02/welcome-to-celtic--jordan-lotomba/ | title=Welcome to Celtic, Jordan Lotomba | publisher=Celtic FC | date=2 September 2026 | access-date=2 September 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Lotomba made his [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland national team]] debut on 7 October 2020 in a friendly against [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[ESPN]]|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match?gameId=573691|title=Switzerland v Croatia game report|date=7 October 2020}}</ref>

On 2 June 2021, he was included in the final 26-man squad for the rescheduled [[UEFA Euro 2020]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4211030/2021/06/01/switzerlands-full-26-man-euro-2020-squad/|title=Switzerland's full 26-man Euro 2020 squad|website=The Athletic|date=2 June 2021|access-date=2 June 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Lotomba was born in Switzerland, and is of DR Congolese descent through his father and of Angolan descent through his mother.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ruffieux |first1=François |title=Lotomba, une force vive pour le Lausanne-Sport |url=https://www.24heures.ch/sports/lotomba-force-vive-lausannesport/story/27047170 |newspaper=[[24 heures (Switzerland)|24 heures]] |accessdate=23 April 2019 |language=French |date=18 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Redaction Voila|title=DECOUVREZ JORDAN MVULA LOTOMBA DE BSC YOUNG BOYS|url=https://voila.cd/foot-rdc-decouvrez-jordan-mvula-lotomba-de-bsc-young-boys/|website=voila.cd|accessdate=6 July 2021|language=French|date=4 August 2017}}</ref>

'''Ross McCrorie''' (born 18 March 1998) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]], [[wing-back (association football)|right wing-back]], or [[defensive midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]].

McCrorie has previously played for [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]], [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]], [[Aberdeen FC|Aberdeen]] and [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]]. He captained the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21 team]], and made his full international debut for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] in 2024.

==Club career==
===Early careers and loans out===
McCrorie, alongside his twin brother [[Robby McCrorie|Robby]] (a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]]), worked his way through the Rangers [[youth system]],<ref name=extensions18>{{cite news | url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/news/local-news/ross-robby-mccrorie-sign-contract-11828251| work=Daily Record / Ayrshire Post|author=Lochlin Highet| title=Ross and Robby McCrorie sign contract extensions with Rangers| date=10 January 2018|access-date=16 February 2019}}</ref> becoming captain of their [[Rangers F.C. Under-20s and Academy|U20s side]]. McCrorie joined [[Scottish League One]] side [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] on loan in February 2016,<ref>{{cite web|last1=Wilson|first1=Mike|title=Ayr United sign Rangers teenager Ross McCrorie on loan|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/ayr-united-sign-rangers-teenager-7448993|website=Daily Record|date=26 February 2016 |access-date=27 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=http://rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/mccrorie-heads-loan/?| publisher=Rangers Football Club| title=McCrorie Heads Out On Loan| date=26 February 2016| work=Rangers.co.uk}}</ref> playing fifteen times and scoring twice as Ayr won promotion.

After signing a new contract in December 2016, at the same time as his brother,<ref name="New Deals For McCrories">{{ cite news | url=https://rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/new-deals-mccrories/ | title=New Deals For McCrories | publisher=Rangers Football Club| work=Rangers.co.uk | first=Nick |last=Thomson| date=24 December 2016 }}</ref> he joined his former coach at [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], [[Ian Durrant]], at [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]]  on a loan deal until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Findlay|first1=Alan|title=Transfer window: Ross McCrorie|url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=2861|website=Dumbarton FC|access-date=27 January 2017}}</ref><ref name="Duo Head Out On Loan">{{cite news | url=https://rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/duo-head-loan/| title=Duo Head Out On Loan| date=28 January 2017| work=Rangers.co.uk| publisher=Rangers Football Club}}</ref>

===Rangers first breakthrough===
McCrorie made his debut for the Rangers senior team in September 2017, when he replaced [[Bruno Alves]] in a [[2017–18 Scottish League Cup|League Cup]] quarter-final against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] at [[Firhill Stadium]], won 3–1 after [[Overtime (sports)#Association football (soccer)|extra time]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41232974| title=Partick Thistle 1–3 Rangers|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=19 September 2017|access-date=20 September 2017}}</ref> Following the match, manager [[Pedro Caixinha]] praised McCrorie, stating that he was "going to be the future of this country, not only this club, as a centre-half. We are very glad to have him with us".<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41328476| title=Rangers face anxious fitness wait on two defenders ahead of Old Firm game|publisher=BBC Sport|date=19 September 2017|access-date=20 September 2017}}</ref> Later in the same week he made his first start – also his [[Scottish Premiership]] debut and maiden experience of the [[Old Firm]] derby – against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]]. Rangers lost the match 2–0, but McCrorie's performance was reported favourably by the press and both Rangers and Celtic fans.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/sep/23/rangers-celtic-scottish-premiership-match-report| title=Tom Rogic and Leigh Griffiths set slick Celtic apart from Rangers|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=23 September 2017|access-date=23 September 2017}}</ref>

McCrorie scored his first senior goal for Rangers with a header in the first half against Partick Thistle on 4 November 2017 at Ibrox; Rangers won the match 3–0.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41785740| title=Rangers make it two wins out of two under interim manager Graeme Murty|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 November 2017|access-date=4 November 2017}}</ref> On 3 December he was deployed as a [[defensive midfielder]] in a fixture away to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], which his team won to overtake their opponents into second place in the table.<ref>{{cite news|title=Aberdeen 1 Rangers 2: Derek McInnes remains favourite for Ibrox job despite losing dress rehearsal at Pittodrie|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/12/03/aberdeen-1-rangers-2derek-mcinnes-remains-favourite-ibrox-job/|last=Forsyth|first=Roddy|newspaper=Daily Telegraph|date=3 December 2017|access-date=4 December 2017}}</ref> On 28 December he signed a new four-year contract.<ref name=extensions18/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/teams/rangers/ross-mccrorie-and-twin-brother-robbie-agree-new-deals-with-rangers-1-4649815|title=Ross McCrorie and twin brother Robbie agree new deals with Rangers|newspaper=The Scotsman|date=29 December 2017|access-date=1 January 2018}}</ref> After he scored an important goal in the second visit to Aberdeen in May 2018, McCrorie received praise from both the [[Pittodrie Stadium|Pittodrie]] boss [[Derek McInnes]] and the Rangers caretaker manager [[Jimmy Nicholl]] for his overall performance and influence in bringing his team back into the match; the player himself dedicated the strike to his dying grandmother.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44048358| title=Ross McCrorie 'dragged Rangers back into the game' - Aberdeen's Derek McInnes|work=BBC Sport|date=8 May 2018|access-date=10 May 2018}}</ref>

====Loan to Portsmouth====
In July 2019, McCrorie agreed a deal to move to English club [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] on loan for the [[2019–20 in English football|2019–20 season]]; it was reported that ''Pompey'' had an option to buy him outright,<ref>[https://www.footballscotland.co.uk/spfl/scottish-premiership/ross-mccrorie-leaves-rangers-loan-16538063 Ross McCrorie leaves Rangers for loan deal at Portsmouth with option to buy], Football Scotland, 5 July 2019</ref> but this was refuted by Rangers manager [[Steven Gerrard]] a few days later.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48901730 Rangers: Portsmouth don't have clause to buy Ross McCrorie - Steven Gerrard], BBC Sport, 7 July 2019</ref> He made his competitive debut for Pompey on 3 August, a 1–0 defeat away at [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]], during which he was sent off in the 81st minute for a late challenge on Shrewsbury's [[Donald Love]].<ref>{{cite web |title = Shrewsbury Town 1 Portsmouth 0 - Report and pictures |url = https://www.shropshirestar.com/sport/football/shrewsbury-town-fc/2019/08/03/shrewsbury-town-1-portsmouth-0-report-and-pictures/ |work = [[Shropshire Star]] |date = 3 August 2019 |access-date = 4 August 2019 |archive-date = 19 April 2022 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220419221914/https://www.shropshirestar.com/sport/football/shrewsbury-town-fc/2019/08/03/shrewsbury-town-1-portsmouth-0-report-and-pictures/ |url-status = dead }}</ref>

===Aberdeen===
On 17 August 2020, McCrorie joined [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], initially on a one-year loan, with an obligation to buy for a reported fee of around £350,000.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53809695 Ross McCrorie: Aberdeen sign Rangers midfielder on loan before three-year deal], BBC Sport, 18 August 2020</ref> A clause in the deal meant he would not be eligible to play against his 'parent club' during the [[2020–21 Scottish Premiership]] campaign, although he would not return to Rangers before becoming a permanent Aberdeen signing.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.edinburghlive.co.uk/sport/football/hibs-aberdeen-ross-mccrorie-rangers-18785827|title=Why Aberdeen beat Hibs to the signing of Rangers youngster Ross McCrorie|first=James|last=Delaney|date=18 August 2020|website=Edinburgh Live}}</ref> The deal was made permanent on 1 February 2021, ahead of schedule, as [[Scott Wright (footballer)|Scott Wright]] moved in the opposite direction.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55879820 |title=Aberdeen: Florian Kamberi, Fraser Hornby & Callum Hendry join on loan |publisher=BBC |website=BBC Sport |date=1 February 2021 |access-date=2 February 2021}}</ref>

===Bristol City===
On 6 June 2023, McCrorie joined [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] on a three-year deal with the option of a further year, for an undisclosed fee. After an injury lay off, McCrorie made his debut for City in a 2–0 loss away at Preston on 13 January 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=✍️ McCrorie joins City |url=https://www.bcfc.co.uk/news/mccrorie-joins-city/ |access-date=6 June 2023 |website=Bristol City |date=6 June 2023 |language=en}}</ref> On 22 May 2026, the club announced it had exercised an option to extend the player's contract to the end of the 2026/27 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-22 |title=Ross McCrorie: Bristol City defender to stay until end of 2026-27 |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cp3p2ed6599o |access-date=2026-05-24 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

===Rangers return===
On 25 June 2026, McCrorie returned to Rangers on a three-year contract with the option of a further year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-25 |title=Rangers Announce Signing Of Ross McCrorie |url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/Article/rangers-announce-signing-of-ross-mccrorie/3ZriARz70BEMP6Lt7SCbrl |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=rangers.co.uk|language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Украина U-21 - Шотландия U-21 3-1. 12 октября 2018 года — 915146.jpg|thumb|McCrorie (No 20, captain) with [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21s]] in Ukraine, 2018, alongside twin brother [[Robby McCrorie|Robby]] (No 21, goalkeeper)]]
With his brother [[Robby McCrorie|Robby]], [[Scotland national under-16 football team|Scotland U16]] won the [[Victory Shield]] in [[2013–14 in Scottish football|2013–14]],<ref>{{ cite web | url = https://www.thefa.com/news/2013/nov/29/scotland-vs-report | title = SCOTLAND PIP ENGLAND TO VICTORY SHIELD TRIUMPH | publisher = The [[The Football Association|FA]] | date = 29 November 2013 | access-date = 22 May 2021 }}</ref> and were selected for [[Scotland national under-17 football team|Scotland U17]] in the [[2015 UEFA European Under-17 Championship|2015 UEFA European U-17 Championship]].<ref>{{ cite web | url = https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/under-17-squad-for-uefa-euros-confirmed/ | title = Under-17 squad for UEFA EUROs confirmed | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association|Scottish FA]] | date = 28 April 2015 | access-date = 2 July 2022 }}</ref>

McCrorie was named in the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland U19]] squad for the elite round of the European Championships in March 2017<ref>{{cite web|last1=Findlay|first1=Alan|title=Cap calls for loan duo |url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=2902|access-date=3 March 2017}}</ref> alongside [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] teammate [[Daniel Harvie]]. He had captained the side in the qualifying phase of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=1961&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=16609 |title=Skipper McCrorie satisfied as Under-19s progress |publisher=Scottish Football Association |date=31 October 2016 |access-date=11 November 2017}}</ref> He also captained the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21 team]] on several occasions.<ref>[https://www.rangersnews.uk/news/ross-mccrorie-leads-scotland-under-21s-to-massive-win/ Ross McCrorie leads Scotland Under-21s to massive win], Rangers News, 12 September 2018</ref>

McCrorie was selected for the [[Scotland national under-20 football team| Scotland under-20]] squad in the [[2017 Toulon Tournament]].<ref>{{ cite web | title = Scotland squad for Toulon announced | url = http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=1957&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=16955 | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]] | date = 17 May 2017 | access-date = 1 July 2022 }}</ref> The team went on to claim the bronze medal,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-finish-third-at-toulon-tournament-with-3-0-win/ | title = Scotland finish third at Toulon Tournament with 3-0 win | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]] | date = 10 June 2017 | access-date = 1 July 2022}}</ref> the nation's first ever medal at the competition.<ref name = "bronze"/>

McCrorie received his first call-up to the senior [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] squad in October 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54477749 |title=Scotland calls for Ross McCrorie, Andrew Considine & Paul McGinn for double-header |website=BBC Sport |date=10 October 2020 |accessdate=6 June 2023}}</ref> He was called up again in June 2023 for games against [[Norway national football team|Norway]] and [[Georgia national football team|Georgia]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65817267 |title=Scotland: McCrorie replaces Ralston; Cooper, Souttar & Patterson doubts |date=5 June 2023 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=6 June 2023 |publisher=BBC}}</ref>

McCrorie  made his Scotland debut on 3 June 2024 in a friendly against [[Gibraltar national football team|Gibraltar]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/697146/scotland-gibraltar|title=Gibraltar v Scotland game report|date=3 June 2024|access-date=4 June 2024}}</ref> Two years later, he made his second appearance in a 1-0 friendly loss against [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]].<ref>{{cite news |last=McPheat |first=Nick |date=31 March 2026 |title=Ivory Coast 1-0 Scotland |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cew75ny45v9t#Report |work=BBC Sport Scotland |location=Glasgow, Scotland |publisher=BBC |access-date=1 April 2026}}</ref>

'''João Pedro Neves Filipe''' (30 March 1999), known as '''Jota''' ({{IPA|pt|ʒɔtɐ}}), is a Portuguese professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[winger (association football)|winger]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]. He is known for his passing and dribbling ability.

Born in [[Lisbon]], Jota came through [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]]'s youth academy. He began playing for [[S.L. Benfica B|Benfica B]] in 2018 and was promoted to the first team a year later, but played only a few minutes. He was loaned to [[La Liga]] club [[Real Valladolid]] in 2020 and [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2021, winning the [[2021–22 Scottish Premiership|league]] and [[Scottish League Cup]], before joining the club permanently for [[pound sterling|£]]6.5 million in the summer of 2022. In July 2023, Jota joined [[Saudi Pro League]] side [[Al-Ittihad Club (Jeddah)|Al-Ittihad]] for a reported £25 million. In August 2024, he joined [[Ligue 1]] club [[Rennes F.C.|Rennes]]. After just five months at the club, he returned to Celtic in January 2025.

Jota is a former Portugal youth international, representing his country at various levels, including [[Portugal national under-17 football team|the under-17 team]] that won the [[UEFA European Under-17 Championship|2016 European Championship]], the [[Portugal national under-19 football team|under-19 team]] that won the [[2018 UEFA European Under-19 Championship|2018 European Championship]] and the [[Portugal national under-21 football team|under-21 team]] that finished as runners-up at the [[2021 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2021 European Championship]].

==Club career==

===Benfica===

====2017–2019: Early years====
Born in [[Lisbon]], Jota started his career at Ginásio de Corroios, before joining [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]]'s youth ranks in 2007. He made his debut for the club's [[S.L. Benfica B|B team]] on 23 January 2016, replacing [[Dálcio]] in the 62nd minute in a 2–1 home loss to [[Varzim SC|Varzim]]. On 18 October 2018, he made his debut for the first team in a 3–0 away win over [[Sertanense F.C.|Sertanense]] in the third round of the [[2018–19 Taça de Portugal|Taça de Portugal]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Rocha|first=Pedro|date=19 October 2018|title=Jota, mais um produto da geração 99 (o segredo mais bem guardado da formação do Benfica)|trans-title=Jota, another product of the 99 generation (the most well-kept secret of Benfica's youth academy)|url=https://observador.pt/2018/10/19/jota-mais-um-produto-da-geracao-99-o-segredo-mais-bem-guardado-da-formacao-do-benfica/|language=pt|work=Observador|access-date=19 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|date=19 October 2018|title=Jota e a realização de um sonho|trans-title=Jota and the fulfillment of a dream|url=https://www.abola.pt/Clubes/Noticias/Ver/755239/40|language=pt|work=[[A Bola]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181019160938/https://www.abola.pt/Clubes/Noticias/Ver/755239/40|archive-date=19 October 2018|access-date=19 October 2018}}</ref> He won the 2017–18 [[Campeonato Nacional de Juniores]] and helped the team reach the final of the [[2016–17 UEFA Youth League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefayouthleague/history/season=2017/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170829213438/http://www.uefa.com/uefayouthleague/history/season=2017/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=29 August 2017|title=Salzburg succeed Chelsea as Youth League winners|date=24 April 2017|publisher=UEFA|access-date=24 April 2017}}</ref>

On 1 February 2019, Jota was promoted to Benfica's first team, alongside three other Benfica B players.<ref>{{cite news|last=Sanches|first=João|date=1 February 2019|title=Zlobin, Ferro, Florentino, and Jota permanently in the first team|url=https://www.slbenfica.pt/en-us/agora/noticias/2018-2019/02/01/futebol-benfica-quarteto-zlobin-ferro-florentino-jota-integrados-em-definitivo-no-plantel-principal|work=S.L. Benfica|access-date=1 February 2019}}</ref> Following his [[Primeira Liga]] debut in a 4–0 home win over [[G.D. Chaves|Chaves]] on 24 February, he made his European debut on 14 March, as a first choice, in a 3–0 [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]] win over [[GNK Dinamo Zagreb|Dinamo Zagreb]] in the second leg of [[2018–19 UEFA Europa League knockout phase#Round-of-16|UEFA Europa League round of 16]]. After failing to impress manager [[Bruno Lage]], Jota was used sporadically and found limited first-team minutes, scoring only two goals in the [[2019–20 Taça da Liga]] against [[S.C. Covilhã|Sporting da Covilhã]] on 3 December and [[Vitória FC|Vitória de Setúbal]] on 21 December.<ref name=":Career">{{Cite web|url=https://breakingthelines.com/player-analysis/jotas-emergence-at-celtic/|title=Jota’s Emergence at Celtic - Breaking The Lines|date=5 October 2021}}</ref>

====2019–2020: Loan to Valladolid====
On 5 October 2020, Jota moved to [[La Liga]] side [[Real Valladolid]] on loan for the [[2020–21 La Liga|2020–21 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realvalladolid.es/noticia/jota-refuerza-el-ataque|title=Jota refuerza el ataque|trans-title=Jota bolsters the attack|publisher=Real Valladolid|language=es|date=5 October 2020|access-date=5 October 2020}}</ref> On his debut on 22 November he came on as a 77th-minute substitute for [[Óscar Plano]] and scored the final goal of a 3–1 win at [[Granada CF|Granada]], but he added no more goals in 17 games for the rest of the season, which saw the team relegated.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Posada |first1=Arturo |title=Debut de "ensueño" para Jota, con una celebración mayúscula |trans-title="Dream" debut for Jota, with a capital celebration|url=https://www.elnortedecastilla.es/realvalladolid/debut-ensueno-jota-20201123140341-nt.html |access-date=16 February 2022 |work=[[El Norte de Castilla]] |date=23 November 2020 |language=Spanish}}</ref>

=== Al-Ittihad ===
On 3 July 2023, [[Al-Ittihad Club (Jeddah)|Al-Ittihad]] confirmed the signing of Jota for £25 million, a club record fee paid for a player.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 July 2023 |title=Jota: Al-Ittihad sign Portuguese winger from Celtic in £25m deal |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11787/12914378/jota-al-ittihad-sign-portuguese-winger-from-celtic-in-25m-deal |access-date=3 July 2023 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref> He joined the likes of [[Karim Benzema]] and [[N'Golo Kanté]] at Al-Ittihad as part of the massive investment into [[Saudi Pro League]] football by the [[Public Investment Fund|PIF]]. He scored his first goal for the club on 28 August 2023 in a 3–0 win against [[Al Wehda FC|Al-Wehda]] after coming on as a substitute for Benzema,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://spl.sa/en/matchcenter?competition=ea0h6cf3bhl698hkxhpulh2zz&season=8jrlomlpzrt4e327fxgdxwxec&match=6ele0h4zmznf6sgu2fpsltxxw|title=Al Wehda FC 0-3 Al Ittihad FC|website=SPL|language=Arabic|date=28 August 2023|accessdate=22 October 2023}}{{Dead link|date=September 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> but was later left out of the club's domestic squad by manager [[Nuno Espírito Santo]], with only eight foreign players being allowed as per Saudi league rules.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/23909059.ex-celtic-ace-jota-alert-nuno-al-ittihad-sacking/|title=Ex-Celtic ace Jota on alert after Nuno Al-Ittihad sacking|last=Paton|first=Ewan|date=8 November 2023|work=The National|access-date=27 January 2025}}</ref>

=== Rennes ===
On 30 August 2024, Jota signed for [[Ligue 1]] club [[Stade Rennais FC|Rennes]] on a three-year contract, with the transfer fee reported as €10 million.<ref>{{cite web |title=Official {{!}} Jota joins Rennes from Al-Ittihad |url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2024/official-jota-joins-rennes-from-al-ittihad/ |website=Get French Football News |access-date=30 August 2024 |date=30 August 2024 }}</ref> He later told French media that his former teammate [[N'Golo Kanté]] had recommended the move to [[Brittany (administrative region)|Brittany]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2024/i-dont-regret-at-all-going-to-saudi-arabia-rennes-jota-opens-up-on-al-ittihad-spell/|title='I don't regret at all going to Saudi Arabia' - Rennes' Jota opens up on Al-Ittihad spell|last=Cheval|first=Bastien|date=14 September 2024|work=Get French Football News|access-date=27 January 2025}}</ref>

After less than five months in France, and being frozen out of the first team,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2025/feature-jota-at-rennes-what-went-wrong-and-what-celtic-can-expect-from-former-cult-hero/|title=FEATURE | Jota at Rennes: What went wrong and what Celtic can expect from former cult hero|last=Cheval|first=Bastien|date=25 January 2025|work=Get French Football News|access-date=27 January 2025}}</ref> he made a return to Celtic.

=== Return to Celtic ===
Jota's return to Celtic for a £8.4 million fee was announced on 27 January 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2025/january/27/jota-delighted-to-be-back-home-in-paradise/|title=Jota delighted to be back home in Paradise|date=27 January 2025|website=Celtic FC}}</ref> He took the number 7 shirt—previously worn by club legends [[Jimmy Johnstone]] and [[Henrik Larsson]]—after [[Luis Palma]] went on loan to [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/24902504.jotas-new-celtic-squad-number-confirmed/|title=Jota’s new Celtic squad number confirmed, ties in with another winger's exit|first=Robbie|last=Hanratty|date=1 February 2025|website=The Herald}}</ref> He made his official re-debut with Celtic on 2 February 2025, scoring in the 94th minute against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] at [[Fir Park]], in a 3–1 Celtic victory.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cpdx2ny40det|title=Motherwell vs Celtic: Scottish Premiership report, reaction & stats|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 26 April 2025, he suffered a cruciate ligament injury in a 5–0 win away to [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], with the initial injury report being that he would be out of action for a nine-month spell.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c4gr74y02d8o|title=Celtic's Jota ruled out for up to nine months|date=2 May 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> In January 2026, Celtic manager [[Martin O'Neill]] provided an update on Jota's injury, stating that he had suffered a setback in his recovery that would require keyhole surgery, meaning he would miss the entire of the [[2025–26 Celtic F.C. season|2025–26]] season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/25763323.real-reason-behind-jotas-latest-celtic-injury-setback/|title=The real reason behind Jota's latest Celtic injury setback|last=McMillan|first=Martin|date=13 January 2026|website=The Herald}}</ref>

On 3 October 2026, after 18 months out of the game, Jota made his long-awaited return from injury in a closed-doors friendly at Celtic's [[Lennoxtown]] training ground.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/26617681.spfl-coach-provides-celtic-verdict-bounce-match/|title=Having attended Jota's comeback behind closed doors, this is my Celtic verdict|last=McMillan|first=Martin|date=8 October 2026|website=Glasgow Times|access-date=11 October 2026}}</ref> His first competitive appearance since the injury came in a 2–0 win away to [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on 11 October, when he came on as a 74th-minute substitute for [[Sebastian Tounekti]] to make his 100th appearance for Celtic in all competitions.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/26626254.celtics-jota-returns-18-months-acl-injury/|title=Celtic's Jota returns after 18 months out with ACL injury|last=McMillan|first=Martin|date=11 October 2026|website=Glasgow Times|access-date=11 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cqdjv37mx21mt|title=Celtic back on top as win at Motherwell halts losing run|last=O'Neill|first=George|date=11 October 2026|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=11 October 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Jota earned 73 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] and scored 26 goals for Portugal across all youth levels, starting with a 2–1 win for the [[Portugal national under-15 football team|under-15 team]] against Switzerland in [[Campo Maior, Portugal|Campo Maior]] on 10 June 2014. He went with the [[Portugal national under-17 football team|under-17 team]] to the [[2016 UEFA European Under-17 Championship|2016 UEFA European Championship]] in Azerbaijan, scoring in the penalty shootout win over neighbours [[Spain national under-17 football team|Spain]] in the final.<ref>{{cite news |title=Portugal sagra-se campeão europeu de sub-17! |trans-title=Portugal crowned European under-17 champions!|url=https://www.dn.pt/desporto/seleccao/portugal-disputa-o-titulo-europeu-de-sub-17-5186636.html |access-date=7 May 2022 |work=[[Diário de Notícias]] |date=21 May 2016 |language=Portuguese}}</ref>

At the [[2017 UEFA European Under-19 Championship]] in Georgia, Jota was part of the [[Portugal national under-19 football team|Portugal team]] that finished runners-up to [[England national under-19 football team|England]]. In the final group game, he scored a late penalty as they came back to draw 2–2 with [[Sweden men's national under-19 football team|Sweden]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Portugal recupera dois golos e empata com Suécia|trans-title=Portugal come from two goals down and draw with Sweden |url=https://www.dn.pt/desporto/euro-sub-19-portugal-recupera-dois-golos-e-empata-com-suecia-8623282.html |access-date=7 May 2022 |work=Diário de Notícias |date=8 July 2017 |language=Portuguese}}</ref> He was in the squad for the [[2018 UEFA European Under-19 Championship|2018 tournament]], beating [[Italy national under-19 football team|Italy]] 4–3 in the final after extra time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.whufc.com/news/articles/2018/july/29-july/quina-becomes-european-champion-second-time|title=Quina becomes European champion for a second time!|publisher=West Ham United F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Italy 3–4 Portugal|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=30 July 2018|access-date=30 July 2018|url=https://www.uefa.com/under19/match/2024510--italy-vs-portugal/}}</ref> He also finished joint top scorer in the tournament with five goals,<ref>{{cite web|title=Domingos Quina, Moise Kean, João Filipe impress at Under-19 Euros|website=[[Sky Sports]]|date=30 July 2018|access-date=30 July 2018|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/11454150/domingos-quina-moise-kean-joao-filipe-impress-at-under-19-euros}}</ref> and was named in the Team of the Tournament.<ref name=u19>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under19/news/0257-0dee5d528f37-d719efae43a3-1000--under-19-euro-team-of-the-tournament/|title=Under-19 EURO team of the tournament|publisher=UEFA|date=1 August 2018}}</ref>

In March 2021, Jota took part in the [[2021 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] in Hungary and Slovenia. He scored in extra time as the team beat [[Italy national under-21 football team|Italy]] 5–3 in the quarter-finals at the [[Stožice Stadium]]. Portugal finished as runners-up, after losing in the final 1–0 to [[Germany national under-21 football team|Germany]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cardoso Oliveira |first1=Diogo |title=''Ciao'', meia-final: Portugal supera Itália no Euro sub-21|trans-title=''Ciao'', semi-final: Portugal overcome Italy in the under-21 Euros|url=https://www.publico.pt/2021/05/31/desporto/cronica_de_jogo/ciao-meiafinal-portugal-supera-italia-euro-sub21-1964810 |access-date=7 May 2022 |work=[[Público (Portugal)|Público]] |date=31 May 2021 |language=Portuguese}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=6 June 2021|title=Highlights, report: Germany beat Portugal for third U21 EURO title|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/026a-127532d17acc-e079bf3c8a1c-1000--highlights-report-germany-beat-portugal-for-third-u21-euro-/|access-date=7 June 2021|website=[[UEFA]]|language=en}}</ref>

In October 2022, he was included in a provisional squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] in [[Qatar]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/football/rumor-portugal-reportedly-announce-provisional-55-man-squad-2022-fifa-world-cup-liverpool-star-receives-surprise-call|title=Portugal reportedly name provisional 55-man squad for 2022 FIFA World Cup; Liverpool star receives surprise call up|publisher=[[Sportskeeda]]|first=Dakir Mohammed|last=Thanveer|date=25 October 2022|access-date=9 November 2022}}</ref> but did not make the final cut.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://desporto.sapo.pt/futebol/mundial/artigos/os-26-convocados-de-portugal-para-o-mundial2022|title=Os 26 convocados de Portugal: Gonçalo Ramos, António Silva, Otávio e Matheus Nunes chamados|trans-title=Portugal select 26: Gonçalo Ramos, António Silva, Otávio and Matheus Nunes called|publisher=SAPO|language=pt|date=10 November 2022|access-date=14 November 2022}}</ref>

'''Dujon Henriques Sterling''' (born 24 October 1999) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|right-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Rangers}} club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].

He is a product of the [[Chelsea Academy]] and started his professional career with [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in 2017. During his time with the club, he had been loaned out to [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]], [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]], [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] and [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]].

==Club career==
===Chelsea===
Sterling joined [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in 2007 at under-8 level and made his under-19 debut in a [[UEFA Youth League]] fixture against [[Sporting CP]] in December 2014.<ref name="Dujon Sterling">{{Cite news |title=Dujon Sterling |url=http://thechels.info/wiki/Dujon_Sterling |publisher=TheChels.info |accessdate=20 September 2017}}</ref> Although, recently Sterling had been deployed as a [[Defender (association football)#Wing-back|wing-back]], he has also been played as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] or [[Forward (association football)#Centre-forward|centre-forward]] and impressed during Chelsea's [[2015–16 FA Youth Cup]] campaign, netting in both the semi-final and final.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Manchester City 1-1 Chelsea: The FA Youth Cup Final (first leg) |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2016/apr/22/fa-youth-cup-final-first-leg-report |publisher=The FA |date=22 April 2016 |accessdate=20 September 2017}}</ref> Following an impressive campaign, Sterling was promoted to the U23 squad for the 2016–17 season as a 16-year-old and became a key figure, featuring twenty-four times and scoring four goals.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dujon Sterling |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/teams/development-squad/development-squad/u21-player-profiles/dujon-sterling.html |publisher=Chelsea Official Site |accessdate=20 September 2017}}</ref> In October 2016, Sterling signed his first professional contract upon his 17th birthday.<ref name="Dujon Sterling"/>

On 20 September 2017, Sterling made his Chelsea debut during their [[EFL Cup]] third round tie against [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]], replacing [[Davide Zappacosta]] for the final 14 minutes of the 5–1 victory at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Chelsea 5-1 Nottingham Forest |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41249727 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=20 September 2017 |accessdate=20 September 2017}}</ref>

====Loan to Coventry City====
On 27 June 2018, it was agreed that Sterling would join newly promoted [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea's Sterling in Coventry loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44635689 |accessdate=27 June 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=27 June 2018}}</ref>

====Loan to Wigan Athletic====
On 1 August 2019, Sterling joined [[EFL Championship|Championship]] side [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wiganathletic.com/news/2019/august/Latics-complete-season-long-loan-signing-of-Chelsea-s-Dujon-Sterling/|title=Latics complete season-long loan signing of Chelsea's Dujon Sterling|publisher=Wigan Athletic F.C.|date=1 August 2019|accessdate=2 August 2019}}</ref>

====Loan to Blackpool====
On 31 August 2021, Sterling returned to the Championship with [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] on a season-long loan deal after he signed a two-year contract extension with Chelsea.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sterling's contract and switch to Championship|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/08/31/sterling-s-contract-and-switch-to-championship|date=31 August 2021|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|accessdate=31 August 2021}}</ref> He competed with [[Jordan Lawrence-Gabriel|Jordan Gabriel]] for the right-back berth, covered at left-back when injuries dictated, and made up part of a back three on occasion. He made 25 appearances for Blackpool in all competitions.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Chelsea's Dujon Sterling bids farewell as Blackpool loan comes to an end |url=https://www.blackpoolgazette.co.uk/sport/football/blackpool-fc/chelseas-dujon-sterling-bids-farewell-as-blackpool-loan-comes-to-an-end-3687089 |access-date=2022-05-31 |website=www.blackpoolgazette.co.uk |date=9 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

He damaged his ankle ligaments in a match in early April 2022 and returned to Chelsea for treatment. His loan was kept active, however. At the end of the season, he posted on [[Twitter]] (now X): "Big thanks to all the players, gaffer, coaches and staff for making my time at the club so positive." Chelsea manager [[Thomas Tuchel]] was reportedly impressed with Sterling's season, and informed him to prepare for the pre-season schedule.<ref name=":0" />

====Loan to Stoke City====
On 1 September 2022, Sterling joined fellow Championship side [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] on loan for the [[2022–23 Stoke City F.C. season|2022–23 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Neil secures Sterling loan |url=https://www.stokecityfc.com/news/2022/september/01/neil-secures-sterling-loan/ |website=Stoke City |date=September 2022 |access-date=1 September 2022}}</ref> Sterling made 28 appearances for Stoke as they finished in 16th position.<ref name=DS22/>

===Rangers===
On 30 May 2023, it was announced that Sterling had signed for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] permanently on a four-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rangers Confirm Signing Of Dujon Sterling |url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/rangers-confirm-signing-of-dujon-sterling/66KsJJK5yN1za1cXApjajf |access-date=2023-05-30 |website=www.rangers.co.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref> Sterling was praised by Rangers manager [[Philippe Clement|Phillipe Clement]] for his versatility after performing well in central midfield during an injury crisis against [[Real Betis]] in a key [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] fixture.<ref>{{cite web |title='Versatile' Sterling helped Clement 'find a solution' |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c51zx58x0jxo |website=BBC Sport |date=16 December 2023 |publisher=BBC |access-date=17 December 2023}}</ref>

Sterling won his first title in professional football when he won the [[2023–24 Scottish League Cup|2023-24 Viaplay League Cup]] with Rangers, when they beat [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] 1-0 in the final. Sterling was voted man of the match.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/rangers-win-the-viaplay-cup#:~:text=Ibrox%20midfielder%20Dujon%20Sterling%20was,at%20Hampden%20Park%20was%2049%2C296 | title=Rangers win the Viaplay Cup | SPFL }}</ref>

On 7 March 2024, Sterling scored his first senior goal in the 5th minute of first half stoppage time against [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], off a cross from [[Fábio Silva (footballer, born 2002)|Fábio Silva]], to put Rangers 2-1 ahead in the first leg of the Europa League Round of 16 tie.<ref>{{ cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68409242 | title=Benfica 2-2 Rangers | website=BBC Sport | date=7 March 2024}}</ref>

==International career==
Sterling was born in England to Jamaican parents.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe375837/dujon-sterling/|title=Dujon Sterling|website=worldfootball.net}}</ref> Sterling has represented England from [[England national under-16 football team|under-16]] to [[England national under-20 football team|under-20]] level. He represented [[England national under-17 football team|England Under-17]] at the [[2016 UEFA European Under-17 Championship|2016 U-17 Euros]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2016/may/04/euro-finals-squad-announced-040516|title=England Under-17s squad named for Euro Championship|date= 4 May 2016 |publisher=The Football Association|accessdate=2 December 2017 }}</ref> and was included in the team of the tournament.<ref name="U17 Team of tournament">{{cite web|title=2016 UEFA under-17 Team of the Tournament|url=http://www.uefa.com/under17/season=2016/technical-report/uefa-technical-team/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161001160549/http://www.uefa.com/under17/season=2016/technical-report/uefa-technical-team/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=1 October 2016|publisher=[[UEFA]]|access-date=2 December 2017}}</ref>

In September 2016, Sterling made his debut for the [[England national under-19 football team|England Under-19]] team in a 1–1 draw against the [[Netherlands national under-19 football team|Netherlands]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2016/sep/01/netherlands-report-010916|title=England U19s held to draw by Dutch but seal shoot-out win|first=The Football|last=Association|website=www.thefa.com|accessdate=13 February 2020}}</ref> In June 2017 he was selected to represent England at the [[2017 UEFA European Under-19 Championship]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2017/jun/26/england-u19-squad-for-euros-260617|title=England squad selected for UEFA European Under-19 Championship|date= 26 June 2017 |publisher=The Football Association|accessdate=2 December 2017 }}</ref> Despite a Sterling own goal, England defeated [[Portugal national under-19 football team|Portugal]] 2–1 in the final.<ref name="U19 Champion">{{cite web|title=European Under-19 Championship: England beat Portugal in final|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40619862|publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 July 2017|accessdate=2 December 2017}}</ref> He was subsequently named in the team of the tournament.<ref name="U19 Team of tournament">{{cite web|title=2017 UEFA under-19 Team of the Tournament|url=http://www.uefa.com/under19/season=2017/technical-report/uefa-technical-team/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171104084104/http://www.uefa.com/under19/season=2017/technical-report/uefa-technical-team/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=4 November 2017|publisher=[[UEFA]]|access-date=5 October 2017}}</ref>

'''Ross Doohan''' (born 29 March 1998) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]].

Doohan began his career at [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], spending time on loan at [[Cumbernauld Colts F.C.|Cumbernauld Colts]], [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]], [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]], [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] and [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]]. His time at Tranmere became permanent, and he later played for [[Forest Green Rovers F.C.|Forest Green Rovers]] and [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], before returning to first club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2025.

Doohan was a Scotland youth international, playing for them up to under-21 level, before making his senior debut in 2025.

==Club career==
===Celtic===
Doohan began his career with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], spending time on loan with [[Cumbernauld Colts F.C.|Cumbernauld Colts]] in October 2015,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cumbernauldcoltsfc.com/Reports/player.php?id=44&team=1#matchContainer|title=Profile|accessdate=14 August 2018|publisher=Cumbernauld Colts F.C.}}</ref> where he made 4 appearances in all competitions.<ref name=Cumbernauld>{{cite web|url=http://www.cumbernauldcoltsfc.com/playerInfo.php?page=appearances&season=2015&team=1|title=(2015/2016) Senior Squad – Appearance Information|accessdate=14 August 2018|publisher=Cumbernauld Colts F.C.}}</ref> He moved on loan to [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] in August 2017,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/13101|title=Ross Doohan moves to Greenock Morton on loan|date=17 August 2017|accessdate=14 August 2018|author=Mark Henderson|publisher=Celtic F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/news/15480352.Morton_expect_Celtic_kid_Ross_Doohan_to_push_for_first_team_after_sealing_loan/|title=Morton expect Celtic kid Ross Doohan to push for first-team after sealing loan|date=17 August 2017|accessdate=14 August 2018|author=Graeme McGarry|publisher=Scotland Herald}}</ref> returning to Celtic in January 2018, having failed to make any senior appearances whilst at Greenock.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gmfc.net/2018/01/04/goalkeeper-ross-doohan-returns-to-celtic/|title=GOALKEEPER ROSS DOOHAN RETURNS TO CELTIC|date=4 January 2018|accessdate=14 August 2018|author=Jonathan Mitchell|publisher=Greenock Morton F.C.}}</ref>

After signing a new four-year contract with Celtic, he moved on loan to [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in July 2018,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/14591|title=Ross Doohan joins Ayr United on season-long loan|date=12 July 2018|accessdate=14 August 2018|publisher=Celtic F.C.}}</ref> making his senior debut on 14 July 2018 in a [[Scottish League Cup]] game against former club Greenock Morton.<ref name=rd1819>{{soccerbase season|89329|2018|accessdate=14 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ayradvertiser.com/sport/16361339.ayr-united-on-loan-goalie-ross-doohan-has-high-hopes/|title=Ayr United on loan goalie Ross Doohan has high hopes|date=18 July 2018|accessdate=14 August 2018|author=Stewart McConnell|publisher=Ayr Advertiser}}</ref> Having played for Ayr for the whole of the 2018–19 season, Doohan rejoined Ayr on loan for a second spell in July 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48975278 |title=Ross Doohan: Celtic goalkeeper rejoins Ayr Utd on loan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 July 2019 |accessdate=13 July 2019}}</ref>

In July 2020 he was linked with a third spell at Ayr.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/18606624.celtic-need-new-number-one-season-ross-doohan-future-parkhead-star/|title=Celtic need new number one for this season but Ross Doohan could be future Parkhead star|website=Glasgow Times |date=29 July 2020 }}</ref> On 1 August 2020 he signed for [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53615333|title=Ross Doohan: Celtic goalkeeper joins Ross County on loan|work=BBC Sport |date=1 August 2020}}</ref> With [[Ross Laidlaw]] largely preferred in goal, he made only five appearances for Ross County and returned to Celtic in January 2021.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Skinner |first1=Andy |title=Ross County looking for new goalkeeper after Ross Doohan returns to Celtic |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/ross-county/2807041/ross-county-looking-for-new-goalkeeper-after-ross-doohan-returns-to-celtic/ |access-date=24 April 2021 |work=The Press and Journal |date=13 January 2021 |location=Aberdeen}}</ref> He then joined [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on an emergency loan in April 2021 following an injury to their first choice-goalkeeper, [[Benjamin Siegrist]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Temple |first1=Alan |title=Dundee United sign Celtic goalkeeper Ross Doohan on emergency loan as Benjamin Siegrist is 'likely' ruled out for the season |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/2164237/dundee-united-sign-celtic-goalkeeper-ross-doohan-on-emergency-loan-as-benjamin-siegrist-is-ruled-out-for-the-season/ |access-date=24 April 2021 |work=The Courier |date=24 April 2021 |location=Dundee}}</ref>

===Tranmere Rovers===
In August 2021 he moved on loan to [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58088035|title=Tranmere sign Celtic keeper Doohan on loan|work=BBC Sport |date=4 August 2021 }}</ref> The transfer became permanent in July 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62070932|title=Tranmere re-sign goalkeeper Doohan from Celtic|work=BBC Sport |date=6 July 2022 }}</ref>

===Forest Green Rovers===
He transferred to [[Forest Green Rovers F.C.|Forest Green Rovers]] in January 2023.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64229640|title=Forest Green sign Tranmere goalkeeper Doohan|work=BBC Sport |date=10 January 2023 }}</ref>

===Aberdeen===
He transferred to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in July 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2023/07/06/doohan-is-a-don/|title=Doohan is a Don|via=www.afc.co.uk}}</ref> He struggled for playing time at [[Pittodrie]], however, with [[Dimitar Mitov]] preferred in goal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/6645790/aberdeenfc-ross-doohan-st-johnstone-preview/|title=Ross Doohan determined to be Aberdeen's No.1 - even after Dimitar Mitov returns from injury|first=Sean|last=Wallace|date=6 December 2024|work=The Press and Journal}}</ref>

His last Aberdeen game was the 2–2 league home draw versus Rangers on 13 April 2025.<ref name=sb2425/> He was unused from the bench when Aberdeen defeated Celtic on penalties in the [[2025 Scottish Cup final]].<ref name=abcel25>{{Cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2025/05/24/scotland/scottish-cup/aberdeen/celtic/4642308/|title=Aberdeen vs Celtic - 24 May 2025 - Soccerway|website=Soccerway}}</ref>

Doohan was released in May 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/25201063.aberdeen-confirm-exit-celtic-bound-ross-doohan/|title=Aberdeen confirm exit of Celtic-bound Ross Doohan as retained list released|date=29 May 2025|website=The Herald}}</ref>

=== Return to Celtic ===
Doohan returned to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on 20 June 2025, signing a three-year deal with his boyhood club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=FC |first=Celtic |date=20 June 2025 |title=Welcome back to Celtic, Ross Doohan |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2025/june/20/welcome-back-to-celtic--ross-doohan/ |access-date=20 June 2025 |website=Celtic FC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cy0wgvz15k2o |website=BBC Sport |title=Doohan returns to Celtic as free agent |date=20 June 2025 |access-date=21 June 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Doohan represented Scotland at various youth international levels.<ref>{{SFA player|142868}}</ref>

Selected for the [[Scotland national under-20 football team|Scotland under-20]] squad in the [[2017 Toulon Tournament]],<ref>{{ cite web | title = Scotland squad for Toulon announced | url = http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=1957&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=16955 | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]] | date = 17 May 2017 | access-date = 3 July 2022 }}</ref> he played in the third place play-off match, as Scotland won the [[bronze medal]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-finish-third-at-toulon-tournament-with-3-0-win/ | title = Scotland finish third at Toulon Tournament with 3–0 win | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]] | date = 10 June 2017 | access-date = 3 July 2022}}</ref> It was the nation's first ever medal at the competition.<ref>{{ cite web | title = JULES AND HOLSGROVE TAKE BRONZE WITH SCOTLAND IN TOULON | url = https://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/2017/june/jules-and-holsgrove-take-bronze-with-scotland-in-toulon/ | publisher = Reading FC | date = 11 June 2017 | access-date = 3 July 2022 }}</ref> Selected for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] squad in the [[2018 Toulon Tournament]],<ref>{{ cite web | title=Scotland Under-21 squad announced for Toulon tournament | url = https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-under-21-squad-announced-for-toulon-tournament/ | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]] | date = 3 May 2018 | access-date = 3 July 2022 }}</ref> he played as the team lost to [[Turkey national under-21 football team|Turkey]] in a penalty shoot-out for third-place.<ref>{{ cite web | url = https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-finish-fourth-at-the-toulon-tournament-after-shoot-out-defeat-to-turkey/ | title = Scotland finish fourth at the Toulon tournament after shoot-out defeat to Turkey | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]] | date = 10 June 2018 |access-date = 3 July 2022 }}</ref>

On 8 June 2025, head coach [[Steve Clarke]] called up Doohan to the Scotland senior team to travel for the friendly against [[Liechtenstein national football team|Liechtenstein]] on 9 June 2025, following injuries to fellow goalkeepers [[Zander Clark]], [[Craig Gordon]], [[Angus Gunn]], [[Liam Kelly (footballer, born 1996)|Liam Kelly]] and [[Robby McCrorie]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/ross-doohan-could-make-scotland-debut-after-late-call-up-for-liechtenstein-game|title=Ross Doohan could make Scotland debut after late call-up for Liechtenstein game|first=P. A.|last=Media|date=8 June 2025|website=STV News}}</ref> Doohan made his international debut in the game, keeping a clean sheet in a 4–0 win.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cvg5zn4p785t|title=Liechtenstein vs Scotland: International friendly LIVE - BBC Sport - watch, listen, updates, stats & head-to-head|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

'''Cameron Peter Devlin''' (born 7 June 1998) is an Australian professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|defensive midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia national team]].

Born in [[Sydney]], Devlin began his career as youth with local sides [[Sutherland Sharks FC|Sutherland Sharks]], [[Western Sydney Wanderers FC Youth|Western Sydney Wanderers]] and [[Sydney FC Youth|Sydney]]. He has subsequently played for [[Wellington Phoenix FC|Wellington Phoenix]], [[Newcastle Jets FC|Newcastle Jets]] and [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. 

Devlin has represented [[Australia]] at [[Australia men's national under-20 soccer team|under 20]], [[Australia men's national under-23 soccer team|under 23]] and [[Australia men's national soccer team|at full international level]].

==Club career==
===Sydney FC===
After playing most of his elite youth with the Western Sydney Wanderers NPL team (29 games), Devlin got a call up to play for [[Sydney FC]] in the [[2018–19 A-League]] season, making seven appearances off the bench including an [[AFC Champions League]] appearance against [[Kawasaki Frontale]]. He scored his first professional goal on 1 March 2019 in a 2–0 win over Adelaide.<ref>{{cite web |title=Soccerway Sydney v Adelaide |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2019/03/01/australia/a-league/sydney-fc/adelaide-united/2835019/ |website=Soccerway |accessdate=4 July 2019 |archive-date=7 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190707015649/https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2019/03/01/australia/a-league/sydney-fc/adelaide-united/2835019/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Wellington Phoenix===
[[File:Cameron Devlin 2021.png|left|thumb|280x280px|Devlin playing for [[Wellington Phoenix FC|Wellington Phoenix]] in 2021]]
On 4 July 2019, Devlin signed a two-year deal with the [[Wellington Phoenix FC|Wellington Phoenix]] after turning down a contract to stay with Sydney.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rollo |first1=Phillip |title=Wellington Phoenix coach Ufuk Talay brings Cameron Devlin over from Sydney |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/a-league/113975336/wellington-phoenix-coach-ufuk-talay-brings-cameron-devlin-over-from-sydney |publisher=[[Stuff.co.nz]] |date=4 July 2019 |access-date=3 July 2019 |archive-date=21 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220121165628/https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/a-league/113975336/wellington-phoenix-coach-ufuk-talay-brings-cameron-devlin-over-from-sydney |url-status=live }}</ref> In his first few months, Devlin only made sporadic appearances off the bench alongside two appearances for the [[Wellington Phoenix FC Reserves|reserve team]].

On 14 December 2019, following an injury to regular midfielder [[Alex Rufer]], Devlin made his starting debut for the Phoenix in a 0–0 draw with [[Melbourne Victory FC|Melbourne Victory]]; he quickly became an integral player for the team, being named [[A-League Player of the Month]] for December and retaining his starting spot even when Rufer recovered.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/a-league/119867709/cameron-devlin-soaring-to-new-heights-at-wellington-phoenix-after-spreading-his-wings|title=Cameron Devlin soaring to new heights at Wellington Phoenix after spreading his wings|first=Phillip|last=Rollo|newspaper=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]|date=29 February 2020|access-date=25 March 2020|archive-date=25 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200325061205/https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/a-league/119867709/cameron-devlin-soaring-to-new-heights-at-wellington-phoenix-after-spreading-his-wings|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Heart of Midlothian===

predicts bright future for Jets |url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/7316835/leap-of-faith-new-coach-predicts-bright-future-for-jets/ |work=Newcastle Herald |date=28 June 2021 |language=en-AU ==International career==
===Youth===
In October 2015, Devlin was selected for the [[Australia men's national under-20 soccer team|Australia under-20 team]] to play in [[2016 AFC U-19 Championship qualification]]. He made his youth international debut on 4 October 2015, playing in a win over [[Laos national under-20 football team|Laos]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theleader.com.au/story/3416870/young-socceroo-cameron-devlin-lives-his-dream/|first=Andrew|last=Parkinson|access-date=15 September 2022|date=14 October 2015|website=[[St George and Sutherland Shire Leader]]|title=Young Socceroo Cameron Devlin lives his dream|archive-date=15 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220915131612/https://www.theleader.com.au/story/3416870/young-socceroo-cameron-devlin-lives-his-dream/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Devlin was initially named as a reserve players for the [[Australia men's national under-23 soccer team|Australian under-23 side]] at the [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics|2020 Olympics]] in Tokyo.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newcastlejetsfc.com.au/news/devlin-named-train-player-olympics|first=Jayden|last=Roni|date=28 June 2021|access-date=15 September 2022|website=[[Newcastle Jets FC]]|title=Devlin named as train on player for Olympics|archive-date=15 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220915140119/https://www.newcastlejetsfc.com.au/news/devlin-named-train-player-olympics|url-status=live}}</ref> He was added to the Australian Olympic squad after the [[International Olympic Committee]] expanded squad sizes for the tournament.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.footballaustralia.com.au/news/tilio-wales-holmes-devlin-added-australian-olympic-team|website=[[Football Australia]]|date=15 July 2021|access-date=15 September 2022|title=Tilio, Wales, Holmes & Devlin added to Australian Olympic Team|archive-date=15 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220915131626/https://www.footballaustralia.com.au/news/tilio-wales-holmes-devlin-added-australian-olympic-team|url-status=live}}</ref>

Devlin made one appearance at the [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics|2020 Olympic Games]], coming on as a late substitute as Australia lost 2–0 to [[Egypt national under-23 football team|Egypt]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58104690|title=Cameron Devlin: Hearts close to signing Australia's Olympic midfielder from Newcastle Jets|quote=He made one appearances for Australia's Under-23 side at the Olympics, as a stoppage-time substitute in a 2–0 defeat by Egypt.|date=5 August 2021|access-date=15 September 2022|website=[[BBC Sport]]|archive-date=10 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220810212315/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58104690|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Senior===
Devlin was called up to the [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australian senior side]] for the first time in September 2022 for two friendly matches against [[New Zealand men's national football team|New Zealand]] in the leadup to the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c6p50m7n1p5o|website=[[BBC Sport]]|date=14 September 2022|access-date=15 September 2022|title=Devlin 'very excited' by Australia call-up|archive-date=15 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220915131613/https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c6p50m7n1p5o|url-status=live}}</ref> He came on for his senior international debut as a second-half substitute in the second game on 25 September 2022, in Auckland.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 June 2022 |title=New Zealand vs Australia, International Friendlies, Round 1, 25th Sep 2022 |url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/match/new-zealand-v-australia-friendlies-25-09-2022/2289966 |access-date=25 September 2022 |website=Socceroos |language=en |archive-date=25 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220925065521/https://www.socceroos.com.au/match/new-zealand-v-australia-friendlies-25-09-2022/2289966 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 8 November 2022, it was announced that Devlin was included in the Australian squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] in Qatar.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/football/socceroos/you-know-youre-going-aussie-star-breaks-down-in-tears-during-phone-call-with-arnie/news-story/52a5fbb381effd2f4588538f42b9a743|title='That is f***ing out of control': The brilliant moment Socceroos bolter breaks down over Cup call-up|first=Alex|last=Conrad|date=11 November 2022|access-date=12 November 2022|website=[[Fox Sports (Australia)|Fox Sports]]|archive-date=12 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221112012800/https://www.foxsports.com.au/football/socceroos/you-know-youre-going-aussie-star-breaks-down-in-tears-during-phone-call-with-arnie/news-story/52a5fbb381effd2f4588538f42b9a743|url-status=live}}</ref> Devlin did not take the field in the tournament for Australia, who were eliminated by [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in the round of sixteen.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/soccer/socceroo-who-didn-t-play-a-minute-lands-priceless-messi-souvenir-20221205-p5c3q3.html|title=Socceroo who didn't play a minute lands priceless Messi souvenir|website=[[Sydney Morning Herald]]|access-date=7 December 2022|date=5 December 2022|archive-date=7 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221207063634/https://www.smh.com.au/sport/soccer/socceroo-who-didn-t-play-a-minute-lands-priceless-messi-souvenir-20221205-p5c3q3.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 31 May 2026, Devlin was selected in the 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/australia-squad-announcement-world-cup-tony-popovic|title=Popovic includes Volpato in Socceroos selection|date=31 May 2026|access-date=13 June 2026|language=en}}</ref>
