'''Haissem Yousry Fouad A. Hassan'''{{efn-ua|{{langx|arz|هيثم يسرى فؤاد حسن}}}} (born 8 February 2002) is an Egyptian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]. Born in France to a [[Egyptians|Egyptian]] father and [[Tunisians|Tunisian]] mother, he plays for the [[Egypt national football team|Egypt national team]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=read |first=Eoin Morris·2 min |date=2026-07-07 |title=Who is Haissem Hassan? Egypt’s star man who almost knocked Lionel Messi out of the World Cup |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/haissem-hassan-egypt-star-man-193846439.html |access-date=2026-07-23 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Independent |first=Egypt |date=2026-07-15 |title=Liverpool and Celtic compete to sign Haissem Hassan |url=https://www.egyptindependent.com/liverpool-and-celtic-compete-to-sign-haissem-hassan/ |access-date=2026-07-23 |website=Egypt Independent |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="guardianhassan" /> He has been recognised for his proficiency in [[Dribbling#Association football|dribbling]].<ref name="fancast"/><ref name="open">{{cite web |url=https://openthemagazine.com/sports/haissem-hassan-rises-from-the-ashes-of-egypts-defeat|title=Haissem Hassan Rises From The Ashes Of Egypt's Defeat|publisher=[[Open (Indian magazine)|Open]]|date=9 July 2026}}</ref>

== Club career ==
Hassan signed his first professional contract with [[LB Châteauroux|Châteauroux]] on 1 June 2018 at the age of 16.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.footmercato.net/ligue2/info-fm-a-la-decouverte-de-haissem-hassan-16-ans-et-deja-professionnel-a-chateauroux_230535|title=Info FM : à la découverte de Haissem Hassan, 16 ans et déjà professionnel à Châteauroux|publisher=footmercato.net - Alexis Pereira|date=July 2018}}</ref> He made his professional debut with Châteauroux in a 0–0 [[Ligue 2]] tie with [[Paris FC]] on 19 October 2018.<ref>{{cite news|title=FEUILLE DE MATCH PARIS FC - CHÂTEAUROUX|url=https://www.lfp.fr/ligue2/feuille_match/85098|publisher=lfp.fr|year=2018}}</ref>

===Villarreal===
On 2 October 2020, Hassan signed a four-year contract with [[Villarreal CF]], being initially assigned to [[Villarreal CF B|the reserves]] in [[Segunda División B]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://villarrealcf.es/en/news/item/28669-villarreal-b-sign-talented-youngster-haissem-hassan|title=Villarreal B sign talented youngster Haissem Hassan|publisher=Villarreal CF|date=2 October 2020|accessdate=9 August 2021}}</ref> The following 9 August, he moved to [[Segunda División]] side [[CD Mirandés]] on a one-year loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cdmirandes.com/noticia/haissem-hassan-nuevo-fichaje-del-c-d-mirandes-cedido-por-el-villarreal-cf|title=Haissem Hassan, nuevo fichaje del C.D. Mirandés cedido por el Villarreal CF|trans-title=Haissem Hassan, new signing of C.D. Mirandés on loan from Villarreal CF|publisher=CD Mirandés|language=es|date=9 August 2021|accessdate=9 August 2021}}</ref>

On 1 August 2023, Hassan renewed his contract with the ''Yellow Submarine'' until 2025, and was loaned to [[Sporting de Gijón]] in the second division for [[2023–24 Segunda División|the season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://villarrealcf.es/haissem-renueva-y-se-va-cedido-al-sporting/|title=Haissem renueva y se va cedido al Sporting|trans-title=Haissem renews and moves out on loan to Sporting|publisher=Villarreal CF|language=es|date=1 August 2023|accessdate=1 August 2023}}</ref>

===Real Oviedo===
On 11 August 2024, Hassan moved to Segunda División club [[Real Oviedo]], on a three-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Haissem Hassan, nuevo futbolista del Real Oviedo |trans-title=Haissem Hassan, new Real Oviedo footballer|url=https://www.realoviedo.es/noticias/haissem-hassan-nuevo-futbolista-del-real-oviedo |access-date=11 August 2024 |website=Real Oviedo |language=es}}</ref> Later that year, on 22 October, he scored his first goal in a 4–1 victory over his former club CD Mirandés.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/709397/mirandes-real-oviedo |title=Real Oviedo 4–1 Mirandés |publisher=ESPN |date=22 October 2024 }}</ref> In the 2024–25 season, he was part of the team that earned promotion to La Liga for the first time in 24 years.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.laliga.com/en-MX/news/real-oviedo-secure-a-historic-promotion |title=Real Oviedo secure a historic promotion |publisher=La Liga |date=24 June 2025 }}</ref>

Following the conclusion of Egypt's [[2026 FIFA World Cup|2026 World Cup]] campaign in July 2026, Hassan was linked with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in Scotland,<ref name="celtichassan">{{cite web |last=Sinat |first=Patrick |url=https://www.67hailhail.com/opinion/haissem-hassans-world-cup-leaves-celtic-facing-a-4m-question/|title=Haissem Hassan’s World Cup leaves Celtic facing a £4m question|publisher=67HailHail|date=9 July 2026}}</ref><ref name="hassanherald">{{cite web |last=Walker |first=Mark |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/26261934.celtic-linked-world-cup-stars-transfer-release-clause-revealed/|title=Celtic-linked World Cup star's transfer release clause revealed|publisher=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]]|date=9 July 2026}}</ref> and later [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] in France.<ref name="Hassan.ktf1."/> On 10 July, Real Oviedo rejected an opening €4 million (£3.4 million) bid for Hassan from Celtic,<ref name="Hassan.ktf1."/> submitted two days prior.<ref name="Hassan.ktf2.">{{cite web |url=https://www.kingfut.com/2026/07/08/celtic-submit-3-4m-bid-for-egypt-winger-haissem-hassan/|title=Celtic Submit £3.4m Bid for Egypt Winger Haissem Hassan|publisher=[[KingFut]]|date=8 July 2026}}</ref> Oviedo reportedly also referred Celtic to his €12 million release clause.<ref name="Hassan.ktf1.">{{cite web |url=https://www.kingfut.com/2026/07/10/marseille-join-race-for-haissem-hassan-as-celtic-bid-rejected/|title=Marseille Join Race for Haissem Hassan as Celtic Bid Rejected|publisher=[[KingFut]]|date=10 July 2026}}</ref> On 19 July, reports stated that Celtic had submitted a new and "substantial financial offer" for Hassan.<ref name="Hassan.gh.">{{cite web |url=https://www.gomhuriaonline.com/Gomhuria/1783205.html|title=ريال أوفييدو يوافق على بيع هيثم حسن|trans-title=Real Oviedo Agrees to Sell Hassem Hassan|publisher=[[Al Gomhuria|Gomhuria Online]]|lang=ar|date=19 July 2026}}</ref>

===Celtic===
On 12 August 2026, Hassan signed a four-year contract with Celtic with an option for another year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2026/august/12/celtic-delighted-to-sign/ |title=Celtic delighted to sign Haissem Hassan |publisher=Celtic F.C. |date=12 August 2026 }}</ref>

==International career==
Hassan was born in [[Paris]], [[France]] to an [[Egyptian diaspora|Egyptian]] father from [[Aswan]], and a [[Tunisians in France|Tunisian]] mother.<ref name="berrichonne">{{cite news|last=Le Ruyet|first=Jean-Marc|title=Berrichonne : Haïssem Hassan, le rêve éveillé|url=https://www.lanouvellerepublique.fr/chateauroux/haissem-hassan-le-reve-eveille|publisher=La Nouvelle République|language=fr|date=1 September 2018}}</ref> He was a youth international for France.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://maligue2.fr/2018/09/27/haissem-hassan-chateauroux-offre-la-victoire-a-lequipe-de-france-u17/|title=Haissem Hassan (Châteauroux) offre la victoire à l'équipe de France U17 - MaLigue2|date=27 September 2018|website=maligue2.fr }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.elbalad.news/7032183 |title=من النوبة إلي العالمية.. أبرز المعلومات عن هيثم حسن نجم منتخب مصر |website=elbalad.news |language=ar |date=9 July 2026 }}</ref>

In March 2026, Hassan decided to join the [[Egypt national football team|Egyptian national team]] ahead of the March International Window and to play for his father's country at the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref name="JoinPharaohs">{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/egypt-haissem-hassan-set-join-231000595.html |title=Egypt: Haissem Hassan set to join the Pharaohs |publisher=Yahoo! Sports |date=3 March 2026 }}</ref> He made his World Cup debut as a substitute in the round of 32 victory against [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://english.ahram.org.eg/WorldCup2026/Article/572174 |title=Haissem Hassan hails Egyptian fans after historic World Cup triumph |publisher=Ahram Online |date=4 July 2026 }}</ref> After the match, Hassan said: "Honestly it's incredible, because you know that in Egypt there are 120 million people you've made happy today, and you know that today there will be celebrations across the whole country ... Knowing that you made so many people happy makes you happy too. ... Today is a day to celebrate."<ref name="Hassan.f1fa.">{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/egypt-reaction-hasseim-hassan-mostafa-shoubir|title=Hassan: We made 120 million people in Egypt happy|publisher=[[FIFA]]|date=3 July 2026}}</ref> Head coach [[Hossam Hassan]] later revealed that Hassan did not play in the opening group-stage games against [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]], [[New Zealand men's national football team|New Zealand]] and [[Iran national football team|Iran]] "due to certain internal matters that I cannot go into, as some paperwork caused a delay in his participation."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kooora.com/كرة-قدم/أخبار/أوراق-مؤجلة--كيف-أخرت-الإجراءات-ظهور-هيثم-حسن-في-كأس-العالم/bltb06ce38de048932f|title=أوراق مؤجلة.. كيف أخرت الإجراءات ظهور هيثم حسن في كأس العالم؟|trans-title=Delayed Papers: How Did Procedures Hold Up Haissem Hassan’s World Cup Appearance?|lang=ar|publisher=Kooora|date=4 July 2026 }}</ref> Hassan started against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in the round of 16. He produced a "possessed run down the right wing in the second half, weaving his way through half the pitch," to set up an attack from which [[Mostafa Ziko]] scored, but the goal was later controversially disallowed.<ref name="guardianhassan"/><ref name="bbcegypt"/> Taha Hashim of ''[[The Guardian]]'' called Hassan's contribution "a move straight out of the Messi playbook", and described the effort as "the greatest goal that never was".<ref name="guardianhassan">{{cite web |last=Hashim |first=Taha |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/08/football-daily-email-gwc-argentina-egypt|title=Argentina, VAR machinations and the greatest goal that never was |publisher=[[The Guardian]]|date=7 July 2026 }}</ref> Hassan then assisted Ziko for another goal, helping his team take a 2–0 lead before they eventually lost 3–2.<ref name="bbcegypt">{{cite web |last=Howarth |first=Matthew |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cdr4m2122lgt |title=Argentina 3–2 Egypt |publisher=BBC Sport |date=7 July 2026 }}</ref>

==Style of play==
Hassan is a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] known for his direct attacking style, dribbling ability, and willingness to take on defenders. Primarily operating on the right flank, he is noted for his ball-carrying and chance creation.<ref>{{cite web |last=Benson |first=Ryan |last2=Jolly |first2=Aryan |url=https://theanalyst.com/articles/world-cup-2026-breakout-players-transfers |title=Bouaddi, Vite, Nakamura and the Breakout Players Who Could Be on the Move After Impressing at the 2026 World Cup |publisher=Opta Analyst |date=20 July 2026 }}</ref> He ranks among the top 7% of wingers in Europe's top five leagues for successful dribbles and the top 1% for progressive carries, although he has been criticised for his lack of goalscoring.<ref name="fancast">{{cite web |url=https://www.footballfancast.com/better-than-hassan-celtic-kieron-bowie-transfer/|title=Better than Hassan: The club-record £13m signing Celtic could make|first=Matt|last=Dawson|publisher=Football Fan Cast|date=9 July 2026}}</ref>

'''Daniel James Neil''' (born 13 December 2001) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].

==Club career==
Born in [[South Shields]],<ref name="soccerway" /> Neil grew up as  a [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] fan,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/sport/19461527.dan-neil-determined-seize-chance-first-team-squad/|title=Sunderland's Dan Neil: 'The gaffer said I needed to improve'|website=The Northern Echo}}</ref> and began his career with the club after a stint with [[Hebburn Town F.C.|Hebburn Town]] Juniors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.safc.com/players/1st-team/dan-neil|title=Profile|accessdate=21 September 2021|publisher=Sunderland A.F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.shieldsgazette.com/sport/football/inside-the-hebburn-production-line-that-has-produced-manchester-united-starlet-shola-shoretire-plus-sunderland-leeds-and-norwich-trio-bali-mumba-dan-neil-and-sam-greenwood-3163870|title=Inside the Hebburn production line that has produced Manchester United starlet Shola Shoretire plus Sunderland, Leeds and Norwich trio Bali Mumba, Dan Neil and Sam Greenwood|website=www.shieldsgazette.com}}</ref>

He made his senior debut on 13 November 2018, in the [[EFL Trophy]], appearing as a late substitute in injury time.<ref name = "SWdebut">{{Cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2018/11/13/england/football-league-trophy/morecambe-fc/sunderland-association-football-club/2884204/|title=Morecambe vs. Sunderland – 13 November 2018 – Soccerway|website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref><ref name = "debut">{{cite web|url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/match-reports/morecambe-0-1-sunderland-report-15413083|title=Morecambe 0–1 Sunderland report: Josh Maja's late strike send Black Cats through|date=13 November 2018|accessdate=16 November 2018|author=James Hunter|publisher=Chronicle Live}}</ref> Neil scored his first professional goal when he scored against [[Accrington Stanley]] on 11 September 2021 in a 2–1 win.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58444782|title=Sunderland 2–1 Accrington Stanley|publisher=[[BBC]] |date=11 September 2021 |access-date=13 September 2021}}</ref>

In December 2021 and January 2022 he was linked with possible transfers to [[Premier League]] clubs [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] and [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], however he remained with Sunderland.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/burnley-test-sunderlands-resolve-dan-22574415|title=Burnley to test Sunderland's resolve with Dan Neil bid|first=Kieran|last=King|date=26 December 2021|website=ChronicleLive}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/steven-gerrard-plotting-aston-villa-22769256|title=Steven Gerrard plotting Aston Villa approach for Dan Neil, according to reports|first=Matty|last=Hewitt|date=16 January 2022|website=ChronicleLive}}</ref> This speculation came on the back of Neil being awarded the [[EFL Young Player of the Month]] award for December 2021.<ref name="Dec21 EFL YPOTM">{{cite web|url=https://www.efl.com/news/2022/january/dan-neil-claims-efl-young-player-of-the-month-award-for-december/|title=Dan Neil claims EFL Young Player of the Month award for December|website=www.efl.com|date=15 January 2022|accessdate=10 February 2022}}</ref>

On 27 January 2026, Neil joined [[EFL Championship]] club [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] on loan until the end of the season, when he would become a free agent.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 January 2026 |title=Dan Neil: Sunderland midfielder joins Ipswich Town on loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c4gld6ned0ro |access-date=27 January 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 1 July 2026, Neil signed for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on a three-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 July 2026 |title=Rangers Announce Signing Of Dan Neil|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/Article/rangers-announce-signing-of-dan-neil/4pgPzDcH4JgTwvCRc0myeJ|access-date=1 July 2026 |website=rangers.co.uk|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c2lyrw20n80o|title=Dan Neil: Rangers sign midfielder from Sunderland on three-year deal|date=1 July 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 13 September 2026, Neil scored his first goals for Rangers, scoring two goals in a 3–0 victory against Celtic in the quarter finals of the League Cup.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/dan-neil-its-an-unbelievable-feeling/1uAkmXfdLfqJcRl5oreFk9|title=Dan Neil: It's An Unbelievable Feeling|website=www.rangers.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/scottish/article/rangers-celtic-scottish-league-cup-score-result-match-r0wvlcvgc|title=Rangers make statement by blowing away Celtic in Premier Sports Cup|first=Michael|last=Grant}}</ref> In that match he served as captain in the absence of the injured [[Lawrence Shankland]], and was compared by [[Peter Lovenkrands]] to former player [[Barry Ferguson]] for his performance.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/crl62l7z6p4o|title=Barry Ferguson-esque Dan Neil 'ran the show' for Rangers|date=14 September 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> After making an error in a league match, he was defended by teammate [[Ivor Pandur]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cqy7lylern05o|title=Pandur backs Neil after Dundee error costs Rangers|date=19 October 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==International career==
On 11 November 2021, Neil made his [[England national under-20 football team|England U20]] debut during a 2–0 defeat to [[Portugal national under-20 football team|Portugal]] in the [[2021–22 Under 20 Elite League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Portugal 2–0 England MU20s|url=https://www.englandfootball.com/articles/2021/Nov/11/england-mu20s-portugal-match-report-20211111|first=Nicholas|last=Veevers|publisher=EnglandFootball.com|date=11 November 2021|access-date=12 November 2021}}</ref>

'''Erik Benjamin Nygren''' (born 8 July 2001) is a Swedish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as an [[attacking midfielder]] or [[winger (association football)|winger]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and the [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden national team]].

==Club career==
===IFK Göteborg===
Nygren began playing football at Utbynäs SK when he was 5–6 years old. In 2013, at the age of 12, he joined [[IFK Göteborg]]. After impressing in the youth teams, Nygren made his first-team debut for IFK Göteborg in a friendly game against [[Örgryte IS]] on 24 March 2018.<ref>[https://www.aftonbladet.se/sportbladet/fotboll/a/7lQnz4/16-aring-fralste-blavitt 16-åring frälste Blåvitt], aftonbladet.se, 24 March 2018</ref> Two months after his debut, in May 2018, Nygren signed his first professional contract with Göteborg, a deal running until the end of 2020, despite interest from foreign clubs such as Manchester City, Bayern Munich and Inter.<ref>[https://www.expressen.se/gt/sport/fotboll/allsvenskan/loftet-skriver-pa-for-ifk-goteborg/ "Jag tackade nej till Manchester City"], expressen.se, 23 May 2018</ref> The new contract also saw the 16-year old Nygren promoted to the first team squad.<ref>[https://ifkgoteborg.se/nyheter/a-lag/2018/a-lagskontrakt-for-benjamin/ A-lagskontrakt för Benjamin], ifkgoteborg.se, 23 May 2018</ref>

Nygren's official debut for Göteborg came against [[Torns IF]] in the [[Svenska Cupen|Swedish Cup]] on 23 August 2018, where he made a brief appearance in the 4–0 win.<ref>[https://ifkgoteborg.se/match/2018/torns-if-ifk-goteborg/?t=matchrapport Nu väntar gruppspel i cupen], ifkgoteborg.se, 23 August 2018</ref> Before the season ended, Nygren also made his [[Allsvenskan]] debut in a game against [[Djurgårdens IF Fotboll|Djurgårdens IF]] on 31 October 2018, and he played in the last three games of the season. In the following match against [[Malmö FF]], Nygren started the game<ref>[https://www.fotbollskanalen.se/allsvenskan/17-aringen-nygren-gjorde-sin-forsta-allsvenska-start-i-blavitt-betyder-valdigt/ 17-åringen Nygren gjorde sin första allsvenska start i Blåvitt: "Betyder väldigt mycket"], fotbollskanalen.se, 5 November 2011</ref> and was in the starting line-up in the final game of the season against [[Örebro SK]], scoring twice in Göteborg's 3–1 victory.<ref>[https://www.aftonbladet.se/sportbladet/fotboll/a/G19GaQ/17-aringen-matchvinnare--blev-tvamalsskytt 17-åringen matchvinnare – blev tvåmålsskytt], aftonbladet.se, 11 November 2018</ref>

===Genk===
On 20 June 2019, 17-year old Nygren joined Belgian club [[K.R.C. Genk|Genk]] in a record deal for a fee around five million euros.<ref>[https://ifkgoteborg.se/nyheter/a-lag/2019/klart-med-genk-for-benjamin/ Klart med Genk för Benjamin], ifkgoteborg.se, 20 June 2019</ref><ref>[https://www.expressen.se/gt/sport/fotboll/allsvenskan/rekordaffaren-lamnar-sverige-for-50-miljoner/ Rekordaffären: Lämnar Sverige för 50 miljoner], expressen.se, 20 June 2020</ref> He signed a deal until June 2024.<ref>[https://www.krcgenk.be/en/news/3563/benjamin-nygren-chooses-genk BENJAMIN NYGREN CHOOSES GENK!], krcgenk.be, 20 June 2019</ref> Nygren made his debut for Genk in a [[Belgian Super Cup]] win against [[K.V. Mechelen]] on 20 July 2019.<ref>[https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2019/07/20/belgium/super-cup/krc-genk/kv-mechelen/3025379/ GENK VS. MECHELEN  3 - 0], Soccerway, 20 July 2019</ref> Nygren also scored Genk's first goal in his home debut on 27 July in a 2–1 win over [[K.V. Kortrijk]].<ref>[https://www.expressen.se/gt/sport/fotboll/just-nu-nygrens-succe-mal-direkt/ Nygrens drömdebut: "En jävligt go start"], expressen.se, 26 July 2019</ref>

To get some more playing time and experience, Nygren was loaned out to Dutch side [[SC Heerenveen]] on 6 October 2020 for two seasons.<ref>[https://www.expressen.se/gt/sport/fotboll/svenske-u21-stjarnan-byter-klubb-kvalitet/ Svenske U21-stjärnan byter klubb: "Kvalitet"], expressen.se, 6 October 2020</ref> In his first season, Nygren scored seven goals in 32 games (16 from start and 16 from the bench). Already after the first season, there was talk that he was on his way out of the club because he was not getting enough playing time, but he ended up staying and started the 2021–22 season out at the Dutch club.<ref>[https://fotbolltransfers.com/site/news/139560 Benjamin Nygren öppnar för att lämna Heerenveen], fotbolltransfers.com, 1 June 2021</ref>

===Nordsjælland===
[[File:Benjamin Nygren (cropped).jpg|left|thumb|212x212px|Nygren playing for [[FC Nordsjælland|Nordsjælland]] in 2023]]
On 30 January 2022, Nygren got his loan-spell at SC Heerenveen terminated and joined [[Danish Superliga]] club [[FC Nordsjælland]] on a deal until the end of 2025.<ref>[https://fcn.dk/2022/01/fc-nordsjaelland-koeber-svensk-angriber-i-belgien/ FC NORDSJÆLLAND KØBER SVENSK ANGRIBER I BELGIEN] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220131051748/https://fcn.dk/2022/01/fc-nordsjaelland-koeber-svensk-angriber-i-belgien/ |date=2022-01-31 }}, fcn.dk, 30 January 2022</ref>

===Celtic===
On 27 June 2025, Nygren signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] champions [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on a five-year-contract for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2025/june/27/welcome-to-celtic--benjamin-nygren/|title=Welcome to Celtic, Benjamin Nygren|first=Celtic|last=FC|date=27 June 2025|website=Celtic FC}}</ref> On 3 August, he made his debut for the club in a 1–0 win against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in the league.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celtic began their Scottish Premiership season with a victory, but were far from convincing as they struggled to break down a resilient St Mirren |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c3dpe12k9z8t#Report |website=bbc.com |access-date=9 August 2025}}</ref> On 10 August, he scored his first goal for the club in a 2–0 win against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in the league.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celtic made it two wins from two at the start of their Scottish Premiership title defence |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c0kzxnrpxvyt |website=bbc.com |access-date=15 August 2025}}</ref>
On 27 December 2025, Nygren scored a double against Livingston in the league, his 9th and 10th goal of the season and his Celtic career until then.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celtic made it two wins from two at the start of their Scottish Premiership title defence |url= https://www.celticfc.com/news/2025/december/27/benjamin-nygren-delighted-with-his-double-as-hoops-win-again/ |website=celticfc.com|access-date=28 December 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
After having represented the [[Sweden men's national under-17 football team|Sweden U17]], [[Sweden men's national under-19 football team|U19]], and [[Sweden men's national under-21 football team|U21]] teams, Nygren made his full international debut for the [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden national team]] on 22 March 2025 in a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] 1–0 loss against [[Luxembourg national football team|Luxembourg]], replacing [[Jesper Karlström]] in the 82nd minute.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sweden vs. Luxembourg |url=https://www.svenskfotboll.se/matchfakta/luxemburg-sverige-landskamper-herr-senior/6155569/ |website=SvFF}}</ref> He scored his first international game goal three days later in a friendly 5–1 win against [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland]] on 25 March 2025.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=Sweden vs. Northern Ireland |url=https://www.svenskfotboll.se/matchfakta/sverige-nordirland-landskamper-herr-senior/6163347/ |website=SvFF}}</ref>

On 26 March 2026, Nygren assisted [[Viktor Gyökeres]]' opening goal in Sweden's 3–1 win against [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]] in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA second round|World Cup playoffs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/25974725.play-highest-level-epl-rate-celtic-star-highly/|title=I play at the highest level in EPL and rate Celtic star very highly|last=Meikle|first=Blair|date=27 March 2026|website=The Herald|access-date=3 April 2026}}</ref>

On 12 May 2026, Nygren was named in the Sweden squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-12 |title=Mystiskt inlägg efter petningen |url=https://www.expressen.se/sport/fotboll/landslaget/har-ar-sveriges-trupp-till-fotbolls-vm-2026/ |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=www.expressen.se |language=sv}}</ref> He made his World Cup debut on 14 June 2026, starting in a 5-1 group stage win against [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/17/285023/289273/400021474 |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=www.fifa.com}}</ref>

'''Luke McCowan''' (born 9 December 1997) is a Scottish professional footballer who plays as a [[midfielder]] or [[left wing-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].

==Early life==
McCowan was born in [[Greenock]], Scotland<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/15339303.greenock-footballer-nets-deal-at-ayr-united/|title=Greenock footballer nets deal at Ayr United|last=Corner|first=Paul John|date=11 June 2017|website=Greenock Telegraph|language=en|access-date=26 January 2019}}</ref> and attended St. Laurence's Primary School and [[Notre Dame High School, Greenock|Notre Dame High School]].<ref name=":1" />

==Career==

===Youth career===
In 2015, McCowan won the West of Scotland Title with East End United F.C.<ref name=":1" /> While at the [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]]'s youth teams, he had a busy day as he had to be up at 5am to work as a lifeguard at Waterfront Leisure Complex before attending gym sessions in the afternoon, then driving for over an hour to train with Ayr.<ref name=":1" />

===Ayr United===
On 1 July 2017, McCowan signed his first professional contract for Ayr United lasting one year.<ref name=":1" /> In his first season, he made five appearances, scoring one goal in all competitions, with one appearance coming in the [[Scottish League One|League]]. On 6 June 2019, it was announced that McCowan had been given a two-year contract after getting rave reviews from the game against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in late April.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/sport/17689825.greenock-footballer-ready-to-make-impact-at-ayr-united/|title=Greenock footballer ready to make impact at Ayr United|website=Greenock Telegraph|language=en|access-date=21 October 2019}}</ref>

=== Dundee ===
On 1 June 2021, McCowan signed a two-year deal with [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=1 June 2021|title=Luke signs|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/luke-signs/|access-date=1 June 2021|website=dundeefc.co.uk}}</ref> He made his debut for the club in the [[Scottish League Cup]] against [[Brora Rangers F.C.|Brora Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 July 2021|title=Dundee v Brora Rangers|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57825426|access-date=14 July 2021|website=BBC}}</ref> McCowan got his first competitive goal for the Dee the following week against [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Montrose v Dundee|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57915927|access-date=21 July 2021|website=BBC}}</ref> He later scored his first Premiership goal which clinched a win over [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Aberdeen woes deepen as Dundee win|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58796044|access-date=16 October 2021}}</ref>

In December 2022, McCowan scored a brace away against his former club Ayr United to help Dundee win and put them top of the [[Scottish Championship]] for Christmas.<ref>{{Cite news |title=McCowan double as Dundee beat Ayr to go top |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63995718 |access-date=23 December 2022}}</ref> He concluded a strong season with an excellent performance and goal against [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] to help Dundee clinch the Scottish Championship title.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |title=Dundee back in Premiership after eight-goal epic |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65420805 |access-date=5 May 2023}}</ref>

On 4 June 2023, Dundee announced that McCowan had signed a new two-year deal, keeping him at the club until the summer of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 June 2023 |title=McCowan signs new deal |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/mccowan-signs-new-deal/ |access-date=4 June 2023 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> McCowan marked his 100th appearance for the ''Dark Blues'' with an eventful performance, scoring a goal and receiving a red card in a comfortable away win over [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Martindale future a 'conundrum' as Dundee thrash Livingston |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68039655 |access-date=31 January 2024 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Near the end of a successful season which saw Dundee reach top six and McCowan switch from the wing to [[centre midfield]]er with ease and [[Captain (association football)|captaining]] the squad following an injury to [[Joe Shaughnessy]], McCowan was awarded as the [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners#2023–24 season|Scottish Premiership Player of the Month]] for April 2024.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Luke McCowan wins April award {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/luke-mccowan-wins-april-award |access-date=10 May 2024 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=10 May 2024 |title=Dundee: McCowan named Premiership player of the month |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cp0g79ld195o |access-date=10 May 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> At the end of the season, McCowan was named Dundee's [[Dundee F.C.#Andrew De Vries Player of the Year|Player of the Year]] and [[Dundee F.C.#Players' Player of the Year|Players' Player of the Year]].<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |date=19 May 2024 |title=2024 DSA Player of the year winners |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/24-dsa-winners/ |access-date=20 May 2024 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Celtic===
On 30 August 2024, McCowan signed for Scottish champions [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on a three-year deal, for a reported fee of around £1 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pirie |first=Mark |date=30 August 2024 |title=Luke McCowan seals Celtic transfer as midfielder makes last gasp Dundee exit |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/luke-mccowan-seals-celtic-transfer-33572507 |access-date=30 August 2024 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref> He made his Celtic debut on 1 September, coming on as a substitute in an [[Old Firm]] win over [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celtic 3-0 Rangers: Scottish Premiership |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cvg4jy57pkjt |access-date=1 September 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He opened his scoring account for his boyhood club in his next game, netting at home in a win against [[Hearts F.C.|Hearts]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celtic 2-0 Hearts: Scottish Premiership |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cm2nm8jgyp3t |access-date=14 September 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 23 October, McCowan made his [[UEFA Champions League]] debut off the bench in a draw in Italy away to [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atalanta 0-0 Celtic: Brendan Rodgers' side secure hard-fought Champions League point |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c70z2qy2eeet |access-date=23 October 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He won the [[Scottish Premiership]] title with Celtic at [[Tannadice Park]] in April 2025.<ref name=":0" />

On 3 August 2025, McCowan scored Celtic's first competitive goal of the 2025–26 season, in a 1–0 win against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporting |first=Live |title=Scottish Premiership LIVE: Celtic vs St Mirren radio commentary, updates & match report, BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c3dpe12k9z8t |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He also scored the Bhoys' fourth goal in their 6–2 win against the same opponent in the Scottish Cup semi-final on 19 April 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Duncan |first=Live ReportingThomas |title=Celtic vs St Mirren LIVE: Scottish Cup semi-final - radio, updates, team news, report, reaction, stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c3w33753j9yt |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Five days later, he extended his contract at [[Celtic Park]] until 2028.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-24 |title=Celtic: Liam Scales and Luke McCowan extend their contracts |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cr51g41mjnqo |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Style of play==
McCowan is left footed and right handed. A versatile player, he often plays across all sides of the midfield and even sometimes plays as a winger.<ref name=":1" />

'''Kasper Waarts Thenza Høgh''' (born 6 December 2000) is a Danish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[striker (association football)|striker]] for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and the [[Denmark national football team|Denmark national team]].

==Early life and career==
Høgh grew up in [[Vorup]], a suburb of [[Randers]], [[Central Denmark Region]], and began playing football with local club [[Vorup Frederiksberg Boldklub|Vorup]] at the age of four.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Matthiesen |first1=Anne Bjørnskov |title=Stolt sportschef får gåsehud: - Det er prisværdigt |url=https://www.tv2ostjylland.dk/randers/det-er-prisvaerdigt-d7f49 |access-date=17 March 2026 |work=TV 2 Østjylland |date=25 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260304025955/https://www.tv2ostjylland.dk/randers/det-er-prisvaerdigt-d7f49 |archive-date=4 March 2026 |language=da |trans-title=Proud sporting director gets goosebumps: 'It's admirable'}}</ref> He also played [[handball]] in his youth, following his parents, Ulla Waarst Sørensen and Peter Høgh, both former divisional handball players, before deciding to focus on football at the age of 12.<ref name="TV2Sport2026">{{cite news |last1=Jørgensen |first1=Marie Juul |title=Det begyndte med en kontrakt på 1000 kroner. Nu har alle fået øjnene op for ham |url=https://sport.tv2.dk/fodbold/2026-03-16-det-begyndte-med-en-kontrakt-paa-1000-kroner-nu-har-alle-faaet-oejnene-op-for-ham |access-date=17 March 2026 |work=TV 2 Sport |date=17 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260317160534/https://sport.tv2.dk/fodbold/2026-03-16-det-begyndte-med-en-kontrakt-paa-1000-kroner-nu-har-alle-faaet-oejnene-op-for-ham |archive-date=17 March 2026 |language=da-DK |trans-title=It started with a contract worth 1,000 kroner. Now everyone has taken notice of him}}</ref><ref name="HF2025">{{cite news |last1=Abildgaard |first1=Lars |title=Fra festglad Randers-knægt til fuldvoksen topangriber: Bliver han den første i rødt og hvidt? |url=https://hsfo.dk/sport/holdkammerat-ser-en-baby-der-er-blevet-voksen-bliver-kasper-hoegh-den-foerste-paa-landsholdet |access-date=17 March 2026 |work=Horsens Folkeblad |date=29 August 2025 |language=da |trans-title=From party-loving Randers youngster to fully fledged top striker: Will he be the first in red and white?}}</ref>

After progressing from Vorup, he joined the [[Randers FC|Randers]] youth system in January 2014, where he developed into a prolific goalscorer.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kasper Høgh – Landsholdsdatabasen |url=https://www.dbu.dk/landshold/landsholdsdatabasen/playerInfo/7914 |website=DBU |access-date=17 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250810155124/https://www.dbu.dk/landshold/landsholdsdatabasen/playerInfo/7914 |archive-date=10 August 2025 |language=da}}</ref> During one under-19 league season, he scored 23 goals in 19 matches, finishing as the division's top scorer despite being young for the age group.<ref name="TV2Sport2026" /><ref name="HF2025" />

==Club career==
===Randers===
In December 2017, Høgh signed a new contract with [[Randers FC|Randers]], keeping him at the club until 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kasper Høgh underskriver ny kontrakt med Randers FC |url=https://www.randersfc.dk/kasper-hoegh-underskriver-ny-kontrakt-med-randers-fc/ |website=Randers FC |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190916035954/https://www.dbu.dk/landshold/landsholdsdatabasen/playerInfo/7914 |archive-date=16 September 2019 |language=da-DK |date=7 December 2017 |url-status=dead |trans-title=Kasper Høgh signs new contract with Randers FC}}</ref> He was first included in the senior matchday squad on 4 April 2018 for a [[Danish Cup]] match against [[Silkeborg IF|Silkeborg]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Randers FC – Silkeborg 1:3 |url=https://www.soccerway.com/match/randers-fc-x0NnnfrU/silkeborg-4dCl8IE5/summary/lineups/?mid=CK5sjdI3 |website=Soccerway |publisher=Perform Group |access-date=17 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260317162412/https://www.soccerway.com/match/randers-fc-x0NnnfrU/silkeborg-4dCl8IE5/summary/lineups/?mid=CK5sjdI3 |archive-date=17 March 2026}}</ref> Eleven days later, he made his first-team debut, replacing [[Mikael Boman]] in the 80th minute of a 3–0 away defeat to [[Odense Boldklub|OB]] in the [[Danish Superliga]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Superliga OB–RFC, 2018-04-15 12:00 |url=https://superstats.dk/kampe/5344 |website=SuperStats |access-date=17 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250707203246/https://superstats.dk/kampe/5344 |archive-date=7 July 2025}}</ref>

Having established himself as the club's top scorer at under-19 level, Høgh signed a five-year contract with Randers on 19 March 2019 and was scheduled to be promoted permanently to the first-team squad from the start of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maajen |first1=Anton Græsdal |title=Randers giver U19-topscorer lang kontrakt |url=https://bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/randers-giver-u19-topscorer-lang-kontrakt/ |access-date=17 March 2026 |work=Bold |date=19 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052606/https://bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/randers-giver-u19-topscorer-lang-kontrakt/ |archive-date=26 January 2025 |language=da}}</ref> He subsequently featured only intermittently for the senior side, making 17 first-team appearances and scoring once before being loaned out in July 2020.<ref name="Tipsbladet2020">{{cite web |title=Randers udlejer ung angriber: Har brug for fast spilletid |url=https://www.tipsbladet.dk/nyhed/superliga/randers-udlejer-ung-angriber-har-brug-fast-spilletid |website=Tipsbladet |date=29 July 2020 |access-date=17 March 2026 |archive-date=7 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251207184002/https://www.tipsbladet.dk/nyhed/superliga/randers-udlejer-ung-angriber-har-brug-fast-spilletid |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 29 July 2020, Høgh joined Icelandic club [[Valur men's football|Valur]] on loan for the remainder of the calendar year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kasper Høgh udlejes til Valur |url=https://www.randersfc.dk/kasper-hoegh-udlejes-til-valur/ |website=Randers FC |date=29 July 2020 |access-date=17 March 2026 |archive-date=11 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811184948/https://www.randersfc.dk/kasper-hoegh-udlejes-til-valur/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Randers stated that, having recently returned from injury, he needed regular playing time as part of his development.<ref name="Tipsbladet2020" /> The move was later described by Randers as having been disrupted by injuries.<ref name="rfchobro">{{cite web |title=Kasper Høgh solgt til Hobro |url=https://randersfc.dk/nyheder-superliga/2021/juni-2021/kasper-hogh-solgt-til-hobro |website=Randers FC |date=18 June 2021 |access-date=17 March 2026 |archive-date=10 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260810140821/https://randersfc.dk/nyheder-superliga/2021/juni-2021/kasper-hogh-solgt-til-hobro |url-status=live }}</ref>

Høgh left Randers permanently on 18 June 2021, when he was sold to [[Danish 1st Division]] club [[Hobro IK|Hobro]]. Randers described him as a talented goalscorer who needed consistent playing time to continue his development, and stated that the club had secured a buy-back option as part of the transfer. He left having made 22 first-team appearances and scored one goal for the club.<ref name="rfchobro" />

===Hobro===
On 18 June 2021, Høgh joined [[Danish 1st Division]] club [[Hobro IK|Hobro]] on a three-year contract after leaving [[Randers FC|Randers]], who retained a buy-back clause as part of the transfer.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hobro IK køber angriber i Randers FC |url=https://hobroik.dk/hobro-ik-koeber-angriber-i-randers-fc/ |website=Hobro IK |date=18 June 2021 |access-date=17 March 2026 |archive-date=9 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250209174236/https://hobroik.dk/hobro-ik-koeber-angriber-i-randers-fc/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Randers sælger 20-årig angriber til Hobro |url=https://bold.dk/fodbold/stillinger/1-division/nyheder/randers-saelger-20-aarig-angriber-til-hobro |website=Bold |date=18 June 2021 |access-date=17 March 2026 |archive-date=10 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260810143516/https://bold.dk/fodbold/stillinger/1-division/nyheder/randers-saelger-20-aarig-angriber-til-hobro |url-status=live }}</ref> His start to the season was disrupted by injury, which kept him out of Hobro's opening fixtures.<ref>{{cite web |title=Godt nyt i Hobro: To spillere tilbage fra skade |url=https://bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/godt-nyt-i-hobro-to-spillere-tilbage-fra-skade/ |website=Bold |date=16 August 2021 |access-date=17 March 2026 |archive-date=10 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260810035505/https://bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/godt-nyt-i-hobro-to-spillere-tilbage-fra-skade/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

He went on to score four goals in twelve appearances for the club, including goals against [[Hvidovre IF|Hvidovre]] and [[Nykøbing FC|Nykøbing]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Høgh sørgede for sent Hobro-point i Hvidovre |url=https://bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/hoegh-soergede-for-sent-hobro-point-i-hvidovre/ |website=Bold |access-date=17 March 2026 |archive-date=10 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260810055443/https://bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/hoegh-soergede-for-sent-hobro-point-i-hvidovre/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Hobro med vigtig triumf mod Hvidovre |url=https://bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/hobro-med-vigtig-triumf-mod-hvidovre/ |website=Bold |date=7 November 2021 |access-date=17 March 2026 |archive-date=10 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260810070400/https://bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/hobro-med-vigtig-triumf-mod-hvidovre/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Nykøbing FC - Hobro IK - 07 Nov 2021 |url=https://hobroik.dk/kampe/nykoebing-fc-hobro-ik-07-nov-2021/ |website=Hobro IK |date=6 November 2021 |access-date=17 March 2026}}</ref>

===AaB===
On 14 January 2022, it was reported that Høgh had gone to Malta for a training camp with [[AaB Fodbold|AaB]].<ref>[https://www.bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/hoegh-med-aab-til-malta-formaliteter-fra-koeb/ Høgh med AaB til Malta: Formaliteter fra køb] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052133/https://bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/hoegh-med-aab-til-malta-formaliteter-fra-koeb |date=26 January 2025 }}, bold.dk, 14 January 2022</ref> Later in the same month, on 21 January, Høgh's transfer to the [[Danish Superliga]] club AaB was confirmed, signing a deal until June 2026.<ref>[https://aabsport.dk/nyheder/2022/januar/aab-henter-kasper-hoegh/ AaB henter Kasper Høgh] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250408205108/https://aabsport.dk/nyheder/2022/januar/aab-henter-kasper-hoegh/ |date=8 April 2025 }}, aabsport.dk, 21 January 2022</ref> Høgh got his debut for AaB on 20 February 2022 against [[FC Midtjylland|Midtjylland]], scoring the second goal in a 2–0 win.<ref>[https://www.bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/debutanten-hoegh-saenkede-fcm-i-aab-triumf/ Debutanten Høgh sænkede FCM i AaB-triumf] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230906150252/https://bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/debutanten-hoegh-saenkede-fcm-i-aab-triumf |date=6 September 2023 }}, bold.dk, 20 February 2022</ref>

===Stabæk===
On 18 January 2023, Høgh joined newly promoted Norwegian [[Eliteserien]] side [[Stabæk Fotball|Stabæk]] on a year-long loan deal with a purchase option.<ref>[https://www.stabak.no/nyheter/dansk-spiss-klar-for-stabaek DANSK SPISS KLAR FOR STABÆK] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251102213714/https://www.stabak.no/nyheter/dansk-spiss-klar-for-stabaek |date=2 November 2025 }}, stabak.no, 18 January 2023</ref> On 2 July 2023, after scoring eight goals in 14 games, Stabæk confirmed that the club had exercised the purchase option on Høgh with immediate effect, with Høgh signing a deal until the end of 2025.<ref>[https://www.stabak.no/nyheter/hogh-signerer-permanent-avtale HØGH SIGNERER PERMANENT AVTALE] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230711113831/https://www.stabak.no/nyheter/hogh-signerer-permanent-avtale |date=11 July 2023 }}, stabak.no, 2 July 2023</ref>

===Bodø/Glimt===
On 2 October 2023, it was confirmed that Høgh had signed a pre-contract with [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]], which would take effect from January 2024.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.glimt.no/nyheter/kasper-hogh-blir-glimt-spiller |title=KASPER HØGH BLIR GLIMT-SPILLER |website=glimt.no |date=2 October 2023 }}</ref> In the [[2024 FK Bodø/Glimt season|2024 season]], he finished as the club's top scorer with 12 goals as they retained their [[2024 Eliteserien|Eliteserien]] title.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/stats/_/league/NOR.1/season/2024/norwegian-eliteserien |title=Norwegian Eliteserien Scoring Stats - 2024-25 |publisher=ESPN }}</ref> He also impressed in the [[2024–25 UEFA Europa League]] as his club reached the semi-finals, scoring seven goals to share the competition's top scorer award with [[Bruno Fernandes]] and [[Ayoub El Kaabi]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0291-1bf34aa5b3f9-7a7e48b6c525-1000--2024-25-europa-league-top-scorers-three-players-finish-on-/ |title=2024/25 Europa League top scorers: Three players finish on seven |website=UEFA |date=21 May 2025 |access-date=20 January 2026 |archive-date=16 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250716104650/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0291-1bf34aa5b3f9-7a7e48b6c525-1000--2024-25-europa-league-top-scorers-three-players-finish-on-/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the [[2025 FK Bodø/Glimt season|2025 season]], he retained his club's top-scorer status with 17 goals, as Bodø/Glimt finished second in the league, one point behind [[Viking FK|Viking]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/stats/_/league/NOR.1/season/2025/norwegian-eliteserien |title=Norwegian Eliteserien Scoring Stats - 2025-26 |publisher=ESPN }}</ref> On 20 January 2026, he scored his first [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League league phase|UEFA Champions League]] goals by netting a brace in a 3–1 victory over [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Hafez |first=Shamoon |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cd0ydymjd81t |title=Bodø / Glimt 3–1 Manchester City |website=BBC Sport |date=20 January 2026 |access-date=20 January 2026 |archive-date=20 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260120171733/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cd0ydymjd81t |url-status=live }}</ref> A week later, on 28 January, he netted a goal in a 2–1 away win over [[Atlético Madrid]], securing his club's spot in the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League#Knockout phase play-offs|Champions League knockout play-offs]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/uefa-champions-league/articles/atletico-madrid-1-2-bodoglimt-sjovold-and-hogh-the-heroes-as-visitors-clinch-play-off-berth-2026-01-28 |title=Atletico Madrid 1-2 Bodo/Glimt: Sjovold and Hogh the heroes as visitors clinch play-off berth |publisher=beIN SPORTS |date=29 January 2026 |access-date=29 January 2026 |archive-date=29 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260129042239/https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/uefa-champions-league/articles/atletico-madrid-1-2-bodoglimt-sjovold-and-hogh-the-heroes-as-visitors-clinch-play-off-berth-2026-01-28 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Celtic===
On 28 July 2026, it was confirmed that Høgh had signed a contract to join [[Scottish Premiership]] Champions [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2026/july/28/celtic-delighted-to-sign-kasper-h-gh/ |title=Celtic delighted to sign Kasper Høgh |publisher=Celtic F.C. |date=28 July 2026 |access-date=28 July 2026 |archive-date=28 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260728153327/https://www.celticfc.com/news/2026/july/28/celtic-delighted-to-sign-kasper-h-gh/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He was part of the starting squad for Celtic's opening fixture against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on 3 August. Høgh scored his first goals for the club on 9 August, netting a first half hat-trick away to [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in a 5–1 win.<ref>{{cite web |last=McCulloch |first=Gerry |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2026/august/09/hat-trick-for-h-gh-in-five-star-celtic-performance/ |title=Hat-trick for Høgh in five-star Celtic performance |publisher=Celtic F.C. |date=9 August 2026 |access-date=10 August 2026 |archive-date=10 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260810165948/https://www.celticfc.com/news/2026/august/09/hat-trick-for-h-gh-in-five-star-celtic-performance/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==International career==
On 17 March 2026, Høgh received his first call-up to the [[Denmark national football team|senior Denmark squad]] from head coach [[Brian Riemer]] for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA second round#Path D|2026 FIFA World Cup qualification play-off]] against [[North Macedonia national football team|North Macedonia]].<ref name="TV2Sport2026" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Grønborg |first1=Matias |title=Riemer overrasker: Udtager Rønnow og Høgh |url=https://bold.dk/fodbold/klubber/danmark/nyheder/riemer-overrasker-udtager-ronnow-og-hogh |access-date=26 March 2026 |work=Bold |date=17 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260320104615/https://bold.dk/fodbold/klubber/danmark/nyheder/riemer-overrasker-udtager-ronnow-og-hogh |archive-date=20 March 2026 |language=da |trans-title=Riemer surprises with call-ups of Rønnow and Høgh}}</ref> He made his senior debut in the 4–0 victory over North Macedonia nine days later, coming on for [[Rasmus Højlund]] in the 81st minute.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Svedborg |first1=Mathias Leerberg |last2=Roth |first2=Christopher |title=Danmark moser modstander – er én kamp fra VM |url=https://sport.tv2.dk/live/fodbold/2026-03-26-danmark-moser-modstander-er-en-kamp-fra-vm |access-date=26 March 2026 |work=TV 2 Sport |date=26 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260326214535/https://sport.tv2.dk/live/fodbold/2026-03-26-danmark-moser-modstander-er-en-kamp-fra-vm |archive-date=26 March 2026 |language=da-DK |trans-title=Denmark thrash opponents – one match away from the World Cup}}</ref> On 31 March, Høgh made his second appearance in the play-off final against the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] in [[Prague]]. Introduced as a substitute for [[Morten Hjulmand]] in the 105th minute with Denmark trailing 2–1 in extra time, he headed in a corner delivered by [[Anders Dreyer]] in the 111th minute to equalise and force a penalty shoot-out—his first goal for the senior national team.<ref name="ESPN1">{{cite news |title=Czechia 2–2 Denmark (3–1 on pens) |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/761955/denmark-czechia |work=ESPN |date=31 March 2026 |access-date=19 April 2026 |archive-date=16 April 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260416223927/https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/761955/denmark-czechia |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Czechia 2–2 Denmark highlights (3–1 on pens): Czechia book 2026 World Cup spot with play-off final win |url=https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/02a3-2047bcf476d8-369543fe9786-1000--czechia-2-2-denmark-highlights-3-1-on-pens-czechia-book-202/ |website=UEFA.com |date=31 March 2026 |access-date=19 April 2026 |archive-date=29 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260529175844/https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/02a3-2047bcf476d8-369543fe9786-1000--czechia-2-2-denmark-highlights-3-1-on-pens-czechia-book-202/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Denmark were defeated 3–1 in the shoot-out, eliminating them from [[2026 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] qualification.<ref name="ESPN1" />

'''José Adoni Cifuentes Charcopa''' (born 12 March 1999) is an Ecuadorian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[central midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Rangers}} club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador national team]].

Cifuentes began his club career in Ecuadorian football with [[C.D. Universidad Católica del Ecuador|Universidad Católica]] and [[América de Quito]]. He joined [[MLS]] club [[Los Angeles FC]] in January 2020. He made more than 100 appearances for LAFC and helped them win the [[Supporters' Shield]] and [[MLS Cup]] double in 2022. Cifuentes signed for Rangers in August 2023.

Cifuentes played youth international football for Ecuador at [[Ecuador national under-20 football team|under-20]] and [[Ecuador national under-23 football team|under-23]] levels. He made his senior international debut in September 2019.

==Club career==
===Universidad Católica and América de Quito===
Cifuentes began his career at Ecuadorian club [[C.D. Universidad Católica del Ecuador|Universidad Católica]], having joined their youth system in 2014.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.benditofutbol.com/la-tri/jose-cifuentes-capitan-ecuadorsub20-mundialpolonia.html |title=A José Cifuentes, capitán de la Sub 20, lo rechazaron en Liga por su estatura |website=benditofutbol.com |date=19 February 2019 |access-date=18 August 2023}}</ref> He was sent on loan to [[América de Quito]] from the 2017 season until the end of the 2019 season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.benditofutbol.com/la-tri/visita-jose-cifuentes-universidad-catolica.html |title=José Cifuentes fue a saludar en la Universidad Católica |website=benditofutbol.com |date=19 June 2019 |access-date=18 August 2023}}</ref>

===Los Angeles FC===
In January 2020, Cifuentes joined [[Major League Soccer]] club [[Los Angeles FC]] on a four-year contract, for a reported transfer fee of $3 million.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.benditofutbol.com/legionarios/josecifuentes-jugara-losangelesfc-mls.html |title=José Cifuentes jugará en Los Ángeles FC de la MLS |website=benditofutbol.com |date=11 January 2020 |access-date=18 August 2023}}</ref> He helped LAFC win the [[Supporters' Shield]] and [[MLS Cup]] double in the [[2022 Los Angeles FC season|2022 season]], and reach the final of the [[2023 CONCACAF Champions League]].<ref name="LAFChonours">{{cite news |url=https://www.lafc.com/news/lafc-transfers-jose-cifuentes-to-rangers-f-c-of-the-scottish-premiership |title=LAFC Transfers José Cifuentes To Rangers F.C. Of The Scottish Premiership |website=lafc.com |date=3 August 2023 |access-date=18 August 2023}}</ref>

===Rangers===
On 3 August 2023, he signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] for an undisclosed fee, signing a four-year contract.<ref>{{ cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66348803  | title=Jose Cifuentes: Rangers sign Ecuador midfielder from Los Angeles for undisclosed fee | work=BBC Sport | date=3 August 2023 }}</ref> The reported fee paid for Cifuentes was £1.2 million ($1.5 million).<ref>{{ cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66145572  | title=Scottish Gossip: Tierney, Cifuentes, Ajeti, Johnston, Doig, Rieder, Tavares, Han, Soro, Teklic | work=BBC Sport | date=9 July 2023 }}</ref> He made his Rangers debut on 9 August, during a [[UEFA Champions League]] qualifying match against Swiss side [[Servette FC|Servette]].<ref>{{ cite news  | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66441834 | title=Rangers 2-1 Servette   | work=BBC Sport |date=9 August 2023 }}</ref>

====Loan to Cruzeiro====

On 7 February 2024, Cifuentes joined Cruzeiro on loan until the end of 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/futebol/times/cruzeiro/noticia/2024/02/07/cruzeiro-anuncia-jose-cifuentes.ghtml|title=Cruzeiro anuncia Jose Cifuentes|trans-title=Cruzeiro announces Jose Cifuentes|language=Portuguese|website=ge.globo.com}}</ref>

====Loan to Aris====

Cifuentes joined Aris on a one-year loan spell on 13 August 2024.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ο Jose Adoni Cifuentes Charcopa στον ΑΡΗ!
|url=https://arisfc.com.gr/index.php/gr/enimerosi/item/5-anakoinoseis/4141-o-jose-adoni-cifuentes-charcopa-ston-ari |website=arisfc.com.gr |date=13 August 2024}}{{in lang|el}}</ref>

====Loan to Toronto FC====

Cifuentes joined Toronto FC on loan on 22 August 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=mlssoccer |title=Toronto FC add José Cifuentes on loan from Rangers {{!}} MLSSoccer.com |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/toronto-fc-add-jose-cifuentes-on-loan-from-rangers |access-date=2025-08-22 |website=mlssoccer |language=en}}</ref> The loan is set to run until June 2026, with a purchase option included in the deal.

The midfielder did not occupy an international roster spot from the club, due to MLS rules regarding [[Green card|US Green Card]] holders and rules for Canadian [[Major League Soccer|MLS]] teams.

==International career==
===Youth===
Cifuentes played youth international football for Ecuador at [[Ecuador national under-20 football team|under-20]] and [[Ecuador national under-23 football team|under-23]] levels, making 19 appearances for the under-20 team and six appearances for the under-23 team.<ref>{{cite web |title=José Cifuentes's matches |url=https://www.besoccer.com/player/matches/r-jaramilo-325714 |website=besoccer.com |access-date=18 August 2023}}</ref> He represented the under-20 team at the [[2019 South American U-20 Championship]], which Ecuador won, and the [[2019 FIFA U-20 World Cup]], where Ecuador finished third. In the latter tournament, Cifuentes scored the opening goal in a 2–1 victory over the United States.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cifuentes: I never gave up on my dream|url=https://www.fifa.com/u20worldcup/news/cifuentes-i-never-gave-up-on-my-dream|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190609161027/https://www.fifa.com/u20worldcup/news/cifuentes-i-never-gave-up-on-my-dream|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 June 2019|publisher=[[FIFA.com]]|date=9 June 2019|accessdate=11 September 2019}}</ref>

===Senior===
Cifuentes was called up to the senior [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador national team]] for the first time for friendlies against [[Peru national football team|Peru]] and [[Bolivia national football team|Bolivia]] in September 2019.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.benditofutbol.com/la-tri/jose-cifuentes-debutara-seleccion-debut.html |title=El volante José Cifuentes debuta en la Tri mayor |website=benditofutbol.com |date=2 September 2019 |access-date=18 August 2023}}</ref> He made his senior international debut on 5 September 2019, against Peru.<ref>{{cite web|title=PERU VS. ECUADOR 0 – 1|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2019/09/05/world/friendlies/peru/ecuador/3150894/|publisher=Soccerway|accessdate=6 September 2019}}</ref>

Cifuentes was a member of Ecuador's squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] and made two appearances at the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/soccer/wc/player/231101?team=830&season=2022t|title=World Cup Player Profile – Cifuentes|access-date=26 November 2023|website=USA Today}}</ref>

Cifuentes was called up to the final 26-man Ecuador squad for the [[2024 Copa América]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eluniverso.com/deportes/futbol/ecuador-presenta-lista-oficial-para-la-copa-america-gonzalo-plata-y-robert-arboleda-quedaron-relegados-nota/|title=Ecuador presenta lista oficial para la Copa América: Gonzalo Plata y Robert Arboleda quedaron relegados|trans-title=Ecuador presents official roster for Copa America: Gonzalo Plata and Robert Arboleda left off the list|publisher=[[El Universo]]|date=29 May 2024|language=es}}</ref>
