'''Alistair William Johnston''' (born October 8, 1998) is a Canadian professional [[association football|football]] player who plays as a [[right-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and the [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada national team]].

Johnston began his senior career with [[Vaughan Azzurri]]. He later had spells with [[Major League Soccer]] teams [[Nashville SC]] and [[CF Montréal]] before signing for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in late 2022. He made his debut for Canada in 2021 and represented the country at the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] and [[2024 Copa América]].

==Early life==
Johnston was born in [[Vancouver]] to a Canadian father and an Irish mother from [[Poleglass]]. His family moved to [[Montreal]] when he was four, where he began playing soccer with [[Lakeshore SC]]. The family again moved to [[Aurora, Ontario]] when he was seven.<ref>{{Canada Soccer player|id=3772|accessdate=May 3, 2026}}</ref> There, he played youth soccer with [[Aurora FC (Canada)|Aurora FC]] and [[Richmond Hill SC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yorkregion.com/news-story/10504794-aurora-s-alistair-johnston-has-canada-s-back-on-fifa-world-cup-qualifying-trail/|title=Aurora's Alistair Johnston has Canada's back on FIFA World Cup qualifying trail|first=John|last=Cudmore|work=Aurora Banner|date=October 27, 2021|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>

He made his debut in the Canadian youth program at an under-18 camp in 2015, when he was 16.<ref name="heads">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/soccer/2020/11/19/canadian-fullback-alistair-johnston-turning-heads-with-expansion-nashville-sc.html|title=Canadian fullback Alistair Johnston turning heads with expansion Nashville SC|first=Neil|last=Davidson|date=November 19, 2020|work=[[Toronto Star]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> He played youth soccer with [[ANB Futbol]], and earned a tryout with French club [[Troyes AC]] while there.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.anbfutbol.com/news_and_buzz_june_30-2_2014.htm|publisher=[[ANB Futbol]]|title=Player Success|date=June 30, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://socceracademyalliancecanada.wordpress.com/tag/anb-futbol/page/2/|title=Seven ANB players travel to Europe|date=April 22, 2016|publisher=Soccer Academy Alliance Canada}}</ref> In 2015, he joined [[Vaughan SC]], helping them win the 2015 U-18/U-19 Disney Soccer Showcase, the 2015 OYSL U-18 League title,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://redstormsports.com/sports/mens-soccer/roster/alistair-johnston/1223|title=Alistair Johnson profile|publisher=[[St. John's Red Storm men's soccer|St. John's Red Storm]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> and the 2016 and 2017 U21 [[Ontario Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ontariosoccer.net/news_article/show/816045|title=Vaughan SC Win Fourth U-21 Men's Ontario Cup in a Row|date=July 23, 2017|publisher=[[Ontario Soccer Association]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Johnston attended [[St. John's University (New York City)|St. John's University]] for two years, before moving to [[Wake Forest University]] in 2018 in search of a bigger challenge both in soccer and academically. He switched positions from central midfield to right-back upon joining Wake Forest.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/sports/article/canadian-alistair-johnston-looks-to-take-next-soccer-step-in-mls-superdraft/|title=Canadian Alistair Johnston looks to take next soccer step in MLS SuperDraft|first=Neil|last=Davidson|date=January 9, 2020|publisher=[[CTV News]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
{{unreferenced section|date=June 2026}}
While in college, Johnston returned to Canada to play with [[League1 Ontario]] side [[Vaughan Azzurri]] from 2015 to 2019 during the college offseason. He played in the [[2019 Canadian Championship]] for Vaughan Azzurri and was sent off in the second leg of the away goals defeat to the [[HFX Wanderers FC|HFX Wanderers]].

===Nashville SC===
On January 9, 2020, Johnston was selected 11th overall by [[Nashville SC]] in the [[2020 MLS SuperDraft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/mls/mls-draft-ryan-raposo-selected-vancouver-whitecaps-1.5421252 |title=Crop of Canadians taken early in MLS draft |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]] |date=January 9, 2020|first=Neil|last=Davidson|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> He officially signed with the club on February 25, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nashvillesc.com/post/2020/02/25/nashville-sc-extends-offers-2020-mls-superdraft-selections |title=Nashville SC Extends Offers to 2020 MLS SuperDraft Selections |date=February 25, 2020|access-date=May 3, 2026|website=Nashville SC}}</ref> Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], which included Nashville withdrawing from the [[MLS is Back Tournament]] due to an outbreak amongst the team,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://torontoobserver.ca/2020/06/03/aurora-soccer-player-johnston-focuses-on-positive-mental-state-during-pandemic/|title=Aurora soccer player Johnston focuses on positive mental state during pandemic|first=Keegan|last=Lavigne|date=June 3, 2020|work=The Toronto Observer|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> his debut was delayed until August 12 against [[FC Dallas]], coming on as a substitute.<ref name=heads /> He made his first start four days later, also against Dallas.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2020/08/17/nashville-sc-youngster-alistair-johnston-hailed-coach-gary-smith-after-impressive|title=Nashville SC youngster Alistair Johnston hailed by coach Gary Smith after impressive first MLS start|date=August 17, 2020|first=Jason|last=Le Miere|publisher=[[Major League Soccer]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> He helped the club reach the [[MLS Cup Playoffs|MLS Playoffs]] in their debut season, making 18 appearances.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fox17.com/sports/scoreboard/one-on-one-with-nashville-scs-alistair-johnston-on-2020-season-and-a-look-at-playoffs|title=One-on-one with Nashville SC's Alistair Johnston on 2020 season and a look at playoffs|first=Tatum|last=Everett|date=November 16, 2020|publisher=[[WZTV|WZTV Nashville - Fox 17]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>

On September 22, 2021, Johnston scored his first MLS goal in a 5–1 victory over [[Inter Miami]].<ref>{{Cite web|title= Recap: Inter Miami CF 1, Nashville SC 5|url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/recap-inter-miami-cf-1-nashville-sc-5|publisher=[[Major League Soccer]]|accessdate=September 22, 2021}}</ref> In December 2021, Nashville announced they were exercising Johnston's contract option, keeping him at the club through the [[2022 Major League Soccer season|2022 MLS season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nashvillesc.com/news/nashville-soccer-club-announces-2021-roster-decisions|title=Nashville Soccer Club Announces 2021 Roster Decisions|date=December 10, 2021|publisher=[[Nashville SC]]}}</ref>

===CF Montréal===
On December 23, 2021, [[CF Montréal]] acquired Johnston from Nashville in exchange for $1 million in allocation money, with Nashville also retaining a percentage of a transfer fee in a future sale.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tsn.ca/alistair-johnston-cf-montreal-nashville-sc-canada-canmnt-1.1738401|title=CF Montreal acquires CanMNT's Johnston|publisher=[[The Sports Network|TSN]]|date=December 23, 2021}}</ref> Montreal confirmed the deal on December 27 and announced Johnston had also signed a new contract taking him through 2023, with options for 2024 and 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.cfmontreal.com/news/cf-montreal-acquires-canadian-international-alistair-johnston|date=December 27, 2021|title=CF Montréal acquires Canadian international Alistair Johnston|publisher=[[CF Montréal]]}}</ref>

He made his debut for Montreal on February 23, as a substitute against [[Liga MX]] side [[Santos Laguna]] in the club's second leg of their [[2022 CONCACAF Champions League]] tie.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.cfmontreal.com/news/live-at-8pm-montreal-v-santos-laguna|title=CF Montréal 3–0 Santos Laguna|date=February 23, 2022|publisher=[[CF Montréal]]}}</ref> Johnston scored his first goal for Montreal on May 14, the second goal in a 2–0 victory against [[Charlotte FC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.cfmontreal.com/news/live-at-7pm-charlotte-fc-v-cf-montreal|title=Charlotte FC 0–2 CF Montréal|date=May 14, 2022|publisher=[[CF Montréal]]}}</ref>

===Celtic===
[[File:Alistair Johnston, Rangers v Celtic 2 January 2023.jpg|thumb|upright=0.55|Johnston with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2023]]

In December 2022, CF Montréal announced they had transferred Johnston to [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], taking effect January 1, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.cfmontreal.com/news/alistair-johnston-transferred-to-celtic-fc|title=Alistair Johnston transferred to Celtic FC|date=December 3, 2023|publisher=[[CF Montréal]]}}</ref> He signed a 5-year contract with the [[Glasgow]] club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2022/december/03/celtic-delighted-to-sign-canadian-internationalist-alistair-johnston-on-five-year-deal/|title=Celtic delighted to sign Canadian internationalist Alistair Johnston on five-year deal|date=December 3, 2022|publisher=[[Celtic F.C.]]}}</ref> Upon the announcement, Johnston stated at a press conference that former Celtic and current CF Montréal midfielder [[Victor Wanyama]] was a major influence on his decision to move to ''the Bhoys.''<ref>{{Cite web |last= |title=Agent Victor Wanyama: Celtic FC transfer easy sell for Alistair Johnston |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/agent-victor-wanyama-celtic-fc-transfer-easy-sell-for-alistair-johnston |access-date=January 8, 2023 |website=MLSSoccer.com |publisher=[[Major League Soccer]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |title=Alistair Johnston reveals Wanyama Celtic advice | date=December 13, 2022 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zc2FgIxvmp0 |language=en |access-date=January 8, 2023}}</ref>

Johnston made his debut for Celtic on January 2, starting against [[Old Firm|rivals]] [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and playing the entire match in a 2–2 away draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2023/january/02/kyogo-strikes-late-at-ibrox-as-honours-even-in-glasgow-derby-/|title=Kyogo strikes late at Ibrox as honours even in Glasgow derby|first=Ryan|last=Maher|date=January 2, 2023|publisher=[[Celtic F.C.]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> He then made his home debut a few days later, starting again in a 2–0 win against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scots Prem (Sky Sports) |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/celtic-vs-kilmarnock/teams/465140 |access-date=January 8, 2023 |publisher=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref>

On March 5, 2023, Johnston scored his first goal for Celtic in a 5–1 away win against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 5, 2023 |title=St Mirren 1-5 Celtic: Ruthless Scottish Premiership leaders restore nine-point lead |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64775002 |access-date=May 3, 2026 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Johnston ended his first season at [[Celtic Park]] having helped them to a domestic treble, winning the [[2022–23 Scottish Premiership|Premiership]], the [[2023 Scottish League Cup final (February)|League Cup]] and the [[2023 Scottish Cup final|Scottish Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=FC |first=Celtic |date=June 3, 2023 |title=Eightsome Reel… Celtic make history with another Treble triumph |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2023/june/03/eightsome-reel--celtic-make-history-with-another-treble-triumph/ |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Celtic FC |language=en}}</ref> On November 22, 2024, Johnston signed a new five-year contract with Celtic, keeping him at the club until 2029.<ref>{{Cite web |last=FC |first=Celtic |date=November 22, 2024 |title=Alistair Johnston signs new Celtic contract |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2024/november/22/alistair-johnston-signs-new-celtic-contract/ |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Celtic FC |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Alistair Johnston Canada v Qatar 18 June 2026-149.jpg|thumb|271x271px|Johnston with [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada]] at the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]]]]
Johnston accepted an invitation to the [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada national team]] camp in January 2021.<ref name="can2021">{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/canada-soccer-ayo-akinola-national-team-camp-1.5853734|title=TFC's Ayo Akinola accepts invite to Canada national team camp|date=December 23, 2020|first=Neil|last=Davidson|publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> He made his debut for Canada on March 25, 2021, as a 69th-minute substitute against [[Bermuda national football team|Bermuda]] in the first round of [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONCACAF)|2022 FIFA World Cup qualifying]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/canada-honduras-world-cup-qualifying-soccer-1.5964733|title=Larin, Davies team up to help Canada crush Bermuda in World Cup qualifier|accessdate=March 25, 2021}}</ref> He scored his first goal for his country in the following match, an 11–0 win against the [[Cayman Islands national football team|Cayman Islands]], which became the largest victory in the team's history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://northerntribune.ca/canada-world-cup-cayman-islands/|first=John|last=Jacques|title=Canada Coasts Past Cayman Islands In Historic Eleven-Goal Win|date=March 29, 2021|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>

In June 2021, Johnston was named to the 60-man preliminary squad for the [[2021 CONCACAF Gold Cup]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tsn.ca/canada-names-60-man-preliminary-roster-for-next-month-s-gold-cup-1.1656962 |date=June 18, 2021 |title=Davies, David highlight Canada's preliminary roster for Gold Cup}}</ref> and on July 1 he was named to the final squad.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/canada-soccer-announces-2021-concacaf-gold-cup-roster |title=Canada Soccer Announces 2021 Gold Cup Roster |date=July 1, 2021 |publisher=[[Canadian Soccer Association]]}}</ref>

In November 2022, Johnston was called up to Canada's squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://canpl.ca/article/canada-announces-26-man-squad-for-2022-fifa-world-cup-in-qatar|date=November 13, 2022|title=Canada announces 26-man squad for 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar|publisher=[[Canadian Premier League]]|first=Charlie|last=O'Connor-Clarke|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> where he played in all three of Canada's matches. In June 2023, he was named to Canada's 23-man squad for the [[2023 CONCACAF Nations League Finals]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Former CPLers Loturi, Zator called up by Canada for 2023 Concacaf Nations League Finals|date=June 7, 2023|url=https://canpl.ca/article/canada-canmnt-2023-concacaf-nations-league-final-roster|first=Mitchell|last=Tierney|publisher=[[Canadian Premier League]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>

In June 2024, Johnston was named in Canada's squad for the [[2024 Copa América]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/canmnt-announce-2024-copa-america-roster|title=CANMNT ANNOUNCE 2024 COPA AMÉRICA ROSTER|date=June 15, 2024|publisher=[[Canadian Soccer Association]]}}</ref> Following the conclusion of the competition, he was named in the Team of the Tournament, being the only non-South American player included.<ref name="tott">{{Cite web|url=https://copaamerica.com/en/news/best-xi-team-tournament-copa-america-2024|title=The CONMEBOL Copa América 2024™ Best XI|website=copaamerica.com|date=July 31, 2024}}</ref> In July 2025, Johnston was called up to Canada's squad for the [[2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.onesoccer.ca/a/canmnt-announce-2025-conacaf-gold-cup-squad-roster-canada-soccer|date=July 5, 2025|title=CanMNT name full-strength squad for 2025 Concacaf Gold Cup|first=Mitchell|last=Tierney}}</ref>

In May 2026, Johnston was named to Canada's 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://northerntribune.ca/world-cup-2026-canada-squad/|first=John|last=Jacques|date=May 29, 2026|title=Here’s The Canada World Cup Roster|work=Northern Tribune}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Johnston's younger brother, [[Malcolm Johnston (soccer)|Malcolm]], is also a football player and was selected in the first round of the [[2023 MLS SuperDraft]] by [[New York City F.C.|New York City]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://celtsarehere.com/proud-older-brother-moment-celtic-stars-brother-drafted-by-mls-club/|title= 'Proud Older Brother Moment' – Celtic Star's Brother Drafted by MLS Club|website=Celtsarehere.com|date=December 22, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/alistair-johnston-malcolm-mls-super-draft-canada-soccer-1.6693147|title=Canada's Malcolm Johnston looks to follow brother Alistair ahead of MLS SuperDraft|website=cbc.ca|publisher=[[CBC Sports]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>

Johnston proposed to his girlfriend in July 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.glasgowlive.co.uk/news/glasgow-news/inside-celtic-star-alistair-johnstons-29556498|title=Inside Celtic star Alistair Johnston's engagement at stunning Scots beauty spot|first=Fahad|last=Tariq|date=July 17, 2024|website=Glasgow Live|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Callaghan |first=Joe |date=March 20, 2025 |title=Canada’s Alistair Johnston: ‘Our country is under threat, under attack’ |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/mar/20/alistair-johnston-canada-nations-league-celtic |access-date=May 3, 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

'''Ivor Pandur''' (born 25 March 2000) is a Croatian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[Croatia national football team|Croatia national team]].<ref>{{Soccerway|ivor-pandur/557480}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Rijeka===
Pandur made his professional debut for [[HNK Rijeka|Rijeka]] in October 2019 in a [[2019–20 Croatian Football Cup|cup]] tie against Buje.<ref>{{cite web |title=Buje vs. Rijeka – 1 October 2019 |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2019/10/01/croatia/hr-nogometni-cup/nk-buje/hnk-rijeka/3160642/ |website=Soccerway |publisher=Perform Group |accessdate=16 May 2023 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220926044236/https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2019/10/01/croatia/hr-nogometni-cup/nk-buje/hnk-rijeka/3160642/ |archivedate=26 September 2022}}</ref> He then made his [[2019–20 Croatian First Football League|league]] debut on 14 December 2019, playing the full 90 minutes of a 3–1 victory over [[NK Varaždin (2012)|Varaždin]].<ref>{{cite press release|title=Ivor Pandur nakon Varaždina: Ovo je bilo nešto o čemu sam dugo maštao|url=http://www.nk-rijeka.hr/vijest/ivor-pandur-nakon-varazdina-ovo-je-bilo-nesto-o-cemu-sam-dugo-mastao/|date=31 August 2020|publisher=[[HNK Rijeka|Rijeka]]|accessdate=1 September 2020|language=hr|archivedate=19 October 2020|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019210134/http://nk-rijeka.hr/vijest/ivor-pandur-nakon-varazdina-ovo-je-bilo-nesto-o-cemu-sam-dugo-mastao/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Hellas Verona===
On 31 August 2020, Pandur signed with Italian [[Serie A]] club [[Hellas Verona F.C.|Hellas Verona]] a five-year contract.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Ivor Pandur potpisao za Veronu: Rijeka je moj dom i jednog dana ću se vratiti|url=http://www.nk-rijeka.hr/vijest/ivor-pandur-potpisao-za-veronu-rijeka-je-moj-dom-i-jednog-dana-cu-se-vratiti/|language=hr|date=31 August 2020|publisher=[[HNK Rijeka|Rijeka]]|accessdate=1 September 2020|archivedate=1 September 2020|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200901064731/http://www.nk-rijeka.hr/vijest/ivor-pandur-potpisao-za-veronu-rijeka-je-moj-dom-i-jednog-dana-cu-se-vratiti/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|title=Ufficiale: Ivor Pandur a titolo definitivo dall'HNK Rijeka|url=https://www.hellasverona.it/2020/08/31/ufficiale_ivor_pandur_a_titolo_definitivo_dall_hnk_rijeka|publisher=[[Hellas Verona]]|language=it|date=31 August 2020|accessdate=1 September 2020}}</ref> He made his debut on 28 October in a [[2020–21 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]] tie with [[Venezia F.C.|Venezia]] that ended 3–3 after extra time, with Verona progressing thanks to Pandur saving two [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalties]] in the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|shoot-out]].<ref>{{cite web|date=28 October 2020|title=Pandur debitirao s dva obranjena penala za Veronu: "Mogao sam i bolje"|url=https://www.index.hr/clanak.aspx?id=2225718|accessdate=14 May 2021|website=Index.hr|language=hr}}</ref> He made his [[2020–21 Serie A|league]] debut on 9 May 2021 in a 1–1 draw with [[Torino F.C.|Torino]].<ref>{{cite web|last=[[Croatian News Agency|HINA]]|date=9 May 2021|title=Bivši vratar Rijeke Ivor Pandur debitirao u remiju protiv Torina, petarda Rome kod fenjeraša|url=https://www.novilist.hr/sport/nogomet/bivsi-vratar-rijeke-ivor-pandur-debitirao-u-remiju-protiv-torina-petarda-rome-kod-fenjerasa/|accessdate=14 May 2021|website=Novi list|language=hr}}</ref>

===Fortuna Sittard===
On 7 July 2022, Pandur agreed to a one-season loan with option to buy at [[Eredivisie]] club [[Fortuna Sittard]].<ref>{{cite press release |title=Ivor Pandur en Vasilios Sourlis op huurbasis naar Sittard |url=https://www.fortunasittard.nl/ivor-pandur-en-vasilios-sourlis-op-huurbasis-naar-sittard/ |website=[[Fortuna Sittard]] |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230208045548/https://www.fortunasittard.nl/ivor-pandur-en-vasilios-sourlis-op-huurbasis-naar-sittard/ |archivedate=8 February 2023 |language=nl |date=7 July 2022 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut on 27 August, taking over the starting job from [[Yanick van Osch]] in a 2–1 league loss to [[SC Heerenveen]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Caelen |first1=Sem |title=Van Osch: 'Klaar zijn voor Fortuna of een andere club' |url=https://www.1limburg.nl/sport/1897684/van-osch-klaar-zijn-voor-fortuna-of-een-andere-club |accessdate=14 April 2023 |work=1limburg |date=6 December 2022 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221206204310/https://www.1limburg.nl/sport/1897684/van-osch-klaar-zijn-voor-fortuna-of-een-andere-club |archivedate=6 December 2022 |language=nl}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=sc Heerenveen – Fortuna Sittard 2:1 (Eredivisie 2022/2023, 4. Round) |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/report/eredivisie-2022-2023-sc-heerenveen-fortuna-sittard/ |website=worldfootball.net |publisher=HEIM:SPIEL |accessdate=16 May 2023}}</ref> He remained a starter throughout the [[2022–23 Eredivisie|season]] for Fortuna.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ivor Pandur » Eredivisie 2022/2023 |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/player_summary/ivor-pandur/ned-eredivisie-2022-2023/fortuna-sittard/3/ |website=worldfootball.net |publisher=HEIM:SPIEL |accessdate=16 May 2023}}</ref>

On 28 April 2023, the club exercised their purchase option and signed Pandur to a four-year contract, starting from 1 July.<ref>{{cite press release |title=Fortuna licht koopoptie in contract Ivor Pandur |url=https://fortunasittard.nl/nieuws/fortuna-licht-koopoptie-in-contract-ivor-pandur |website=Fortuna Sittard |accessdate=16 May 2023 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230510134717/https://fortunasittard.nl/nieuws/fortuna-licht-koopoptie-in-contract-ivor-pandur |archivedate=10 May 2023 |language=nl |date=28 April 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Schreurs |first1=Joost |title=Fortuna licht koopoptie in contract Ivor Pandur |url=https://www.1limburg.nl/sport/2178656/fortuna-licht-koopoptie-in-contract-ivor-pandur |accessdate=16 May 2023 |work=1limburg |date=28 April 2023 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230514080152/https://www.1limburg.nl/sport/2178656/fortuna-licht-koopoptie-in-contract-ivor-pandur |archivedate=14 May 2023 |language=nl}}</ref>

===Hull City===
On 20 January 2024, Pandur signed a three-and-a-half-year deal with [[EFL Championship]] side [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] for an undisclosed fee, rumoured to be around €2,000,000.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68042386|title=Ivor Pandur: Hull City sign Croatian goalkeeper from Fortuna Sittard|work=BBC Sport|date=20 January 2024|accessdate=20 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://the72.co.uk/2025/09/20/hull-city-ivor-pandur-estimated-worth/|title=Less than Giles: Data estimates how much Hull City 'keeper Ivor Pandur is worth after summer interest|work=the72.co.uk|date=17 September 2025|accessdate=24 October 2025}}</ref> After nearly eight months at the club, on 10 August, he made his debut in the opening game of the [[2024–25 Hull City A.F.C. season|2024–25]] season, a 1–1 home draw with [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wearehullcity.co.uk/news/2024/august/10/hull-city-1-1-bristol-city/|title=Hull City 1–1 Bristol City|date=10 August 2024|publisher=Hull City A.F.C.|accessdate=10 August 2024}}</ref> Pandur became the Tigers' starting goalkeeper for the remainder of the campaign, with his performances often garnering praise. In particular, in a match against [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] on 14 April 2025, he was cited as the sole reason Hull earned a 1–1 draw amidst their fight for league survival. He won the Player of the Match award as a result of his efforts.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c39jd39x1eyo|title=Pandur a 'one-man barrier' in Coventry draw|work=BBC Sport|date=15 April 2025|accessdate=18 April 2025}}</ref> Ultimately, the team survived relegation on the final day,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cd02mrpkd4xt|title=Portsmouth 1–1 Hull City|work=BBC Sport|date=3 May 2025|accessdate=24 October 2025}}</ref> and Pandur received further acclaim for his role in the achievement. On 6 May, the club announced that the Croatian had won the Player of the Year award, Players' Player of the Year award, and Supporters' Player of the Year award for the [[2024–25 Hull City A.F.C. season|2024–25]] season.<ref name="POTY">{{cite news|url=https://www.wearehullcity.co.uk/news/2025/may/06/hull-city-awards-2024-25-round-up/|title=Hull City Awards 2024/25: Round-Up|work=Hull City A.F.C.|date=6 May 2025|accessdate=6 May 2025}}</ref>

That summer, several clubs expressed an interest in buying Pandur. Links to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] were initially thought to be true, however they were eventually reported to be "wide of the mark".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hulldailymail.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/hull-city-prepared-ivor-pandur-10459862|title=Hull City prepared for Ivor Pandur transfer decision with late bid now expected|work=Hull Daily Mail|date=29 August 2025|accessdate=24 October 2025}}</ref> Elsewhere, [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] expressed a genuine desire to sign the 25-year-old, but they were unwilling to meet Hull's asking price of £5,000,000. A transfer to [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] was also briefly discussed, as was a move to German side [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]], whilst a return to [[Northeast Italy|northeastern Italy]] with [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]] was considered less likely.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://footballleagueworld.co.uk/hull-city-boost-middlesbrough-leicester-werder-bremen-swerve-ivor-pandur/#:~:text=Interest%20in%20the%2025%2Dyear,emergency%20loans%20and%20free%20transfers.|title=Hull City get big transfer boost as Middlesbrough, Leicester City & Werder Bremen swerve Ivor Pandur|work=the72.co.uk|date=1 September 2025|accessdate=24 October 2025}}</ref> In the end, Pandur remained in [[East Riding of Yorkshire|East Yorkshire]] for the upcoming [[2025–26 Hull City A.F.C. season|2025–26]] season, later stating that he had always planned to stay with Hull, regardless of any interest from other clubs.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hulldailymail.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/ivor-pandur-makes-hull-city-10578373|title=Ivor Pandur makes Hull City transfer confession after 'tough' summer of exit talk|work=Hull Daily Mail|date=17 October 2025|accessdate=24 October 2025}}</ref> The return of football saw Pandur struggle amid the news of his possible departure. Although overall results were good, Hull's leaky defence had conceded 16 goals in their first nine games of the campaign, with a home match on 30 September against [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] proving to be a personal nadir for the Croatian.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hulldailymail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/ivor-pandur-makes-confession-early-10553518|title=Ivor Pandur makes confession about early season Hull City form after vital contribution|work=Hull Daily Mail|date=6 October 2025|accessdate=24 October 2025}}</ref> The visitors scored twice in the opening 10 minutes, with Pandur at fault for the second goal. Having saved an effort from [[Lewis Gibson (footballer)|Lewis Gibson]], he cleared the ball straight to [[Benjamin Whiteman|Ben Whiteman]], who set up [[Michael Smith (footballer, born 1991)|Michael Smith]] to score into a scarcely defended net.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cwynrd7g07qt|title=Hull City 2–2 Preston North End|work=BBC Sport|date=30 September 2025|accessdate=24 October 2025}}</ref> Despite his poor performances up to that point, Pandur returned to his expected standard on 4 October, saving a late penalty from [[Harrison Burrows]] to secure an important 1–0 home win over [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cdjz78jngrvt|title=Hull City 1–0 Sheffield United|work=BBC Sport|date=4 October 2025|accessdate=24 October 2025}}</ref>

===Rangers===
On 30 June 2026, [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] announced the signing of Pandur on a four-year deal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/rangers-announce-signing-of-ivor-pandur-from-hull-city/1XKF2aiaLWotZp38qik8Tv|title=Rangers Announce Signing Of Ivor Pandur From Hull City|work=Rangers|date=30 June 2026|accessdate=30 June 2026}}</ref>

== International career ==
Pandur was capped several times by [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] at youth level.<ref name="HNS">{{cite web |title=Ivor Pandur |url=https://hns-cff.hr/en/players/209341/ivor-pandur/ |website=[[Croatian Football Federation]] |accessdate=16 May 2023 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221008091855/https://hns-cff.hr/en/players/209341/ivor-pandur/ |archivedate=8 October 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wearehullcity.co.uk/news/2024/january/20/the-story-so-far--ivor-pandur/|title=The Story So Far: Ivor Pandur|publisher=Hull City A.F.C.|date=20 January 2024|accessdate=24 October 2025}}</ref> On 22 September 2025, he was named as a standby member of the senior squad for fixtures against the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] and [[Gibraltar national football team|Gibraltar]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://hns.team/vijesti/29975/izbornik-dalic-objavio-popis-igraca-za-susrete-s-ceskom-i-gibraltarom/|title=Izbornik Dalić objavio popis igrača za susrete s Češkom i Gibraltarom|work=hns.team|date=22 September 2025|accessdate=24 October 2025}}</ref> The following month, Pandur announced his hopes of being selected for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c5y9xz9rpeqo|title=Pandur hopes performances will earn World Cup spot|work=BBC Sport|date=17 October 2025|accessdate=24 October 2025}}</ref> Then, on 10 November, he received his first senior call-up for upcoming qualifiers against the [[Faroe Islands national football team|Faroe Islands]] and [[Montenegro national football team|Montenegro]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cy8v2z3mev5o|title=Hull keeper Pandur receives first senior Croatia call-up|work=BBC Sport|date=10 November 2025|accessdate=10 November 2025}}</ref>

On 18 May 2026, Pandur was selected in the 26-man squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/croatia-squad-named|title=Dalic blends youth and experience with Croatia squad|date=18 May 2026|access-date=18 June 2026|language=en}}</ref>

'''Sebastian Tounekti''' (born 13 July 2002) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left winger]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]. Born in Norway, he plays for the [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia national team]].

==Club career==

=== Tromsdalen ===
Tounekti was born in [[Tromsø (city)|Tromsø]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.altomfotball.no/element.do?cmd=player&personId=347029&tournamentId=1&seasonId=342&teamId=307&useFullUrl=false |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200617043212/http://www.altomfotball.no/element.do?cmd=player&personId=347029&tournamentId=1&seasonId=342&teamId=307&useFullUrl=false |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 June 2020 |title=Sebastian Tounekti |work=altomfotball.no |publisher=TV2 |accessdate=17 June 2020}}</ref> He made his senior debut for [[Tromsdalen UIL|Tromsdalen]] on 30 September 2018 against [[Ullensaker/Kisa IL|Ullensaker/Kisa]]; Tromsdalen won 3–0.<ref name="nff">{{NFF|2748925}}</ref>

=== Bodø/Glimt===
He made his senior debut for [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]] on 16 June 2020 against [[Viking FK|Viking]]; Bodø/Glimt won 4–2. He scored his first and only goal in October 2020 against Molde.<ref name=nff/> Tounekti and [[George Lewis (footballer, born 2000)|George Lewis]] were both players at Tromsdalen who were discovered by clubs other than Tromsdalen's larger neighbour [[Tromsø IL]], the failure to pick them up being lamented by Tromsø fans. Tounekti was part of the Bodø/Glimt squad that won the Eliteserien title in 2020. He also appeared as a substitute in both legs of the UEFA Champions League qualifying round against Legia Warsaw.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.aftenposten.no/sport/fotball/i/dOXyl1/de-seks-stoerste-talentene-som-glapp-for-til|title=De seks største talentene som glapp for TIL|date=3 June 2020|work=Aftenposten|language=no|access-date=30 October 2021}}</ref>

=== Groningen ===
In the end of the transfer window, the 19-year-old joined Dutch Eredivisie club FC Groningen on loan from Bodø/Glimt for the remainder of the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nrk.no/tromsogfinnmark/tounekti-leies-ut-til-fc-groningen-1.15630647|title=Tounekti leies ut til FC Groningen|date=31 August 2021|website=NRK}}</ref>

=== Haugesund ===
On 30 August 2022, Tounekti signed a four-year contract with the Eliteserien club. He had his breakthrough during the 2024 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.glimt.no/nyheter/sebastian-tounekti-selges-til-haugesund|title=Sebastian Tounekti selges til Haugesund|website=Bodø/Glimt}}</ref>

=== Hammarby ===
Tounekti moved to Sweden on 9 February 2025, joining [[Allsvenskan]] side [[Hammarby Fotboll]] on a five-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hammarby värvar Sebastian Tounekti |url=https://www.hammarbyfotboll.se/nyheter/hammarby-vaervar-sebastian-tounekti |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=Hammarby Fotboll}}</ref>

=== Celtic ===
Tounetki joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on 1 September 2025 on a five-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-09-01 |title=Welcome to Celtic, Sebastian Tounekti |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2025/september/01/welcome-to-celtic--/ |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=Celtic FC |language=en}}</ref> He made his debut against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] at [[Rugby Park]] on 14 September 2025. He scored his first goal on the 21 September 2025 in a [[Scottish League Cup]] [[2025-26 Scottish League Cup#Quarter-finals|Quarter final]] 4-0 win against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] at [[Firhill Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= Dowden |first= Martin |date=2025-09-21 |title=Partick Thistle 4-0 Celtic: Brendan Rodgers' side cruise into last four for Rangers showdown|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c5yg8ygm4p7t |access-date=2026-06-03 |website=[[BBC Sport]] |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
Tounekti was born in Norway to a Tunisian father and Norwegian mother.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nettavisen.no/12-95-3424102755|title=Tounekti velger Tunisia – tatt ut på A-landslaget|date=16 March 2021|website=Nettavisen}}</ref> He was a youth international for Norway up until [[Norway national under-19 football team|U19]] level.<ref name=nff/> He was called up to represent the senior [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia national team]] on 19 March 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kawarji.com/actu-64765-en-la-liste-de-mondher-kebaier-pour-affronter-la-libye-et-la-guinee-equatoriale.html|title=EN : La liste de Mondher Kebaier pour affronter la Libye et la Guinée Equatoriale|website=www.kawarji.com}}</ref> He debuted with Tunisia in a 3–0 [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification]] win over [[Mauritania national football team|Mauritania]] on 7 October 2021.<ref name="Global Sports Archive 2021">{{cite web | title=Match Report of Tunisia vs Mauritania - 2021-10-07 - WC Qualification | website=Global Sports Archive | date=7 October 2021 | url=https://globalsportsarchive.com/match/soccer/2021-10-07/tunisia-vs-mauritania/2358534/ | access-date=7 October 2021}}</ref>

Tounekti did not receive another call up for four years, returning for an international friendly against [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]] in June 2025. He also played in a World Cup playoff against Equatorial Guinea in September 2025.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/celtic/latest-celtic-news/celtic-star-lands-world-cup-spot-in-dramatic-fashion-as-hamza-igamanes-dream-spell-after-rangers-goes-on-5308367|title=Celtic star lands World Cup spot in dramatic fashion as Igamane's dream spell after Rangers goes on|last=Atkinson|first=Mark|date=8 September 2025|website=The Scotsman}}</ref>

Tounekti was named to Tunisia’s 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] on 15 May 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/tunisia-squad-named-sabri-lamouchi |title=Lamouchi names much-changed Tunisia squad |access-date=2026-06-21 |website=www.fifa.com}}</ref> He made his World Cup debut against [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]] on 14 June 2026 and earned his first World Cup start against [[Japan national football team|Japan]] on 21 June 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/17/285023/289273/400021474 |title=Sweden 5–1 Tunisia |access-date=2026-06-21 |website=www.fifa.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/tunisia-japan-match-report-highlights |title=Historic Japan win sends Tunisia crashing out |access-date=2026-06-21 |website=www.fifa.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Tounekti is the cousin of the Norwegian footballer [[Bryan Fiabema]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aftenposten.no/sport/fotball/i/lEAyGL/sebastian-18-scoret-faa-timer-etter-at-soeskenbarnet-herjet-for-chelsea-jeg-maatte-score-siden-han-leverte-saa-bra|title=Sebastian (18) scoret få timer etter at søskenbarnet herjet for Chelsea: – Jeg måtte score siden han leverte så bra|date=18 October 2020|website=www.aftenposten.no}}</ref>

'''Bojan Miovski''' ({{langx|mk|Бојан Миовски}}; born 24 June 1999) is a Macedonian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[North Macedonia national football team|North Macedonia national team]].<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|bojan-miovski}}</ref>

==Club career==
=== Early career ===
Miovski started his professional career at the age of 18 by making his [[Macedonian First Football League|Macedonian First League]] debut for [[FK Bregalnica Štip|Bregalnica]] in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Miguel|last=Ruiz|title=Quién es Bojan Miovski, el nuevo 'killer' que el Girona eligió a conciencia para olvidarse de Dobvyk?|trans-title= Who is Bojan Miovski, the new 'killer' that caused Girona to forget Dobvyk?|url=https://www.relevo.com/futbol/liga-primera/girona-quiere-repetir-jugada-delantero-20240825122238-nt.html|website=Relevo|date=25 August 2024|access-date=7 June 2025|language=es}}</ref> In July 2020, he made his first professional transfer abroad, by signing for Hungarian side [[MTK Budapest FC|MTK Budapest]].<ref>{{Cite web|title="Nagyon komoly céljaim vannak egyéni és csapatszinten is" {{!}} Miovski bemutatkozott (videó)|trans-title="I have serious goals at both individual and team levels", Miovski introduced himself (video)|url=http://mtkbudapest.hu/hu/hirek/nagyon-komoly-celjaim-vannak-egyeni-es-csapatszinten-is-miovski-bemutatkozott-video|website=MTK Budapest|access-date=14 October 2020|language=hu}}</ref> Two months after joining his club, he also made his league debut in the fourth round of the [[Nemzeti Bajnokság I]] by playing 23 minutes in a 3–0 loss to [[Zalaegerszegi TE|Zalaegerszegi]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Adatbank|url=http://ada1bank.mlsz.hu/match?itemId=1544792&evad=54&szervezet=0&verseny=22649&fordulo=4|website=Ada1bank|date=13 September 2020|access-date=14 October 2020|language=hu}}</ref>{{Better source needed|date=August 2024}}

=== Aberdeen ===
On 23 June 2022, Miovski signed a four-year contract with Scottish Premiership side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dons capture international striker |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2022/06/23/dons-capture-international-striker/|website=[[Aberdeen F.C.]]|date=23 June 2022}}</ref> The same year on 24 July, he debuted for [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] against [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] during a group stage match of the [[2022–23 Scottish League Cup]].<ref name="BBC Sport">{{Cite news|title=Miovski scores on Aberdeen debut as Raith exit cup |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62210657|website=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|access-date=5 February 2024}}</ref> Miovski scored from a [[penalty shot]] after being brought down in the box as Aberdeen won 3–0.<ref name="BBC Sport"/>

=== Girona ===
On 15 August 2024, Miovski signed a four-year deal with [[La Liga]] club [[Girona FC|Girona]] for a fee or £6.8 million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c05jm3mjml1o|title=Aberdeen receive record fee as Miovski joins Girona|date=15 August 2024|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC}}</ref> On 2 October, during the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League]], Miovski debuted for the club in a 3–2 loss against [[Feyenoord]].<ref>{{Cite web|script-title=mk:Миовски по лошо ќе го памети дебито во ЛШ, Жирона загуби од Феенорд! (Видео)|trans-title=Miovski will remember his debut in the Champions League badly, as Girona lost to Feyenoord! (Video)|url=https://sport1.mk/fudbal/uefa/miovski-po-losho-kje-go-pameti-debito-vo-lsh-zhirona-zagubi-od-feenord-video|website=sport1.mk|date=2 October 2024|access-date=7 June 2025|language=mk}}</ref> On 30 October, he scored his first two goals for the club during a Copa Del Ray match against [[CD Extremadura]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Live Commentary - CD Extremadura vs Girona|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/cd-extremadura-vs-girona/522796|url-status=live|website=[[Sky Sports]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241030232112/https://www.skysports.com/football/cd-extremadura-vs-girona/522796 |archive-date=30 October 2024|access-date=1 September 2025}}</ref> On 23 November, he scored a brace and registered an assist against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] in a league match at the [[Estadi Montilivi]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Girona 4–1 Espanyol|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/704794/espanyol-girona|publisher=[[ESPN]]|location=United Kingdom|date=23 November 2024|access-date=1 September 2025}}</ref>{{Better source needed|date=September 2025}} Having been used as a substitute, Miovski struggled for playing time during the season and only scored four goals in 22 appearances.{{Citation needed|date=September 2025}}

=== Rangers ===
Miovski returned to Scotland on 30 August 2025, signing for Premiership club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on a four-year contract for an undisclosed fee, which was widely reported to be an initial fee of £2.6 million which could rise to £4.2 million with add-ons.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bhardwaj |first=Peter Cassidy, Raman |date=28 August 2025|title=Rangers agree multi-million pound fee for forward Bojan Miovski |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/football/bojan-miovski-rangers-agree-multi-million-pound-fee-for-former-aberdeen-forward|website=STV News|access-date=1 September 2025}}</ref> He made his debut the next day, playing 72 minutes in a goalless [[Old Firm]] match against Rangers rivals [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Harris |first=Daniel |date=31 August 2025|title=Rangers 0–0 Celtic: Scottish Premiership updates – at it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2025/aug/31/rangers-v-celtic-scottish-premiership-updates-live|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=1 September 2025|issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Miovski scored his first goal for Rangers in a 2–0 victory over Hibernian at Ibrox in a [[2025–26 Scottish League Cup|League Cup]] quarter-final match on 20 September 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Binnie |first=Adam |title=Rangers 2-0 Hibernian: Under-fire Russell Martin leads Gers into Scottish League Cup semi-final amid fan protests |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/rangers-vs-hibernian/report/547872 |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref> On 5 October 2025, he scored his first Scottish Premiership goal for Rangers in a 1–1 draw with Falkirk at [[Falkirk Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Falkirk 1-1 Rangers: Draw heaps more pressure on Gers boss Martin |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c33r2d61mvnt |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 11 December 2025, he scored his first Europa League goal in a 2–1 loss away to [[Ferencvárosi TC|Ferencváros]] at [[Ferencváros Stadion]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |title=Ferencváros vs Rangers {{!}} UEFA Europa League 2025/26 |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2046248--ferencvaros-vs-rangers/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=UEFA.com |language=en}}</ref> On 16 January 2026, he scored his first career hatrick as Rangers defeated [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]] 5–0 at Ibrox in the [[Scottish Cup]] fourth round.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rangers 5-0 Annan Athletic: Miovski nets hat-trick as Gers progress in Scottish Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c62n8x5qyv1t |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
Miovski debuted for [[North Macedonia national under-21 football team|North Macedonia U21]] on 8 October 2020 in the [[2021 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification]], coming on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in the 62nd minute against [[Kazakhstan national football team|Kazakhstan]]. The away match finished as a 1–4 victory for North Macedonia.<ref>{{Cite web|title=North Macedonia vs. Kazakhstan|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/match/2026726/|website=[[UEFA]]|date=8 October 2020|access-date=14 October 2020}}</ref> Exactly one year later, on 8 October 2021, he debuted for the [[North Macedonia national football team|senior squad]] in a [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group J|2022 FIFA World Cup qualification]] against [[Liechtenstein national football team|Liechtenstein]].<ref>{{Cite web|script-title=mk:Миовски: Среќен сум за дебито…, целосната надмоќ која ја демонстрираме на терен сега резултираше со победа!|trans-title=Miovski: "I'm happy for my debut... The complete dominance we demonstrate on the field has now resulted in a victory!"|url=https://ekipa.mk/miovski-sreken-sum-za-debito-tselosnata-nadmok-koja-ja-demonstrirame-na-teren-sega-rezultirashe-so-pobeda/|website=ekipa.mk|date=9 October 2021|access-date=7 June 2025|language=mk}}</ref> In 2023, Miovski scored the winning goal for North Macedonia during a 1–0 friendly victory against [[Faroe Islands national football team|Faroe Islands]].<ref>{{Cite news|script-title=mk:Бојан Миовски: Сонувам да играм во англиската Премиер лига!|url=https://popup.mk/bojan-miovski-sonuvam-da-igram-vo-angliskata-premier-liga/|website=PopUp.mk|date=29 March 2023|access-date=13 August 2024|language=mk}}</ref>

'''Viljami Kari Veikko Sinisalo''' ({{respell|Vil-YAH-mee|Sin-uh-SAL-oh}},<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=htw-vwKrfp8|title=Viljami Sinisalo: Growing up in Finland, his career so far & the fight for the title (09/04/26)|author=Celtic FC|date=9 April 2026|via=YouTube}}</ref> born 11 October 2001) is a Finnish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], and the [[Finland national football team|Finland national team]]. 

Sinisalo previously played for a number of junior sides in Southwest Finland, ending up at amateur side [[FC Espoo|Espoo]] in the Finnish [[Kakkonen]] (third tier), where he made his league debut aged only fifteen; he joined Aston Villa's [[Aston Villa Under-21s and Academy|academy side]] the following year. Sinisalo has played on loan at [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] and [[Burton Albion F.C.|Burton Albion]]. He has appeared regularly at youth international level for [[Finland]] before debuting for their [[Finland national football team|senior side]] in 2023.

==Club career==
===Early career===
Sinisalo spent his youth career with [[Hyvinkään Palloseura|HyPS]], [[Helsingin Jalkapalloklubi|HJK]] and [[FC Honka|Honka]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 June 2018 |title=Nuori suomalaismaalivahti siirtyy perinteikkääseen englantilaisseuraan |url=https://www.iltalehti.fi/jalkapallo/a/201806292201045246 |access-date=18 October 2020 |website=www.iltalehti.fi |language=fi}}</ref> and made his senior league debut for [[FC Espoo]] in third-tier level [[Kakkonen]] in June 2017, aged only 15.<ref name="soccerway">{{Soccerway|viljani-sinisalo/480670|accessdate=18 October 2020}}</ref>

===Aston Villa===
He joined the [[avfc U21 academy|U21 academy]] at [[Steve Bruce]]'s [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] [[2018-19 avfc|in 2018]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dick |first=Brian |date=30 June 2018 |title=Aston Villa's first signing of the summer as young prospect arrives |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/aston-villas-first-signing-summer-14849627 |access-date=18 October 2020 |website=BirminghamLive}}</ref> and was a regular player in their [[Aston Villa F.C. Under-23s and Academy|under-18 and under-23 sides]].

On 25 September 2020, Sinisalo joined [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in the [[Scottish Championship]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Preece |first=Ashley |date=26 September 2020 |title=Villa youngster Viljami Sinisalo heads to Scotland on loan deal |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/aston-villa-transfers-sinisalo-ayr-19002003 |access-date=18 October 2020 |website=BirminghamLive}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Stuart |date=25 September 2020 |title=United land Aston Villa goalkeeper starlet on loan |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/aston-villa-starlet-viljami-sinisalo-22744757 |access-date=18 October 2020 |website=Daily Record}}</ref> He made his Ayr United debut on 6 October 2020, in a 5–2 away [[Scottish League Cup]] victory over [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=McGilvray|first=Andy|date=6 October 2020|title=Albion Rovers 2 Ayr United 5: Rovers lose out to classy Ayr United|work=Daily Record|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/albion-rovers-2-ayr-united-22803397|access-date=27 April 2021}}</ref> On 8 April 2021, Sinisalo's loan was cut short, after he suffered a [[Groin|groin injury]] and returned to Aston Villa.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Wilson|first=Stuart|date=8 April 2021|title=Aston Villa goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo 'gutted' to cut loan spell short at Ayr United|work=Daily Record|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/aston-villa-goalkeeper-viljami-sinisalo-23876868|access-date=27 April 2021}}</ref>

On 6 July 2021, Sinisalo was amongst several Academy players who were given new professional contracts.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=6 July 2021|title=Seven Villa U23s pen new deals|url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2021/july/Seven-Villa-U23s-pen-new-deals/|access-date=6 July 2021|website=Aston Villa Football Club}}</ref> One year on, on 6 July 2022, Sinisalo renewed his Aston Villa contract once again.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=6 July 2022 |title=Viljami Sinisalo pens new deal |url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2022/july/06/sinisalo-pens-new-deal/ |access-date=6 July 2022 |website=Aston Villa Football Club}}</ref>

On 11 July 2022, Sinisalo signed for [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Burton Albion F.C.|Burton Albion]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Slater |first=Rob |date=11 July 2022 |title=BURTON ALBION SIGN GOALKEEPER VILJAMI SINISALO ON LOAN FROM ASTON VILLA |url=https://www.burtonalbionfc.co.uk/news/2022/july/1107-sinisalo/ |access-date=11 July 2022 |website=Burton Albion Football Club |language=en-gb}}</ref> He made his debut on 9 August 2022, in a 2–0 [[EFL Cup]] defeat to [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=9 August 2022 |title=Rochdale 2-0 Burton Albion |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62388052 |access-date=10 August 2022}}</ref> The loan was ended early and Sinisalo returned to Villa on 1 January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 January 2023 |title=Jalkapallo {{!}} Suomalaismaalivahti Viljami Sinisalo palaa Aston Villaan |url=https://www.hs.fi/urheilu/art-2000009301375.html |access-date=1 January 2023 |website=Helsingin Sanomat |language=fi}}</ref> He made a total of eight appearances for the League One outfit.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2023/january/02/sinisalo-returns-to-villa/ | title = Viljami Sinisalo has returned to Aston Villa following his loan spell at Burton Albion |  publisher = [[Aston Villa]] | date = 2 January 2023 | access-date = 8 July 2023}}</ref>

On 19 July 2023, Sinisalo joined [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Exeter City sign Villa keeper Sinisalo on loan |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66244556 |access-date=19 July 2023}}</ref> He was given the number 1 shirt, and got a clean sheet on his debut, a 3–0 League One victory over [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]] on 5 August 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 August 2023 |title=📝 Match Report: Wycombe Wanderers 0 City 3 |url=https://www.exetercityfc.co.uk/news/2023/august/wycombe-a/ |access-date=31 August 2023 |website=www.exetercityfc.co.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref> During the season, Sinisalo made 50 appearances for the club in all competitions combined, recording 14 clean sheets. He was named The Player of the Year by the players and by the supporters of Exeter City, additionally winning four other awards in the club's end of season gala on 29 April 2024.<ref>[https://www.exetercityfc.co.uk/news/2024/april/awards-results/  23/24 Awards: The Winners], exetercityfc.com, 29 April 2024</ref><ref>[https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c296npgrppxo Exeter on-loan keeper Sinisalo set for 'incredible career'], [[BBC]], bbc.com, 26 April 2024</ref>

===Celtic===
On 16 July 2024, Sinisalo signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on a five-year deal for an undisclosed fee,<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=16 July 2024 |title=Celtic delighted to sign Finland international goalkeeper, Viljami Sinisalo |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2024/july/16/welcome-to-celtic-viljami-sinisalo/ |access-date=16 July 2024 |website=Celtic FC |language=en}}</ref> reported to be £1 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hendry |first=Mark |date=15 July 2024 |title=Viljami Sinisalo Celtic transfer fee as Aston Villa keeper agrees five-year deal |url=https://www.footballscotland.co.uk/spfl/scottish-premiership/viljami-sinisalo-celtic-transfer-fee-29547649 |access-date=16 July 2024 |website=Football Scotland |language=en}}</ref> He was given the number 12 shirt. On 8 February 2025, he made his debut for the club in a 5–0 home victory against [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] in the [[Scottish Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cd7d0jn983yt|title=Celtic 5–0 Raith Rovers|first=Kheredine|last=Idessane|date=8 February 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Following an injury to [[Kasper Schmeichel]] whilst on international duty, Sinisalo made his league debut in a 3–0 home victory against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] on 29 March 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cedy1qq63zxo|title='It feels like the man scores every game' - Sinisalo hails Maeda's Celtic impact|date=31 March 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.celticway.co.uk/news/25048728.sinisalo-delivers-verdict-celtic-league-debut-performance/|title=Viljami Sinisalo delivers honest verdict on Celtic league debut performance|date=30 March 2025|website=Celtic Way}}</ref> After the game, his performance was praised by Celtic manager [[Brendan Rodgers]], who called him "excellent".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/goalkeeper-who-incredible-career-makes-31312206|title=Goalkeeper 'who will have incredible career' makes breakthrough after £1m move|first=Joseph|last=Chapman|date=30 March 2025|website=Birmingham Live}}</ref>

In his second season, he again played second fiddle to Schmeichel for most of the season, only playing in a handful of cup games, though he was given the chance to start against [[VfB Stuttgart|Stuttgart]] in the [[UEFA Europa League]] on 26 March 2026,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/football/europa-league/2025-2026/celtic-viljami-sinisalo-reveals-he-idolised-kasper-schmeichel-growing-up-after-taking-his-place-for-uefa-conference-league-tie-at-stuttgart_vid60060378/video.shtml|title=Celtic's Viljami Sinisalo reveals he 'idolised' Kasper Schmeichel growing up after taking his place for UEFA Europa League tie at Stuttgart|date=26 February 2026|publisher=TNT Sports}}</ref> which was also his debut in [[UEFA club competitions]]. He kept a clean sheet as Celtic won 1–0, though it was not enough to keep them in the tournament. Within the same week, due to Schmeichel suffering another injury, coinciding with a drop in form, Sinisalo played in an [[Old Firm]] game  which ended in a 2–2 draw at [[Ibrox Stadium]], and made an outstanding save against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] to enable a 2–1 victory at [[Pittodrie]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/25898919.ex-hearts-rangers-icon-hails-celtics-viljami-sinisalo/|title=Ex-Hearts & Rangers icon hails Celtic's Viljami Sinisalo|first=Martin|last=McMillan|date=2 March 2026|website=Glasgow Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.footballinsider247.com/chris-sutton-hails-outstanding-viljami-sinisalo-after-incident-in-celtics-win-vs-aberdeen/|title=Aberdeen vs Celtic News: Chris Sutton Hails ‘Outstanding’ Viljami Sinisalo after Incident|first=Jack|last=Dawson|date=5 March 2026|website=Football Insider}}</ref>

Following Schmeichel's retirement, Sinisalo was handed the number 1 jersey for the 2026–27 season.<ref>https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/ive-always-wanted-celtic-no-37446348</ref>

==International career==
===Youth===
Sinisalo has played for Finland at [[Finland national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Finland national under-19 football team|under-19]] levels.<ref name="auto" /> On 17 November 2020, he made his debut for the [[Finland national under-21 football team|Under-21s]] in a [[UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] qualifier against [[Malta national under-21 football team|Malta]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/match/2026670--malta-vs-finland/|title=Malta-Finland | Under-21|website=[[UEFA]]|access-date=22 November 2020}}</ref> Sinisalo was named Finland U21's captain for their 15 November 2021 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualifier against [[Estonia national under-21 football team|Estonia]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=16 November 2021|title=Internationals: Tyrone Mings nets maiden England goal against San Marino|url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2021/november/16/internationals--mings-nets-maiden-england-goal/|access-date=16 November 2021|website=Aston Villa Football Club}}</ref> In December 2022, Sinisalo was named Finland's ''U21 Player of the Year'' for 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 December 2022 |title=🏆 Vuoden U21-pelaajaksi on valittu Viljami Sinisalo. Paljon onnea, Viljami! |url=https://twitter.com/palloliitto/status/1598394172150513664 |access-date=3 December 2022 |website=Suomen Palloliitto on Twitter |language=Finnish}}</ref>

===Senior===
On 14 September 2022, Sinisalo was called up in the [[Finland national football team|Finland senior squad]], previous to their [[UEFA Nations League]] matches against [[Romania national football team|Romania]] and [[Montenegro national football team|Montenegro]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Powlson |first=Nigel |date=14 September 2022 |title=SINISALO CALLED UP FOR INTERNATIONAL DUTY |url=https://www.burtonalbionfc.co.uk/news/2022/september/1409-sinisalo/ |access-date=14 September 2022 |website=Burton Albion Football Club |language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2022/september/23/Debuting-at-15--becoming-a-Brummie-and-life-on-loan--Sinisalo-s-road-to-the-Finland-national-team/</ref> However, he was an unused substitute in both games.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Internationals: John McGinn, Robin Olsen and Ludwig Augustinsson in action |url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2022/september/25/internationals--mcginn--olsen-and-augustinsson-in-action/ |access-date=27 September 2022 |website=Aston Villa Football Club}}</ref>

On 12 January 2023, Sinisalo made his debut in the Finland senior national team in a 1–0 friendly defeat to [[Estonia national football team|Estonia]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=VAVEL.com |date=12 January 2023 |title=Summary and goals of Finland 0-1 Estonia in Friendly Match {{!}} 1 December 2023 |url=https://www.vavel.com/en-us/soccer/2023/01/12/1134236-finland-vs-estonialive-updates-score-stream-info-lineups-and-how-to-watch-friendly-match.html |access-date=13 January 2023 |website=VAVEL |language=en-us}}</ref> Sinisalo made his competitive international debut on 20 November 2023, in a [[UEFA Euro 2024 qualification|UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying]] match against [[San Marino national football team|San Marino]].<ref>[https://www.hs.fi/urheilu/art-2000009963626.html Soiri upotti maaleillaan San Marinon, Galvez syötti maalin – ”olimme kärsivällisiä”], [[Helsingin Sanomat]], Ari Virtanen, 20 November 2023</ref>

==Personal life==
Viljami Sinisalo's grandfather was the actor [[Veikko Sinisalo]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Virtanen |first=Ari |date=14 October 2023 |title=Tulevaisuudessa tarvitaan uusi Hradecky, ja paikkaa havittelee yksi Englannissa koulittu torjuja |url=https://www.hs.fi/urheilu/art-2000009915108.html |access-date=15 October 2023 |publisher=Helsingin Sanomat |language=fi}}</ref> and his great-grandfather was the politician [[Väinö Sinisalo]].<ref name="Kalemaa 1986">{{cite book |last=Kalemaa |first=Kalevi |year=1986 |title=Sinisalon Veikko: suomalainen näyttelijä |trans-title=Veikko of Sinisalo: a Finnish Actor |location=Porvoo; Helsinki |publisher=WSOY |pages=11–23 |isbn=951-01397-2-6 |language=fi}}</ref>

'''Dane Ben Murray''' (born 26 June 2003) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defender (association football)|centre-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2021/april/Dane-Murray-excited-for-more-after-experiencing-first-team-training/|title=Dane Murray excited for more after experiencing first-team training|last=Connelly|first=Tony|date=7 April 2021|publisher=Celtic FC}}</ref>

==Club career==
Murray's footballing journey began by being scouted by [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] as a six-year-old and steadily progressed through their youth academy. In June 2019, Murray signed his first professional contract with Celtic.

Murray’s senior debut came on 20 July 2021, during a [[UEFA Champions League]] qualifier against [[FC Midtjylland]]. At just 18 years old, he was introduced as a substitute in the 1-1 draw.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Champions League qualifying: Celtic held by Midtjylland in Postecoglou's first game |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/57885987 |access-date=2025-03-22 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Murray was entrusted with a starting position in the return leg on July 28, 2021, playing the full 120 minutes in a match that concluded with a 2-1 [[extra-time]] defeat for Celtic.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-07-27 |title=Midtjylland 2-1 Celtic (agg 3-2): Postecoglou's side undone in extra time |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57972180.amp |access-date=2025-03-22 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-gb}}</ref>

To continue his development and provide regular first-team experience, Murray was loaned to [[Scottish Championship]] side, [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen’s Park]] for the 2024-2025 season. He made his debut for the club in August 2024 and quickly established himself as a key figure in their defense. Over the course of his loan spell, Murray amassed 20 appearances and an assist across all competitions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cairns |first=Ian |date=2024-08-09 |title=Dane Murray on loan from Celtic |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/dane-murray-on-loan-from-celtic/ |access-date=2025-03-22 |website=Queen's Park Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref>

In January 2025, Celtic exercised a recall clause, bringing Murray back to the club. This decision was influenced by squad dynamics, notably the anticipated loan departure of fellow defender [[Stephen Welsh]] to [[K.V. Mechelen|KV Mechelen]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McGilvray |first=Andy |date=2024-12-30 |title=Celtic star 'heading out on loan move' as Queen's Park kid set to return |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/celtic-star-heading-out-loan-34394074.amp |access-date=2025-03-22 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==

Murray has represented [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] at various youth levels.

Murray currently represents [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21]].

==Playing style==

Standing at 1.93 meters, Murray is a left-sided centre-back known for his composure on the ball and tactical awareness. His height and physical presence make him a formidable opponent in aerial duels, while his ability to read the game contributes to effective defensive positioning. Though he has been known to score own goals on a number of occasions.
