'''Liam Scales''' (born 8 August 1998) is an Irish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] or a [[left-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland national team]].

==Personal life==
Born in [[Wicklow]],<ref name="auto7">{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/soccer/soccer-news/celtic-ireland-defender-reveals-end-33609115|title=Ireland defender details which team his London-born dad will support on Saturday|first=Mark|last=McCadden|date=5 September 2024|website=Irish Mirror}}</ref> Scales is from [[Barndarrig]], [[County Wicklow]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |url=https://www.balls.ie/football/who-is-liam-scales-celtic-shamrock-rovers-478833 |title=The Rapid Rise Of Liam Scales: From Arklow Town To The Doorstep Of Paradise |first=Andrew |last=Dempsey |website=Balls.ie|date=27 August 2021 }}</ref> His father is from [[London]].<ref name="auto7"/> He studied Irish and geography at [[University College Dublin]].<ref name="auto"/> He is a fluent [[Irish language|Irish]] speaker.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web |url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/soccer/liam-scales-determined-end-season-23081683 |title=Liam Scales determined to end season of firsts with double glory |first=Paul |last=O'Hehir |date=28 November 2020 |website=Irish Mirror}}</ref> Scales is close friends with fellow professional footballer [[Daire O'Connor]], with the pair growing up together since the age of 5 and playing together at [[University College Dublin A.F.C.|UCD]], before Scales was O'Connor's best man at his wedding.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/how-liam-scales-found-balance-ireland-defender-created-winning-moment-in-hungary-after-a-road-less-travelled/a702736500.html|title=How Liam Scales found balance: Ireland defender created winning ‘moment’ in Hungary after a road less travelled|date=21 November 2025|website=www.independent.ie}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
Scales began his career with [[Arklow Town F.C.|Arklow Town]] before signing for [[University College Dublin A.F.C.|UCD]] in 2015.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |url=https://www.fai.ie/ireland/player/888845506 |title=Liam Scales | Football Association of Ireland |website=www.fai.ie|access-date=2026-03-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191203235513/https://www.fai.ie/ireland/player/888845506|archive-date=2019-12-03|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his [[League of Ireland]] debut on 8 July 2016 <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.extratime.com/articles/18005/season-review-2016---ucd/|title=Season Review 2016 - UCD|first=John|last=McDermott|website=extratime.com}}</ref> and made over 100 appearances for the club, winning the [[Collingwood Cup]]<ref name="auto5">{{Cite web |url=https://www.fai.ie/domestic/news/ucd-win-the-collingwood-cup |title=UCD win the Collingwood Cup | Football Association of Ireland |website=www.fai.ie}}</ref> as well as the [[League of Ireland First Division]] title in [[2018 League of Ireland First Division|2018]].<ref name="auto"/> He was described as "a key player for UCD as they won the First Division title".<ref name="auto6">{{Cite web |url=https://www.the42.ie/collie-oneill-on-liam-scales-4522937-Mar2019/ |title='He's a top-class player and he will go and win league titles with other clubs' |first=Paul |last=Dollery |website=The42 |date=4 March 2019}}</ref> Scales was voted by his fellow League of Ireland First Division players into the [[PFAI Team of the Year|PFAI First Division Team of the Year]] for [[PFAI Team of the Year#First Division 10|2018]].<ref name="auto4">{{cite web |url=https://www.the42.ie/michael-duffy-pfai-player-of-the-year-dundalk-league-of-ireland-sse-airtricity-league-4333614-Nov2018/ |title=Double-winner Michael Duffy named PFAI Player of the Year following stellar season with Dundalk |website=the42.ie |date=11 November 2018 |accessdate=1 September 2021}}</ref>

In 2019 he underwent trials at English clubs [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/ucd-duo-of-liam-scales-and-neil-farrugia-earn-trial-at-manchester-city-38041598.html |title=UCD duo of Liam Scales and Neil Farrugia earn trial at Manchester City |website=independent|date=23 April 2019 }}</ref> and [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]], with him seeming to be set to sign for the latter before the deal fell through.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/liam-scales-bristol-rovers-transfer-3113204 |title=UCD manager says Liam Scales is set to sign for Bristol Rovers |first=Krishan |last=Davis |date=19 July 2019 |website=BristolLive}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.dublinlive.ie/sport/bristol-rovers-step-back-liam-16689088 |title=Bristol Rovers step back from Liam Scales chase |first=David |last=Byrom |date=2 August 2019 |website=DublinLive}}</ref>

===Shamrock Rovers===
He moved to [[Shamrock Rovers F.C.|Shamrock Rovers]] for the 2020 season,<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/national-league/ireland-u21-defender-liam-scales-joins-shamrock-rovers-from-ucd-1.4097235 |title=Ireland U21 defender Liam Scales joins Shamrock Rovers from UCD |first=Emmet |last=Malone |newspaper=The Irish Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.otbsports.com/sport/shamrock-rovers-sign-liam-scales-929641 |title=Shamrock Rovers sign highly-rated Irish U21 international Liam Scales |first=Stephen |last=Doyle |website=Off The Ball}}</ref> and "played a significant part in their league success".<ref name="auto2"/> He also made seven appearances for the club in European competitions, scoring once,<ref name = "SW"/> and getting sent off on his European debut.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.extratime.com/articles/25495/europa-league-report-shamrock-rovers-2---2-ilves-tampere-shamrock-rovers-win-12---11-on-penalties-aet/|title=Europa League Report: Shamrock Rovers 2 - 2 Ilves Tampere (Shamrock Rovers win 12 - 11 on penalties AET)|website=extratime.com}}</ref> In July 2021 he was described as "the hottest property in the League of Ireland" and linked with a transfer away from the club.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-40338089.html |title=Graham Cummins: Liam Scales now the hottest property in the League of Ireland |first=Graham |last=Cummins |date=16 July 2021 |website=Irish Examiner}}</ref> On 26 November 2021, he was named in the [[PFAI Team of the Year]] for 2021, as voted by his fellow players.<ref name="2021TotY">{{Cite web |url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2021/1126/1263306-bohs-earn-four-spots-on-pfai-team-of-the-year/ |title=Bohs earn four spots on PFAI Team of the Year |date=26 November 2021 |via=www.rte.ie}}</ref>

===Celtic===
After 51 appearances for Shamrock Rovers, Scales signed a four-year contract with Scottish club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in August 2021.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58355420 |title=Irish defender Scales joins Celtic |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/national-league/celtic-confirm-signing-of-liam-scales-from-shamrock-rovers-1.4657693 |title=Celtic confirm signing of Liam Scales from Shamrock Rovers |newspaper=The Irish Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2021/0827/1243134-liam-scales-completes-celtic-switch-on-four-yeal-deal/ |title=Liam Scales completes Celtic switch on four-yeal deal |date=27 August 2021 |via=www.rte.ie}}</ref> On 23 September 2021, he made his debut for Celtic in a 3–0 win over [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] at [[Celtic Park]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.the42.ie/liam-scales-celtic-debut-5556801-Sep2021/ |title=Ireland defender Liam Scales makes debut as Celtic ease past Raith Rovers |agency=Press Association |website=The42 |date=23 September 2021}}</ref> Scales made his league debut on 5 December 2021, coming on as a substitute to score the third goal in [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]'s 3–0 away win at [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2021/december/05/dominant-and-classy-celts-show-their-cutting-edge-in-victory/ |title=Dominant and classy Celts show their cutting edge in victory |first=Celtic |last=FC |website=Celtic FC|date=5 December 2021 }}</ref> On 24 February 2022, Scales started in a 2–0 away defeat against [[Eliteserien]] side [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]] in the [[UEFA Europa Conference League]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Europa Conference League (Sky Sports) |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/bodo-glimt-vs-celtic/teams/461080?authId=1%2A3824dg%2A_a%2AcmVHOXFFN1U0UC1xV0pLTGFqZXV2LWVwbWhUQVFQZnZycmhOWGpER3ozYWVSUk9zQU0yNV9sYTV4Tk5pb3oxUg.. |access-date=3 January 2023 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref>

====Aberdeen (loan)====
Scales went to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] for a season-long loan in June 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celtic's Liam Scales joins Aberdeen on loan after Jayden Richardson moves to Pittodrie |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61874918 |website=BBC Sport |date=21 June 2022 |access-date=21 June 2022}}</ref> This transfer caused controversy amongst a section of the Aberdeen support, who launched criticism at their board for continuing to sign players on loan from Celtic. Aberdeen manager [[Jim Goodwin]] defended his signature, with him stating that: "I'm a big fan of the loan market as it gives you the opportunity to sign players that you would maybe not normally be able to afford. The size of club we are we want to be signing players on permanent contracts. That conversation was had with Celtic initially. We wanted to know what the number was and could we make it happen. Celtic are not willing to sell Liam at this moment".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Young |first=Graeme |date=19 July 2022 |title=Aberdeen fans demand 'no more Celtic loans' in firm boardroom message |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/aberdeen-fans-demand-no-more-27524856 |access-date=3 January 2023 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref>

On 10 July 2022, Scales made his Aberdeen debut in a 2–0 [[Scottish League Cup]] win at [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Premier Sports Cup (Sky Sports) |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/peterhead-vs-aberdeen/teams/463677 |access-date=3 January 2023 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref> On 17 September 2022, Scales was sent off in 3–1 defeat at [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] after he was shown a second [[Yellow card (football)|yellow card]] by referee David Dickinson.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hibernian 3-1 Aberdeen: Josh Campbell scores twice in second half to help Hibs to comeback win |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11781/12698065/hibernian-3-1-aberdeen-josh-campbell-scores-twice-in-second-half-to-help-hibs-to-comeback-win |access-date=3 January 2023 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref> Four months later he was shown [[Red card (association football)|red]] again in a 6–0 loss against the same opposition, a result that saw manager Jim Goodwin removed from his position shortly after the match.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Hibs thump Aberdeen as Goodwin's exit is confirmed |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64356678 |access-date=29 January 2023}}</ref> Scales first goal for Aberdeen was in a 2–0 win over [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Aberdeen stun Rangers to move Celtic closer to title |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65290257 |access-date=23 July 2023}}</ref>

====Return to Celtic====
[[File:Liam Scales with a fan (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Scales in 2023.]]
Scales was linked with a return to Aberdeen ahead of the 2023–24 season,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/5621968/aberdeen-loan-defender-liam-scales-admits-his-future-is-out-of-my-hands/|title=Aberdeen loan defender Liam Scales admits his future 'is out of my hands'|first=Sean|last=Wallace|date=17 April 2023}}</ref> but became a Celtic first-team player following injuries to other players.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aberdeenlive.news/sport/football/football-news/liam-scales-would-been-happy-8840495|title=Liam Scales would have been 'happy' with Aberdeen return according to pundit|first=Anthony|last=Evans|date=18 October 2023|website=Aberdeen Live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aberdeenlive.news/sport/football/liam-scales-admits-expected-aberdeen-8907890|title=Liam Scales admits he expected Aberdeen return before landing Celtic chance|first=Ruaraidh|last=Britton|date=15 November 2023|website=Aberdeen Live}}</ref> He became a regular player for Celtic following his return to the club in the 2023–24 season, and signed a new four-year contract in May 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cljd045kwyeo|title=Liam Scales: Celtic defender signs four-year deal|date=3 May 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2024/0503/1447282-scales-commits-to-celtic-with-new-four-year-deal/|title=Scales commits to Celtic with new four-year deal|date=3 May 2024|via=www.rte.ie}}</ref> He was named in the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#Premiership 10|2023–24 PFA Scotland Scottish Premiership Team of the Year]] for his performances throughout the season.<ref name="auto8">{{cite tweet |number=1781601474864111813 |title=PFA Scotland on X: "🏆 PFA Scotland Premiership Team of the Year. As voted by the players, here's your selection for 23/24: Jack Butland James Tavernier Cameron Carter-Vickers Liam Scales Owen Beck Matt O'Riley John Lundstram Callum McGregor Bojan Miovski Lawrence Shankland Theo Bair |user=PFAScotland |date=20 April 2024 |access-date=20 April 2024}}</ref> He scored 3 goals in 40 appearances in all competitions in the [[2024–25 Celtic F.C. season|2024–25 season]]<ref>https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=100193&season_id=157</ref> as his side won the [[Scottish League Cup]]<ref name="bbc">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cdd6e6yrr04t#Line-ups |title=Celtic 3–3 Rangers: Line-ups |website=BBC Sport |date=15 December 2024 |access-date=15 December 2024}}</ref> and retained their [[Scottish Premiership]] title for the fourth year in a row.<ref name="theguardian">{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/apr/26/celtic-win-55th-scottish-league-title|title=Brendan Rodgers '200% staying' after Celtic clinch 55th Scottish league title|work=The Guardian |date=26 April 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Scales was a Republic of Ireland under-21 international,<ref name="auto3"/><ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.extratime.com/player/11121194/liam_scales/ |title=Extratime.com - Extratime.ie - Liam Scales |website=www.extratime.com}}</ref> winning six caps.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.the42.ie/celtic-reach-agreement-with-shamrock-rovers-to-sign-liam-scales-5533824-Aug2021/ |title=Celtic boss tips Liam Scales for 'a big future' after reaching agreement to sign Irish defender |first=Paul |last=Dollery |website=The42 |date=27 August 2021}}</ref>

He was called up to the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] senior team for the first time on 3 September 2021 alongside [[Alan Browne (footballer)|Alan Browne]] and [[Callum Robinson]] for the games against [[Azerbaijan national football team|Azerbaijan]] and [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]], with the trio replacing the injured [[Dara O'Shea]], [[Nathan Collins]] and [[Shane Long]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/12020/12398336/republic-of-ireland-call-up-liam-scales-callum-robinson-and-alan-browne-for-azerbaijan-world-cup-qualifier |title=Republic of Ireland call up Liam Scales, Callum Robinson and Alan Browne for Azerbaijan World Cup qualifier |website=Sky Sports}}</ref> On 19 September 2022, Scales was called up again for [[UEFA Nations League]] group matches against [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] and [[Armenia national football team|Armenia]] after [[Andrew Omobamidele]] was ruled out due a groin injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robertson |first=Euan |date=19 September 2022 |title=Liam Scales earns Ireland call up as Celtic loanee rewarded for Aberdeen form |url=https://www.footballscotland.co.uk/spfl/scottish-premiership/liam-scales-earns-ireland-call-25055451 |access-date=3 January 2023 |website=footballscotland |language=en}}</ref>

He was recalled by Ireland in October 2023.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67017953|title=Scales in Republic squad as Ferguson returns|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> On 13 October 2023, he made his senior international debut for the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] in a 2–0 defeat at against [[Greece national football team|Greece]] at the [[Aviva Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-41247724.html|title=Liam Scales handed debut against Greece as Kenny chases elusive win|first=John|last=Fallon|date=13 October 2023|website=Irish Examiner}}</ref>

[[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] manager [[Stephen Kenny (football manager)|Stephen Kenny]] revealed on 7 November 2023 that Scales would be called up again as part of the squad to play against [[Netherlands national football team|The Netherlands]] and [[New Zealand men's national football team|New Zealand]].<ref>{{Citation |title=EXCLUSIVE: Liam Scales to be named in ROI squad {{!}} Interview with Stephen Kenny | date=7 November 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yATlCp69RqE |access-date=2023-11-07 |language=en}}</ref>

On 10 October 2024, Scales scored his first goal for the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]], an equalising header against [[Finland national football team|Finland]], in a match that ended in a 2–1 win to the Republic of Ireland.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/24645183.liam-scales-delighted-check-scoring-ireland-goal-off-list/?ref=rss|title='Always been top of the list': Liam Scales reflects on netting maiden Ireland goal|date=11 October 2024|website=The Herald}}</ref>

On 16 November 2025, Scales provided the headed assist for the third [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] goal against [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]], which was scored by [[Troy Parrott]] in second-half added time. The match ended in a 3–2 win to the Republic of Ireland and they advanced to the playoff stage of their [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] qualifying campaign.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/2025/11/17/ken-early-has-any-irish-team-in-any-sport-undergone-such-an-incredible-transformation/?ref=rss|title='The most astonishing quarter-hour in Irish football history|date=17 November 2025|newspaper=The Irish Times}}</ref>

To gain some more experience, Sørensen was on 26 January 2020 loaned out to Midtjylland affiliate club, [[Danish 1st Division]]-side [[FC Fredericia]], for the rest of the season.[https://www.bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/fcm-udlejer-u19-anfoerer-til-i-1-divisionsklub/ FCM udlejer U19-anfører til i 1. divisionsklub], bold.dk, 26 January 2021 Sørensen had a good spell at Fredericia, where he played 11 games and scored one goal. Sørensen returned to Midtjylland for the 2021–22 season. On 31 March 2022, Sørensen was loaned out to Norwegian club [[Hamarkameratene|HamKam]] until the end of the year.[https://www.hamkam.no/nyheter/oliver-sorensen-har-signert OLIVER SØRENSEN HAR SIGNERT], hamkam.no, 31 March 2022 Two days later, he made his [[Eliteserien]] debut against [[Lillestrøm SK]].[https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2022/04/02/norway/eliteserien/hamar-kamaratene-fotball/lillestrom-sportsklubb/3729781/ HAMKAM VS. LILLESTRØM 2 - 2], soccerway.com, 2 April 2022 However, Midtjylland decided to recall Sørensen on 16 June 2022, presumably due to lack of playing time.[https://www.fcm.dk/nyheder/oliver-soerensen-retur-til-fcm/ OLIVER SØRENSEN RETUR TIL FCM], fcm.de, 16 June 2022 Sørensen managed to play just 275 minutes over 6 matches. ====Back at Midtjylland==== After a season where Sørensen was a big part of Midtjylland's success, winning the [[2023–24 Danish Superliga]] title, the Dane was named FC Midtjylland's Player of the Year and Find of the Year.[https://www.fcm.dk/nyheder/aarets-spiller-og-aarets-fund-i-fc-midtjylland/ ÅRETS SPILLER OG ÅRETS FUND I FC MIDTJYLLAND], fcm.dk, 31 May 2024 ===Parma=== On 12 August 2025, Sørensen signed a five-season contract with [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]] in Italy.{{cite web|publisher=Parma Calcio 1913|url=https://www.parmacalcio1913.com/news/oliver-sorensen-e-gialloblu/|title=OLIVER SØRENSEN È GIALLOBLU|trans-title=OLIVER SØRENSEN IS YELLOW AND BLUE|date=12 August 2025|access-date=13 August 2025|language=it}} ====Loan to Celtic==== On 1 September 2026, Sørensen signed on loan with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in Scotland until the end of the season with an option to buy.{{cite web |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2026/september/01/celtic-welcomes-oliver-s-rensen-to-paradise/ |title=Celtic welcomes Oliver Sørensen to Paradise |publisher=Celtic F.C. |date=1 September 2026 }} Sørensen made his Celtic debut the following day, appearing as a substitute in a 3–0 win over '''Tuur Rommens''' (born 26 March 2003) is a Belgian professional footballer who plays as a [[left-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{Soccerway|id=tuur-rommens/632461|accessdate=28 December 2021}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Born and raised in [[Oud-Turnhout]], in the [[Flanders|Flemish]] [[Antwerp Province|province]] of [[Antwerp]], Rommens joined [[K.R.C. Genk|Genk]]'s academy from [[K.V.C. Westerlo|Westerlo]] when he was nine.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|last=Geukens|first=Marnik|date=29 September 2021|title=Genk-aanvoerder Tuur Rommens kijkt uit naar Youth League|trans-title=Genk captain Tuur Rommens is looking forward to Youth League|work=[[Het Belang van Limburg]]|url=https://www.hbvl.be/cnt/dmf20210928_95651387?adh_i=&adh_i=&articlehash=DL0C1xmGeTlEKGSuTB2XXfKcCwJ2uyNC2VyLI3MXbkGrWoiB%2BLJSMWU3me%2BYaEr3RRCQUS1mXkh6fCrpcSklZ0IxVJneSQxjHgeXmSwHC7AvhYCucKHfALnB64JOXvuuH%2BEdmthYDYwOgt2G%2FPEsEyXrg299ENwST84addehfZ%2Bp1Di8sqIzwwcCW1LYyuptBqaVS5iPHWxVUWWoB4KeaojkZd8JlsDeqdZI2rKa5%2FFRLnvy3ZGEETJ%2FDZ%2FvMm65sGFrlvxvL1YXGuOdml58BPq%2BCtjk3EQcxYF4fxlOL9X1cCW9A%2B%2Fw0Rw8zBRepqa0J8lCKy7ZPgfHOkYS4oNykQ%3D%3D|url-access=registration|access-date=29 December 2021|quote=Rommens is geboren en getogen in Oud-Turnhout en werd al op zijn negende door Genk bij Westerlo weggeplukt.}}</ref>

== Club career ==
Rommens was a regular with [[K.R.C. Genk|Genk]] under-19s, since the [[2019–20 UEFA Youth League|2019–20 Youth League]], eventually captaining his side during the [[2021–22 UEFA Youth League|2021–22 edition]], as well as the reserve team for that [[2021–22 K.R.C. Genk season|season]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=15 December 2021|title=Storck haalt Rommens bij Genkse kern, Cuesta, Lucumi en Arteaga missen nog twee matchen|url=https://www.hbvl.be/cnt/dmf20211215_94784251|access-date=29 December 2021|website=Het Belang van Limburg|language=nl-BE}}</ref>

Having signed his first professional contract with Genk in February 2020,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Marynissen|first=Joost|date=27 February 2020|title=Racing Genk biedt zestienjarige Tuur Rommens zijn eerste profcontract aan|url=https://www.nieuwsblad.be/cnt/dmf20200227_04868074|access-date=29 December 2021|website=[[Het Nieuwsblad]]|language=nl-BE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=[[Belga (news agency)|Belga]]|date=27 February 2020|title=Tuur Rommens (16 ans) signe son premier contrat pro à Genk|url=https://www.dhnet.be/sports/football/division-1a/jupiler-pro-league-tuur-rommens-16-ans-signe-son-premier-contrat-pro-a-genk-5e57f9759978e231069bfd07|access-date=29 December 2021|website=[[La Dernière Heure]]|language=fr}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=27 February 2020|title=Eerste contract voor Tuur Rommens (16)|url=https://www.krcgenk.be/nl/nieuws/3882/eerste-contract-voor-tuur-rommens-16|access-date=29 December 2021|website=[[KRC Genk]]|language=nl}}</ref> he signed an extension at the end of April 2021, until mid-2024.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Schepers|first=Arno|date=30 April 2021|title=KRC Genk legt drie jonge talenten vast tot 2024|url=https://www.hbvl.be/cnt/dmf20210430_95351624|url-access=registration|access-date=29 December 2021|website=[[Het Belang van Limburg]]|language=nl-BE}}</ref>

Rommens made his first team debut on 27 October 2021 coming on as a halftime substitute for [[Gerardo Arteaga]], during the 6–0 away cup win against [[Sint-Eloois-Winkel Sport|Sint-Eloois-Winkel]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Geukens|first=Marnik|date=27 October 2021|title=Scherp KRC Genk klaart bekerklus bij Winkel Sport al voor rust: 0-6|url=https://www.nieuwsblad.be/sportwereld/live/voetbal/330124/|access-date=29 December 2021|website=[[Het Nieuwsblad]]|language=nl-BE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=28 October 2021|title=Genkse debutanten Leysen en Rommens: "Jongens van Westerlo doen het"|url=https://www.hbvl.be/cnt/dmf20211027_97493133|access-date=29 December 2021|website=[[Het Belang van Limburg]]|language=nl-BE}}</ref> He made his [[2021–22 Belgian First Division A|league]] debut for Genk on 16 December 2021, replacing [[Simen Juklerød]] at the end of a 4–2 home win against [[R. Charleroi S.C.|Sporting Charleroi]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Lecaillon|first=Stéphane|date=17 December 2021|title=Charleroi subit le réveil du Racing Genk|url=https://www.dhnet.be/sports/football/division-1a/charleroi/charleroi-subit-le-reveil-du-racing-genk-61bbb7db9978e253986e53ab|url-access=limited|access-date=28 December 2021|website=[[La Dernière Heure]]|language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=17 December 2021|title=Debuut Tuur, eerste goal Luca|url=https://www.krcgenk-jeugd.be/nl/news/detail/1874/debuut-tuur-eerste-goal-luca|access-date=29 December 2021|website=[[KRC Genk]] Jeugdopleiding}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=16 December 2021|title=Racing Genk 4-2 Charleroi SC, Jupiler Pro League, résultat du match|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/match-direct/championnat-de-belgique/2021-2022/racing-genk-charleroi-sc-live/514072|access-date=28 December 2021|website=[[L'Équipe]]|language=fr}}</ref>

On 4 July 2023, Rommens signed a four-year contract with [[K.V.C. Westerlo|Westerlo]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Westerlo|url=https://kvcwesterlo.be/2023/07/04/welcome-tuur/|title=Welcome Tuur|date=4 July 2023|access-date=7 September 2023}}</ref>

After 2 and a half years at [[K.V.C. Westerlo|Westerlo]], Rommens left the club to join [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Rangers|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/rangers-announce-signing-of-tuur-rommens/1O45bnV6o80hdXVcYmEep7|title=Rangers Announce Signing of Tuur Rommens|date=14 January 2026|access-date=14 January 2026}}</ref>

== International career ==
Already a [[Belgium national under-17 football team|Belgium under-17]] international,<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> Rommens played with the [[Belgium national under-19 football team|under-19]] in 2021, scoring his first goal with the team on 10 November 2021, during a [[2022 UEFA European Under-19 Championship qualification|Euro qualifier]] game against [[Azerbaijan national under-19 football team|Azerbaijan]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=[[Belga (news agency)|Belga]]|date=10 November 2021|title=Qualifications Euro U19 2022: la Belgique lance ses qualifications par un large succès face à l'Azerbaïdjan|url=https://www.dhnet.be/sports/football/diablesrouges/qualifications-euro-u19-2022-la-belgique-lance-ses-qualifications-par-un-large-succes-face-a-l-azerbaidjan-618c19569978e25ff062063a|access-date=29 December 2021|website=[[La Dernière Heure]]|language=fr}}</ref> having become a regular starter for the team at left-back,<ref>{{Cite web|last=Niesen|first=Gilles|date=13 November 2021|title=Belgische U19 naar eliteronde in EK-kwalificaties, Oyen scoort opnieuw|url=https://www.hbvl.be/cnt/dmf20211114_96570480|url-access=registration|access-date=29 December 2021|website=[[Het Belang van Limburg]]|language=nl-BE|quote=Vic Chambaere en Tuur Rommens, die net als Oyen gewisseld werd toen de buit binnen was, stonden eveneens in de basis.}}</ref> before eventually captaining the Belgian side during the qualifying game against [[Javi Serrano]]'s [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spain]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|date=16 November 2021|title=Belgium-Spain {{!}} Under-19|url=https://www.uefa.com/under19/match/2031182--belgium-vs-spain/?iv=true|access-date=29 December 2021|website=[[UEFA]]|language=en}}</ref>

'''Mika Joel Baur''' (born 9 July 2004) is a German professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and the [[Germany national football team|Germany national team]].

==Club career==

=== SC Paderborn ===
On 13 June 2024, Baur signed with [[2. Bundesliga]] club [[SC Paderborn 07|SC Paderborn]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=SC Paderborn|url=https://www.scp07.de/Newsarchiv/Kreative-Offensive-1.html|title=KREATIVE OFFENSIVE|trans-title=CREATIVE OFFENSIVE|date=13 June 2024|access-date=3 July 2024|language=de}}</ref> Over two seasons with the club, he 44 appearances and scored four goals.

==== Loan to Dynamo Dresden ====
On 17 January 2025, Baur was loaned to [[3. Liga]] side [[Dynamo Dresden]] until the end of the 2024–25 season,<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Dynamo Dresden|url=https://www.dynamo-dresden.de/aktuelles/news/profis/sgd-leiht-mika-baur-aus-paderborn|title=SGD leiht Mika Baur aus Paderborn|trans-title=SGD loans Mika Baur from Paderborn|date=17 January 2025|access-date=17 January 2025|language=de}}</ref> scoring one goal across 18 appearances.

=== Celtic ===
On 13 August 2026, Baur signed a four-year contract with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-13 |title=Welcome to Celtic, Mika Baur |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2026/august/13/welcome-to-celtic--mika-baur/ |access-date=2026-08-13 |website=Celtic FC |language=en}}</ref> Baur made his debut on 15 August 2026, appearing as a substitute in a 4–0 win over [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporting |first=Live |title=Dundee United vs Celtic: Scottish League Cup radio commentary, updates & match report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ck78glz4g9ent |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
Baur is a German youth international, having represented the [[Germany national under-18 football team|U18]], [[Germany national under-19 football team|U19]], [[Germany national under-20 football team|U20]] and [[Germany national under-21 football team|U21]] teams.<ref>{{DFB|mika-baur}}</ref>

In September 2026, he was one of players who were called up with the [[Germany national football team|Germany national team]] by head coach [[Jürgen Klopp]] for the [[2026–27 UEFA Nations League A|2026–27 UEFA Nations League]] matches against [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]], [[Greece national football team|Greece]], [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]] and Greece between 24 September and 4 October 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/news/bundestrainer-klopp-beruft-erstes-aufgebot-fuer-nations-league|title=Bundestrainer Klopp beruft erstes Aufgebot für Nations League|publisher=[[German Football Association]]|language=de|date=17 September 2026|access-date=17 September 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Baur was born in Germany to German and [[Malagasy peoples|Malagasy]] roots.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/celtic-transfer-target-mika-baur-37461875|title=Celtic transfer target Mika Baur is son of a German handball legend|first=Ross|last=Pilcher|date=22 July 2026|website=Daily Record}}</ref> Baur is the son of the German [[handball]] player [[Markus Baur]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.liga3-online.de/freiburgs-mika-baur-stellt-bei-debuet-neuen-drittliga-rekord-auf/|title=Freiburgs Mika Baur stellt bei Debüt neuen Drittliga-Rekord auf}}</ref>

'''Djeidi Hamara Gassama''' (born 10 September 2003) is a Mauritanian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|Rangers}} club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[Mauritania national football team|Mauritania national team]]. He has also represented France at youth international level.<ref name="soccerway">{{Soccerway|632959}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Paris Saint-Germain===
A former youth academy player of [[Stade Brestois 29|Brest]], Gassama joined [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] (PSG) in 2019.<ref>{{cite web |date=14 May 2022 |title=Le grand jour pour Djeidi Gassama? Focus sur le serial buteur! |url=https://www.lestitisdupsg.fr/a-la-une/37j-l1-le-grand-jour-pour-djeidi-gassama-focus-sur-le-serial-buteur/ |access-date=14 May 2022 |website=Les Titis du PSG}}</ref> He signed his first professional contract with the club in July 2020.<ref>{{cite web |date=23 July 2020 |title=Djeidi Gassama signs his first professional contract |url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/djeidi-gassama-signs-his-first-professional-contract-with-paris-saint-germain |access-date=14 May 2022 |publisher=[[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.]]}}</ref> On 14 May 2022, he made his professional debut in a 4–0 league win against [[Montpellier HSC|Montpellier]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 May 2022 |title=Gassama makes first appearance |url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/gassama-makes-first-appearance-psg-ligue-1-histoire-club |access-date=14 May 2022 |publisher=[[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.]]}}</ref>

On 6 September 2022, Gassama joined Belgian club [[K.A.S. Eupen|Eupen]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|date=6 September 2022|title=Teddy Alloh und Djeidi Gassama von PSG zur KAS Eupen|url=https://www.as-eupen.be/teddy-alloh-und-djeidi-gassama-von-psg-zur-kas-eupen/|publisher=[[K.A.S. Eupen|Eupen]]|language=de|access-date=6 September 2022}}</ref>

===Sheffield Wednesday===
On 15 August 2023, Gassama joined [[EFL Championship]] club [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Djeidi Gassama joins Wednesday!|url=https://www.swfc.co.uk/news/2023/august/djeidi-gassama-joins-wednesday/ |access-date=15 August 2023 |publisher=Sheffield Wednesday FC |date=15 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Sheffield Wednesday sign Paris St-Germain forward|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66511887|access-date=15 August 2023 |publisher=BBC|date=15 August 2023}}</ref> He made his debut on 19 August 2023 against [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] coming off the bench.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wednesday 0–1 Preston|url=https://www.swfc.co.uk/news/2023/august/report--wednesday-0-1-preston/|access-date=19 August 2023 |publisher=Sheffield Wednesday FC |date=19 August 2023}}</ref> His first goal came on 1 January 2024 against [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] with a fine effort from 25 yards.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sheffield Wednesday 3–1 Hull City|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67818417|access-date=1 January 2024 |publisher=BBC |date=1 January 2024}}</ref>

The following season, he won the clubs player of the month for January scoring twice.<ref>{{cite web|title=Djeidi Gassama voted Owls Player of the Month!|url=https://www.swfc.co.uk/news/2025/january/31/djeidi-gassama-voted-owls-player-of-the-month-/|website=Sheffield Wednesday Football Club|access-date=31 January 2025}}</ref> He finished the season winning the Wise Old Owl Player of the Year award.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gassama wins WOO Player of the Year|url=https://www.swfc.co.uk/news/2025/april/16/gassama-wins-woo-player-of-the-season/|access-date=16 April 2025 |publisher=Sheffield Wednesday FC|date=16 April 2025}}</ref> During pre-season for the [[2025–26 Sheffield Wednesday F.C. season|2025–26 season]], Gassama was heavily linked with a move to [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], with manager [[Russell Martin (footballer)|Russell Martin]] saying the move was "all done at our end."<ref>{{cite web|title=Gassama move 'done' at Rangers end as Propper nears exit|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cq8zggjej5eo|website=BBC Sport|access-date=11 July 2025}}</ref>

===Rangers===
On 15 July 2025, Gassama joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on a four-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Djeidi Gassama joins Rangers from Sheffield Wednesday on four-year deal in £2.2m switch to Scottish Premiership club|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11788/13394901/djeidi-gassama-joins-rangers-from-sheffield-wednesday-on-four-year-deal-in-2-2m-switch-to-scottish-premiership-club|date=15 July 2025|access-date=15 July 2025}}</ref> A week later, he made his debut as a second-half substitute and subsequently scored on his debut in Rangers' [[UEFA Champions League]] qualifier against [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]] in a 2–0 victory.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rangers 2-0 Panathinaikos|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cm2lgl1x1vpt|publisher=BBC Sport |date=22 July 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Born in Mauritania, Gassama represented France at youth international level. In September 2022, he was called up to the [[France national under-20 football team|France under-20 team]] for two [[exhibition match|friendly]] matches against [[Tunisia national under-20 football team|Tunisia]].<ref>{{cite web|title=EDF U20 : 22 éléments pour le stage en Tunisie|url=https://www.actufoot.com/edf-u20-22-elements-pour-le-stage-en-tunisie|date=15 September 2022|access-date=15 July 2025}}</ref>

In March 2026, Gassama received his first call-up to the [[Mauritania national football team|Mauritania national team]]. On 27 March 2026, he made his debut for Mauritania in a 2–1 loss to [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]].<ref>{{ cite news|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/mens-international-review-2026-04-02/5iqC7KW5HuSUWw2yDkYVcF|title=Men's International Review|date=2 April 2026|first=Craig|last=Vickers|work=Rangers.co.uk }}</ref>

'''Yang Hyun-jun''' ({{Korean|hangul=양현준}}; born 25 May 2002) is a South Korean professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] (or [[Defender (association football)#Wing-back|right wing-back]] if necessary) for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and the [[South Korea national football team|South Korea national team]].

==Club career==

===Gangwon FC===
Yang joined [[Gangwon FC]] just after graduating from high school in 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20210107131400007 |script-title=ko:강원FC, 박상혁·양현준·김기환·김대우 '신인 계약' |language=ko |publisher=Yonhap News Agency |date=2021-01-07 |access-date=2024-03-28}}</ref> He was evaluated as the best [[K League]] talent by winning four Young Player of the Month awards and the [[K League Young Player of the Year Award|Young Player of the Year award]] in his second professional season.<ref name="awards">{{cite news |url=https://www.goal.com/kr/%EB%89%B4%EC%8A%A4/goal-live-%E1%84%8B%E1%85%A3%E1%86%BC%E1%84%92%E1%85%A7%E1%86%AB%E1%84%8C%E1%85%AE%E1%86%AB-k%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%84%80%E1%85%B31-%E1%84%8B%E1%85%A7%E1%86%BC%E1%84%91%E1%85%B3%E1%86%AF%E1%84%85%E1%85%A6%E1%84%8B%E1%85%B5%E1%84%8B%E1%85%A5%E1%84%89%E1%85%A1%E1%86%BC-%E1%84%89%E1%85%AE%E1%84%89%E1%85%A1%E1%86%BC--%E1%84%89%E1%85%B5%E1%84%8C%E1%85%B3%E1%86%AB-%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A5%E1%86%AB%E1%84%81%E1%85%A1%E1%84%8C%E1%85%B5%E1%84%86%E1%85%A1%E1%86%AB-%E1%84%92%E1%85%A2%E1%84%83%E1%85%A9-%E1%84%87%E1%85%A1%E1%86%AE%E1%84%8B%E1%85%B3%E1%86%AF-%E1%84%8C%E1%85%AE%E1%86%AF-%E1%84%86%E1%85%A9%E1%86%AF%E1%84%85%E1%85%A1%E1%86%BB%E1%84%83%E1%85%A1/blt89f51b053ac17cb0 |script-title=ko:[GOAL LIVE] 양현준, K리그1 영플레이어상 수상…"시즌 전까지만 해도 받을 줄 몰랐다" |website=Goal.com |language=ko |date=2022-10-24 |access-date=2024-03-28}}</ref> He attracted Koreans with his dribbling skills during the season, especially in the [[K League All-Star Game]] against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://sports.news.nate.com/view/20220728n33723 |script-title=ko:[인터뷰] '토트넘전 라이징스타' 양현준 "언젠간 국대로 뛰고파" |language=ko |website=Nate.com |publisher=Ilyo Shinmun |date=2022-07-28 |access-date=2024-03-28}}</ref>

===Celtic===

On 15 July 2023, Gangwon FC announced that Yang would be transferring to [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://gangwon-fc.com/news/222109 |script-title=ko:강원FC 양현준 셀틱 이적 '한국 축구 발전 위한 대승적 결정' |language=ko |publisher=Gangwon FC |date=15 July 2023 |access-date=15 July 2023}}</ref> On 24 July, Celtic announced that Yang had signed on a five-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66288703 |title=Celtic sign Hyunjun Yang on five-year deal from Gangwon FC |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 July 2023 |access-date=24 July 2023}}</ref> Yang made his Celtic debut in a 4–2 victory over [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on 5 August. He also made his [[UEFA Champions League]] debut as a starter in a 2–1 defeat to [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] on 4 October. He scored his first goal for Celtic in a 6–0 victory over [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on 12 November.

On 12 February 2025, Yang provided his first Champions League assist in a 2–1 loss to [[Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://fbref.com/en/matches/b424ad1b/Celtic-Bayern-Munich-February-12-2025-Champions-League |title=Celtic vs. Bayern Munich Match Report – Wednesday February 12, 2025 (Leg 1) |publisher=FBref |access-date=2025-02-14}}</ref> On 1 March, he had come on as a 65th minute substitute against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], and was named the Player of the Match by having two goals and one assist which broke a 2–2 tie.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.celticquicknews.co.uk/st-mirren-2-celtic-5-wham-bang-thank-you-yang/ |title=ST MIRREN 2 CELTIC 5: WHAM, BANG, THANK YOU, YANG |publisher=Celtic Quick News |date=2025-03-01 |access-date=2025-03-03}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://cdn.interfootball.co.kr/news/photo/202503/652057_729582_3222.jpg |script-title=ko:"여친 오고 더 잘한다, 집 갈 때 꽃 사가겠다"...양현준 세인트 미렌전 2골 1도움 활약 비결은 '사랑' |language=ko |publisher=InterFootball |date=2025-03-02 |access-date=2025-03-03}}</ref>

On 3 January 2026, Yang broke down [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]' defense with his dribbling to score the opening goal, but Celtic lost 3–1 in the [[Old Firm]] derby despite his solo goal.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/742456 |title=Celtic 1-3 Rangers (Jan 3, 2026) Game Analysis |publisher=ESPN |date=2026-01-03 |access-date=2026-01-03}}</ref> On 10 May, he once again scored a goal in the Old Firm derby, and Celtic won 3–1 this time.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj9p1dvvyxyt |title=Scottish Premiership: Celtic 3-1 Rangers |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2026-05-10 |access-date=2026-05-17}}</ref> In the 2025–26 season, he was promoted from substitute to starter at the club, and helped them surpass the record of 55 Scottish league titles, set by Rangers.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11787/13544351/celtic-3-1-hearts-martin-oneills-side-crowned-scottish-premiership-champions-on-final-day-as-jambos-miss-out-on-historic-title |title=Celtic 3-1 Hearts: Martin O'Neill's side crowned Scottish Premiership champions on final day as Jambos miss out on historic title |publisher=Sky Sports |date=2026-05-17 |access-date=2026-05-17}}</ref> The following week, Celtic extended their contract with him until 2030.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2026/may/22/yang-extends-his-stay-with-celtic-until-2030/ |title=Yang extends his stay with Celtic until 2030 |publisher=Celtic F.C. |date=2026-05-23 |access-date=2026-05-23}}</ref>

==International career==
Yang was selected for the [[South Korea national football team|South Korea national team]] for the [[2023 AFC Asian Cup]], playing two matches as a substitute.<ref name=soccerway/>

Yang was called up to the national team for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.goal.com/en/lists/south-korea-squad-world-cup-2026/blt15c57f5be1972d9b |title=South Korea squad World Cup 2026: Which players have made it to the showpiece in USA, Mexico and Canada? |publisher=Goal |date=2026-05-16 |access-date=2026-05-19}}</ref> On 18 June 2026, he made his [[FIFA World Cup]] debut in a 1–0 defeat to [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://fdp.fifa.org/assetspublic/ce281/r12451/pdf/FullTimeMatchReport-English.pdf |title=Match Report, Group A, Mexico v. Korea Republic 1-0 (0-0) |date=2026-06-19 |access-date=2026-07-04 |publisher=FIFA}}</ref>

'''Kevin Jesús Kelsy Genez''' (born 27 July 2004) is a Venezuelan professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[Venezuela national football team|Venezuela national team]].

==Club career==

=== Early career ===
Having broken into the first team at [[A.C.C.D. Mineros de Guayana|Mineros de Guayana]] in 2021, Kelsy went on to establish himself in the 2022 season, scoring his first goals for the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pasionxeldeporte.com/kevin-kelsi-agarra-un-avioncito-para-mejorar-como-delantero-%E2%9A%AB%F0%9F%94%B5/|title=Kevin Kelsy agarra un »avioncito» para mejorar como delantero|trans-title=Kevin Kelsy grabs a »little plane» to improve as a striker|date=27 July 2022|accessdate=9 October 2022|website=pasionxeldeporte.com|language=Spanish}}</ref>
Kelsy transferred to Liga AUF Uruguaya club [[Boston River]] on 1 January 2023. He was subsequently transferred before making any appearances for the [[Montevideo]]-based side.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kevin Kelsy joins Shakhtar |url=https://shakhtar.com/en/news/2023/january/31_news/31_kevin-kelsy/ |website=shakhtar.com |publisher=FC Shakhtar Donetsk |access-date=28 April 2025 |date=31 January 2023}}</ref>

=== Shakhtar Donetsk ===
On 31 January 2023, [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] announced the signing of Kelsy from Boston River on a contract until the end of December 2027.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kevin Kelsy joins Shakhtar |url=https://shakhtar.com/en/news/2023/january/31_news/31_kevin-kelsy/ |website=shakhtar.com |publisher=FC Shakhtar Donetsk |access-date=31 January 2023 |date=31 January 2023}}</ref> He signed with the [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] club during the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=23 February 2023|access-date=23 February 2023|language=English|title=Ukraine war: UN condemns Russian invasion ahead of anniversary|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-64748349|work=[[BBC News]]}}</ref>

On 23 February 2023, Kelsy was a substitute during the [[2023–24 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] Playoff 2nd Leg against [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]].<ref name="2036611--rennes-vs-shakhtar"/> In the penalty shootout he scored the deciding goal that took Shakhtar Donetsk to the Round of 16.<ref name="2036611--rennes-vs-shakhtar">{{Cite news |date=23 February 2023|access-date=23 February 2023|language=English|title=Rennes 2-1 Shakhtar Donetsk|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2036611--rennes-vs-shakhtar-donetsk/|work=[[UEFA]]}}</ref>

On 19 September 2023, Kelsy scored on his [[UEFA Champions League]] debut against [[FC Porto]] in a 3–1 loss, becoming the fourth-youngest South American to score in the competition behind [[Roque Santa Cruz]], [[Lionel Messi]] and [[Rodrygo]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Shakhtar 1-3 Porto |url=https://shakhtar.com/en/news/2023/january/31_news/31_kevin-kelsy/ |publisher=[[UEFA]] |access-date=28 April 2025 |date=19 September 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title= IFFHS CONTINENTAL NEWS - UEFA CHAMPIONS LEAGUE |url= https://iffhs.com/en/news/iffhs-continental-news-uefa-champions-league-3050 |publisher= The International Federation of Football History and Statistics |access-date=28 April 2025 |date=20 September 2023}}</ref>

=== FC Cincinnati ===
On 30 April 2024, [[Major League Soccer|MLS]] side [[FC Cincinnati]] announced Kelsy's acquisition via loan for the remainder of the [[2024 Major League Soccer season|2024 season]] with an option to buy as part of the MLS U-22 initiative program.<ref>FC Cincinnati acquire Kevin Kelsy on loan from Shakhtar Donetsk (https://www.fccincinnati.com/news/fc-cincinnati-acquire-kevin-kelsy-on-loan-from-shakhtar-donetsk) 30 April 2024.
Retrieved 30 April 2024.</ref> On 11 May 2024 Kelsy scored his first goal for the club as part of a 2–1 win over the [[Columbus Crew]] in the [[Hell Is Real derby|Hell is Real Derby]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Columbus Crew 1-2 FC Cincinnati (May 11, 2024) |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/692764/fc-cincinnati-columbus-crew |access-date=2024-05-12 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

=== Portland Timbers ===
On 25 January 2025, Kelsy completed a transfer from [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] to the [[Portland Timbers]] for a fee reported to be near $6 million. Kelsy signed a four-year contract with a club option for a fifth year.<ref name="timbers.com">Timbers sign forward Kevin Kelsy
(https://www.timbers.com/news/timbers-sign-forward-kevin-kelsy) 22 January 2025.
Retrieved 28 April 2025.</ref>

Additionally, Portland sent $75k in General Allocation Money with performance-related escalators to [[FC Cincinnati]] for Kelsy’s MLS rights.<ref name="timbers.com"/>

Kelsy made his Timbers debut in a 4–1 loss to the [[Vancouver Whitecaps FC|Vancouver Whitecaps]] on 23 February. He tallied his first goal for Portland in his fifth league appearance for the club, a 3–0 home win against the [[Colorado Rapids]] on 22 March.<ref>Timbers down Colorado Rapids in 3-0 shutout win on the road
(https://www.timbers.com/news/recap-timbers-rout-rapids-3-0-in-colorado) 22 March 2025.
Retrieved 28 April 2025.</ref>

could rise with add-ons becoming Rangers second most expensive signing after [[Tore André Flo|Tore Andrè Flo]] in 2000 this was also a club record sale for Portland Timbers with a sell on clause also ==International career==
===Youth===
Kelsy was called up to the [[Venezuela national under-20 football team]] as part of their [[2022 South American Games]] squad and scored on his debut on the 4th of October 2022 against [[Uruguay national under-20 football team|Uruguay U-20]] in a 3–1 loss. He started all three of their group games during the campaign scoring again in their third match against the hosts [[Paraguay national under-20 football team|Paraguay U-20]] in a 2–0 victory but Venezuela were eliminated from the competition on goal difference finishing 3rd in Group A behind Paraguay.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CONMEBOL South American Games 2022 - Scores & Standings |url=https://www.futbol24.com/international/CONMEBOL/South-American-Games/2022 |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=Futbol24 |language=en}}</ref> He was again called up to the squad for the [[2023 South American U-20 Championship]] hosted in [[Colombia]] playing in 8 of the 9 games Venezuela were involved in at the tournament but failed to score any goals with the team finishing 5th in the final stages.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mobile football scores - livescore at Flashscore Mobile |url=https://www.flashscore.co.uk/ |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=www.flashscore.co.uk |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Kelsy was called up to [[Venezuela national under-23 football team]] as part of their [[2024 CONMEBOL Pre-Olympic Tournament]] squad making his debut on the 20th of January 2024 in a 3–3 draw against [[Bolivia national under-23 football team|Bolivia U-23]]. Three days later he scored his first goal in a 1–1 draw against [[Ecuador national under-23 football team|Ecuador U-23]]. Venezuela qualified from the preliminary stages with Kelsy playing 5 games in total at the tournament scoring a 2nd goal in a 2–2 draw against [[Argentina national under-23 football team|Argentina U-23]] during the final stages but Venezuela were eliminated after finishing 4th and did not reach the [[2024 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/table/_/league/fifa.conmebol.olympicsq |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=www.espn.co.uk}}</ref>

===Senior===
Kelsy was called up to the [[Venezuela national football team]] for the first time for their [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2026 FIFA World Cup qualification]] matches against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] and [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]]. On 10 September 2025, he made his senior debut in a 6–3 loss to Colombia at the [[Estadio Monumental de Maturín]] coming on as a 63rd minute substitute for [[Miguel Navarro (footballer)|Miguel Navarro]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/684667/colombia-venezuela |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=www.espn.co.uk}}</ref> On 28 September 2026, he scored his first goal for Venezuela in a 2–1 loss to Japan during a friendly match at the [[Edion Peace Wing Hiroshima]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/401902642/venezuela-japan |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=www.espn.co.uk}}</ref>

'''Youssef Ramalho Chermiti''' (born 24 May 2004) is a Portuguese professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].

== Club career ==
=== Youth career ===
Chermiti is a youth product of Os Marienses, ACF Pauleta, and GD São Pedro, before moving to the youth academy of [[Sporting CP]] in 2016.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sporting.pt/pt/futebol/equipa-principal/plantel/youssef-ramalho-chermiti|title=Youssef Ramalho Chermiti|date=16 October 2019|website=sporting.pt}}</ref>

=== Sporting CP ===
On 22 July 2020, Chermiti signed his first professional contract with Sporting for three seasons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-bwin/sporting/detalhe/youssef-chermiti-assina-contrato-profissional-com-o-sporting|title=Youssef Chermiti assina contrato profissional com o Sporting|website=record.pt|access-date=15 January 2023|archive-date=15 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230115225752/https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-bwin/sporting/detalhe/youssef-chermiti-assina-contrato-profissional-com-o-sporting|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was promoted to their [[Sporting CP B|B-team]] in 2021, but was sidelined with injuries for eight months before training with the senior team in November 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.abola.pt/nnh/2022-11-25/sporting-chermiti-regressa-com-renovacao-na-mira/https%3a%2f%2fwww.abola.pt%2fnnh%2f2022-11-25%2fsporting-chermiti-regressa-com-renovacao-na-mira%2f966049|title=Chermiti regressa com renovação na mira (Sporting)|website=A Bola|access-date=15 January 2023|archive-date=15 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230115225825/https://www.abola.pt/nnh/2022-11-25/sporting-chermiti-regressa-com-renovacao-na-mira/https:%2F%2Fwww.abola.pt%2Fnnh%2F2022-11-25%2Fsporting-chermiti-regressa-com-renovacao-na-mira%2F966049|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Chermiti made his debut for Sporting's main team on 15 January 2023, coming off the bench to replace [[Paulinho (footballer, born November 1992)|Paulinho]] in the 78th minute of a 2–2 [[Primeira Liga]] draw away at [[Lisbon derby|local rivals]] [[S.L. === Everton ===
On 11 August 2023, Chermiti signed a four-year contract with [[Premier League]] club [[Everton F.C.|Everton]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.evertonfc.com/news/3626211/chermiti-signs-for-everton |title=Chermiti Signs For Everton |publisher=Everton F.C. |date=11 August 2023 }}</ref> for a fee of £11.5 million, which could rise to £14 million with add-ons. Sporting CP are also owed 12.5% of any profit Everton receive from a future transfer of the player.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 November 2023 |title=Sporting divulga números do mercado de transferências |trans-title=Sporting discloses transfer market numbers |url=https://www.abola.pt/futebol/noticias/sporting-divulga-numeros-do-mercado-de-transferencias-2023111515540109816 |access-date=15 November 2023 |website= |publisher=A Bola |language=pt-pt}}</ref>

Chermiti made his debut for Everton on 26 August, coming off the bench in the 66th minute to replace [[Lewis Dobbin]] in a 1–0 league loss to [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] at [[Goodison Park]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 August 2023 |title=Wolverhampton sofre mas vence Everton na estreia de Chermiti |trans-title=Wolverhampton suffers but beats Everton on Chermiti's debut |url=https://www.noticiasaominuto.com/desporto/2387286/everton-wolverhampton-ja-ha-onzes-em-goodison-park |access-date=21 November 2023 |website=Notícias ao Minuto |language=pt-pt}}</ref> Four days later, he made his first start for the club in an [[EFL Cup]] match away at [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]]; at half-time, with the ''Toffees'' losing 1–0 to the [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side, Chermiti was replaced by compatriot [[Beto (footballer, born 1998)|Beto]], who went on to score the equaliser; Everton ended up achieving a 2–1 comeback win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 August 2023 |title=Beto estreia-se no Everton com um golo |trans-title=Beto debuts at Everton with a goal |url=https://rr.sapo.pt/bola-branca/noticia/futebol-internacional/2023/08/30/beto-estreia-se-no-everton-com-um-golo/344754/ |access-date=21 November 2023 |website=Rádio Renascença |language=pt-pt}}</ref> On 7 November 2023, Chermiti started for [[Everton F.C. Reserves and Academy|Everton U21s]] in an [[EFL Trophy]] [[2023–24 EFL Trophy|group stage]] match against [[Mansfield Town F.C.|Mansfield Town]], scoring the only goal of the game through an [[Overtime (sports)|extra-time]] [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 November 2023 |title=Chermiti já marca pelo Everton... mas pelos sub-21 |trans-title=Chermiti's already scoring for Everton... but for the U21s |url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/chermiti-ja-marca-pelo-everton-mas-pelos-sub-21-38525326 |access-date=21 November 2023 |website=OneFootball |language=en}}</ref>

=== Rangers ===
On 1 September 2025, Chermiti moved to [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in a deal worth £8 million, which could rise to £10 million with add-ons becoming  Rangers most expensive signing since [[Tore André Flo|Tore Andrè Flo]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite news |title=Youssef Chermiti has joined Rangers from Everton in a deal worth £8m |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11788/13423145/youssef-chermiti- Rangers-to-sign-striker-from-everton-in-10m-deal-on-transfer-deadline-day |access-date=1 September 2025 |publisher=Sky Sports |date=1 September 2025}}</ref> He made his debut for Rangers in a league match on 13 September 2025 in a 2–0 defeat to [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rangers 0-2 Hearts: Visitors go top of Scottish Premiership after Lawrence Shankland double |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4g7ze5187zt |access-date=4 January 2026 [[Danny Röhl|Danny Röhl’s]] first game in charge.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Rangers 3-1 Kilmarnock: New Gers boss Danny Röhl wins first game in charge at Ibrox |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11781/13454504/rangers-3-1-kilmarnock-new-gers-boss-danny-rohl-wins-first-game-in-charge-at-ibrox |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251028114405/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11781/13454504/rangers-3-1-kilmarnock-new-gers-boss-danny-rohl-wins-first-game-in-charge-at-ibrox |archive-date=28 October 2025 |access-date=4 January 2026 |work=Sky Sports |language=en-GB |url-status=live }}</ref> On 3 January 2026 Rangers found themselves 1–0 down to [[Old Firm]] rivals [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] at [[Celtic Park]], Chermiti scored a brace as Rangers came back to win the match 3–1 and go level on points in the Scottish Premiership with their rivals after being 13 points behind them earlier in the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celtic 1-3 Rangers: Youssef Chermiti scores twice in stunning comeback success |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cm20290eg4et |access-date=4 January 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 15 February 2026, he scored his first professional hat-trick as Rangers defeated [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] 4–2 at Ibrox to move within two points of the league leaders.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Murray |first=Ewan |date=15 February 2026 |title=Youssef Chermiti hat-trick powers Rangers to victory over leaders Hearts |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/feb/15/rangers-hearts-scottish-premiership-match-report |access-date=15 February 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/czd8lg0lylpo|title=The curious case of Youssef Chermiti in Danny Rohl's (The)Rangers revolution|date=15 Celtic.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Valente |first=Allan |title=Rangers 2-2 Celtic: Reo Hatate rescues point for champions in stoppage time after Youssef Chermiti wonder goal |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11781/13513040/rangers-2-2-celtic-reo-hatate-rescues-point-for-champions-in-stoppage-time-after-youssef-chermiti-wonder-goal |access-date=2026-03-01 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref>

On 16 May 2026, he scored his second hat-trick of the season on the final match day as Rangers defeated [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] 5–2 at [[Falkirk Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporting |first=Live |title=Rangers sign off in style with thumping win at Falkirk |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c98rjgz0gj2t |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> In doing so he became the first player to score two league hat-tricks in the same Scottish Premiership season since [[Lawrence Shankland]] in [[2022–23 Scottish Premiership|2022–23]] and the first Rangers player to do so since [[Jermain Defoe|Jermaine Defoe]] in the [[2019–20 Rangers F.C. season|2019–20 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shaw |first=Evan |date=2026-05-17 |title=Youssef Chermiti moves into elite Rangers company after heroics vs Falkirk, he cannot be sold |url=https://www.footballinsider247.com/youssef-chermiti-moves-into-elite-rangers-company-after-heroics-vs-falkirk-he-cannot-be-sold/ |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=Football Insider |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 9 August 2026, it was widely reported that Rangers had turned down a £22 million bid from [[Galatasaray S.K.|Galatasaray]] for Chermitti just hours later he suffered a serious ACL knee ligament injury during a match against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] which required him to undergo surgery.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-18 |title=Transfer-linked Rangers star provides hospital social media update after injury blow |url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/26475998.rangers-star-provides-update-hospital-injury-blow/ |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=Glasgow Times |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-11 |title=Rangers suffer 'significant' injury nightmare as ace sidelined long-term after transfer bid rejected |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/rangers/latest-rangers-news/rangers-suffer-significant-injury-nightmare-star-sidelined-long-term-bumper-transfer-bid-rejected-8882030 |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=The Scotsman |language=en}}</ref>

== International career ==
He is a youth international for Portugal, having played up to the [[Portugal national under-21 football team|Portugal U21]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://leonino.pt/youssef-chermiti-com-contrato-profissional/|title=YOUSSEF CHERMITI COM CONTRATO PROFISSIONAL|date=23 July 2020}}</ref>

On 21 November 2023, after representing [[Portugal national under-20 football team|Portugal U20]] in a 2–1 loss in a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] against [[Italy national under-20 football team|Italy U20]], Chermiti announced on social media that an opponent had [[Racism|racially abused]] him during the match.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Costa |first=Eduardo Pedrosa |date=21 November 2023 |title=Chermiti acusa adversário de racismo. "Sei que não vai acontecer nada" |language=pt-pt |trans-title=Chermiti accuses opponent of racism. "I know nothing will happen" |work=[[Jornal de Notícias]] |url=https://www.jn.pt/1164087267/chermiti-acusa-adversario-de-racismo-sei-que-nao-vai-acontecer-nada/ |access-date=21 November 2023}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Chermiti was born in Azores, Santa Maria in Portugal to a Tunisian-French father and Bissau-Guinean mother. Chermiti holds Portuguese, Tunisian, French and Bissau-Guinean citizenship.<ref name="auto" /> Chermiti is the cousin of the Tunisian footballer [[Amine Chermiti]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tunisie-foot.com/2019/08/14/expatries-qui-est-youssef-ramalho-chermiti/|title=[Expatriés] : Qui est Youssef Ramalho Chermiti ?}}</ref>

'''Olwethu Mpilwenhle Makhanya''' (born 30 April 2004) is a South African professional [[Association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[South Africa national soccer team|South Africa national team]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.snl24.com/soccerladuma/local/sa-players-abroad/makhanya-the-anticipation-was-killing-me-20230808|title=Makhanya: The Anticipation Was Killing Me|publisher=snl24.com}}</ref>

==Club career==
Makhanya started his career with South African side [[Stellenbosch F.C.|Stellenbosch]], where he was regarded to have performed well for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sowetanlive.co.za/sport/soccer/2023-07-18-stellies-proud-to-release-makhanya-to-us-league-club/|title=Stellies proud to release Makhanya|publisher=sowetanlive.co.za}}</ref>

He was nominated for South Africa Young Footballer of the Year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.snl24.com/soccerladuma/fan-park/what-could-olwethu-makhanya-bring-to-mamelodi-sundowns-20230621|title=What could Olwethu Makhanya offer at Downs?|publisher=snl24.com}}</ref>

He won the [[2022-23 Nedbank Cup]] Most Promising Player award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.snl24.com/soccerladuma/local/sa-players-abroad/olwethu-makhanya-how-i-got-signed-by-philadelphia-union-20230723|title=Makhanya: How Philadelphia Scouted Me In SA|publisher=Soccer Laduma}}</ref>

In 2023, he signed for American side [[Philadelphia Union]], becoming the club's first under-22 initiative signing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sabcsport.com/soccer/news/olwethu-makhanyas-special-mls-status-explained|title=Olwethu Makhanya's special MLS status explained|publisher=sabcsport.com}}</ref>

On 30 July 2026, Makhanya signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on a four-year deal with the option for an additional year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/Article/rangers-sign-olwethu-makhanya-from-philadelphia-union/6AoV8I0ox6dKCjET9sXWAM| title=Rangers Sign Olwethu Makhanya From Philadelphia Union|publisher=[[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] }}</ref> Makhanya was named the [[Scottish Professional Football League|SPFL]] Player of the Month for September 2026.<ref name=sept2026potm>{{Cite web |last=Shaw |first=Louise |date=8 October 2026 |title=McInnes and Makhanya Win September Awards |url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/news/mcinnes-and-makhanya-win-september-awards |access-date=16 October 2026 |publisher=Rangers Football Club |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
On 28 May 2026, he was selected by manager [[Hugo Broos]] to represent his nation at the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=9 June 2026 |date=28 May 2026 |language=fr |title=La liste de l'Afrique du Sud pour le Mondial, adversaire du Mexique dans le match d'ouverture de la Coupe du monde |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/La-liste-de-l-afrique-du-sud-pour-le-mondial-adversaire-du-mexique-dans-le-match-d-ouverture-de-la-coupe-du-monde/1679499 |website=L'Équipe}}<!-- auto-translated from French by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Union |first=Philadelphia |title=Philadelphia Union Agree To Transfer Of Defender Olwethu Makhanya to Rangers F.C. |url=https://www.philadelphiaunion.com/news/philadelphia-union-agree-transfer-defender-olwethu-makhanya-to-rangers-fc |access-date=2026-08-01 |website=Philadelphia Union |language=en}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Makhanya is known for his bravery.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.timeslive.co.za/sport/soccer/2023-07-01-young-players-who-need-to-play-their-last-season-in-the-psl-and-move-overseas/|title=Olwethu Makhanya - Times Live article}}</ref> He can operate as a central defender in a back four or a back three.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.snl24.com/kickoff/sanews/sa-players-abroad/philadelphia-union-director-opens-on-signing-explosive-makhanya-20230720|title=Philadelphia Union director opens up on signing 'explosive' Makhanya|publisher=Kick Off}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Makhanya has regarded England international [[John Stones]] as one of his soccer idols.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://947.co.za/articles/2023/07/20/former-stellenbosch-fc-star-olwethu-makhanya-living-the-american-dream-in-mls|title=Olwethu Makhanya living the American dream in MLS|publisher=947.co.za}}</ref> Olwethu was born in Durban South Africa.

'''Kim Min-su''' ({{Korean|hangul=김민수}}; born 19 January 2006) is a South Korean professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] or [[attacking midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[South Korea national football team|South Korea national team]].

== Early life ==
Born in [[Gwangju, Gyeonggi]], South Korea, Kim moved to [[Spain]] in 2016 and joined Penya Blaugrana Cinc Copes. Then, he joined Escola de Futbol Premier Barcelona after two seasons,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Segura |first=Arnau |date=15 November 2024 |title=«Ell no venia a divertir-se, venia a treballar»: el camí de Minsu Kim |url=https://www.diaridegirona.cat/girona-fc/2024/11/15/ell-venia-divertir-venia-treballar-111697545.html |journal=Diari de Girona}}</ref> and {{ill|CE Mercantil|es|Club Esportiu Mercantil}}'s youth sides in 2020.

In 2022, after two years at [[CF Damm|Damm]], Kim joined [[Girona FC|Girona]] and was initially assigned to the ''Juvenil'' squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lesportiudecatalunya.cat/girona/article/2470269-minsu-solucio-de-futur.html|title=Minsu, solució de futur|trans-title=Minsu, solution of the future|publisher=[[L'Esportiu]]|language=ca|date=21 October 2024|accessdate=21 October 2024}}</ref>

== Club career ==
===Girona===
Kim made his senior debut with [[Girona FC B|Girona B]] on 30 October 2022, coming on as a second-half [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Jastin García]] in a 1–0 [[Tercera Federación]] home loss to [[CF Peralada|Peralada]]. He scored his first goal on 18 December, netting the B team's third in a 4–3 away win over [[UE Vilassar de Mar|Vilassar de Mar]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gironafc.cat/es/noticias/el-girona-b-supera-al-vilassar-y-cierra-con-buen-pie-el-2022|title=El Girona B supera al Vilassar y cierra con buen pie el 2022|trans-title=Girona B defeat Vilassar and end 2022 in a good foot|publisher=Girona FC|language=es|date=19 December 2022|accessdate=21 October 2024}}</ref>

On 21 August 2024, after establishing himself as a regular starter for the B team, Kim renewed his contract until 2027.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lesportiudecatalunya.cat/girona/article/2450946-minsu-kim-renova-fins-al-2027-amb-el-girona.html|title=Minsu Kim renova fins al 2027 amb el Girona|trans-title=Minsu Kim renews until 2027 with Girona|publisher=[[L'Esportiu]]|language=ca|date=21 August 2024|accessdate=21 October 2024}}</ref> He made his first team debut and [[La Liga]] debut on 19 October, replacing [[Alejandro Francés]] in a 1–0 home loss to [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.diaridegirona.cat/girona-fc/2024/10/21/minsu-tresor-l-academia-debuta-109909826.html|title=Minsu, el tresor de l’Acadèmia debuta al primer equip|trans-title=Minsu, the treasure of the Academy makes his first team debut|publisher=[[Diari de Girona]]|language=ca|date=21 October 2024|accessdate=21 October 2024}}</ref> He scored 11 goals in the [[2024–25 Tercera Federación|regular season]] and two goals in the [[2025 Tercera Federación play-offs|promotion play-offs]] as he helped the B team promote to the [[Segunda Federación]].<ref name="besoccer"/>

On 15 July 2025, Kim was loaned to [[Segunda División]] side [[FC Andorra|Andorra]], for one year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gironafc.cat/noticies/minsu-jugara-aquesta-temporada-amb-landorra|title=Minsu jugarà aquesta temporada amb l’Andorra|trans-title=Minsu will play this season at Andorra|publisher=FC Andorra|language=ca|date=15 July 2025|accessdate=15 July 2025}}</ref> On 31 August, he scored his first goal for Andorra in a 2–1 win over [[Burgos CF|Burgos]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcandorra.com/en/matches/season-2025-2026-laliga-hypermotion-3-fc-andorra-vs-burgos-cf|title=FC Andorra vs Burgos CF - LALIGA HYPERMOTION M3|language=En|date=31 August 2025|accessdate=16 January 2026}}</ref> Back to Girona in July 2026, he was assigned to the main squad also in division two in the following month.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gironafc.cat/es/noticias/minsu-y-jastin-tendran-ficha-del-primer-equipo|title=Minsu y Jastin tendrán ficha del primer equipo|trans-title=Minsu and Jastin will have a first team registration|publisher=Girona FC|language=es|date=13 August 2026|accessdate=27 August 2026}}</ref>

===Rangers===
On 27 August 2026, Kim signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on a four-year deal with the option of a further year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/Article/rangers-confirm-signing-of-minsu-kim-from-girona/TnXd0YC1uDZzzQqTv1s2x |title=Rangers Confirm Signing Of Minsu Kim From Girona |publisher=Rangers F.C. |date=27 August 2026 |accessdate=27 August 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
On 24 September 2026, Kim made his debut for the [[South Korea national football team|South Korea national team]] in a friendly against Ecuador.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/401905196/ecuador-south-korea|title=South Korea 3-0 Ecuador (Sep 24, 2026) Final Score - ESPN|date=24 September 2026|access-date=13 October 2026}}</ref>
