'''Vanja Dragojević''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Вања Драгојевић}}; born 11 January 2006) is a Serbian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Rangers}} club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[Serbia national football team|Serbia national team]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/vanja-dragojevi/934070/ |title=Vanja Dragojević |website=soccerway.com |date=2025-05-20 |language=en}}</ref>

==Club career==
Dragojević began training at the "FK Altina" football school in [[Zemun]], where [[Dušan Vlahović]] also took his first steps in football.<ref name="Meridian">{{cite news|url=https://meridiansport.rs/fudbal/vanja-dragojevic-intervju/|title=Dragojević krenuo stopama Vlahovića|last=Kalajdžić|first=Luka|publisher=Meridian Sport|date=21 April 2025|accessdate=5 May 2025}}</ref> Dragojević later went through all the junior levels of [[FK Partizan|Partizan]],<ref name="Šaranov">{{cite news|url=https://www.mozzartsport.com/fudbal/vesti/ko-je-vanja-dragojevic-i-zasto-se-probio-u-partizanu-devet-od-deset-ljudi-mi-je-reklo-da-bezim-od-njega/511428|title=Ko je Vanja Dragojević i zašto se probio u Partizanu: Devet od deset ljudi mi je reklo da bežim od njega!|last=Rakanović|first=N.|publisher=Mozzart Sport|date=4 May 2025|accessdate=5 May 2025}}</ref> and also played for the club in the [[UEFA Youth League]].<ref name="HotSport">{{cite news|url=https://hotsport.rs/2023/11/01/biser-humske-vanja-dragojevic-za-hs-potpisivanje-ugovora-sa-partizanom-je-ostvarivanje-decackih-snova-foto/|title=Biser Humske Vanja Dragojević ZA HS: 'Potpisivanje ugovora sa Partizanom je ostvarivanje dečačkih snova!' (foto)|last=Jojić|first=Sava|publisher=HotSport|date=1 November 2023|accessdate=5 May 2025}}</ref> He signed his first professional contract in September 2023, when he was presented to the public with peers including goalkeeper Vanja Radulaški and [[Ognjen Ugrešić]] and [[Zoran Alilović]], also midfielders.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://partizan.rs/sr/article/3195|title=Profesionalni ugovori za buduće nade!|website=partizan.rs|date=18 September 2023|accessdate=5 May 2025}}</ref> During the summer of 2024, after playing for the youth team, Dragojević was immediately transferred to [[FK Teleoptik|Teleoptik]], for whom he played his first senior matches in the [[Serbian League Belgrade]].<ref name="Šaranov"/> He made 12 appearances and scored 2 goals in that competition,<ref>{{Instagram|p/DGOfsbpIEdg|@pbg.news 🚨 𝐁𝐑𝐄𝐀𝐊𝐈𝐍𝐆: Defanzivni vezista Vanja Dragojević (‘06) priključen je prvom timu. Prethodne polusezone nosio je dres Teleoptika za koji je odigrao dvanaest utakmica i postigao dva gola.}}</ref> before the sports department decided to terminate his loan.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://meridiansport.rs/fudbal/partizan-vratio-talentovanog-vezistu-sa-pozajmice/|title=Partizan vratio talentovanog vezistu sa pozajmice|last=Brnjašević|first=Marko|publisher=Meridian Sport|date=18 February 2025|accessdate=5 May 2025}}</ref>

Dragojević made his debut for the first team in the round of 16 of the [[Serbian Cup]] away against [[FK Radnik Surdulica|Radnik Surdulica]], replacing [[Mihajlo Ilić]] in the 83rd minute.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.zurnal.rs/scc/clanak/210001/fudbal/kup-srbije/partizan-lako-sa-radnikom-u-kupu-srbije-video|title=Партизан лако са Радником у Купу Србије (видео)|last=С|first=С.|publisher=[[Sportski žurnal]]|date=12 March 2025|accessdate=5 May 2025}}</ref> Ten days later, he played, paired with [[Aleksandar Filipović (footballer)|Aleksandar Filipović]] in the [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre-back]] positions,<ref name="Meridian"/> against [[PFC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] in a friendly match.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tvarenasport.com/fudbal/vesti-iz-fudbala/44071/cska-partizan-prijateljski-mec-izvestaj/news|title=Od najavljenog spektakla do indijske serije: Moskovljani nose pobedu iz Beograda|publisher=[[Arena Sport]]|date=22 March 2025|accessdate=5 May 2025}}</ref> In the following period, he also established himself in the [[Serbian SuperLiga]], and at the end of the [[2024-25 Serbian SuperLiga|2024/25]] season. he appeared as a regular as one of the bonus players.<ref name="Intervju_FKP">{{cite news|url=https://partizan.rs/sr/article/4642/vanja-dragojevic-zdjelar-je-bio-kapiten-i-grobar-do-koske-ugledam-se-na-njega|title=Vanja Dragojević – Zdjelar je bio kapiten i grobar do koske, ugledam se na njega!|website=partizan.rs|date=1 April 2025|accessdate=5 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="Baby_Zdjelar">{{cite news|url=https://www.mozzartsport.com/fudbal/vesti/baby-zdjelar-stupa-na-veliku-pozornicu/508861|title="Baby Zdjelar" stupa na veliku pozornicu|last=Rakanović|first=N.|publisher=Mozzart Sport|date=2 April 2025|accessdate=5 May 2025}}</ref> He played the entire match against [[Red Star Belgrade]] at the [[Rajko Mitić Stadium]] as part of the 176th [[Eternal derby (Serbia)|eternal derby]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sportal.blic.rs/prica/vanja-dragojevic-govorio-posle-poraza-od-crvene-zvezde-2025041217202900933|title=Vanja Dragojević govorio posle poraza od Crvene zvezde|last=Krga|first=Iva|publisher=[[Sportal.rs]]|date=12 April 2025|accessdate=5 May 2025}}</ref> He ended his first season in professional competition with an assist for [[Milan Vukotić]] in a win over [[FK Vojvodina|Vojvodina]] in the final round. After that, he officially extended his contract with Partizan until 2030. A release clause of 15 million euros was added to the contract. Following the departure of [[Aleksandar Jovanović (footballer, born December 1992)|Aleksandar Jovanović]], [[Bibars Natcho]] was elected as the new captain of Partizan, and Dragojević as the vice captain. He wore the armband in a friendly match against [[FK Radnički Niš|Radnički Niš]] on the first day of summer 2025. Dragojević scored his first goal for Partizan in the 10th round of the [[Serbian SuperLiga]], against [[OFK Beograd]] at the [[Kraljevica Stadium]] in [[Zaječar]], when, after a possession and a solo run, he hit the net guarded by [[Balša Popović]].

On 23 July 2026, Dragojevic signed for Scottish club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on a four-year deal with the option of an additional year.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/Article/rangers-announce-signing-of-vanja-dragojevic/3Hb8p2vcLmzCdj88TMn17T|title=Rangers Announce Signing Of Vanja Dragojević|publisher=[[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]|date=23 July 2026|accessdate=23 July 2026}}</ref> On 16 August 2026, Dragojević scored his first goal at the [[Ibrox Stadium]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] round of 16 against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

==Playing style==
Standing at 184 centimetres tall,<ref name="Srbijasport">{{cite web|url=https://srbijasport.net/player/27212-vanja-dragojevic|title=Vanja Dragojević|website=srbijasport.net|accessdate=5 May 2024}}</ref> Dragojević primarily plays as a [[defensive midfielder]].<ref name="Meridian"/> [[Bojan Šaranov]], former [[FK Partizan|Partizan]] goalkeeper and Vanja's agent, described him as a player with a strong character and physical predispositions.<ref name="Šaranov"/> Dragojević is characterized by a competitive mentality, impudence and aggressive play, which is why he was often penalized with cards in the younger categories.<ref name="HotSport"/><ref name="Baby_Zdjelar"/> He has a playing style similar to [[Kristijan Belić]],<ref name="Meridian"/> while he singled out [[Saša Zdjelar]] as his footballing role model.<ref name="Intervju_FKP"/> Upon his transition to senior football, he was often compared to that player.<ref name="Baby_Zdjelar"/> He was occasionally dropped to the last line, in the position of a [[Defender (association football)|defender]].<ref name="Meridian"/><ref name="FK_Partizan"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://informer.rs/sport/partizan/991691/vanja-dragojevic-pojacanje-fk-partizan|title=Stiže pojačanje u Humsku! Vezista priključen prvom timu! (foto)|last=S|first=M.|newspaper=[[Informer (newspaper)|Informer]]|date=18 February 2025|accessdate=5 May 2025}}</ref>

'''Callum James Osmand''' (born 8 November 2005) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]. A former youth international for [[Football Association of Wales|Wales]], he is only eligible to represent [[The Football Association|England]] at senior level due to a rule change concerning players from the [[Channel Islands]].<ref name="auto">{{cite news|url=https://nation.cymru/sport/wales-boss-craig-bellamy-disappointed-he-cannot-consider-celtics-callum-osmand/|title=Wales boss Craig Bellamy disappointed he cannot consider Celtic's Callum Osmand|first=Stephen|last=Price|date=6 November 2025|work=Nation.Cymru|access-date=6 November 2025}}</ref> He is affectionately nicknamed 'The Heartbreak Kid'<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-10-18 |title=CeltsAreHere (@HereCelts) on X |url=https://x.com/HereCelts/status/2111854400423510072 |access-date=2026-10-24 |work=X (formerly Twitter) |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Fulham===
Osmand signed with [[Premier League]] club [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] at youth and development level in 2018, at the age of 13,<ref name=jep/> following time playing in Jersey for [[Grouville F.C.|Grouville]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://uogjsport.co.uk/how-jersey-produced-an-old-firm-winner-and-the-struggles-of-nurturing-young-talent-on-an-island|title=How Jersey produced an Old Firm Winner and the Struggles of Nurturing Young Talent on an Island
|date=3 November 2025|work=Park Life Sport|access-date=16 May 2026}}</ref> before signing his first professional contract in June 2023.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bailiwickexpress.com/news/jersey-teenager-17-signs-contract-premiership-side-fulham/|title=Jersey teenager signs contract with Premiership side Fulham|author=Bailiwick Express News Team|date=13 July 2023|work=Bailiwick Express News|access-date=7 November 2025}}</ref>

===Celtic===
On 30 June 2025, Osmand signed a four-year contract with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-30 |title=Celtic confirm fourth summer signing as Brendan Rodgers details excitement |url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/25277504.celtic-confirm-signing-callum-osmand-fulham/ |last=Meikle |first=Blair |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=The National |language=en |archive-date=3 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250703035351/https://www.thenational.scot/sport/25277504.celtic-confirm-signing-callum-osmand-fulham/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He cited the club's "winning mentality" as a reason for joining.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-30 |title="The winning mentality at Celtic is unbelievable," Callum Osmand |url=https://onefootball.com/pt-br/noticias/the-winning-mentality-at-celtic-is-unbelievable-callum-osmand-41313940 |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=OneFootball |language=en |archive-date=3 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250703035351/https://onefootball.com/pt-br/noticias/the-winning-mentality-at-celtic-is-unbelievable-callum-osmand-41313940 |url-status=live }}</ref> Manager [[Brendan Rodgers]] said, "We are really pleased to bring Callum to Celtic. He is a highly-rated, talented young player. He has some real attributes. He's a quick and powerful striker and I'm really looking forward to working with him. I'm sure he can be really successful with us".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-30 |title=Celtic delighted to sign Callum Osmand |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2025/june/30/celtic-delighted-to-sign-callum-osmand/ |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=Celtic FC |language=en |archive-date=30 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250630140350/https://www.celticfc.com/news/2025/june/30/celtic-delighted-to-sign-callum-osmand/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=30 June 2025 |title=Thanks Matt – Former Hoops hero O'Riley helped sell Celtic to Callum Osmand |url=https://thecelticstar.com/thanks-matt-former-hoops-hero-oriley-helped-sell-celtic-to-callum-osmand/ |access-date=3 July 2025 |website=The Celtic Star |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=10 June 2025 |title=How Celtic can get the best out of Callum Osmand as Fulham boss talks 'profile' |url=https://www.celticway.co.uk/news/25229677.celtic-can-get-best-striker-callum-osmand/ |access-date=3 July 2025 |website=Celtic Way |language=en}}</ref>

Despite this praise, Osmand did not play a single minute under Rodgers, failing to even make a matchday squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.footballinsider247.com/celtic-fans-puzzled-by-baffling-brendan-rodgers-decision-hes-certainly-proved-him-wrong/|title=Celtic fans puzzled by 'baffling' Brendan Rodgers decision, 'he's certainly proved him wrong'|first=Ciaran|last=Morrison|date=2 November 2025|website=Football Insider}}</ref> After Rodgers' resignation, his replacement [[Martin O'Neill]] gave Osmand his debut on 29 October 2025 against [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] in the [[Scottish Premiership]], in O'Neill's first game in charge. He came on as a substitute for the final 15 minutes; this was also his first senior appearance as a footballer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2025/october/29/celts-secure-three-points-with-an-impressive-performance-at-paradise/|title=Celts secure three points with an impressive performance at Paradise|date=29 October 2025|website=Celtic FC}}</ref> Four days later, Osmand netted his first senior goal, scoring Celtic's third in their 3–1 victory over [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] semi-final.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cj41w1584w7t|title=Celtic 3-1 Rangers|last=Dowden|first=Martin|date=2 November 2025|website=BBC Sport|access-date=2 November 2025}}</ref> In his third game, a [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] tie against [[FC Midtjylland|Midtjylland]], he was stretchered off with a hamstring injury. O'Neill stated that Osmand would be out of action "for months".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/celtic-manager-martin-oneill-gives-injury-update-on-alistair-johnston-marcelo-saracchi-and-callum-osmand|title=Martin O'Neill counting cost of Celtic’s win at Kilmarnock as injuries pile up|author=PA Media|date=10 November 2025|work=STV News|access-date=10 November 2025}}</ref>

He finally made his return to action on 16 May 2026, coming on as a substitute against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] in the final game of the league season. Osmand provided the assist for [[Daizen Maeda]]'s goal to give their side the lead, then in injury time he scored the final goal in a 3–1 victory to seal the title.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/may/16/celtic-v-hearts-scottish-premiership-title-decider-live|title=Celtic break Hearts with late double in tense final-day decider to retain Scottish title – as it happened|first=Simon|last=Burnton|date=16 May 2026|via=www.theguardian.com}}</ref>

Following Celtic's 2–0 win over Falkirk on 29 August 2026, in which he came on as a 70th-minute substitute, Osmand was seen leaving Celtic Park on crutches. It was later reported that he faced several weeks out with an ankle injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.celticway.co.uk/news/26511363.oneill-provides-celtic-injury-update-tierney-hogh-osmand/|title=Martin O'Neill provides Celtic injury update on Tierney, Hogh and Osmand|date=1 September 2026|website=Celtic Way}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aol.com/articles/celtic-v-aberdeen-team-news-195830000.html|title=Celtic v Aberdeen: Team news - AOL|date=1 September 2026|website=AOL.com}}</ref> He made his long-awaited return on 15 October against [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in the Europa League, coming on as a substitute for [[Sebastian Tounekti]] and playing the second half in an unfamiliar left wing role.<ref>https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/26643210.celtic-player-offered-fresh-hope-new-position-vs-benfica/</ref> This was followed by his first ever start against Hearts three days later where he scored twice in a 7–1 demolition at Celtic Park.<ref>https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/50210960/celtic-hearts-painful-lesson-match-report-callum-osmand-benjamin-nygren-kieran-tierney</ref>

==International career==
Osmand was born in Jersey and played for [[Football Association of Wales|Wales' under-16 and under-17 sides]] in 2021, which he was eligible to do as the rules at the time permitted someone born in the [[Channel Islands]] to represent any UK nation internationally, regardless of family ties. These rules were subsequently changed, however, meaning that Osmand is only eligible to represent [[England national football team|England]] at senior level as he has no Welsh, Scottish or Northern Irish family.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/25601670.celtic-stars-international-career-scuppered/|title=How obscure football rule change has scuppered Celtic star's international hopes|last=McCafferty|first=Josh|date=6 November 2025|website=The National|access-date=6 November 2025|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="auto"/>

'''Camilo Andrés Durán Márquez''' (born 10 February 2002) is a Colombian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and the [[Colombia national football team|Colombia national team]].

A youth product of [[Independiente Medellín]], Durán spent time with the under-20 side of [[CR Flamengo|Flamengo]] before moving to Portugal in 2022, where he began his senior career in the fifth tier with [[S.C. Lusitânia|Lusitânia]] of the [[Azores]]. He helped the club to successive promotions, reaching [[Liga 3 (Portugal)|Liga 3]] in 2024, before joining [[Liga Portugal 2]] club [[Portimonense S.C.|Portimonense]]. In August 2025 he signed for [[Qarabağ FK|Qarabağ]], and scored five goals in his first [[UEFA Champions League]] campaign, beginning with a goal on his debut in the club's first win in the competition proper. He joined Celtic in July 2026 in a transfer reported as a record sale for Qarabağ.

Durán received his first call-up to the [[Colombia national football team]] in September 2026.

==Early life==
Durán was born on 10 February 2002 in [[Santa Marta]],<ref name=capsulas2021 /> and grew up in a poor neighbourhood of the city as the youngest son of Hugo Durán, a bicycle repairman.<ref name=elcolombiano2026>{{cite news |last=Martínez González |first=Brandon |date=22 January 2026 |title=Camilo Durán: el "rebelde" que deambuló por Santa Marta, se volvió delantero en el DIM y ahora brilla en Champions |url=https://www.elcolombiano.com/deportes/futbol/camilo-duran-historia-santa-marta-qarabag-dim-cantera-champions-CP32793450 |work=[[El Colombiano]] |language=es |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref> He joined the local youth club Cozi Córner Niko at the age of nine and later played for Huracán La Ocho.<ref name=capsulas2021 /><ref name=elcolombiano2026 />

==Club career==
===Youth career===
After interest from [[Unión Magdalena]] fell through when he was 13,<ref name=elcolombiano2026 /> Durán joined the academy of [[Independiente Medellín]] in 2015 on the recommendation of scout Humberto "Tucho" Ortiz.<ref name=capsulas2021 /> He arrived as a midfielder and was converted into a forward by his under-15 coach, Sebastián Botero, scoring 38 goals in one season while playing above his age group.<ref name=elcolombiano2026 /> On 26 March 2021, he scored the winning goal in the 76th minute of the final of the Liga Antioqueña's Primera A against Estudiantes de Medellín.<ref name=capsulas2021 />

In September 2021, Durán joined Flamengo on loan until the end of 2022, with two options to buy, and was assigned to the club's under-20 side.<ref name=gazeta2021>{{cite news |author=Redação |date=3 September 2021 |title=Time colombiano confirma empréstimo de atacante ao Flamengo |url=https://www.gazetaesportiva.com/times/flamengo/time-colombiano-confirma-emprestimo-de-atacante-ao-flamengo/ |work=Gazeta Esportiva |language=pt-BR |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref><ref name=colunadofla2021>{{cite news |date=4 September 2021 |title=Flamengo acerta contratação de atacante colombiano |url=https://colunadofla.com/2021/09/flamengo-acerta-contratacao-de-atacante-colombiano/ |work=Coluna do Fla |language=pt-BR |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref>

===Lusitânia and Estrela da Amadora===
In 2022, Durán moved to Portugal to join [[S.C. Lusitânia|Lusitânia]] of [[Angra do Heroísmo]], then competing in the Azores regional championship, the fifth tier of Portuguese football.<ref name=abola2026>{{cite news |author=Redação |date=18 September 2026 |title=Camilo Durán: do distrital açoriano à seleção da Colômbia em três épocas |url=https://www.abola.pt/noticias/camilo-duran-do-distrital-acoriano-a-selecao-da-colombia-em-tres-epocas-2026091809344869268 |work=[[A Bola]] |language=pt |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref> He scored 19 goals in 20 matches in the 2022–23 season as Lusitânia won the Azores championship and the [[Angra do Heroísmo Football Association]] cup, earning promotion to the [[Campeonato de Portugal (league)|Campeonato de Portugal]].<ref name=record2023>{{cite news |last=Guerra |first=Francisco |date=9 July 2023 |title=Extremo colombiano contratado ao Lusitânia dos Açores a treinar com a equipa principal |url=https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-betclic/e--amadora/detalhe/extremo-colombiano-contratado-ao-lusitania-dos-acores-a-treinar-com-a-equipa-principal |work=[[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]] |language=pt |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref>

On 9 July 2023, with his contract at Lusitânia having expired, Durán joined [[Primeira Liga]] club [[C.F. Estrela da Amadora|Estrela da Amadora]] on a free transfer to play for their under-23 side under [[Sérgio Vieira (football manager)|Sérgio Vieira]].<ref name=record2023 /> He scored three goals in three matches for the club's B team,<ref name=portimonense2024>{{cite web |date=3 September 2024 |title=Camilo Duran é alvinegro |url=https://www.portimonensesad.pt/camilo-duran-e-alvinegro_22152 |publisher=Portimonense SAD |language=pt |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref> before returning to Lusitânia, where he scored 12 goals as the club, coached by [[Ricardo Pessoa]], won promotion from the Campeonato de Portugal to [[Liga 3 (Portugal)|Liga 3]] in May 2024.<ref name=abola2026 /><ref name=abola2024>{{cite news |author=Redação |date=25 May 2024 |title=Campeonato de Portugal: Lusitânia dos Açores sobe à Liga 3 |url=https://www.abola.pt/noticias/campeonato-de-portugal-lusitania-dos-acores-sobe-a-liga-3-2024052515052688749 |work=[[A Bola]] |language=pt |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref>

===Portimonense===
On 3 September 2024, Durán signed a four-year contract with [[Liga Portugal 2]] club [[Portimonense S.C.|Portimonense]], reuniting with Pessoa, who had become the club's coach.<ref name=portimonense2024 /><ref name=abola2024b>{{cite news |last=Anjinho |first=Jorge |date=3 September 2024 |title=Camilo Durán «feliz» por reencontrar Pessoa no Portimonense |url=https://www.abola.pt/noticias/camilo-duran-feliz-por-reencontrar-pessoa-no-portimonense-2024090316502638860 |work=[[A Bola]] |language=pt |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref> He scored five goals in 26 league appearances in the [[2024–25 Liga Portugal 2]] season.

===Qarabağ===
On 25 August 2025, Durán joined [[Azerbaijan Premier League]] club [[Qarabağ FK|Qarabağ]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://baku.ws/en/sport/fc-karabakh-strengthened-its-squad-with-a-new-player |title=FC "Karabakh" strengthened its squad with a new player |date=25 August 2025 |website=Baku.ws}}</ref> Three weeks later, on 16 September, he made his [[UEFA Champions League]] debut away to [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] at the [[Estádio da Luz]]; with Qarabağ trailing 2–0, he scored their second goal two minutes after half-time with an angled finish from a [[Marko Janković (footballer, born 1995)|Marko Janković]] pass, and they went on to win 3–2. The result was the club's first victory in the Champions League proper, and Durán was named man of the match.<ref name=flashscore2025>{{cite web |last=Hilsum |first=James |title=Qarabag mount incredible comeback against Benfica for first-ever Champions League win |url=https://www.flashscore.com/news/champions-league-benfica-qarabag-report/Gt8SjiqJ |publisher=Flashscore |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref><ref name=vavel2025>{{cite web |last=Monteiro |first=Lucas |date=16 September 2025 |title=Goals and Highlights: Benfica 2-3 Qarabag in UEFA Champions League |url=https://www.vavel.com/en-us/soccer/2025/09/16/1233876-benfica-vs-qarabag-live-score-updates-in-champions-league.html |website=VAVEL |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref>

He also scored in a 4–2 defeat to [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]],<ref name=flashscoreajax>{{cite web |last=Winters |first=Paul |title=Danish dynamite earns youthful Ajax first Champions League win of the season vs Qarabag |url=https://www.flashscore.com/news/soccer-champions-league-danish-dynamite-earns-youthful-ajax-first-champions-league-win-of-the-season/r5H7yYyq/ |publisher=Flashscore |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref> and scored twice in a 3–2 win over [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] that all but secured Qarabağ's place in the knockout phase.<ref name=flashscorefrankfurt>{{cite web |last=Radcliffe |first=Jon |title=Qarabag get late winner to stun Frankfurt & all but seal Champions League progression |url=https://www.flashscore.com/news/qarabag-frankfurt-report-champions-league/UVjdIGH0 |publisher=Flashscore |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref> In the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knockout phase play-offs]], Qarabağ were eliminated 9–3 on aggregate by [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]; Durán scored in the 3–2 second-leg defeat at [[St James' Park]].<ref name=vavel2026>{{cite web |last=Rodriguez Arias |first=Juan Sebastian |date=25 February 2026 |title=Highlights and Goals Newcastle vs Qarabag (3-2) in UEFA Champions League |url=https://www.vavel.com/en-us/soccer/2026/02/24/1251893.html |website=VAVEL |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref> He finished the season with 15 goals in all competitions, including five in the Champions League.<ref name=sky2026>{{cite news |date=10 July 2026 |title=Camilo Duran: Celtic make first new summer signing as striker joins from Qarabag on five-year deal |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/13561241/camilo-duran-celtic-make-first-new-summer-signing-as-striker-joins-from-qarabag-on-five-year-deal |publisher=[[Sky Sports]] |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref>

===Celtic===
On 10 July 2026, Durán joined [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on a five-year contract, becoming manager [[Martin O'Neill]]'s first signing of the summer.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celtic are delighted to sign Colombian forward, Camilo Duran |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2026/july/10/celtic-are-delighted-to-sign-colombian-forward--camilo-duran-/ |publisher=Celtic F.C. |date=10 July 2026 |access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref><ref name=sky2026 /> The fee was reported as around £6 million including add-ons,<ref name=sky2026 /><ref name=scotsman2026>{{cite news |last=Elder |first=Matthew |date=10 July 2026 |title=Camilo Duran's first words as a Celtic player as transfer confirmed and contract details revealed |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/celtic/latest-celtic-news/camilo-durans-first-words-as-a-celtic-player-as-transfer-confirmed-and-contract-details-revealed-8788901 |work=[[The Scotsman]] |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref> and Colombian media described it as the highest transfer fee Qarabağ had ever received.<ref name=infobae2026>{{cite news |last=Ariza |first=Diego |date=10 July 2026 |title=Camilo Durán fichó con el Celtic de Escocia y ya hizo historia con el club: esta es la razón |url=https://www.infobae.com/colombia/deportes/2026/07/11/camilo-duran-ficho-con-el-celtic-de-escocia-y-ya-hizo-historia-con-el-club-esta-es-la-razon/ |work=[[Infobae]] |language=es |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref>

On 19 August 2026, Durán scored twice in a 3–0 home win over [[LASK]] in the first leg of the [[2026–27 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] play-off round,<ref name=sky2026lask>{{cite news |last=Conroy |first=Alison |date=19 August 2026 |title=Celtic 3-0 LASK: Camilo Duran nets stunning double as Hoops edge towards Champions League return |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11787/13574093/celtic-3-0-lask-camilo-duran-nets-stunning-double-as-hoops-edge-towards-champions-league-return |publisher=[[Sky Sports]] |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref> after which O'Neill described his display as "a world-class performance".<ref name=goal2026>{{cite news |last=Makayasa |first=Adhe |date=20 August 2026 |title=Martin O'Neill hails 'world-class' Camilo Duran as Celtic cruise past LASK in Champions League play-off |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/lists/celtic-martin-oneill-camilo-duran-lask-champions-league-play-off/blt85e75a15f3a18dd7 |work=[[Goal (website)|Goal]] |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref> Celtic lost the second leg 5–1 and were eliminated 5–4 on aggregate, entering the [[2026–27 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] instead.<ref name=tnt2026>{{cite web |last=Baynes |first=Ciaran |date=25 August 2026 |title=LASK v Celtic - Champions League play-off, second leg result as the hosts produce remarkable recovery to dump Scottish champions into Europa League |url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/football/champions-league/2026-2027/live-lask-celtic_mtc21878414/live-commentary.shtml |publisher=[[TNT Sports (United Kingdom)|TNT Sports]] |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref> Durán was named the [[Scottish Professional Football League|SPFL]] Player of the Month for August 2026.<ref name=celtic2026potm>{{cite web |date=4 September 2026 |title=Camilo Durán is August's SPFL Player of the Month |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2026/september/04/camilo-dur-n-is-august-s-spfl-player-of-the-month/ |publisher=Celtic F.C. |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
In September 2026, Durán received his first call-up to the senior [[Colombia national football team]] from head coach [[Néstor Lorenzo]], for friendlies against [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]], [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]] and [[Peru national football team|Peru]].<ref name=elheraldo2026>{{cite news |agency=[[EFE]] |date=18 September 2026 |title=Estos son los 26 jugadores de la Selección Colombia para los amistosos contra México, Paraguay y Perú |url=https://www.elheraldo.co/deportes/2026/09/18/estos-son-los-26-jugadores-de-la-seleccion-colombia-para-los-amistosos-contra-mexico-paraguay-y-peru/ |work=[[El Heraldo (Colombia)|El Heraldo]] |language=es |access-date=26 September 2026}}</ref><ref name=abola2026 />

==Style of play==
Durán is a left-footed forward who can play on either wing or through the centre.<ref name=record2023 /><ref name=elcolombiano2026 /> He was a midfielder until the age of 15, when he was converted into a striker at Independiente Medellín, and his youth coach Sebastián Botero has credited his composure in front of goal.<ref name=elcolombiano2026 />

'''Colby Donovan''' (born 7 September 2006) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].

==Club career==
A youth product of [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], Donovan graduated from their academy and signed his first professional contract with the club on 2 July 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thecelticstar.com/nine-academy-graduates-sign-first-professional-contracts-celtic-confirm/|title=Nine Academy Graduates sign first professional contracts, Celtic confirm|date=2 July 2022|website=thecelticstar.com}}</ref> 

He was promoted to their [[Celtic F.C. B Team and Academy|B-team]] in 2023 which his performances earned him opportunities with the senior squad. He travelled with the first team for pre-season in the [[United States]] during the summer of 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sinat |first=Patrick |date=2024-07-29 |title=Brendan Rodgers shares what Colby Donovan learned from facing Raheem Sterling in Celtic's win vs Chelsea |url=https://www.67hailhail.com/news/brendan-rodgers-shares-what-colby-donovan-learned-from-facing-raheem-sterling-in-celtics-win-vs-chelsea/ |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=67 Hail Hail |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In the summer of 2025 he was promoted to their senior team, and signed a new contract at the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.celticway.co.uk/news/25409479.celtic-youth-update-new-emerging-name-colby-donovans-situation/|title=Celtic youth update: A new name to look out for and Colby Donovan's situation|date=22 August 2025|website=Celtic Way}}</ref> 

He was rewarded with his senior and professional debut with Celtic after coming on as a substitute for [[Anthony Ralston]] in a 3–0 [[Scottish Premiership]] win over [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on 23 August 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/celtic-vs-livingston-live-score-35781266|title=Celtic vs Livingston – LIVE updates|first1=Graeme|last1=Young|first2=Ryan|last2=McDonald|first3=Anthony|last3=Evans|date=23 August 2025|website=Daily Record}}</ref>

Donovan’s first European start came on 24 September 2025 away in [[Serbia]] against [[Red Star Belgrade]] in their opening [[UEFA Europa League]] league-phase match which ended 1–1.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Red Star 1-1 Celtic (24 Sep, 2025) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/757799/celtic-red-star-belgrade |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=www.espn.co.uk}}</ref> When asked about his performance after the game, Donovan said "I just try and play with no fear and have as much confidence as I can,"<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-25 |title=Celtic's Colby Donovan plays 'with no fear' in maiden European start |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/ckg3z78dqxvo |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> 

On October 26, 2026 [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] announced that Donovan signed a new long-term contract ending 2031.<ref>{{Cite web |last=FC |first=Celtic |date=2026-10-26 |title=Celtic delighted as Colby Donovan signs new long-term deal |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2026/october/26/celtic-delighted-as-colby-donovan-signs-new-long-term-deal/ |access-date=2026-10-27 |website=Celtic FC |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
Donovan was called up to the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21]]s for a set of [[2027 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification]] matches in September 2025.<ref>{{cite news |title=Scotland Men's Under-21 squad finalised ahead of new European Championship qualifying campaign |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-mens-under-21-squad-finalised-ahead-of-new-european-championship-qualifying-campaign/?rid=13925 |access-date=26 August 2025 |publisher=Scottish FA |date=25 August 2025}}</ref> He was later called up to the senior national team ahead of international friendlies in September 2026, but has yet to make an appearance.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Colby Donovan {{!}} Scotland - Scottish FA |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/en/teams/mens-team/colby-donovan |access-date=2026-10-02 |website=www.scottishfa.co.uk |language=en}}</ref>

'''Ryan Don Naderi''' ([[Bulgarian language|Bulgarian]]: Райън Дон Надери; born 10 July 2003) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]. Born in [[Germany]] to a [[Czechs|Czech]] mother and [[Bulgarians|Bulgarian]] father,<ref name="podcast">{{cite web|access-date=2025-11-27 |date=2025-11-05 |title=Neue Folge des Hansa-Podcast mit Ryan Naderi |url=https://www.fch.de/news/neue-folge-des-hansa-podcast-mit-ryan-naderi.html |website=fch.de|language=de}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> he plays for the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic national team]].<ref name="soccerway">{{cite web|url=https://www.soccerway.com/player/naderi-ryan-don/jar3Kipo/|title= R. Naderi - Profile with news, career statistics and history|website=Soccerway|access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref>

==Early life==
Naderi grew up in Dresden.<ref name="CTZ26">{{cite news |url=https://www.liga3-online.de/hansa-auf-stuermersuche-kommt-gladbach-talent-ryan-naderi/|title=Hansa auf Stürmersuche: Kommt Gladbach-Talent Ryan Naderi|website=liga3-online.de|date=27 August 2024|access-date=3 February 2026|language=de}}</ref> He started his journey in football playing for SG Dresden Striesen and Soccer for Kids in Dresden before moving to the youth academy of [[Dynamo Dresden]] in 2015. With Dynamo Dresden he played two seasons in the [[Under 17 Bundesliga|Under-17 Bundesliga]] and in the [[Under 19 Bundesliga|Under-19 Bundesliga]] in 2020–21. For the 2021–22 season, he moved to [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]], where he played in the West division of the Under-19 Bundesliga.

==Career==

===Borussia Mönchengladbach===
Naderi made his debut in the [[2021–22 Regionalliga|2021–22 season]] when he came on as a substitute for [[Borussia Mönchengladbach II]] during a [[Regionalliga West]] home match against [[FC Schalke 04 II|Schalke 04 II]] on 22 January 2022. Despite having a professional contract, he was not included in the [[Bundesliga]]'s [[Borussia Mönchengladbach|senior squad]].<ref name="CTZ26" />

===Hansa Rostock===
Naderi then transferred to [[3. Liga]] side [[FC Hansa Rostock|Hansa Rostock]] at the end of August 2024, after two years at Borussia Mönchengladbach II.<ref>{{cite web |website=Hansa Rostock|url=https://www.fch.de/news/stuermer-ryan-naderi-wechselt-aus-gladbach-zum-f-c-hansa.html|title=Stürmer Ryan Naderi wechselt aus Gladbach zum F.C. HansaStürmer Ryan Naderi wechselt aus Gladbach zum F.C. Hansa |date=3 February 2026|language=de}}</ref> On 14 September 2024, Naderi made his professional debut in a home game against [[SV Waldhof Mannheim|Waldhof Manheim]] that finished in a 1–1 draw, coming on as a substitute in the 59th minute. A week later, Naderi scored his first goal for Hansa Rostock in an away game against his former club Dynamo Dresden that finished as a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.ostsee-zeitung.de/sport/regional/hansa-rostocks-torschuetze-ryan-naderi-und-seine-emotionale-reise-zurueck-4UPMH7HB7FE2RCEIPQNF6GGOUE.html |title=Ein unbeschreibliches Gefühl“ – Hansa Rostocks Ryan Naderi und seine emotionale Reise zurück|website=Ostsee Zeitung|date=22 September 2024|access-date=3 February 2026|language=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dnn.de/sport/regional/naderi-zeigt-hansa-rostock-und-seiner-mutter-was-er-bei-dynamo-dresden-gelernt-hat-MCB4LETLTBFP7HOYDMXIUVGLQU.html |title=Naderi zeigt Hansa Rostock und seiner Mutter, was er bei Dynamo Dresden gelernt hat |website=dnn.de|date=22 September 2024|access-date=3 February 2026|language=de}}</ref> In the [[2024–25 FC Hansa Rostock season|2024–25 season]], Naderi finished fifth with Hansa and won the [[Mecklenburg-Vorpommern Cup]]. After scoring two goals in a 4–2 away win against [[FC Viktoria Köln|Viktoria Köln]], Naderi was voted "Player of Matchday 12" in the [[2025–26 3. Liga|2025–26 season]].<ref name=Liga3>{{cite news |url=https://www.liga3-online.de/leser-waehlen-ryan-naderi-zum-spieler-des-12-spieltages/|title=Leser wählen Ryan Naderi zum "Spieler des 12. Spieltages"|website=liga3-online.de|date=28 October 2025|access-date=3 February 2026|language=de}}</ref> Naderi was also voted "Player of Matchday 21" after a 4–0 away win over Waldhof Manheim, in which he collected a hat-trick of assists.<ref name=Liga3/>

===Rangers===
On 3 February 2026, Naderi signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on a long-term deal for an undisclosed fee, which was widely reported to be £4.7 million.<ref name=Sky>{{ cite news | url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11788/13502536/ryan-naderi-rangers-sign-striker-from-hansa-rostock-on-deadline-day-as-club-seal-fourth-january-arrival| title=Ryan Naderi: Rangers sign striker from Hansa Rostock on Deadline Day as club seal fourth January arrival | work=Sky Sports | date=3 February 2026}}</ref> Rangers had initially agreed to sign the striker in the summer for a fee of £3 million but increased their offer in order to push through the deal on transfer deadline day.<ref name=Sky/> Two days later Naderi made his debut for Rangers coming on as a second half substitute as Rangers defeated Kilmarnock 5–1 in a league match at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rangers 5-1 Kilmarnock {{!}} Rangers Football Club |url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/node/19194 |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=www.rangers.co.uk |language=en}}</ref> On 8 February 2026, Naderi started his first game for Rangers against [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queens Park]] in the [[Scottish Cup]] and scored a brace as Rangers won the match 8–0 to advance to the quarter-final.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rangers 8 - 0 Queen's Park|url=https://www.theguardian.com//football/match/2026/feb/08/rangers-v-queenspark |access-date=2026-02-08 |work=The Guardian}}</ref> On 4 April 2026, he scored his first Scottish Premiership goal in a 4–2 victory over [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee Utd]] but also suffered a muscle injury during the match which required him to be substituted at half-time causing him to only play in one more game the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-10 |title=Ryan Naderi muscle injury 'serious', says Rangers head coach Danny Rohl |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/crr1k4wzr2ko |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 16 August 2026, Naderi started the season by scoring his first ever [[Scottish League Cup]] goal in a 5–1 victory over [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] a game in which he also got an assist.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rangers 5-1 St Mirren (16 Aug, 2026) Final Score - ESPN (UK) |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/401901388/st-mirren-rangers |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> Four days later he scored his first [[UEFA Conference League]] goal in a 1–0 victory over [[FK Jablonec|Jablonec]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rangers 1-0 Jablonec {{!}} Rangers Football Club |url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/node/19125 |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=www.rangers.co.uk |language=en}}</ref> On 5 September 2026, he scored his first league goal of the season in a 1–0 win over [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporting |first=Live |title=Rangers 1-0 Motherwell: Scottish Premiership radio commentary, updates & match report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c3n071wq9edet |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 20 September 2026, Naderi scored his first [[Old Firm]] goal against Rangers rivals [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] which was the only goal in a 1–0 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celtic 0-1 Rangers (20 Sep, 2026) Final Score - ESPN (UK) |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/401878375/rangers-celtic |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> On 24 September, Naderi scored his fifth league goal in six games in a 4–0 victory over [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone (13 Aug, 2022) Final Score - ESPN (UK) |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/639066/st-johnstone-rangers |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> On 31 October 2026, he scored the only goal in the Scottish League Cup semi-final against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] to put Rangers into the final.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moffat |first=Live ReportingColin |last2=Cohen |first2=Charlotte |last3=Gilkison |first3=Cal |title=Rangers vs Aberdeen LIVE: Scottish League Cup radio commentary, live text, team news, stats, match report & reaction |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cmx23ln75zk0t |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
Naderi was eligible to represent [[Germany national football team|Germany]], [[Bulgaria national football team|Bulgaria]] and [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]]. In March 2026 he was approached by Bulgaria's manager [[Aleksandar Dimitrov]] to join the team for the [[2026 FIFA Series (men's matches)|2026 FIFA Series]].<ref>[https://www.ibroxnews.com/2026/03/15/ryan-naderi-rangers-striker-approached-by-bulgaria-ahead-of-fifa-series/ Ryan Naderi: Rangers striker approached by Bulgaria ahead of FIFA series]</ref><ref>[https://btvsport.bg/bgfootball/borim-se-s-germanija-i-chehija-za-futbolen-nacional-eto-kakvo-reshi-toj.html Борим се с Германия и Чехия за футболен национал. Ето какво реши той!]</ref> In September 2026, he made the definitive decision to represent the Czech Republic.<ref>{{cite web |title=Naderi je odhodlaný reprezentovat Česko. Mrzí mě, že jsme ještě nedotáhli papírování, říká Nedvěd|url=https://www.irozhlas.cz/sport/fotbal/naderi-je-odhodlany-reprezentovat-cesko-mrzi-me-ze-jsme-jeste-nedotahli_2609191016_rej|publisher=[[Czech Radio]]|language=cs|date=19 September 2026|access-date=2 October 2026}}</ref> On 29 September 2026, Naderi was called up to the Czech Republic national team for [[2026–27 UEFA Nations League]] fixtures.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ryan Naderi se připojil k národnímu týmu|url=https://www.fotbal.cz/repre/ryan-naderi-se-pripojil-k-narodnimu-tymu/a24631|publisher=[[Football Association of the Czech Republic]]|language=cs|date=29 September 2026|access-date=2 October 2026}}</ref> He made his full international debut on 3 October in a Nations League match against [[FIFA World Cup]] holders [[Spain national football team|Spain]].

'''Joël van den Berg''' (born 11 February 2007) is a Dutch [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].

== Club career ==
Van den Berg is a product of the youth academies of the Dutch clubs SV Houten, [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]], and [[SBV Vitesse|Vitesse]] before signing a professional contract with [[PSV Eindhoven|PSV]] on 6 July 2023 until 2026, where he finished his development.<ref name="q985">{{cite web | title=PSV acquires Joël van den Berg from Vitesse | website=PSV | date=2023-07-06 | url=https://www.psv.nl/en/media/article/psv-professional-contract-acquires-joel-van-den-berg-from-vitesse | access-date=2026-08-03}}</ref> He was promoted to their [[Jong PSV|reserves]] in 2024, and on 23 April 2025, he extended his contract with PSV until 2028.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://studio040.nl/nieuws/artikel/jong-psv-weet-joel-van-den-berg-langer-aan-zich-te-binden|title=Jong PSV weet Joël van den Berg langer aan zich te binden|website=studio040.nl}}</ref> He debuted with the senior PSV team in a 4–2 [[Eredivisie]] win over [[FC Groningen]] on 23 August 2025.<ref name="p050">{{cite web | title=Joël van den Berg: creatieve middenvelder met overzicht | website=PSV | date=2026-05-21 | url=https://www.psv.nl/media/artikel/spelersprofiel-joel-van-den-berg-creatieve-middenvelder-met-overzicht | language=nl | access-date=2026-08-03}}</ref>

On 2 September 2026, Van den Berg signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] for an undisclosed fee on a four-year deal, with an option for a further year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2026/september/02/celtic-delighted-to-sign-joel-van-den-berg/ |title=Celtic delighted to sign Joel van den Berg |publisher=Celtic F.C. |date=2 September 2026 }}</ref> Injury kept him out of action until his first day of training in October 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.celticway.co.uk/news/26673931.oneills-celtic-updates-van-den-berg-yang-alistair-johnston/|title=O'Neill's Celtic updates on Van den Berg, Yang and being 'careful' with Johnston|date=October 27, 2026|website=Celtic Way}}</ref>

== International career ==
Van den Berg is a youth international for the Netherlands.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2549014-de-toekomst-van-oranje-twintig-grote-talenten-van-nederland-anno-2024|title=De toekomst van Oranje: twintig grote talenten van Nederland anno 2024|date=December 20, 2024|website=nos.nl}}</ref> He captained the [[Netherlands national under-19 football team|Netherlands U19]]s in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://voetbalflitsen.nl/nieuws/v62sj7/psv-excelsior-eredivisie-talenten-jeugdspelers-bosz|title=Dit zijn de 6 jeugdspelers in PSV-selectie die indruk maakte op Bosz|date=January 10, 2026|website=Voetbalflitsen.nl}}</ref>
